entries.title: Variable Speed Push-in Cinematic Prompt
entries.description: A highly detailed cinematic prompt for a subway scene with variable speed camera movement, designed for high-end video models like Seedance 2.0.
entries.prompt:
Character appearance and identity reference [Image 1]. Late-night subway car, last carriage in motion, no other passengers except her. She sits alone, head down, hands naturally crossed on her lap. Amber overhead lights illuminate her, while the surrounding carriages are deep cyan-grey-blue, creating a quiet and oppressive atmosphere.

Total duration 10 seconds, one continuous shot, no cuts. Use the texture of a 50mm Cooke Speed Panchro vintage lens, soft highlights, restrained halos. Fixed focal length, the camera actually pushes forward along the axis facing the character, focus continuously follows the character's face.

0–3s: Almost static.
Start from a medium shot showing the character's sitting posture and crossed hands. The camera moves forward extremely slowly, almost imperceptibly. She sits quietly with head down, shoulders relaxed, only subtle natural breathing. Audio is primarily low-frequency subway rumble, with nearly inaudible ambient music without melody or drums.
3–6s: Sudden high-speed approach.
The camera suddenly accelerates significantly, approaching her at high speed along the same axis. The character rapidly grows larger in the frame, carriage perspective changes naturally as the camera moves forward, creating strong frontal pressure. Acceleration is decisive, motion continuous, cannot be processed as uniform or gentle push throughout. She still keeps her head down, breathing gradually shallow, shoulder and neck tensing slightly, crossed fingers tightening gently. Low-frequency drone increases rapidly with the push, kept restrained, not overpowering environmental sounds.

6–6.2s: Abrupt braking, sudden stop.
The camera brakes abruptly within approx 0.2 seconds, stopping suddenly at a facial close-up, fully preserving forehead and chin with some space. Speed is still evident before stopping, braking is short and forceful, presenting the impact of high-speed motion being suddenly cut off. No early easing, no face-hugging, no rushing into the face. After stopping, camera position stabilizes immediately, no sliding, rebound, or shaking; character's breathing and movements continue naturally, image must not freeze.
At the moment of braking, surrounding cyan-grey-blue ambient light decays rapidly, amber warm light on her face remains, forming stylized light-dark convergence, dark areas still faintly reveal carriage structure. Only change lighting and tonal layers, keep carriage structure, object positions, and materials continuous and consistent.

Simultaneously with the camera stop, ambient music cuts cleanly, no sound effect hits or reverb tails. Subway rumble continues, clearly indicating only the camera stopped, train is still moving.
6.2–6.7s: Brief pause.
Camera completely static. She still keeps her head down, briefly maintaining posture, only subtle breathing. Only low-frequency subway rumble and character's breathing remain, music does not enter again.
6.7–9s: Slowly raising head.
She slowly raises her head, gaze naturally shifts to the lens, finally looking directly at the camera. Jaw, neck, and shoulder movements are coordinated, actions restrained and coherent, shoulder and neck still carrying tension. Her slow movement forms a distinct rhythmic contrast with the previous rapid push.

9–10s: Gaze.
Maintain static close-up. She continues to look directly at the camera, only subtle breathing, leaving a quiet yet pressurized emotional pause. Do not add music, sudden sound effects, or other actions.

4K Ultra HD, 3840x2160, 16:9 landscape. Realistic cinematic photography texture, preserving natural skin texture, hair, and fabric details, soft highlights, layered shadows. Allow natural motion blur during high-speed push phase, eyes and facial features clear after abrupt stop. Character identity, facial proportions, and structure always consistent, expressions change naturally with actions, hand structures correct.
Only this one woman in the frame. No duplicates, ghosts, facial distortion, clipping, stuttering, over-sharpening, skin smoothing, or HDR feel. No dialogue, subtitles, watermarks, or logos.

entries.title: Seedance 2.0 Cinematic Optical Zoom Video Prompt
entries.description: A detailed video generation prompt for Seedance 2.0 featuring a cinematic optical zoom technique in an ancient Jiangnan town setting, focusing on character interaction and realistic camera physics.
entries.prompt:
[Global Settings]
Ancient-style realistic cinematic shot, Eastern classical life narrative, Jiangnan ancient town after rain: bluestone steps, blue bricks and black tiles, wooden corridors, carved wooden doors, bamboo curtains, wet stone alleys. Soft diffused light under cloudy skies, low contrast, fusion of cold gray-green and warm wood tones, slight 35mm film grain, realistic skin, wood, stone, and fabric textures, cinematic shallow depth of field, 8K, 16:9.

Female Lead A: Image 1
Female Lead B: Image 2

Strictly maintain character identity, spatial position, left-right relationship, direction of movement, weather, lighting, and color tone continuity throughout the video.

[Core Cinematography Technique]
The entire video uses "progressive optical zoom" as the sole core camera movement. The camera remains as fixed as possible, relying not on physical movement but on slow, continuous optical push-ins and pull-outs to change the characters' screen proportion and spatial relationships. Maintain real lens compression, depth of field changes, and optical characteristics; prohibit digital cropping. Foreground occlusion, shallow depth of field, and focus shifts assist the narrative, forming "discovery from afar -> eye contact across the alley -> spatial compression -> emotional confirmation."

[0-4s]
Medium shot start, 35mm, fixed camera, eye level. Female Lead A slowly descends along the bluestone steps to the alley entrance, stops, turns, and looks up, seeing Female Lead B under the distant corridor eaves. The shot begins with a wider environmental relationship composition, only slowly optically pushing in, gradually tightening to a medium shot of Female Lead A, with no camera movement.

Town pedestrians pass horizontally through the foreground from left and right, creating natural blurred occlusions at close range, while Female Lead A remains clear; exposure, color temperature, and light/shadow remain stable during occlusion. The zoom continues smoothly and restrainedly, finally forming an eye contact between Female Lead A and Female Lead B across the alley.

[4-9s]
Continuing from the previous segment, the camera position remains completely unchanged. Female Lead B slowly enters from the right foreground, approaching the wooden corridor pillar, forming a natural foreground frame with the pillar; Female Lead A is deep in the left-middle alley.

Slow continuous optical zoom, Female Lead A initially remains clear, then the shot gradually tightens, Female Lead B's foreground proportion increases, and Female Lead A recedes into the background with soft blur. Gradually entering the telephoto end, real space compression makes the depth of the ancient alley appear compressed; the actual distance between the two remains unchanged, but the visual distance is clearly shortened. Focus shifts smoothly from Female Lead A to Female Lead B, ending with Female Lead B's side profile clear and Female Lead A blurred. No lateral movement, panning, or orbiting; exposure and tone are continuous.

[9-13s]
Maintain fixed camera and telephoto relationship. Female Lead B stands by the wooden corridor pillar, slowly turning to look at Female Lead A. Perform only one extremely slow optical push-in, tightening from a two-person relationship composition to a medium close-up of Female Lead B. Retain a partial blurred outline of Female Lead A on the left side of the screen, forming a peeping-style foreground frame.

Female Lead B becomes the main focus, looking at Female Lead A, pausing briefly before softly saying: "Long time no see." Showing a faint smile. Bamboo curtains are blown by the gentle post-rain breeze, water drops fall naturally from the eaves, and wet bluestone reflects soft sky light. The camera advances steadily, ending in close-range emotional confirmation.

[Camera Control]
The core must be "optical zoom creating narrative distance changes," rather than camera movement. Camera language completes sequentially: environment establishment -> discovery of Female Lead A -> slow tightening -> Female Lead B enters foreground -> telephoto space compression -> focus shift -> emotional confirmation. Zoom speed is slow and continuous, with real lens inertia; maintain natural character proportions, real depth of field, and stable exposure, clearly presenting the optical zoom feel without cheap digital enlargement.

[Continuity and Negative Constraints]
Strictly follow character cards, prohibit drift in appearance, hairstyle, or clothing; maintain consistency in spatial geographic relationships, left/right positions, movement directions, and light directions. Prohibit modern buildings, vehicles, road signs, modern objects, subtitles, watermarks; prohibit adding major characters, character duplication, limb abnormalities, or identity swaps. Prohibit lateral movement, orbiting, sudden panning, drone movement, strong handheld shake, digital zoom, digital cropping, perspective anomalies, focal length jumps, instant depth of field cuts, exposure flickering, color temperature drift, excessive fogging, excessive smoothing, AI plastic skin.

entries.title: Samurai Castle Assault One-Take
entries.description: An intense action video prompt for a one-take samurai battle sequence with specific camera movements, character consistency locks, and visual effects instructions.
entries.prompt:
KAZEMIRU: THE JADE-WIND BLADE: ONE-TAKE CASTLE ASSAULT
Duration: 30 seconds | Aspect Ratio: 16:9 | No music

ONE-TAKE LOCK:
This is ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN CONTINUOUS SHOT lasting the full 30 seconds.
ZERO cuts. ZERO dissolves. ZERO fades. ZERO match-cuts. ZERO time jumps.
ZERO scene resets. The camera never leaves the action and every location
change happens physically inside the shot: the camera passes through torn
doors, over railings and up the roof with Kazemiru. Time runs in real time.

STYLE:
Ultra-photorealistic live-action Japanese dark-action cinema with restrained
subtle VFX. Impossible anime-inspired dual-sword choreography performed by
real human bodies. Large-format cinema look, natural daylight, muted earthy
color palette, soft realistic shadows, no oversaturated colors.

@Image1 is KAZEMIRU. Preserve her exact face, silver-white ponytail, torn
ivory kimono, charcoal split hakama, wind-swirl forearm tattoo and gold hoop
earrings in every frame.
@Image2 shows the five elite guards. @Image3 shows Captain Tetsugan.

POSITIVE LOCKS (true for all 30 seconds):
- Exactly ONE Kazemiru with exactly TWO real steel katanas, one in each
  hand, both always visible and independently controlled.
- Her face always matches @Image1.
- Every enemy comes from @Image2 or @Image3 and stays visually consistent.
- Her body physically crosses every distance, with no teleportation.
- It is always daytime with bright natural light.

PERSONALITY:
Cold, calm, battle-hungry. Minimal expression, steady breathing, focused
eyes. Her hunger shows through relentless speed and escalating ferocity,
never through grinning or shouting.

JADE-WIND EFFECT:
Every fast movement leaves a thin, soft jade-green wind trace that follows
her exact physical path and fades almost instantly: sword arcs leave fine
blade trails, spins bend the air, footsteps kick tiny wakes, supersonic
bursts add a brief compressed-air ripple. Always thin, subtle and realistic.
No aura, no smoke, no glowing body, no effects moving on their own.

CAMERA (one continuous handheld-style pursuit):
Constant dutch angle of 25–35°. Wide field of view around 75° in the
interior and courtyard, tightening to about 50° for the rooftop duel.
Kazemiru moves first and the camera follows 0.1–0.3 seconds late: whip-pan,
overshoot, correct, reacquire at the moment of contact. The camera flows
through rear over-the-shoulder, low-angle pursuit, side tracking,
ground-level chase and front three-quarter retreat, always in one connected
movement. Never static, never perfectly smooth.

══ 0:00–0:10: THE GRAND AUDIENCE HALL ══
Setting: bright daylight through large shoji panels, gold folding screens,
tall dark timber pillars, tatami sections, raised platform, armor displays,
low lacquer tables, silk curtains.

0:00–0:03: Rear over-the-shoulder, five guards closing in. Her fingers tighten
on both hilts. BURST: a thin jade streak snaps across the hall and the silk
curtains whip. The camera loses her, whip-pans, and finds her inside
Guard 1's reach. Left blade parries, right blade slashes diagonally, a pivot,
a reverse cut. He drops.

0:03–0:06: Guards 2 and 3 converge. She ducks under a swing, plants a foot on
a pillar and pushes off, dust bursting from the wood. Mid-air her left
sword deflects Guard 2 and her right sword cuts down. She lands on the edge
of a lacquer table, which slides back, and rebounds straight toward Guard 3.

0:06–0:10: Aerial right slash, left reverse slash, dual cross-slash with two
separate jade trails. She lands low and bursts across the floor. Guard 4's
spear thrusts: she runs two steps up a wall, flips off, and cuts him down
through a folding screen. Guard 5 charges: she catches his blade with one
sword, vaults the railing above him, and finishes with a cross-slash as she
lands behind him.

══ 0:10–0:20: THE PALACE COURTYARD ══
Transition inside the same shot: she does not pose. Both swords still in
hand, she drives straight through the paper doors in one burst. The torn
paper flutters past the lens as the camera follows her through the doorway
onto the wooden veranda and out into a stone courtyard with lanterns, a koi
pond, a red lacquer arched bridge and pine trees. Eight new guards: swordsmen
below and archers on the roofs.

0:10–0:13: A volley of arrows. She cuts two out of the air with a spinning
double slash and a third grazes her sleeve. She sprints along the veranda,
pivoting off each post, a jade ripple following her feet.

0:13–0:16: She kicks off a stone lantern, which tips over, and leaps onto the
bridge railing. Three swordsmen charge. She runs along the rail, slashes the
first, flips over the second, and lands in the koi pond with a huge splash.
In the water she parries two blades and cuts both guards. Droplets scatter
across the lens.

0:16–0:20: She bursts out of the pond and sprints up a pine trunk in three
steps. The camera tilts up with her. She launches onto the roof among the
archers: left sword disarms, right sword strikes, roof tiles scatter. Two
archers fall.

══ 0:20–0:30: THE ROOFTOP DUEL ══
Transition inside the same shot: she keeps climbing over the roof ridge and
the camera rises with her, tightening to a 50° field of view. The tiled
castle rooftop opens up with wind in her ponytail and the town far below.
Captain Tetsugan (@Image3) waits with his naginata, calm and unflinching.

0:20–0:23: Tetsugan sweeps the naginata in a wide arc. Kazemiru ducks, slides
down the sloping tiles, and crosses both swords to stop the blade. Sharp
metal sound as his strength pushes her back a step. Her expression stays
cold.

0:23–0:27: Fast exchange: his thrust, her left parry, her right slash that cuts
his armor cord. He spins the pole and sweeps for her feet: she jumps, kicks
off the shaft, and flips over him. Mid-air she cuts both swords across his
back armor. Tiles crack under their feet and a faint jade wake curves around
her path. He staggers, strikes back, and she narrowly dodges as the blade
cuts a roof beam.

0:27–0:30: Supersonic burst along the ridge line, the jade streak slightly
brighter but still thin. She slides under the naginata, and as she rises
both swords slice through the shaft in a clean cross-cut. Tetsugan drops to
one knee, defeated but alive. Kazemiru stands, both swords still in hand,
and the last jade filaments disappear. She turns her cold eyes toward the
courtyard far below, where dozens more guards pour in. The camera slowly
pulls back and up to a wide shot of the whole castle. She lowers her body for
the next burst. THE FIGHT CONTINUES.

AUDIO:
Sword resonance, compressed-air whooshes, metal clashes, footsteps on wood
and tiles, arrows, water splashes, fluttering silk and paper, enemy shouts,
wind over the rooftops. No dialogue, no music.

HUMAN-FIRST LOCK:
Kazemiru is always a real human: natural skin pores, real eyes, individual
hair strands, believable anatomy and cloth physics. Only her choreography is
anime-level impossible.

NEGATIVE:
cuts, edits, dissolves, fades, scene transitions, time jumps, multiple
shots, single-sword fighting, missing or duplicate sword, duplicate
Kazemiru, clones, teleportation, thick aura, smoke, glowing body, neon or
oversaturated colors, detached VFX, random flips, decorative acrobatics,
idle pose, static camera, perfectly smooth tracking, slow combat, floating,
broken anatomy, CGI or plastic skin, anime rendering, blood, gore, subtitles,
logos, watermark.

entries.description: Aerial coastline opener that flows into downtown skyline — premium tourism-campaign look with a classic travel-film feel; written as a continuous city transition.
entries.prompt:
Create a cinematic, highly realistic vertical travel-poster style video celebrating San Diego, California, designed to feel like a premium tourism campaign mixed with a classic vintage travel film.

OPENING SHOT:
Start with a breathtaking cinematic aerial view of San Diego from high above the coastline during warm golden hour. The camera slowly glides forward over the deep blue Pacific Ocean toward the city, revealing the beautiful coastline, sandy beaches, palm trees, harbor, marina, boats, and the recognizable downtown skyline in the distance. The ocean should have realistic waves and shimmering sunlight reflections.

CITY TRANSITION:
Smoothly transition from the coastline into an elevated panoramic view of downtown San Diego. Showcase modern skyscrapers, waterfront buildings, bridges, streets, palm-lined roads, and the busy but elegant atmosphere of the city. Use a slow cinematic camera movement with subtle parallax between the foreground, middle ground, and distant skyline.

LANDMARK & CULTURE SHOTS:
Move through a beautiful visual sequence featuring San Diego's iconic coastal lifestyle, historic architecture, palm trees, harbor boats, beach boardwalks, surfers, outdoor cafés, and relaxed California atmosphere. Include recognizable elements of the city without making any single landmark dominate the entire composition.

SUNSET SEQUENCE:
Transition into a spectacular San Diego sunset. The sky gradually changes from warm orange and golden yellow to pink, purple, and deep blue. The sun reflects beautifully across the ocean and harbor while the city skyline becomes softly silhouetted. Add subtle lens flare, realistic atmospheric haze, and cinematic depth.

NIGHT TRANSITION:
As daylight fades, smoothly transition into blue hour and then nighttime. Downtown buildings begin to glow with warm window lights, streetlights illuminate the roads, boats move through the harbor, and reflections of the city lights shimmer naturally across the water. The camera slowly pulls back to reveal the entire illuminated coastline and skyline.

TYPOGRAPHY & POSTER DESIGN:
Throughout the sequence, incorporate elegant vintage travel-poster typography. Display “SAN DIEGO” prominently near the top of the composition in large sophisticated uppercase lettering. Add a subtle secondary line such as “CALIFORNIA” beneath it. The typography should feel integrated into the environment rather than looking like a random digital overlay.

VISUAL STYLE:
Premium cinematic travel advertisement, vintage-inspired California tourism poster, photorealistic environments, realistic human movement, natural ocean physics, detailed architecture, atmospheric perspective, subtle film grain, soft cinematic glow, realistic reflections, sophisticated composition, rich visual depth, and polished professional color grading.

CAMERA & MOTION:
Use slow aerial drone movements, smooth forward glides, gentle camera rotations, cinematic push-ins, wide establishing shots, subtle zoom-outs, and seamless match-cut transitions. Avoid sudden camera movements or artificial-looking motion. Every transition should feel smooth, elegant, and professionally filmed.

LIGHTING:
Natural golden-hour sunlight transitioning gradually into sunset, blue hour, and nighttime. Preserve realistic shadows, highlights, reflections, atmospheric haze, and changing color temperature throughout the sequence.

FINAL SHOT:
End with a majestic wide aerial view of the illuminated San Diego coastline and downtown skyline at night. The ocean fills the foreground while the glowing city stretches across the horizon. Hold the final composition for a moment with “SAN DIEGO — CALIFORNIA” elegantly visible, creating the feeling of a classic collectible travel poster brought to life.

FORMAT:
Vertical 9:16, cinematic composition, ultra-realistic, highly detailed, premium travel commercial aesthetic, smooth motion, realistic physics, natural human proportions, seamless transitions, professional cinematography, immersive atmosphere, no distorted architecture, no flickering, no warped text, no unnatural movements.

entries.description: A complex prompt for generating a 30-second one-shot video traveling through Chinese history, maintaining character consistency while evolving costumes and environments seamlessly.
entries.prompt: Generate a [30-second, 16:9 horizontal, 4K, live-action, high-budget cinematic quality] "Chinese Civilization Time Travel" short film, deeply referencing the actual camera structure and time progression logic of my uploaded reference video: This is not an edit of multiple historical scenes, but a single camera following [the same Chinese male] continuously forward from second 0 to 30, traveling from ancient times through thousands of years of Chinese civilization, and finally continuing past contemporary times into the future like the reference video; Use my uploaded male photo as the [sole and absolute face reference] for the entire film, the photo is only responsible for locking the person's identity, strictly maintaining his face shape, feature proportions, eyebrows/eyes, eye distance, nose bridge/tip, lips, jawbone, facial bone structure, skin tone base, youthful age sense, and recognizability. Absolutely do not reference the blue suit, tie, restaurant, chandelier, roses, jewelry, sitting posture, or background in the photo. Throughout 0-30s, viewers must clearly recognize this is the man from the reference image; prohibit changing actors per era, prohibit feature drift, prohibit becoming different ancient handsome guys or AI template faces. Era changes can only alter his hairstyle, hair length, binding method, beard, clothing materials, footwear, headwear, belts, tools, accessories, status, and habits. The entire film must visually be a true "one-take shot," prohibiting hard cuts, black screens, flash whites, fades, dissolves, sudden scene changes, character teleportation, or background refreshes. The character must never stand still letting the world change around him; he must actively move forward, running, walking fast, crossing, jumping down stairs, dodging sideways, grabbing vehicles, passing through crowds, pushing doors, climbing bridges, passing buildings, going past transport. The camera moves with him, naturally changing framing between side-front tracking, frontal backward tracking, lateral panning, rear chasing, low-angle footsteps, wide shots, and close-ups like the reference video. All era transitions should prioritize hidden cuts using real physical motion, e.g., rocks, pottery wheels, cart wheels, chariots, pillars, flags, fabrics, scrolls, doors, bridge columns, carriages, steam, trains, buses, crowds, glass curtains, transparent barriers passing extremely close to the camera and briefly obscuring for 0.2-0.8 seconds. During obstruction, character styling, held items, ground, and surrounding world must evolve simultaneously. After obstruction ends, stride, center of gravity, direction, speed, and spatial position must completely continue from the previous instant; absolutely no "background changed era but character didn't." 0-3s must be gripping: Early morning sunrise, ancient Chinese cliffs and huge river valleys, low-angle morning light through mist, distant vast mountains/rivers/forests/wildlife/tiny primitive settlements, faint campfire near cave, wind blowing grass and rough long hair. The man is now an ancient Chinese ancestor, face remains him, wearing rough animal skins/plant fibers/primitive weavings, skin with real pores/sweat/dust/light tan, holding stone-tipped wooden spear. He hears a sound, turns quickly, runs forward along slope. Camera drops from wide shot to side-front high-speed tracking. He crosses a large rock, camera lowers following feet; landing moment no cut, dry rock texture spreads forward becoming wet mud/ridges/early farmland. Animal skins turn to hemp/kudzu cloth during run/self-occlusion. Wooden spear shortens to plow/sickle during hand switch. Loose hair binds simply. Surroundings grow semi-subterranean/wood-earth houses/pottery/grain/baskets/mills/livestock/drying racks/people living/laboring. ~3-5s enter Neolithic farming civilization, character rushes through village, dodging residents/animals. Giant rotating pottery wheel passes horizontally extremely close filling frame; clay texture hardens/deepens/gains metallic luster, circular structure evolves into bronze ritual vessel patterns/chariot wheels. ~5-7.5s after obstruction leaves, space continuously enters Xia/Shang/Zhou Bronze Age. Running uninterrupted, coarse hemp clothes become real/simple/structured early Huaxia attire (not Xianxia/idol drama/studio Hanfu). Rammed earth walls/wood structures/bronze casting/furnaces/carriages/horses/flags/ritual vessels/busy residents appear. Runs onto higher road, chariot crosses quickly, he dodges, grabs long flag blown by wind for momentum. Huge flag cloth sweeps camera causing full obstruction; during coverage, hairstyle/collar/leather belt/footwear/road structure evolve toward Qin/Han. ~7.5-10s after cloth leaves, running in real Qin/Han city gates/post roads. Same face unchanged. Ordinary traveler/city male, real bound hair/cross-collar clothes/leather belt/cloth shoes, not emperor/general. Camera tracks from side through gates/inns/crowds/carriages. Briefly grabs edge of moving carriage, carried forward two steps then lets go, keeps running. Giant wooden wheel rolls past close to camera; as wheel leaves, empty road expands/widens along direction adding buildings/shops/goods/crowds/colors. ~10-12.5s continuously enter prosperous Tang Dynasty large city. Character becomes real Tang ordinary city male attire, face kept. Streets not empty film sets but filled with real wood pavilions/vendors/horses/camel teams/diverse merchants/goods/food/cloth/vessels/flags/crowded life flow. Rushes through crowds, ducks under lifted beam, slips between horses/pedestrians. Camera moves from side to frontal backward. Market colored banners fall from above onto camera; fibers thinning turning into unfolded rice paper scroll. Camera slides along surface; ink/river/bridge/building lines gain volume via perspective. No magic glow; painted bridge lines become real railings, landscape lines become river/city structure. ~12.5-15s after passing paper edge, entered extremely prosperous Song Dynasty city. Same man, action uninterrupted, clothes/hair sync to Song. Real rivers/arch bridges/shops/tea houses/boats/vendors/porcelain/calligraphy/printing/goods/dense citizen life extend forward. Runs onto bridge, camera lowers near deck backward tracking. Holds railing dodging large cargo box; box close causes brief obstruction. When found again, rushing down steps pushing giant wooden door. Thick door panel slides past camera; during full obstruction, alleys/buildings/fabric/headwear continue evolving. ~15-17s after passing door, naturally enter Ming/Qing city. Still same man, clothes fit real ordinary resident, no Qing palace drama, no officials/luxury everywhere. entries.title: Seedance 2.0 Travel Vlog Prompt with Consistent Character and City Transitions
entries.description: A detailed prompt for generating a 10-second realistic travel vlog video using Seedance 2.0. entries.prompt:
Generate a 10-second realistic travel vlog style short video. The protagonist is always the same young Asian woman; facial features, hairstyle, clothing, and body proportions must remain consistent throughout. No face swapping or outfit changes.

The entire video consists of 3 independent scenes: Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. City transitions are completed using 'hard cut after snap' method, without background blending, spatial distortion, or architectural dissolving.

0-3s, Beijing.
The girl stands near a representative landmark in Beijing, looking natural and relaxed with empty hands. She looks at the camera, raises her right hand, and snaps her fingers. After the snap, the screen immediately hard cuts to Shanghai.

3-6s, Shanghai.
The girl is already standing near the Bund or Lujiazui in Shanghai, holding a cup of coffee in her right hand. She walks forward naturally two steps, then takes a sip of coffee.
After drinking, she walks to a nearby railing platform or small table where items can be placed, clearly putting down the coffee cup in her right hand. The coffee cup must truly contact the platform, fingers completely release, and the right hand thoroughly leaves the coffee cup. Pause for about half a second to confirm the right hand is empty.
Then she raises her right hand again to snap her fingers. After the snap, the screen immediately hard cuts to Guangzhou. The coffee cup stays in its original position in Shanghai, does not teleport with the person, and is not allowed to disappear into thin air, float, deform, or suddenly switch hands.

6-10s, Guangzhou.
The girl appears empty-handed near Canton Tower. She walks forward naturally two steps, turns to look at Canton Tower, then stands at a suitable position to take a photo with Canton Tower, finally looking gently at the camera and smiling to end.

Maintain real smartphone travel vlog texture throughout, slight handheld feel, natural and simple movements, center of gravity and limb motion conforming to real physical laws.

Special emphasis:
Shanghai segment: Right hand holds coffee → Take a sip → Put coffee cup on fixed platform → Completely release hand → Right hand becomes empty → Snap fingers again.
Do not skip the action of 'putting down coffee', do not allow the coffee cup to directly disappear.

Avoid: Face swapping, clothing changes, body proportion changes, character duplication, extra arms, finger deformities, coffee cup disappearing, coffee cup deforming, cup floating, cup switching hands, character snapping while holding coffee, architectural blending, simultaneous appearance of Beijing/Shanghai/Guangzhou landmarks, city background residuals, overly complex camera movements.

entries.prompt:
Create an explosive, motion-graphics-driven character reveal trailer in 16:9, exactly 13 distinct cuts, 60 fps. AO is a cool, composed anime streetwear girl with a chin-length vivid blue bob with messy bangs, sharp ice-blue eyes, a light-blue knit beanie, an oversized white zip-up hooded windbreaker with blue drawstrings and a blue utility pocket on the left sleeve, a white crop top, light-blue drawstring shorts with a small barcode tag, and chunky white-and-blue platform sneakers. This film is 80% bold graphic design in motion and 20% character action: giant kinetic typography, hard-edged shapes, split-screens, flat color fields, barcode strips, UI ticks, halftone, speed lines and shutter flashes. Palette: ice blue, cobalt, white, silver-grey, black. Style: premium AAA motion-graphics title sequence x streetwear campaign film. Every graphic element moves fast and snaps hard on the beat.

CUT 01 | 0.00–1.00s — Pure graphics: a massive cobalt circle slams onto a white field, two black bars wipe across, tiny UI ticks and a barcode strip flicker; the letters A and O punch in one after another with heavy impact shake.

CUT 02 | 1.00–2.00s — The O becomes a porthole: extreme close-up of her ice-blue eye inside it, glancing up; RGB split flash, then the circle shatters into shards of flat color.

CUT 03 | 2.00–3.10s — Black frame with an enormous white AO; she sprints in from frame left and power-slides across the baseline of the typography, speed lines and ice-blue streaks trailing, shards of the letters kicked up like sparks. Whip-pan out.

CUT 04 | 3.10–4.00s — Split-screen triptych of flat cobalt/white/ice-blue panels; in each panel her silhouette performs a different move in stroboscopic freeze: takeoff, tuck, landing. Huge vertical text FULL SPEED scrolls behind the panels.

CUT 05 | 4.00–5.10s — She leaps through a giant rotating ring of typography reading NO BRAKES NO LIMITS; camera tracks her mid-air spin in slow motion as the letters scatter, then snap-zoom on her confident face.

CUT 06 | 5.10–6.00s — Hard cut: white editorial card, huge black JUMP with a cobalt slash; she vaults over the word itself, palm planted on the J, legs whipping across frame; the word compresses like a spring under her hand and rebounds.

CUT 07 | 6.00–7.00s — Ice-blue field with a black diagonal stripe; she drops into a low street-dance spin and sweeps one leg across the frame, then snaps upright in three stroboscopic freeze frames, each ghost tinted in a different palette color. Giant outlined text SPIN rotates 180 degrees behind her in sync with the movement, while thin cobalt motion arcs trace her silhouette and collapse into a sharp circular graphic at the final pose.

CUT 08 | 7.00–8.00s — Kinetic type barrage: the words COOL / FAST / CLEAN / BLUE slam in one per beat with shutter flashes and camera shake, while she slides on her knees across the foreground, jacket flaring, frost particles bursting from her sneakers.

CUT 09 | 8.00–9.00s — Black frame, giant white wireframe grid tilting in 3D; she runs up the grid like a wall, kicks off, and hangs in the air as everything freezes; a cobalt circle stamps around her frozen pose like a target lock with UI brackets and data ticks.

CUT 10 | 9.00–10.10s — Freeze releases into a burst: she dives toward camera through layered flat-color panes that shatter one by one like glass shutters, each shattering pane revealing a bigger letter of A-O; foreground wipe with her sneaker.

CUT 11 | 10.10–11.10s — Rapid-fire poster montage: four full-screen graphic posters of her in different action poses (mid-flip, sliding, landing, hands-in-pockets) snap past with hard cuts, each with different bold layout, oversized numbers 01–04, barcodes and slashes.

CUT 12 | 11.10–13.00s — Hero moment on a clean white cyclorama: she lands a final backflip dead center in slow motion, straightens with hands in pockets, and a shockwave of concentric cobalt rings, wind streaks and shattered typography blasts outward from her landing; brief iconic freeze with her faint confident smile, overexpose to white.

CUT 13 | 13.00–15.00s — Final identity card: enormous black AO dominates a pale white field with translucent ice-blue rings, technical arcs, halftone and a rough black circular emblem containing a ghosted snow-crystal/barcode motif; she stands relaxed overlapping the letters, wind rippling her jacket; one last ice-blue pulse sweeps through the typography and a frost-ring flash punctuates the end.

EDITING: Extremely aggressive rhythm — hard cuts on every beat, graphic matches, whip pans, snap zooms, stroboscopic freezes, foreground wipes, RGB splits, shutter flashes, impact shakes and speed ramps. Every cut must feel compositionally different. Typography is always fully readable before the character overlaps it.

No weapons, no combat, no fire; all energy comes from motion design, wind, frost, glass and her parkour-style athleticism.

BGM: Hard-hitting electronic / drum-heavy future bass with aggressive drops, risers, sub hits and glitch fills locked to every cut. Sneaker impacts, whooshes, glass shatters and typography slams are rhythmic sound-design elements. Peak at CUT 12 and end with a cold electronic logo stinger.

entries.prompt:
[Basic Settings]
Thoroughly analyze the attached reference image and SNS profile, design a 'small room where the character would actually live' completely originally, and generate a video.
- Aspect Ratio: 9:16 (Vertical)
- Duration: Approx. 10 seconds (Continuous seamless one-cut video without cuts or teleportation)
- Style: Photorealistic macro cinematography combined with handcrafted miniature diorama aesthetics.

[Profile Analysis and Interior Conversion Rules] (*Design instructions for AI*)
Extract the following elements from the reference materials and reflect them directly in the room's interior design.
1. Color Design (Color Palette):
Extract the character's hair color, eye color, main and sub colors of their costume, and the tone of the profile picture, and reflect them in the shades of wallpaper, rugs, curtains, bedding, and lighting.
2. Architectural/Interior Style:
Translate the character's atmosphere and costume taste (Modern, Retro, Fantasy, Japanese, Cyber, Natural, Gothic, etc.) into furniture shapes and wall/floor materials.
3. Symbolic Items (Select 3-5):
From the profile text content (occupation, hobbies, likes, skills, worldview) and belongings, select only 3-5 items that symbolize the personality and place them in visually prominent positions within the room. (*Avoid stuffing too many small objects; maintain a balance where hobbies naturally seep into the living space.*)

[10-Second Video Composition (Continuous One Cut)]
■ 0-2 Seconds (Introduction):
Real indoor setting. A human hand carefully removes the wall outlet cover. Realistic live-action macro photography capturing textures of plastic, wallpaper, and fingertips. From behind the cover, a small warm light tinged with the room's theme color leaks out.
■ 2-4 Seconds (Intrusion):
The camera slowly approaches the opening and peers inside. A deep small residential space gradually appears, and the camera scales down while naturally intruding into the miniature world.
■ 4-8 Seconds (Daily Life):
The camera fully enters the room. The resident reference character is living doing 'the single most fitting daily action inferred from the profile (creation, reading, cooking, playing instruments, plant care, tidying, etc.)'. Avoid excessive posing; emphasize natural daily life as if accidentally peeked upon.
■ 8-10 Seconds (Afterglow):
The character notices the camera, looks at it briefly, and gives a small, charming reaction. End with a lingering feeling that makes you want to peek again, leaving the warm room atmosphere and small movements.

[Character and Craft Material Feel]
- Strictly maintain the original identity (facial features, hairstyle, hair color, eyes, costume, accessories) and unify with the room scale. Characters are miniature residents; animals/mascots are not forcibly anthropomorphized but move naturally in their original form.
- The miniature world has the texture of exquisite handmade crafts. Combine craft materials appropriate for each item, such as wood/clay furniture, fabric/yarn textiles, transparent resin bottles, dried flowers, etc., evoking fibers, knits, and the warmth of handiwork.
- Express with shallow depth of field, natural bokeh from macro lenses, and soft warm indoor lighting.

[Audio/BGM]
- Voice: High-pitched, cute child-like small voice. Speak modestly in short fictional words that convey emotion rather than existing languages.
- BGM: Gentle, warm music-box-style instrumental matching the room's atmosphere. Naturally mix faint daily sounds like small footsteps and rustling cloth.

[Prohibited Items]
Mixing real-sized furniture, normal wiring depiction, overstuffing small objects, character alteration/dehumanization, adding unnecessary people/animals, displaying subtitles/text/logos/watermarks, excessive magic effects, unnatural cut changes, flashy BGM.

entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic documentary-style personal home video capturing a completely ordinary summer day in the life of a Japanese woman in her early 20s. The footage should feel accidental, intimate, nostalgic, imperfect, and genuinely lived rather than scripted or performed.

MAIN SUBJECT
The same Japanese woman throughout the entire video.
Early 20s, naturally pretty without looking like a model, realistic skin texture, slightly tired eyes, relaxed facial expressions, naturally messy shoulder-length dark hair pulled into a loose half-up style, a few loose strands across her forehead.
She wears a loose faded pale-yellow T-shirt, light gray relaxed-fit shorts, worn canvas sneakers, and a simple silver wristwatch.
Her identity, facial features, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, and overall appearance must remain completely consistent throughout.

REFERENCE IMAGE
Use exactly one reference image to define the woman's face, hairstyle, body proportions, and skin texture. Every frame throughout the entire 30 seconds must match this single reference image with no deviation in facial structure, features, or identity. Do not blend, morph, or drift toward a different face at any point. All lighting, angle, and expression changes must still preserve the same identity as shown in the reference image.

SETTING
An older residential part of Japan during a humid summer afternoon. Small apartment buildings, narrow streets, convenience-store refrigerators visible through windows, concrete staircases, old balconies, rooftop water tanks, bicycles, utility poles, tangled overhead wires, potted plants, faded walls, parked cars, open windows, and distant city buildings. The environment should feel ordinary and genuinely inhabited. No tourist landmarks, recognizable brands, advertisements, crowds, or staged-looking locations.

CAMERA
The entire video looks like footage recorded casually by a friend using an inexpensive older compact digital camera. Handheld and imperfect. Natural shake from walking. Occasional awkward framing. Slight autofocus hunting. Brief exposure shifts when moving indoors and outdoors. Mild digital noise. Soft details. Slight motion blur. Muted summer colors. Occasional blown highlights. Subtle compression artifacts. No gimbal. No drone. No cinematic tracking shots. No dramatic lighting. No slow motion. No artificial film grain. No polished commercial aesthetic.

00:00–00:05 — LAUNDRY
She stands on a small apartment balcony hanging freshly washed clothes. A humid breeze moves the laundry around her. One shirt slips from her hand and falls onto the balcony floor. She looks down, sighs with a small amused smile, picks it up, shakes it once, and hangs it again. The camera is positioned from inside the apartment doorway. Someone quietly laughs behind the camera. She briefly looks toward the camera with an expression that says she knows she's being filmed. Natural household ambience.

00:05–00:10 — KITCHEN
She walks into a small apartment kitchen. She opens an old refrigerator. Cold air escapes. She takes out a bowl of watermelon and a bottle of water. She closes the refrigerator with her hip because both hands are occupied. She sits at a small table near the window. She eats one piece of watermelon while looking outside. A drop of juice runs down her finger. She notices it and wipes her hand on a napkin. The camera autofocus briefly locks onto the window instead of her face.

00:10–00:14 — OLD BUS STOP
Cut to outside. She waits alone at a quiet neighborhood bus stop. She checks the time on her silver watch. She looks down the road. A local bus approaches but passes through the frame without stopping. She watches it disappear. She gives a tiny disappointed shrug. The camera operator slightly misses the bus while trying to reframe. No dramatic reaction. Just an ordinary inconvenience.

00:14–00:19 — SMALL STREET / PARKED CAR
She notices a stray cat sleeping underneath a parked car. She crouches down several feet away. The cat opens one eye. She quietly smiles and reaches out her hand without touching it. The cat gets up and walks away — then, unexpectedly, a second smaller cat darts out from behind a nearby bicycle and follows the first one around the corner. She laughs softly, surprised, having not noticed the second cat was there the whole time. She stands up slowly. The camera remains imperfectly framed around her. A distant motorcycle passes.

00:19–00:23 — SUNSET CONCRETE COURT
She reaches a small empty neighborhood basketball court. The evening sun is low. She places her drink beside the fence. She kicks a loose pebble across the concrete. She notices a basketball sitting near the fence. She picks it up and casually shoots once. The ball hits the rim, bounces away, and rolls toward the camera. The camera operator instinctively steps backward as the ball approaches. She laughs.

00:23–00:27 — WALKING HOME
She picks up the basketball and returns it to where she found it. She walks home carrying the empty drink bottle. The sky has become slightly darker. Apartment windows begin glowing in the distance. She walks slowly, occasionally kicking tiny stones along the pavement. The camera follows several steps behind. No posing. No eye contact with the camera. Just an ordinary walk home.

00:27–00:30 — FINAL MOMENT
She reaches the entrance of her apartment building. She stops before going inside. For a second she looks back toward the camera. She gives a small tired smile. She raises the empty bottle slightly like a casual goodbye. Then she turns around and disappears through the entrance. The camera stays pointed at the doorway for a moment. Someone behind the camera quietly says something indistinct. At approximately 00:29, the footage abruptly cuts to black. No fade-out.

PHYSICAL REALISM
Everything must behave according to believable real-world physics. Hands, fingers, facial expressions, hair, clothing, food, bottles, basketball, bicycle, cats, vehicles, laundry, and environmental objects must remain physically consistent. No duplicated objects. No disappearing objects. No warped anatomy. No extra fingers. No fused limbs. No floating objects. No teleportation. No impossible movements. The basketball must bounce and roll naturally. The cats must move like real animals. Laundry must respond naturally to wind. The bottle must remain a separate physical object. Maintain continuity of the subject and environment between every shot.

AUDIO
Only natural location audio. Refrigerator hum. Clothing moving in the wind. Apartment ambience. Distant traffic. Bus engine. Footsteps. Basketball bouncing. Cat movement. Motorcycles. Birds. Distant voices. Faint city noise. Subtle handling sounds from the camera. No music. No soundtrack. No narration. No artificial sound effects. No dramatic audio transitions.

FINAL FEEL
It should feel like an old personal recording that was never meant to become a film. Nothing important happens. That is the point. A young woman doing laundry. Eating watermelon. Missing a bus. Noticing a cat — and then a second one she hadn't seen. Taking one basketball shot. Walking home. Small movements, awkward pauses, ordinary mistakes, and quiet moments should carry the emotion. The video should feel warm, nostalgic, slightly lonely, youthful, intimate, imperfect, and completely believable. The viewer should feel as though they accidentally found a 30-second fragment of someone's real life from a summer years ago. Prioritize human imperfection over cinematic beauty, continuity over spectacle, and authentic observation over performance.

entries.title: Seedance Comedy Story Video Prompt
entries.description: A detailed prompt for generating a 15-second comedic story video using Seedance, involving a couple's dialogue and a wedding scene with green-haired guests.
entries.prompt:
15 seconds, 16:9 aspect ratio, realistic live-action texture, modern Chinese urban background. The first half features natural intimate dialogue between a couple; the second half hard cuts to a Western-style wedding in a future hotel. The camera slowly pulls back to gradually reveal male guests with different colored hair, forming an absurd and awkward comedy twist. Character performances are restrained; environment, skin, fabric, and lighting are realistic and natural.
[Characters and Continuity]
The female lead is a young adult Chinese girl @image (31). In the future wedding, the bride must be the same girl, maintaining facial features and contours, only changing hairstyle, makeup, and clothing.
The male lead is a young adult Chinese man, starting with normal black short hair and daily casual clothes. In the future wedding, his facial features, face shape, body type, and hairstyle contour remain consistent, but he wears a well-fitted suit and dyes his hair distinctly green, fulfilling the girl's request from the opening. He must not look like a different person due to scene/hair changes.
The groom is another adult Chinese man, slightly chubby, with black hair, clearly different appearance from the male lead, wearing formal groom attire.
There are multiple adult male guests at the wedding site, dyed red, blue, purple, yellow, orange, and one other green-haired man. Their appearances, heights, builds, hairstyles, and suits are all distinct. Hair dye retains real hair strands, roots, and luster, looking like natural dyed hair rather than wigs or glowing colors.
[0–7s: Daily Couple Dialogue]
Ordinary city park or residential area downstairs, evening, soft natural light, slight ambient life sounds in the background.
The girl and boy sit side by side on a bench. Medium close-up shot, clearly recognizable faces. The girl turns to look at the boy, holding his hand, speaking affectionately, seriously, with a touch of coquettishness, as if casually mentioning something romantic. The boy looks at her deeply.
The girl speaks completely and clearly:
"Baby, if you're not the one marrying me in the future, you must dye your hair green to come to my wedding, so I can spot you at a glance."
Spoken at a natural, slightly fast, coherent daily pace, not deliberately dragged out, no swallowed words, no mechanical acceleration. While the girl speaks, the boy listens, showing a faint smile moved yet puzzled, adding no response.
Maintain continuous performance, clearly establishing the male lead's appearance. The girl does not smirk early, wink at the camera, or foreshadow the twist.
[7–9s: Hard Cut to Future Wedding, See Same Face Then Green Hair]
Immediately after the girl says "you", hard cut to the hotel wedding scene. Ambient sound switches synchronously from outdoor life sounds to banquet hall applause and blurred voices.
Cut to a frontal close-up of the same male lead's face. Initial frame top edge cropped below the hairline, temporarily hiding hair, letting viewers recognize him as the previous boy.
He sits in the wedding guest seats, wearing a suit, expression slightly reserved with complex anticipation, gaze towards the entrance aisle.
The camera then slowly, steadily moves backward, gradually revealing his full head—he has dyed his hair green.
The green is seen clearly by viewers for the first time. He was already green-haired when entering the wedding shot; no live color-change effect occurs.
[9–12s: Bride and Groom Entrance, Other Colors Appear]
Camera continues moving back, expanding from close-up to medium shot, adjusting horizontally to keep the green-haired male lead on one side and gradually reveal the central wedding aisle.
The site is a real hotel banquet hall arranged for a Western wedding, with light-colored floral arrangements, white/beige chairs, warm ceiling lights, and carpeted entrance aisles. Lighting has clear sources; wedding dress retains fabric details, avoiding dreamy fairy-tale effects.
In the background aisle, the opening girl enters in a wedding dress, arm-in-arm with the slightly chubby groom. The groom's appearance and build are clearly different from the green-haired male lead.
The male lead originally watches the bride, forcing a faint smile. As the camera pulls back, a red-haired male guest and a blue-haired male guest enter the frame near him.
He inadvertently glances at the red-haired man beside him, smile pausing slightly, then looks at the green-haired man on the other side, brow twitching, starting to feel something is wrong.
[12–15s: Reveal More Colored-Hair Men, Male Lead Looks Around in Surprise]
Camera continues moving back along the same trajectory, expanding to a wider frame containing the male lead, several rows of surrounding guests, and the wedding aisle. The wedding segment remains continuous, no further cuts.
More male guests with different hair colors gradually enter the frame: purple, yellow, orange, and another red-haired man distinct from the male lead in appearance, build, and hairstyle.
Including the male lead, about six to eight colored-hair men are scattered across adjacent rows, intermingled with ordinary black-haired guests. Not all guests have dyed hair, nor are they arranged in a neat rainbow line.
They vary: some thin, some sturdy, some chubby; some buzz cuts, some short side parts, some curly. Suits are black, dark blue, gray, brown, with obvious differences in fit, ties, and shirt combinations, resembling independent real wedding guests.
These people were seated in place from the start of the wedding shot, merely hidden by the initial tight framing, becoming visible as the camera pulled back; they cannot appear suddenly or change hair color abruptly.
The male lead looks left, then right, finally turning slightly back to see another green-haired man. His expression shifts from confusion to surprise and embarrassment, lips parting slightly, realizing he might not be the only one who received such a promise.
Other colored-hair men mostly continue watching the wedding; a few may briefly exchange glances with him, not collectively turning heads or reacting in sync.
The ending simultaneously retains the male lead's surprised look-around, surrounding differently colored-hair male guests, and the bride/groom continuing to enter in the background. The screen ends naturally, without extra dialogue explaining the joke.
[Cinematography, Performance, and Realistic Atmosphere]
Opening uses natural daylight; wedding uses hotel warm indoor lighting. Skin tones are normal, retaining texture; suits have real wrinkles; wedding dress has weight; dyed hair has natural shading layers.
The first half feels like real couples chatting casually; the second half feels like an awkward discovery happening at a real wedding. The male lead expresses emotions through eyes, micro-expressions, and looking around, avoiding cartoonish eye-widening, mouth-opening, or face-covering actions.
The wedding pull-back uses actual camera movement, steady speed, with pre-arranged guest positions so different hair colors enter sequentially. Depth of field increases gradually after pull-back, ensuring relationships between male lead, colored-hair guests, and background newlyweds are discernible; do not blur surrounding people into color blocks throughout.
Avoid retro DV quality, exaggerated shaking, fisheye, sudden zooms, high-speed orbits, slow motion, plastic skin, or heavy filters.
[Sound]
Opening retains girl's dialogue and slight outdoor life sounds. After hard cut, enter natural applause, fabric rustle, chair creaks, and blurred conversation of the hotel banquet hall.
Dialogue accurately matches girl's lip movements; male lead does not speak for her or interrupt. No clear dialogue added in wedding segment.
No narration, background music, canned laughter, twist alert sounds, or explanatory subtitles.
[Core Constraints]
Total length 15 seconds. The only hard cut occurs after the girl finishes her line, switching from daily couple scene to future wedding. Wedding part starts with male lead's facial close-up, continuously pulling back slowly.
Information revelation order fixed: Same boy's face -> His green hair -> Same girl and different groom entering -> Surrounding gradual appearance of different colored-hair male guests -> Male lead discovers another green-haired man, looks around in surprise.
Girl's line requests "dye hair green"; male lead indeed dyes hair green in future, consistent.
Bride is same person as opening girl; green-haired male lead is same person as opening boy; groom is different person. Other guests have independent faces, no cloned faces, face swaps, abrupt hair color changes, or sudden appearances.
No subtitles, date stamps, explanatory text, or watermarks.

entries.prompt:
[Task]

Generate a 12-second, 9:16 vertical realistic smartphone selfie video. Replicate the lying-on-bed composition, action sequence, mixed crying-and-laughing expressions, and rhythm from the reference video 'Angry Until Stomach Hurts', replacing the original character with a specified adult female.

[Reference Division and Character Locking]

Lock the face to the female portrait in reference image @0ba07db1-974c-467d-80dc-d9dffddac0ba, including facial proportions and long black hair; do not inherit the male appearance from the original video.

Lock clothing and body proportions to reference image @8149c66e-9a91-4b88-bf26-d0a764075ccf, ensuring clothes are fully worn.

Lock glasses to silver decorative glasses in reference image @d80c71c5-d330-4baf-8ecf-8b793ee0fee8: thin silver metal wireframes, open curved lower rims, transparent nose pads, small bow-tie metal coils near the bridge, and one hanging flower charm on each side. Temples rest normally on ears, eyes clearly visible. Glasses must be worn throughout, not changing into thick-rimmed glasses or display stands.

The original video only locks performance, selfie angle, actions, and rhythm.

Do not inherit the falling shot from the previous nine-grid.

[Scene and Filming]

She lies supine on white bedding, head on a white pillow, long hair naturally spread out.

Left hand holds the phone off-screen; front camera is approx. 40cm above the face, shooting downwards capturing face, shoulders, and upper body. Face occupies the main subject area.

Right hand may reach the bottom edge of the frame to press the abdomen.

One continuous take throughout; camera shakes slightly only due to holding hand, breathing, and shoulder tremors. Natural bedroom lighting, standard smartphone native quality, realistic skin texture, no beauty filters.

[Strict Timing and Performance]

0–2.8s:

Opens immediately in a state of angry crying/laughing. Brows furrowed tightly, eyes squeezed shut, mouth corners pulled horizontally, intermittently emitting "Hahaha... Ah... Haha".

Laughter carries grievance and anger; shoulders tremble lightly, head moves slightly on the pillow.

Silver flower charms sway gently with head movement; nose pads and temples remain fitted to the face.

2.8–5.8s:

She stops to inhale, barely opens eyes to look at the screen, brows still furrowed, mouth corners turned down, speaking with anger and grievance:

"Family, I'm so angry my stomach hurts."

As she says the second half, right hand presses abdomen, head turns to the side, eyes squeeze shut again. Phone shakes slightly with body tremors, face remains clearly readable.

5.8–9.3s:

She tries to catch her breath but emits broken "Hahaha... Ah..."

Mouth opens, briefly purses, then opens again, showing a reaction wanting to laugh yet cry. Brows tighten, nostrils flare slightly, chin trembles, occasionally showing teeth.

Head returns from side position to center of pillow, right hand continues pressing abdomen. Glasses move with head, flower charms sway naturally.

9.3–12s:

Briefly opens eyes looking at screen, angrily saying:

"I'm so angry I could die."

Then closes eyes, scrunches nose, reveals mixed crying/laughing expression, ending with a short bitter laugh and exhale.

Remains lying in place, does not get up, adds no other plot.

[Audio]

Natural adult female voice, close-range phone recording, lip-sync with dialogue.

Intermittent laughter, with inhales and breathy sounds; emotion is a mix of anger, grievance, and bitter laughter.

Slight pillow rustling, fabric friction, and indoor ambient noise; no narration, no background music.

If generation tool supports reference video audio, prioritize matching pauses, laughter, and speech rhythm of the original clip.

[Key Requirements]

Retain exaggerated eye-squeezing, brow-furrowing, mouth-opening, and head-shaking from original; must not become pretty smile or calm talking-head.

Maintain same character identity even when expressions distort features.

Glasses structure, number of flowers, clothing, hairstyle, bed, and lighting consistent throughout.

No face swapping, no floating glasses or clipping through skin, no extra flower charms, no extra arms or abnormal fingers.

No cuts, no falling, no rolling camera angles, no slow motion, no cinematic camera moves.

Do not add subtitles, screenshot stickers, watermarks, or platform UI to generated frames.

entries.title: "Love survived" — devastating drama
entries.description: ~24s dialogue-free post-apocalyptic love story: two infected lovers recognize each other in an abandoned train station; memories flash back, then return to the present.
entries.prompt:
Create a photorealistic, emotionally devastating cinematic video, approximately 24 seconds, 16:9, 24fps. A post-apocalyptic love story told entirely through visuals, without dialogue. Two infected lovers discover each other inside an abandoned train station. Their bodies have succumbed to the infection, but some forgotten part of them still recognizes the person they loved. A familiar touch awakens fragmented memories of their life together before the world collapsed. The memories feel beautiful, imperfect, and painfully real. The ending returns to the present, revealing that although their humanity is fading, their connection remains.

Visual direction: Photorealistic cinema, natural skin textures, anamorphic lens character, subtle film grain, shallow depth of field, realistic handheld movement, soft lens flares, volumetric light, restrained color grading. Present-day scenes feature desaturated green-grey tones, decaying architecture, drifting dust, and cold overcast light. Memories feature warm amber sunlight, rich natural colors, and gentle halation. Emotional restraint over melodrama.

Character continuity — keep identical faces throughout:

Man: Early 30s, short messy dark-brown hair, light stubble, silver curb chain, small silver hoop in his left ear. Present-day appearance: shirtless, dark trousers, ashy grey-green skin, mottled veins, cracked lips, dirt-covered shoulders, bruising around the eyes. His irises are clouded milky-grey, with faintly veined pale sclera and small, dull pupils. His gaze remains subtly responsive. Memory appearance: healthy olive skin, dark charcoal crewneck, warm brown eyes, natural smile.

Woman: Early 30s, long wavy dirty-blonde hair, small silver nose ring, oversized black knit sweater in the present. Her skin is pale and ashy, with realistic discoloration, faint veins, and dark bruising around the eye sockets. Her irises have a cloudy blue-grey film, glassy surfaces, and muted pupils. Memory appearance: healthy skin, heather-grey T-shirt, clear blue-grey eyes, expressive laughter.

Shot-by-shot sequence

0.0–3.0s — The abandoned station

A wide cinematic shot of a deserted railway platform swallowed by weeds. A derailed train rests beneath a broken glass canopy. The infected man sits alone on a rusted bench, staring at an old photograph held between dirty fingers. Wind moves loose paper across the platform. He slowly lifts his head as faint footsteps echo in the distance. His cloudy eyes turn toward the sound. Slow dolly-in, cold green-grey palette, atmospheric silence.

3.0–5.5s — Recognition

At the far end of the platform, the infected woman emerges through drifting mist. Her oversized black sweater hangs loosely from her shoulders, her dirty-blonde hair moving in the wind. She stops beneath a flickering station light. A medium close-up reveals her pale, filmed-over irises and bruised eye sockets. She studies the distant figure as though trying to remember his face. The camera slowly pushes toward her eyes.

5.5–8.0s — The distance between them

Alternating profile shots as they walk toward each other along opposite sides of the platform. Neither moves like a predator. Their steps are uneven and hesitant. The man brushes his fingertips across a rusted metal railing; the woman pauses beside an abandoned child’s bicycle. Their dead eyes remain fixed on one another. A train carriage slides across the foreground, briefly obscuring the frame and revealing them much closer when it clears.

8.0–10.5s — The familiar gesture

They stop face-to-face beneath a shattered station clock. The woman raises one trembling hand and touches the silver chain around his neck, recognizing something familiar. He looks down at her hand, then back into her eyes. His expression barely changes, but his breathing catches faintly. Extreme close-up on their fingers touching the chain, followed by a rack focus to their clouded eyes. No snarling, no sudden movements.

10.5–12.0s — Memory begins

Her thumb brushes the chain.

Match cut to the same gesture in the past: her healthy hand resting against the same silver necklace as the man smiles at her in warm afternoon sunlight. The cold station transforms into a sunlit apartment balcony through a seamless visual transition. The soundtrack remains instrumental, with a delicate piano motif and distant ambient textures.

12.0–14.0s — A life they once had

Memory. The couple stand in a tiny apartment kitchen, cooking together. She playfully steals a piece of food from his plate. He pretends to be offended before breaking into a genuine laugh. Their clear brown and blue-grey eyes reflect the warm window light. Imperfect handheld framing, natural movement, lived-in surroundings, intimate realism rather than polished advertising aesthetics.

14.0–16.0s — The last ordinary day

Memory. They ride a bicycle together along a quiet countryside road at sunset, the woman seated behind him with her arms around his waist. She rests her cheek against his back and closes her eyes. Tall grass sways beside the road. Golden sunlight spills through the trees. The camera follows from behind, creating the feeling of a cherished moment captured before anyone knew it would become a memory.

16.0–18.0s — The world before

A brief, fragmented memory: rain against a bedroom window at night. They lie together beneath a blanket, foreheads touching, smiling quietly. Her fingers trace his cheek while he gently tucks a strand of hair behind her ear. Their eyes are alive, moist, and full of warmth. A lightning flash momentarily illuminates their faces, creating a natural visual bridge to the cold present.

18.0–20.0s — Back to the station

Hard match cut to the same framing in the abandoned station. The woman’s hand is still against his cheek, but the skin beneath her fingers is cracked and grey. Her eyes are cloudy and lifeless in color. His dull milky-grey eyes remain locked on hers. The piano falls away, leaving only wind passing through broken windows and the faint metallic groan of the station.

20.0–22.0s — The almost-human moment

Extreme close-up, both faces filling the frame. The man slowly raises his hand and rests it against the woman’s cheek. A tear-like trace of moisture catches the light beneath her clouded eye, without restoring its color. She leans into his palm by the smallest amount. Their noses almost touch. Fine cracks, subtle veins, dirt, and realistic skin deterioration remain sharply detailed. No supernatural glow, no sudden transformation.

22.0–24.0s — Still together

A wider shot from behind them. They sit side by side on the rusted station bench, hands clasped, facing the abandoned tracks disappearing into the mist. Weeds move in the wind. Far above, the broken canopy lets one narrow beam of golden sunlight fall across their joined hands. The rest of the station remains cold and lifeless. The camera slowly pulls away until they become small figures in the ruined architecture.

End on their clasped hands. Fade to black. No title card.

Cinematography and performance

* Prioritize emotional storytelling through eyes, hands, posture, and subtle facial movement.
* Use motivated match cuts that connect identical gestures, compositions, and character positions across past and present.
* Maintain consistent facial identity, hairstyle, jewelry, clothing, and body proportions in every shot.
* Present-day movement should feel slow, stiff, and physically grounded, with no exaggerated zombie behavior.
* Human memories should feel spontaneous, tender, and imperfect, with believable interactions and natural expressions.
* Use realistic practical infection makeup, restrained discoloration, cracked skin, mottled veins, and bruised sockets.
* Zombie eyes must retain recognizable iris and pupil structure beneath a milky film. Never use glowing eyes, featureless white eyeballs, or black voids.
* Build emotion through visual contrast, ambient sound, and restrained pacing rather than dialogue or excessive effects.

Negative prompt: Cartoon zombies, anime, video-game graphics, plastic skin, exaggerated monster faces, glowing eyes, solid white eyes, black voids, excessive gore, exposed organs, blood splashes, face inconsistency, changing jewelry, changing eye colors in the present, extra fingers, deformed hands, artificial facial expressions, rubbery movement, oversaturated colors, excessive motion blur, random scene transitions, text, subtitles, logos, watermarks.

entries.title: Psychological thriller transformation
entries.description: 27s ultra-real psychological thriller: a romantic memory turns monstrous — dread and slow-burn tension.
entries.prompt:
Create a 27-second ultra-realistic cinematic psychological thriller sequence with a dramatic transition between a terrifying present moment and a beautiful romantic memory.

Overall visual style: premium Hollywood psychological thriller, photorealistic live action, realistic skin texture and pores, natural hair movement, believable fabric physics, dramatic practical lighting, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, anamorphic cinematic composition, realistic motion blur, strong emotional acting. 2.39:1 widescreen. No text, no subtitles, no logos.

CHARACTERS

Woman: Young woman in her mid-20s with long dark-brown hair, expressive brown eyes and natural realistic features. She wears an elegant sleeveless fitted black dress. Keep her face, hairstyle, clothing and body proportions perfectly consistent.

Man: Young man in his late 20s, tall and lean, dark hair, wearing an elegant white dinner jacket, white shirt, black bow tie and black trousers.

In the frightening present-day scenes, the man appears severely transformed: his exposed hand and portions of his skin are dark, charred and corpse-like, with rough burned texture and unnatural gray-black fingers. Keep the effect cinematic rather than excessively graphic.

00:00–00:06 — TERRIFYING CHASE

Open inside a long underground pedestrian tunnel with cold turquoise-green fluorescent lighting, tiled walls, concrete ceiling beams and repeating rectangular ceiling lights disappearing into the distance.

The woman runs desperately toward camera.

Her long hair whips violently behind her. She is breathing hard, terrified and repeatedly looking over her shoulder.

Behind her, the man in the white dinner jacket runs after her.

Use a fast backward tracking camera, staying directly in front of the woman. Alternate briefly between a tight frightened facial close-up and a wider side-tracking shot showing both characters sprinting through the tunnel.

The man stretches one arm toward her.

Cut to an extreme close-up of his horrifying blackened, damaged hand getting closer and closer to her bare shoulder.

Just before his fingers touch her—

00:06–00:12 — MATCH CUT INTO THE MEMORY

Make a seamless visual match cut.

The frightening dark hand instantly becomes the man's normal healthy hand, positioned in exactly the same place.

The cold turquoise tunnel transforms into a beautiful sunset beach.

Warm golden sunlight floods the frame.

The woman is now laughing happily while running barefoot beside the ocean. Her black dress flows naturally in the sea breeze.

The man is completely normal and handsome again, still wearing his elegant white dinner jacket.

He playfully reaches toward her shoulder while chasing her.

She turns around laughing.

They run together along the shoreline, holding hands and smiling.

Golden sun reflects across the ocean behind them. Wind moves their hair and clothing. Their body language shows that this was once a deeply happy relationship.

Use dreamy handheld tracking, warm backlighting, natural lens flare and intimate close-ups.

The sequence should briefly feel like a completely different film: romantic, nostalgic, peaceful and genuinely joyful.

00:12–00:13 — SNAP BACK TO REALITY

Without warning, smash-cut back to the cold underground tunnel.

Same framing.

Same reaching-hand composition.

But his hand is once again dark, damaged and frightening.

All warm colors disappear instantly.

Return to harsh cyan-green fluorescent lighting and deep shadows.

00:13–00:20 — CORNERED

The woman reaches the end/side of the tunnel and backs against the tiled wall.

She has nowhere left to run.

She suddenly pulls out a small black knife and holds it defensively with both hands.

Her hands shake badly.

She is crying, breathing rapidly and staring at the approaching man.

Camera slowly pushes toward her face.

Her expression changes from pure terror to confusion and recognition.

The man approaches slowly instead of attacking.

Show an extreme shallow-focus shot of his damaged hand cautiously reaching toward her.

She raises the knife—

but cannot bring herself to use it.

Tears fill her eyes.

00:20–00:27 — EMOTIONAL REVEAL

The man steps close.

Instead of hurting her, he suddenly embraces her tightly.

She freezes for a fraction of a second.

Then recognition overwhelms her.

The knife lowers out of frame.

She wraps both arms around him.

She begins sobbing uncontrollably against his shoulder, gripping the back of his white jacket as if she has finally found someone she believed she had lost.

Hold an intimate close-up on her face over his shoulder.

Her makeup is slightly disturbed by tears. Her breathing is uneven. Her hands tremble against his back.

The frightening figure is revealed emotionally as someone she once deeply loved.

Slowly push closer to her crying face and her hand clutching his jacket.

End without explaining whether the man is real, dead, imagined, remembered, or something supernatural.

The audience should be left with the unsettling feeling that the terrifying chase and the beautiful beach memory are connected.

CAMERA + EDITING

Use energetic tracking during the chase, intimate handheld movement during the beach memory, and slower controlled push-ins during the emotional ending.

The most important visual transition is:

charred hand reaching toward shoulder → identical composition of healthy hand reaching toward shoulder on the beach → charred hand again in the tunnel.

The match cuts must feel extremely precise so the past and present visually overlap.

Maintain perfect character identity and wardrobe continuity throughout.

Realistic skin pores, natural facial asymmetry, individual hair strands, genuine tears, realistic wet eyes, subtle sweat, natural blinking and breathing. Avoid plastic skin, beauty filters, CGI-looking faces, warped hands, extra fingers, inconsistent clothing, identity changes, exaggerated horror gore or artificial expressions.
