entries.title: Wan 3.0: re-render a white clay animatic as live action (locked camera and timing)
entries.description: Clay-render-to-realism template: an [Absolutely unchanged · highest priority] block locks camera path, cuts and timing, then [Realistic conversion], [Character realistic conversion], [Lighting] and [Image quality] blocks specify materials, skin and light.
entries.prompt:
Using Video 1 (my uploaded pure-white clay render animation) as the sole blueprint, do one realistic re-render: replace every object and character still in pure-white matte raw form with real-world material and color, rendering into a realistic cinematic live-action texture; change nothing except material and color.
[Absolutely unchanged · highest priority] Camera motion trajectory, the speed and direction of every push/pull/pan/tilt/orbit, the timing of shot-size switches, cut points, aspect ratio, total duration, composition and perspective — all frame-for-frame identical to the reference video, not one frame added or removed, not one second out of place. The position, orientation, size ratio, quantity and mutual occlusion of every object in the scene are copied exactly; no additions, no deletions, no moves. The characters' bone structure outline, hairstyle volume, body proportions, garment tailoring and all actions, walking rhythm, the timing of crouching, reaching and pushing doors must be completely identical to the clay video; no action changes, no swapping of characters. Sunlight direction, shadow angle and length, and the light-dark distribution of every frame are copied from the original. The only thing allowed to change is material, color, texture, and the real optical behavior that results.
[Realistic conversion] After realistic conversion, the clay model's cartoon-rounded forms retain their volume outline and proportions, but every surface is replaced with real material: plastered walls are real cement troweled texture with rain streaks, efflorescence white bloom and moss at the wall base; the tile roof is fired clay tile with color variation, chipped edges and dust accumulation, dry grass and moss in the tile gaps; doors and windows are old real wood with clear grain, worn and cracked paint, glass with real refraction, fingerprints and slight smudges reflecting sky and tree shadows; steps are rounded granite with polished trodden edges; wooden buckets and crates are old pine with splinters and nail holes, iron hoops and nail heads with real reddish-brown rust layers and rust runs; the tricycle is chipped blue iron sheet showing primer, galvanized parts with white rust, rubber tires with worn treads and caked mud; the well is unevenly jointed bluestone, hemp rope with fraying and broken strands, the well platform stained dark by water soaking; tree bark has real cracked furrows and lichen patches, leaves are real layered foliage with bug holes and transmittant veins; ground flagstones have real cracks, color spots and soil in the gaps, grass is real blades with dried-yellow tips; brick walls have real fired color variation and hollow mortar joints.
[Character realistic conversion] The little girl becomes a real child: a real East Asian child's face and skin, skin with real pores, peach fuzz and subsurface scattering, natural flush on cheeks and ear rims, eyes with dark-brown irises showing real texture and wet reflection, lashes and brows as individually distinguishable natural dark brown, hair as real strands in bundles with flyaways and frizz, hair tips catching a light-brown edge in sunlight; clothing is real cotton with weave texture, washed-wear feel and folds with real gravity drape, shoes are real soft leather with wear and clay stuck to the soles. The facial features must be a proper East Asian look — eyes on the narrower/longer side, flat brow bone, clear cheekbones, straight nose bridge; not allowed to be drawn as a Western white person, mixed race or with heavy makeup. The kitten becomes a real short-haired house cat, cream-white with orange-yellow patches, fur individually distinct with fluffy edge light, pink nose tip, pupils constricting with light.
[Lighting] Fully follow the clay video's light direction and shadows: warm sunlight slants from the upper-left-back at about forty-five degrees, shadow edges slightly soft, direction uniform; light shafts contain real floating dust and slight aerial perspective; once colored it carries a clear warm-gold color temperature, shadows falling in clear sky-lit cool blue, forming a natural warm-cool contrast; all AO dark corners of the original clay model are retained as transparent dark areas with ambient color bounce, dark areas have color and detail, not crushed to dead black, highlights not overexposed to white blobs.
[Image quality] Ultra-high-definition 8K realistic cinematography texture, full-frame shallow-to-medium depth of field, natural lens blur and slight chromatic aberration, path-traced global illumination and real contact shadows, high texture resolution with no stretching or tiling, natural motion blur, film-grade color layering and soft highlight roll-off.
Style: realistic live-action cinematic texture, natural-light slice-of-life film, real material and weathering detail. Image quality: 8K ultra-high-definition, full-frame shallow depth of field, path-traced global illumination, film-grade color layering. Lighting: warm sun key light from the upper-left-back paired with clear sky-fill light, long shadows in uniform direction, transparent dark areas with ambient color.
Do not change any camera motion, cut point, aspect ratio, duration, composition or object placement of the original video; do not add or remove any object or character; do not change character bone structure, hairstyle, garment tailoring, body proportions or any action timing; no residual clay areas, locally unpainted pure-white objects, material-lost gray blocks or misaligned textures; no cartoon, anime, illustration, plastic toy or fake CG texture; no Western white faces, mixed-race faces, heavy-makeup faces, face swaps or age jumps; no wireframe grid lines, coordinate axes, UI or any UI elements; no text, Chinese characters, English letters, numbers, labels, subtitles, watermarks, logos or platform corner bugs; no flickering, material jitter, texture swimming, clipping, limb distortion, extra fingers, noise or blown-out loss of structure.

entries.title: Wan 3.0: red-line-guided FPV flight around a giant wooden horse (oil-painting look)
entries.description: Draw the camera path as numbered red lines on the reference image, then describe each waypoint segment (speed, pass-through, slow-motion, orbit) and order the model to erase all marks: a single-take FPV that dives under the horse's belly and whips around its head.
entries.prompt:
[Hard requirements for the base image]
The final footage completely removes all red lines, numeric markers, arrows, and auxiliary marks; no text or watermarks appear in the frame. Surreal photorealistic 8K classical-oil-painting texture, thick brushstrokes and pigment grain clearly discernible, UE5 cinematic-grade lighting render, warm-toned side-backlight of a Greek afternoon, golden-brown dust churning and drifting through the light shafts. The giant white wooden horse, the wooden trailer and rollers, the taut thick hemp ropes, the Trojan stone city wall and round watchtower on the left, and the distant mountain-city complex all retain their original form, proportions, and positions unchanged. Human proportions are natural and undistorted; only the original rope-pulling crowd and the defenders on the wall remain — no extra figures are added. Robes stay in the original ochre-red, indigo, earth-yellow, and off-white.
[Core camera-movement rules]
First-person FPV drone-perspective, single take, one uninterrupted continuous motion throughout, flying along the complete path of red line 1→2→3→4→5 in Image 1, skipping no segment, simplifying no trajectory, changing no order. The opening is not a straight flat flight — it first rises up-left to clear the tow-rope zone, then dives down in a large wave arc. Waypoint 2 must genuinely pass through the space beneath the horse's belly; it cannot skirt around the horse body or sweep past its side. The overall speed-layered cadence is fast → slow → fast.
[Segmented by waypoint]
Segment 1 (waypoint 1 → waypoint 2): high-speed cut-in thrust, a dive that first rises then drops.
The camera takes off at low altitude from the right edge of the frame, beside the spear tips of the cheering spear-bearers, rises sharply up-left at extreme speed, sweeping over rows of taut tow ropes, climbing above the distant mountain-city complex to skim past it, then sharply yaws downward at the position just right of the horse's chest, pressing the nose down and diving along the top of the crowd's heads and raised spears. Arms and banners rush past on both sides, kicked-up dust is torn into long streamers by the airflow, and the nose dives straight for the shadow beneath the horse's belly.
Segment 2 (waypoint 2, passing through the belly): ducking beneath the horse, the speed suddenly slows.
The camera drops to an extreme low, threading in between the horse's four massive pillar-like legs, passing through the shadowed space directly beneath the belly — overhead are the wood-grain planks and chisel marks of the belly underside, on both sides are thick ropes, trailer planks, and iron-banded rollers, below is the dusty ground trampled by countless feet. Light dims abruptly, leaving only golden light bars leaking through the gaps; the sense of scale presses to its maximum.
Segment 3 (waypoint 2 → waypoint 3): slow motion, tilting up and turning sharply.
The camera emerges from the other side of the belly and, near the rear of the horse close to the left city wall, pulls out a large U-shaped rising arc in slow motion, sweeping past the carved texture of the tail and hind legs. The airframe slowly tilts up, and the massive bulk of the stone city wall and round watchtower in the background gradually fills the frame as the camera rises.
Segment 4 (waypoint 3 → waypoint 4): maintaining slow motion, climbing and orbiting along the spine.
The camera slowly climbs along the horse's spine line from back to front, sweeping past the wood seams of the back, the curly carved mane, and the undulations of the neck muscles one by one. Circling birds in the sky scatter in front of the lens; the defenders densely packed on the wall and the distant mountain city drift slowly backward below.
Segment 5 (waypoint 4 → waypoint 5): sudden acceleration, a head-circling whip to finish.
After passing the top of the mane, the camera suddenly accelerates, whipping right into a full closed loop around the horse's head — first darting into the open sky to the horse's right-front, then sharply reversing and pressing back, and finally speeding straight toward the horse's head. The motion stops dead in the final instant.
[Final hold frame]
The camera holds on a close-up position directly in front of the horse's head: the horse's eye, nostril, and chiseled mane dominate the frame, rim light traces a golden outline around the head, and the background is the defocused blue sky, drifting clouds, and distant mountain city.
[Lighting and quality notes]
No cuts throughout, no shot splits, no transition breaks — retain the native FPV wide-angle slight-distortion texture of a single continuous shot. The afternoon golden light always comes from the upper-right of the frame; while passing through the belly, it undergoes one natural exposure transition from bright to dark and back to bright. Dust-particle and airborne-microdust density intensifies with speed, and the oil-painting brushstroke and pigment grain stay consistent across the entire piece — no photo-real plastic sheen appears.

entries.title: Halloween-night found tape: fisheye flash camcorder chaos
entries.description: Early-2000s consumer camcorder with a fisheye lens and harsh on-camera flash: barrel distortion, blown highlights, clipping mic audio, rapid chaotic party/creature beats, no music.
entries.prompt:
STYLE: Photoreal raw flash footage, like a found Halloween night tape. Shot on a cheap early-2000s consumer camcorder with a fisheye lens: strong barrel distortion, harsh on-camera flash/light blasting whatever is close to the lens with blown-out highlights and hard shadows, everything past a few meters falls off into an underexposed, near-black background. 

Heavy camcorder noise, video grain, slight interlacing, smeared motion blur, auto-exposure pumping, occasional focus hunting, slightly crushed and green-tinted digital color. Chaotic documentary realism: the operator is a person running and reacting in real time, frantic handheld whip-pans, crash zooms, the camera bumping into things, subjects shoved right up into the fisheye lens. Meme energy: absurd moments played totally real. 

FAST pace: hard jump cuts every 0.5-1 second, no transitions. No on-screen text, no timestamp overlay, no titles, no logos, no watermark. CAST: @image (15) the devil woman. 

Dale the werewolf: a huge, hulking, shaggy grey-brown werewolf with glowing yellow eyes, a long snarling snout full of teeth, and matted fur. He wears a torn red varsity-style bowling jacket hanging off his massive frame, shredded at the sleeves. The skeletons: a trio of full-body human skeletons with bleached off-white bones, wearing mirrored aviator sunglasses and black tactical vests. One of them wears a bright orange baseball cap and white sneakers. The elderly witch: a frail, wrinkled old woman with wild grey hair, wearing a black feathered cape and sharp cat-eye glasses, with a pointed witch's hat and a crooked grin. The Headless Horseman: a tall rider in a burgundy velvet coat with no head, seated on a powerful black horse with a flowing mane. Shot 1 (0-2.2s): Flash-lit fisheye shot at a gas station at night, the devil woman bored against an old pickup, camera close on her face; out of the black behind her, the werewolf sprints into the flash and leaps straight at the lens; she swings up a shotgun and fires, muzzle flash whiting out the frame, camera knocked sideways. Shot 2 (2.2-2.8s): Whip-pan into a dark alley: three skeletons on a low wall lit only by the flash, one raises his rifle and they jump down at the camera. Shot 3 (2.8-3.6s): The devil woman leaps out of a black archway right past the lens, her red tulle skirt and sheer sleeves flaring and filling the frame, firing a rifle. Shot 4 (3.6-4s): Flash-blown close-up of muzzle flash and sparks, camera shaking. Shot 5 (4-5s): Running handheld through a dark farmyard toward a shed with propane tanks; the elderly witch zooms past the lens on a ride-on lawnmower, cape flapping, straight into the tanks. 

Shot 6 (5-6s): Massive fireball overexposes the camera; the witch is blasted up into the black sky; operator falls back. Shot 7 (6-6.6s): Pitch black cornfield, flash pops on: her broom stabs into the dirt right in front of the lens. Shot 8 (6.6-7.8s): 

City street at night, camera on the sidewalk; the Headless Horseman gallops inches past the fisheye lens holding a flaming jack-o'-lantern, fire flaring the image. Shot 9 (7.8-8.8s): 

A parked old sedan explodes, camera recoils, image clips to white then auto-exposes back. Shot 10 (8.8-12.2s): Packed barn Halloween party, flash on, crowd in witch hats and bedsheet ghosts screaming and holding up phones. 

Dance battle filmed from the front row: the devil woman, in her full devil costume with horns and heels, hits a sharp freeze right in the fisheye lens; the skeleton in the orange cap and white sneakers does a headspin, then collapses into a pile of loose bones. 

Crowd goes insane, camera shaking. Shot 11 (12.2-14s): Camera drops to the floor: harsh flash on scattered bones, the skull rolls straight into the lens and stops, distorted by the fisheye, background black. Hold. AUDIO: Raw camcorder mic audio, clipping and distorted: wind, werewolf roar, shotgun blast, people yelling 'YO!', lawnmower engine, explosions blowing out the mic, hooves, party crowd screaming, bones clattering, skull rolling. No music, no score.

entries.title: One-take phone footage: humpback whale floats over a downtown street
entries.description: 30s vertical one-take by a pedestrian on a smartphone: the camera "tilts up with a slight delay, as a real person's would", shakes and refocuses as a whale drifts overhead; auto-exposure shifts, neon flare, crowd reactions.
entries.prompt:
A single continuous 30-second one-take filmed on a smartphone, vertical 9:16, handheld with slight natural shake. A busy downtown street at dusk after light rain, wet asphalt reflecting neon signs and car headlights. The camera operator is a pedestrian standing on the sidewalk, filming casually.

0-6s: The camera pans across the street. People walk past, a delivery rider waits at a red light. Ambient city sound, distant sirens. Then a few people stop and look up. The camera tilts up with a slight delay, as a real person's would.

6-14s: A huge humpback whale glides slowly out from behind the glass towers, floating about 40 meters above the street. Photoreal skin texture, barnacles, water droplets falling off its fins and onto the road. Its shadow passes over cars and crowds. People gasp, raise phones, and one person grabs a friend's arm.

14-24s: The whale drifts overhead and lets out a deep, low call that vibrates through the street. Windows reflect its body, puddles ripple from the sound, and a flag and trees sway in the air it pushes. The camera shakes slightly and refocuses.

24-30s: It continues down the avenue, tail sweeping gently, and fades into low clouds between the buildings. The shot ends with the crowd still looking up and the camera lowering.

Realism: natural phone-camera behavior, mild auto-exposure shifts, slight lens flare from the neon, real-world scale and weight, no cartoon glow, no text or logos on screen. Ordinary, unposed pedestrians with natural reactions.
Audio: @Audio1 or synchronized ambient city sound, crowd murmurs, wind, and a deep whale call. No music, no narration.

Style: photorealistic, shot-on-iPhone look, natural color, light grain, realistic motion blur, sharp 4K.

entries.title: Rainy Seoul bookstore mystery: a letter from her older self
entries.description: Long-form Korean mystery-drama prompt (Visual Style, cast, shot list, sound) with ARRI Alexa 35 anamorphic look, rain-soaked street to a warm used bookstore and an envelope reveal; restrained, believable mood over effects.
entries.prompt:
Visual Style
Ultra-photorealistic live-action Korean mystery drama, indistinguishable from footage captured on an ARRI Alexa 35 with anamorphic lenses. Premium Netflix-quality production. Natural performances, realistic human movement, consistent protagonist throughout every frame, physically accurate lighting, ray-traced reflections, realistic skin texture, authentic Seoul architecture, subtle cinematic color grading, shallow depth of field, realistic handheld stabilization, smooth Steadicam movement, premium production design, HDR, 4K. Absolutely no AI artifacts, morphing, flickering, identity drift, warped hands, unrealistic expressions, impossible transitions, or abrupt scene changes.
0:00–0:05 | Rainy Evening
A peaceful rainy evening in Seoul.
A slow cinematic drone shot reveals narrow streets glowing beneath warm storefront lights. Rain falls gently onto wet pavement, creating beautiful reflections of cafés, bookstores, and street lamps.
The camera slowly descends to street level.
A beautiful young Korean woman, around 24 years old, walks naturally along the sidewalk carrying a transparent umbrella. She wears a beige trench coat, cream knit sweater, black trousers, and white sneakers. Her long black hair moves gently with the breeze. Other pedestrians pass naturally without acknowledging her. Traffic flows realistically in the background.
Everything feels like a real Korean film.
0:05–0:10 | The Bookstore
She notices a quiet independent bookstore tucked between two cafés.
Warm light spills onto the wet pavement through large glass windows.
She pauses.
Closes her umbrella.
Naturally shakes off the rain.
Opens the wooden glass door.
A small bell rings softly.
The camera follows her inside in one continuous Steadicam shot without cutting.
Inside, shelves are filled with books, warm wooden furniture, soft ambient lighting, and a few customers quietly reading.
The environment feels authentic and lived in.
0:10–0:15 | The Discovery
She slowly walks through the aisles.
Running her fingers gently across book spines.
She notices one beautiful hardcover book displayed alone.
She picks it up.
As she opens it...
A single elegant orange envelope slowly slides out and lands gently on the wooden floor.
The envelope carries a subtle warm glow.
Nothing supernatural.
Just enough to draw attention.
She kneels.
Picks it up carefully.
Opens it.
Inside is a perfectly preserved photograph.
0:15–0:21 | The Photograph
Close-up.
The photograph shows...
Her.
Standing inside this exact bookstore.
Wearing the exact same outfit.
Holding the exact same book.
But...
The photograph is dated 10 years in the future.
The camera slowly pushes toward her face.
She studies every tiny detail.
Her breathing becomes slightly heavier.
No exaggerated acting.
Only subtle confusion and disbelief.
The ambient bookstore sounds become quieter, allowing the emotional moment to breathe.
0:21–0:26 | The Stranger
She slowly raises her head.
Across the bookstore...
A woman is quietly reading beside the window.
The camera slowly reveals her.
She looks almost identical.
Same facial features.
Same gentle smile.
Slightly older.
Elegant cream overcoat.
Hair styled a little differently.

entries.title: "Whiteout Express": 30s unarmed fight across a speeding freight train
entries.description: Action-choreography template: HERO/LOCATION/ENEMIES blocks, five distinct enemies always entering from screen-left, 2.5s fight beats with unique defeats, a single slow-motion leap, lens plan (24/35/85mm) and drum accents per defeat.
entries.prompt:
WHITEOUT EXPRESS — 30s CINEMATIC ACTION

FORMAT: Exactly 30 seconds, 16:9, 60fps where supported. Photorealistic Hollywood action thriller, realistic skin, frosted clothing, icy steel, cold blue-white daylight, drifting snow, natural motion blur.

HERO: image1 is the only hero. Preserve his exact face, skin tone, hair, beard, age, physique, black outfit and accessories in every shot. No morphing, duplicates or costume changes. Unarmed combat only.

LOCATION: A freight train races screen-right through a vast frozen desert. Locomotive ahead; boxcars and black tankers behind. Five enemies approach from screen-left, always from the rear. Never reverse direction.

ENEMIES: Scout with steel baton; massive Brute with fur collar and bare fists; Twin-Blade with two short blades; Chain Man with weighted chain; Leader in a long dark coat, arriving last. Distinct appearances and white-grey winter gear.

TIMELINE:
00–05s: Aerial train reveal. Low tracking shot as the hero sprints across the roof, glancing back while five enemies pursue.
05–07.5s: Scout attacks with baton. Hero ducks, traps his arm, elbows his ribs and sweeps him off the train.
07.5–10s: Brute throws a heavy punch. Hero kicks his thigh and ribs, but Brute grabs him and slams him onto the roof.
10–12.5s: Hero hooks Brute's leg, rolls him over an open roof hatch and pushes him off the train.
12.5–15s: ONLY slow-motion sequence. Hero leaps across the gap between cars, orbiting camera, suspended snow, then lands in a roll. Twin-Blade follows.
15–17.5s: Hero deflects both blades, slides beneath a low steel footbridge beam; Twin-Blade is swept off the train.
17.5–22.5s: Chain Man traps the hero's arm. Hero slips over the tanker edge, catches a handrail, kicks the attacker's knee, and uses the tangled chain to pull him off.
22.5–25s: Hero climbs back onto the icy tanker roof and faces the Leader ten meters ahead.
25–28s: Intense martial-arts duel. Hero traps the Leader's arm, lands a palm strike, spinning back kick and final elbow, knocking him off the roof.
28–30s: Hero stands alone, breathing heavily, frost on his clothes. Camera rises to a wide aerial as the train disappears into the snowy wilderness.

CAMERA & AUDIO: Dynamic aerials, 24mm tracking, 35mm combat orbits, 85mm close-ups and one Dutch angle. Original 150 BPM percussion, pulsing synth bass, bowed-metal drone, wind, rail clacks, locomotive rumble, chain rattles and realistic impacts. Each defeat hits a drum accent. Near-silence during the leap, explosive final impact, then fading wind.

CONTINUITY: Readable one-on-one fights, unique defeats, fallen enemies stay gone, consistent identities and geography, escalating tension, decisive hero victory.

entries.prompt:
Create an ultra-realistic comedic video set at an American international airport passport-control counter. A young adult American woman with long light-brown hair arrives after a 12-hour flight, looking exhausted, with messy hair, smudged makeup, and wrinkled travel clothes. She approaches the passport officer and hands over her passport.

The officer compares her passport photo with her tired appearance, looking increasingly confused. She checks the photo herself and gasps, saying, “Girl, who is that?!”

Determined to look presentable, she opens her carry-on bag right beside the counter and performs an exaggerated travel makeover. Show quick, funny close-ups as she changes into a fresh cream-colored sweater, brushes her hair into soft waves, applies foundation, mascara, blush, and glossy lipstick, and checks her appearance in a compact mirror.

The officer watches patiently as she adjusts her hair one final time, sprays a little perfume, and confidently presents her passport again. The officer compares the photo with her refreshed appearance, pauses, and finally stamps her passport with a subtle nod.

She smiles triumphantly and says, “See? Same person. Better lighting!”

She walks away confidently while the officer stares after her in disbelief.

Photorealistic live-action comedy, realistic airport lighting, natural handheld camera movement, detailed makeup application, believable expressions, accurate lip synchronization, authentic airport ambience, and consistent character identity. Keep the makeover playful and non-suggestive. No magical transformations, no face swapping, no subtitles, no logos, and no watermarks.

entries.title: Felt counting-forest lesson: 5 hard cuts with locked optics, light and continuous audio
entries.description: Kling's official long-form example for on-screen text: 5 hard-cut shots in one felt-and-clay forest classroom, with a LOCATION MAP, identical 35mm optics and light direction after every cut, ambience and music that "never reset at the cuts", and burned-in felt subtitles timed to the voiceover to the hundredth of a second.
entries.prompt:
SCENE CONTEXT: EXACTLY 3 UNIQUE CHARACTERS ACROSS THE VIDEO — NO DUPLICATES.EXT. Enchanted counting forest classroom, warm morning. One soft cream cloud teacher teaches the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4 in four separate shots. Two tiny yellow chick pupils appear only in the number-two shot.3 characters across the video, 5 hard-cut shots, 15s, real time.ACTIVE REFERENCES@Video1: content, narration and timing reference only — preserve the educational progression, additive explanations and final recap. Never inherit its white studio environment or visual style.@Image1: visual-world reference only — handmade clay-and-felt materials, rounded toy-like forms, pastel forest trunks, mossy ground, rainbow colours, warm diffused backlight and shallow storybook depth. Never inherit its existing characters, numerals or composition.
LOCATION MAP: All five shots occur on the same circular moss stage inside one enchanted forest classroom.One broad warm-brown tree trunk anchors frame-left; a second tree trunk anchors frame-right. A curved pastel rainbow root crosses the background. The central teaching pedestal remains in the same position in every shot. Camera always stays on the front side of the teaching axis, between 3.0 and 3.3 m from the pedestal. The sun always comes from upper frame-right. Background geometry, material scale and colour palette remain identical after every cut.
FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING: Shot 1: the cloud teacher floats centre-left, facing a large red felt numeral 1 on the central pedestal. One red apple is concealed inside the moss below it. Shot 2: The cloud teacher floats centre-left, facing a large amber felt numeral 2. Two yellow chicks begin concealed behind the pedestal. Shot 3: the cloud teacher floats centre-left, facing a large green felt numeral 3. Three blue felt stars begin nested inside the moss. Shot 4: the cloud teacher floats centre-left, facing a large blue felt numeral 4. Four purple clay blocks begin below the pedestal. Shot 5: the cloud teacher floats alone at centre, facing the viewer beneath the rainbow root. Every shot begins mid-gesture with the teacher already pointing toward the active numeral. No empty establishing beat.
FORMAT MODE: Horizontal 16:9, total 15s, real time, 5 shots connected by clean hard cuts.Shot 1 — 0.00–4.00s: number 1 and one apple.Shot 2 — 4.00–7.08s: number 2 and two chicks.Shot 3 — 7.08–10.21s: number 3 and three stars.Shot 4 — 10.21–13.08s: number 4 and four blocks.Shot 5 — 13.08–15.00s: spoken recap and celebration. Each number receives its own separate shot. Numerals 1, 2, 3 and 4 never share the same teaching frame.No fades, dissolves or split screens.
OPTICS: 35mm equivalent, 54° horizontal FOV, locked across all five shots. Identical natural perspective, camera height, background scale and depth-of-field character after every cut. Focal plane remains on the cloud teacher, active numeral and active quantity. Foreground flowers softly obscure the lower corners. Distant trees dissolve into the same creamy storybook blur.
CAMERA: Every shot is operated handheld at approximately 105 cm height from the front side of the teaching axis. World register: gentle SETTLE. Shot 1: slow 10 cm push toward numeral 1. Shot 2: slow 10 cm push toward numeral 2. Shot 3: slow 10 cm push toward numeral 3.Shot 4: slow 10 cm push toward numeral 4. Shot 5: slow 8 cm push toward the celebrating teacher.Visible handheld character throughout: breath sway, micro-roll, late tiny corrections and gentle but obvious handmade shake. Numerals and subtitles remain readable. Camera height, axis and movement speed match across all cuts.Not a gimbal, slider, tripod lock-off, drone or digitally stabilised camera.
ACTION TIMING 0.00–0.78s: Shot 1 begins. The cloud teacher already points toward the red numeral 1. 0.78–1.98s: numeral 1 rises and completes one soft bounce. 1.98–4.00s: one red apple rises from the moss and settles beneath numeral 1. 4.00–4.86s: hard cut to Shot 2. The amber numeral 2 rises and completes one soft bounce. 4.86–7.08s: one yellow chick hops out from the left, then a second chick joins from the right; they touch shoulders and settle together. 7.08–8.04s: hard cut to Shot 3. The green numeral 3 rises and completes one soft bounce. 8.04–10.21s: two blue felt stars rise together, followed by one additional star; the three stars settle into a clear triangular arrangement. 10.21–11.06s: hard cut to Shot 4. The blue numeral 4 rises and completes one soft bounce. 11.06–13.08s: three purple blocks assemble first; one additional block clicks into the fourth position. 13.08–14.40s: hard cut to Shot 5. Four tiny coloured fireflies pulse sequentially red, amber, green and blue while the teacher points from left to right. 14.40–15.00s: the teacher opens both arms; a small clay sun unfolds above the rainbow and releases a brief sparkle burst.
PHYSICS: The cloud teacher has the buoyancy of a lightweight stuffed felt puppet, with soft vertical drift and delayed arm movement. Each numeral has padded felt weight: it compresses, rebounds once and settles. The apple lands with soft clay weight. The chicks’ feet squash slightly into the moss. Stars descend with gentle air resistance. Blocks connect with firm edge-to-edge contact. Every quantity remains stable and readable until its shot ends. Hard cuts reset the teaching pedestal cleanly while preserving the same forest, teacher identity, material scale and lighting.
LIGHTING: One identical motivated source in every shot: warm morning sunlight filtering through the trees from upper frame-right.The teacher’s lower-left side remains slightly darker in all five shots. Soft rim light separates the felt fibres from the forest. Protect the cream cloud, pastel numerals and rainbow highlights from clipping. The direction, colour temperature, haze density and exposure remain unchanged across every cut.
AUDIO VOICEOVER: The cloud teacher speaks in English with the same warm, clear, medium-high preschool-teacher voice in every shot. Pronunciation is slow, encouraging and rhythmically precise.0.78s: “One.”1.98s: “One means just one.”4.16s: “Two.”4.86s: “Two means one and one together.”7.26s: “Three.”8.04s: “Three means two and one more.”10.32s: “Four.”11.06s: “Four means three and one more.”13.32s: “One, two, three, four.”14.40s: “Great job!”
MUSIC: one continuous original children’s instrumental across all cuts, using soft marimba, toy piano, light ukulele, felt-drum taps and gentle handclaps. The same melody, tempo and instrumentation continue seamlessly through every shot. It rises slightly with each new number and ends with a short celebratory flourish.SFX: one soft felt pop for each numeral bounce; one clay plop for the apple; two tiny moss footsteps for the chicks; three sparkle chimes for the stars; four wooden clicks for the blocks; four soft firefly pings during the recap; one bright celebration chime at the end.
AMBIENCE: continuous close grass rustle, mid-distance leaves and faint woodland birds. The ambience never resets at the cuts.MIX: narration remains clear and centred. Music ducks beneath every spoken line. Sound effects synchronise exactly with the quantities. Music and ambience remain continuous across every hard cut.
SUBTITLES: Burned-in English subtitles, bottom-centre inside the title-safe area, positioned 10% above the lower edge.One or two lines maximum. Rounded cream felt subtitle panel with dark chocolate-brown bold lettering, high contrast and stable placement. Picture: Continue the ink-wash bamboo grove scene from image 1. A swordsman wearing a bamboo hat and a dark robe stands as a silhouette in the center, surrounded by thick mist and swaying bamboo shadows.

(0:03-0:08) Plot introduction, camera movement: extreme close-up.
Plot: The swordsman senses killing intent.
Picture: The camera quickly pushes in to an extreme close-up beneath the swordsman's bamboo hat.
Details: Beneath the hat brim, a pair of sharp, resolute eyes is revealed, the gaze like a blade. Ink-wash sweat beads slide down from his forehead.
Action: The swordsman slowly grips the hilt with his right hand, knuckles turning white. The falling bamboo leaves accelerate.
(0:08-0:13) Camera movement: rapid orbit.
Picture: The camera orbits rapidly around the swordsman as the center.
Plot: Two assassins, also rendered as ink-wash silhouettes, burst from the depths of the bamboo grove, wielding twin hooks and a short blade.
Details: The assassins' movements are likewise formed by ink-brush strokes, flowing like ink traces. The camera sweeps swiftly past the assassins' figures, emphasizing a sense of speed.
(0:13-0:18) Camera movement: handheld feel, high-speed capture.
Combat: The swordsman suddenly draws his blade; the flash of the blade is a pure-white ink-wash fissure. The assassins attack with twin hooks.
Details: First strike — the swordsman turns and slashes; blade meets the assassin's twin hooks, bursting into countless black-and-white sparks and ink splatters with a calligraphic feel. Second strike — the swordsman feints, springs off a bamboo pole, and strikes down from above; the assassin tumbles away, the bamboo pole snaps and scatters into flying ink marks. Third strike — the swordsman's blade tip points straight at another assassin's throat; the assassin parries with a short blade, and the camera captures the fine ink-trace fracturing detail as blade and short blade grind together.
(0:18-0:20) Camera movement: slow motion to freeze-frame.
Picture: The swordsman's blade stops beside the assassin's neck; the assassin freezes.
Details: The swordsman's bamboo hat is slightly tilted from the fight. The bamboo grove returns to calm; more bamboo leaves flutter.
Mood: The camera slowly pulls back to a medium shot, freeze-framing on the swordsman sheathing his blade and the assassin collapsed on the ground.
Text (optional): Ink-wash-style text appears at the bottom of the frame: "The jianghu is but a single stroke of erasure."
Style notes: Maintain the high-contrast black-and-white ink-painting style of image 1 throughout. The action must carry a brush-stroke feel, the speed must be fast, and the details rich (ink drops, sparks, ink-trace fissures).

entries.title: A water drop becomes a goddess: single-take morph in mineral-pigment painting style
entries.description: Official first/last-frame example: a single continuous take where a falling drop's ripples rise and condense into the West Lake water goddess, lotuses bloom under each step, and the last second freezes into a poster composition. Bracketed second ranges.
entries.prompt:
[Single continuous take, slow and aesthetic camera movement, no cuts, 15-second long shot, collision of mineral-pigment rock-color painting texture with 3D rendering, teal-blue × gilded-gold color clash]
Global setting: Chinese-style rock-color painting texture, mineral-pigment granular grain, gold-leaf texture, a strong color clash between teal-blue and gilded gold. The scene is West Lake in morning mist at dawn: the lake surface is a matte teal-blue wash, golden morning light pierces the clouds to form Tyndall light shafts, and the stone pagodas of Three Pools Mirroring the Moon and Leifeng Pagoda loom faintly in the mist, with lotus leaves and flowers nearby. The main subject is the West Lake water goddess "Xizi": rendered in rock-color texture, oval face, willow-leaf eyebrows, phoenix eyes, a vermillion floral mark at the center of her brow, skin like lustrous white jade with a soft glow, and a pale-gold halo suspended behind her head; her hair is coiled high and pinned with a gilded lotus-flower hairpin, and her skirt and sash are formed from flowing lake water, a teal-blue gradient with shimmering ripples on the surface.
Voiceover and sound effects: The background features a gentle guzheng and bamboo flute; ambient sound holds subtle ripples and dawn birdsong. From the 8th second, an ethereal, tender female voice slowly recites "If one were to compare West Lake to Xizi —"; during the glance-back segment it continues with the second half "Lightly adorned or richly made up, always fitting." The pacing is slow, with a faint reverberation and lingering resonance.
[0-3 seconds: A single drop of water]
Extreme macro. At the edge of a lotus leaf at dawn, a water drop gathers full, reflecting the golden morning light, and slowly falls. The camera follows the drop downward (Tilt down); the drop strikes the lake, setting off a ring of gold-blue ripples that expand outward in layers.
[3-7 seconds: Water gathers into form]
At the center of the ripples, the lake water slowly rises and condenses into the figure of the goddess "Xizi": the water becomes her teal-blue skirt and translucent sash, and tiny streams flow around her. She rises slowly from the heart of the lake, her eyes gently closing then slowly opening, the gilded lotus hairpin glowing faintly. The camera slowly orbits (Orbit) her half-lowered eyes and the skirt woven from flowing water.
[7-11 seconds: A lotus with every step]
She walks barefoot and slowly across the lake surface; with each step, a ring of golden ripples spreads beneath her feet, and lotus flowers bloom in succession within the ripples. The camera pulls back to a medium-wide shot: the thin mist parts, the three stone pagodas of Three Pools Mirroring the Moon light up warmly in the distance, Leifeng Pagoda emerges in the morning light, and weeping willows brush the water along the shore. At the 8th second, the female voiceover begins "If one were to compare West Lake to Xizi —"; her sash trails a long streak of gold-blue water-light behind her.
[11-15 seconds: The glance back — always fitting]
She stops and glances back toward the camera; the camera slowly pushes in to a half-body close-up: morning light falls on her face, the lake-water sash drifts gently at her side, and a few glowing water drops fall from the tips of her hair, dissolving into fine points of light in midair. The voiceover continues with the second half "Lightly adorned or richly made up, always fitting." She smiles faintly; behind her are Leifeng Pagoda and the misty Three Pools Mirroring the Moon in the morning light. In the final second, the image fully freezes on her glance-back close-up, locking into a perfect cinematic-poster composition.

entries.description: Long-form supernatural thriller with a REFERENCE LOCK list (@[ref1]..@[ref5]), a creature spec, 8 shots of 7.5 s, a rule-based plot (moonlight blocks the shadow), FINAL RULES for continuity and a one-line "Final hook". Cold blue-gray moonlight, subtle film grain.
entries.prompt:
Style: Photorealistic live-action supernatural action thriller. Cinematic camera movement, realistic combat physics, practical creature textures, wet bark, cold blue-gray moonlight, deep shadows and subtle film grain. No CGI-looking visuals, neon, cartoon aesthetics or excessive slow motion.

REFERENCE LOCK

- @[ref1] Heroine
- @[ref2] Hollow Stalker
- @[ref3] Forest and clearing
- @[ref4] Supernatural shadows
- @[ref5] Katana

Preserve exact character appearances, costumes, proportions, weapon continuity and forest geography. The Stalker has six branch horns, a faceless wooden skull, two white eyes, elongated limbs and black bark-and-root anatomy. Its cut left wrist remains damaged throughout.

SHOT 1 | 0:00–0:07.5 | THE SHADOW RUNS AHEAD
Low tracking shot follows the heroine sprinting through wet leaves as a second human-shaped shadow races ahead without a visible owner. The Stalker charges between the trees. Her own shadow suddenly stops and turns its head toward her.

SHOT 2 | 0:07.5–0:15 | SOMETHING UNDER THE TREES
The Stalker's detached shadow races through connected darkness, catches her ankle and forces her to slash at the ground with her katana. The shadow retreats, leaving a black stain. The creature's white eyes appear behind her between the trees.

SHOT 3 | 0:15–0:22.5 | THE WRONG SHADOW
The shadow stops at a moonlit boundary. The heroine discovers that light blocks its movement. She circles a tree as the shadow crawls vertically up its trunk. Two silhouettes reach toward her feet. Her sword passes harmlessly through the false shadow as the real creature raises its arm behind her.

SHOT 4 | 0:22.5–0:30 | THE FOREST CLOSES
The Stalker merges tree shadows into a dark corridor. The heroine slides beneath reaching shadow extensions and parries its left-arm strike, cutting through its wrist. Black root fibers snap apart. The creature strikes a tree, spreading its shadow over the last safe strip of moonlight.

SHOT 5 | 0:30–0:37.5 | THE TRAP
The Stalker lunges. She dives beneath its arm and rolls across damp earth. Its shadow surrounds her in a complete circle. From overhead, she realizes its darkness connects every shadowy patch, but its feet remain beneath a bright gap in the moonlight. She stops running.

SHOT 6 | 0:37.5–0:45 | SHE STOPS RUNNING
She tests the rule: the shadow recoils from moonlight and surges through darkness. As the Stalker charges, she attacks instead of retreating, sliding beneath its right arm and driving her katana toward the moonlit boundary beneath its front foot.

SHOT 7 | 0:45–0:52.5 | PINNING THE NIGHT
She plunges the katana through the shadow and into the soil at the boundary between darkness and moonlight. The shadow convulses and remains pinned. Black strands wrap around the creature's limbs, torso and six horns. Its damaged wrist unravels as she twists the blade deeper, enduring the pain in her injured shoulder.

SHOT 8 | 0:52.5–1:00 | THE LAST SHADOW
The Stalker disintegrates into black bark, roots and ash. Its white eyes extinguish. Silence. The heroine remains kneeling beside her planted sword. In the distance, dozens of shadows turn toward her despite the trees remaining still. She sees them reflected in the katana's silver blade.

Hard cut to black. No dialogue, title card, subtitles, logos or musical sting.

FINAL RULES: Strict continuity across all shots. Maintain consistent moonlight, geography, costumes, weapon hand and creature damage. Grounded movement, believable weight and contact physics. Shadows remain flat, opaque and connected to darkness, except when climbing trees or forming reaching extensions. No extra characters, extra limbs, random teleportation or premature disintegration.

Final hook: The monster is dead. The forest is still watching.

entries.prompt:
Create a 15-second ultra-photorealistic video showing five spontaneous, happy moments from a young Japanese woman's ordinary day.

FORMAT: 15 seconds, exactly 5 scenes with natural hard cuts. Every scene must look like genuine footage recorded by her friend using an early-2000s MiniDV camcorder.

MAIN CHARACTER

A Japanese woman, 23 years old, natural face, medium-length layered black hair loosely tied. She wears a faded sage-green oversized T-shirt, cream trousers, white canvas sneakers, and a small brown shoulder bag.

Maintain exactly the same face, hairstyle, outfit, and body proportions in every scene.

VISUAL REALISM

Authentic MiniDV footage with natural handheld shake, imperfect framing, slight autofocus hunting, soft CCD highlights, realistic skin texture, subtle motion blur, and slightly faded consumer colors.

Natural daylight, believable physics, genuine expressions, real-world movement. No cinematic grading, slow motion, artificial camera movement, or glossy AI appearance.

CUT 1 — THE PERFECT BUBBLE (00:00–00:03)

A sunny Tokyo neighborhood sidewalk.

Her friend blows soap bubbles toward her. One large bubble floats directly toward her face. She leans away instinctively, then laughs when the bubble lands on her sleeve and pops.

She looks at her friend with a surprised grin.

The camera shakes slightly as the friend laughs.

HARD CUT.

CUT 2 — UNEXPECTED ICE CREAM (00:03–00:06)

Outside a small local ice cream shop.

She holds an ice cream cone while her friend tries to take a photograph. A tiny drip slides down the cone.

She quickly catches it with her tongue, looks at the camera, and bursts into a genuine little laugh.

Her friend says, 「早いね！」 (Hayai ne! — “That was quick!”)

HARD CUT.

CUT 3 — THE DOG THAT CHOSE HER (00:06–00:09)

A quiet neighborhood park.

A friendly small Shiba Inu on a leash walks toward her and sniffs her sneaker. She crouches naturally and offers the back of her hand to sniff.

The dog happily wags its tail and leans against her knee. She smiles warmly and gently scratches its chest while the owner watches.

No dog jumping unnaturally or changing appearance.

HARD CUT.

CUT 4 — IMPROVISED DANCE (00:09–00:12)

A sunny pedestrian street with ordinary shops in the background.

She hears her friend tapping a playful rhythm on a small shopping bag. She responds with two spontaneous, silly dance steps, turns toward the camera, and laughs at herself.

Her bag swings naturally with her movement. The camera operator misses part of the first step, then quickly reframes her.

No professional dancing or exaggerated choreography.

HARD CUT.

CUT 5 — THE HAPPY GOODBYE (00:12–00:15)

Late afternoon on a quiet residential street.

She walks away, then suddenly turns back toward the camera, takes two quick steps backward, and waves enthusiastically at her friend.

She says, 「またねー！」 (“See you!”)

She turns around and walks away smiling. The camera follows for a brief moment before abruptly cutting off with a tiny authentic MiniDV recording glitch.

AUDIO

Real synchronized environmental sound: soft street ambience, soap bubbles popping, a light laugh, ice cream shop sounds, dog paws and collar jingles, footsteps, clothing movement, and natural Japanese conversation.

No background music, narration, artificial sound effects, or exaggerated laughter.

STRICT REALISM

Preserve identity and clothing across all five cuts. Keep faces, fingers, objects, and movements anatomically correct. No duplicated props, morphing, floating objects, unnatural smiles, robotic motion, random transitions, or sudden background changes within a scene.

Every scene must begin with the action already happening, like a friend casually recording without preparation.

FINAL FEELING: Bright, cheerful, spontaneous, intimate, and genuinely human. Five little happy moments captured on an old camcorder — not an advertisement, not a travel montage, and never an obvious AI-generated video.

entries.title: "The First Echo": deadpan cave-tribe comedy where the canyon talks back (FLUX 3 Max)
entries.description: SUBJECTS / LOCATION / 5 timed shots / CAMERA / PERFORMANCE / AUDIO / LAST FRAME / NEGATIVE blocks. Comedy from reaction faces ("Deadpan serious prehistoric acting … No winking at camera") and a delayed natural canyon echo with reverb tail.
entries.prompt:
SUBJECTS: Grukk, a broad shouldered Neanderthal man with heavy brow, tangled brown hair, thick beard, tiger-striped fur wrap, wooden spear in hand. Four tribe members in fur and hide wraps: a tall bearded elder, a red-haired woman, a stocky man, and a small curious child with messy hair. Everyone has authentic prehistoric skin texture, dirt, scars. Wardrobe stays identical in every shot.

LOCATION: A rocky canyon edge above a misty pine valley. A far stone wall across the gap returns echoes. Small campfire smoke drifting behind the group. Moss, boulders, scattered bones.

SHOT 1 (0-4s): Medium shot, Grukk stands at the cliff edge proudly, chest out, and shouts one deep grunting roar into the valley. Pause. From across the canyon his exact roar comes back, slightly deeper. Grukk freezes, eyes wide, slowly turns his head toward the sound. Tribe members behind him stop chewing and look up.

SHOT 2 (4-8s): Close up on Grukk's furious face. He narrows his brow and growls a short insult grunt. The echo growls it back. He gasps with offended shock, points his spear across the valley, and jabs it twice. The echo repeats the jabbing grunts. Grukk shakes with rage and beats his chest.

SHOT 3 (8-13s): Wide shot, the whole tribe lined up behind Grukk. The elder steps forward and calmly barks a deep warning. The echo barks it back. The elder recoils, hands up, taking two big steps backward. The stocky man raises a rock threateningly and yells. The echo yells back louder. He drops the rock on his own foot and hops in pain, the echo mocking his yelp.

SHOT 4 (13-17s): Over the shoulder, the small child squeezes between the adults, walks to the edge, cups both hands around her mouth, and squeaks one tiny high-pitched yell. The echo squeaks back clearly and cutely. The child giggles, and the echo giggles too. Every adult stares, baffled. Grukk slowly lowers his spear.

SHOT 5 (17-20s): Medium wide, Grukk, the elder, and the stocky man all quietly step behind the child as if she is the bravest warrior. The child shrugs, turns, and walks calmly away. The whole tribe follows her in a nervous huddle, Grukk walking backward while keeping his spear aimed at the valley. A last tiny echo squeak drifts back from the canyon.

CAMERA: Handheld with subtle organic sway, 35mm anamorphic character, gentle slow push-ins on faces, quick snap reframes on the echo reactions, natural lens breathing. Comedy timing comes from reaction faces, not camera tricks.

PERFORMANCE: Deadpan serious prehistoric acting, played as completely sincere and offended. Micro-expressions: flaring nostrils, twitching brows, wide disbelieving eyes. No winking at camera.

AUDIO: Diegetic only. Deep guttural grunts and roars, delayed natural canyon echo with realistic reverb tail, wind through pines, distant crackle of fire, bare feet on gravel, fur rustle, rock thud, child's tiny squeak. No music, no narration, no spoken words, no subtitles.

LAST FRAME: Hold on the empty canyon edge with mist drifting and the spear tip left leaning on a rock, tribe already out of frame. Absolutely no on-screen text, no captions, no subtitles, no title card, no logo, no watermark, no UI elements, no letters or symbols anywhere in the image at any point in the video.

NEGATIVE: no text, no logos, no watermarks, no modern objects, no music, no cartoon style, no extra limbs, no face morphing, no clothing changes between shots.

entries.title: "The brim lift": aged dye-transfer 35mm Western close-up, timed to the second
entries.description: A 3,000-character single-shot spec: location and wardrobe wear ("Nothing is new"), a fictional 44-year-old character, a 40 cm low dolly creep where a foreground post slides out and the hat brim crops frame, second-by-second timing, and a film-print look: "35mm colour negative … aged dye-transfer release print … coarse organic film grain, halation around bright edges … faint print dust", plus explicit exclusions (no HDR, scanlines, rounded corners).
entries.prompt:
Create one continuous six-second Western shot of the brim lift: an extreme low-angle close-up of the station keeper against the pale sky, her hat brim cropping the top of frame, as she tips it up at the first sight of the rider's dust. Calm, luminous, natural.
A lone 1870s horse-relay station on a high bleached mesa top at noon: cracked bone-tan clay, grey-green sage, silvered juniper snags, far pale ochre mesas under a faded sky-blue sky. An adobe station house with a sagging grey-timber porch, a split-rail corral, a tarred plank trough and a crooked cedar telegraph pole line. Everyone wears patched, sun-rotted cotton, buckskin, canvas and wool, sweat-stained felt hats, dust in every seam; brass is tarnished, iron hand-forged. Dry tumbleweeds bounce across the open ground on a hot wind. Nothing is new: every board, rope, saddle and cloth is decades-worn and mended. Every person is an original fictional adult.
At the porch rail, filling the lower frame against the sky, stands Honora Coyle, a fictional 44-year-old widow who keeps the relay station: strikingly beautiful in a natural classic-film-star way, fair skin with a soft natural tone and only a light dew of sweat, strong cheekbones, calm grey-green eyes with deep squint lines, tall and straight-backed, dark auburn braid tied with a frayed faded-blue ribbon. She wears a sun-bleached, patched blue calico work dress with rolled sleeves, a stained tan canvas apron, a sweat-stained bone felt hat and cracked brown boots. A sun-greyed porch post stands soft in the near right foreground.
Camera: a low dolly on a short track below the porch rail, looking steeply up at her face against the sky. 50mm lens impression, no wide-angle distortion. One very slow forward creep of forty centimetres. Because the camera inches closer from below, the post slides out of the right edge and her brim comes to crop the top of frame as a hard horizontal line. Not a zoom, not a tilt, not handheld.
Timing: seconds zero to two, Honora stands still against the faded sky, the brim's shadow soft across her brow, skin natural and matte with a faint dew at the temple. Seconds two to four, her eyes shift far off camera-left. Seconds four to five, with two fingers she tips the brim up a finger's width and her eyes narrow. Final second, she holds still, brim edge level across the top of frame. End on her eyeline.
A frame from a 1950s-60s Western feature film shot on location on 35mm colour negative and seen as an aged dye-transfer release print: rich but time-worn colour, deep faded-blue skies, sunburnt earth reds and ochres, warm leathery skin, dense shadows, coarse organic film grain, halation around bright edges, the soft focus fall-off and light vignetting of vintage lenses, faint print dust. Big open vistas and low-angle close-ups against the sky; tripod and dolly only. Hard noon sun overhead, camera-left. Sweat and dust on real sun-leathered skin. No TV-screen frame, rounded corners, scanlines, B&W, HDR or digital crispness. 16:9, 24 fps. No captions, logos or watermarks.
Avoid: orange or shiny skin, heavy sweat, harsh glare, smiling, looking into the lens, a second person, rounded frame corners or black borders.

entries.title: H3 Max shot brief: collapsing sea-cathedral on mirror tideflats (60:30:10 colour, @tags)
entries.description: Official long "shot brief": Style / Cinematography / Lighting / Color as a 60:30:10 ratio / Camera with 180° shutter and motivated operator shake / Physics, then @pilot and @cathedral subject tags, a timecoded ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE action block, constraints and a no-music audio list.
entries.prompt:
BLACK MIRROR TIDEFLATS / THE COLLAPSING SEA-CATHEDRAL
Style: 8K cinematic. Photorealistic, no 3D render, no game engine, no game-cutscene aesthetic.
Cinematography: naturalistic master cinematography.
Lighting: high-contrast dramatic light. Cold storm-blue dusk across the flats vs. blinding sodium-orange furnace glow pouring from the toppling structure. The wet mirror surface doubles every light source into a second inverted world.
Color: 60:30:10, dominant gunmetal blue and wet slate (the tideflats and sky) / secondary sodium amber and rust-red (burning floodlights, corroded steel) / accent magnesium white and cobalt blue (the failing reactor core and its arc-flashes).
Camera: physical cine lens. 180 degree shutter motion blur. Continuous handheld operator shake, motivated by the ground concussions rolling through the shallow water.
Physics: gravity and inertia respected. Steel trusses buckle and fold under their own mass; spray, ash and salt mist obey atmospheric drag.
SUBJECTS:
@pilot: a lone figure in a salt-crusted pressure suit crewing a skeletal wind-skiff, a low wheeled land-yacht with a torn carbon sail, hunched at the tiller, cracked gold-tinted visor reflecting the falling structure, throwing twin walls of white spray from its outriggers.
@cathedral: a colossal derelict sea-rig, a kilometre of rusted iron lattice and floodlight towers, listing and buckling as it collapses into the shallows, shedding burning platform decks and cobalt arc-flash from its ruptured core.
LOCATION: an endless tidal flat of black volcanic glass under two inches of standing water, a perfect mirror to the horizon, broken by rotting mooring pylons and drifting curtains of salt mist, the skyline dominated by the burning collapse.
ACTION, ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE, single unbroken handheld tracking shot, NO cuts, 15 seconds.
0:00-0:05  Medium-Wide on @pilot: camera tracks alongside the skiff as it carves between rotting pylons that burst into splinters and spray behind the wheels; the horizon tears open as @cathedral enters frame, leaning, trailing burning deck plates.
0:05-0:10  continuous zoom-in / tilt up: camera glides past the skiff and tilts up through the pylons onto the collapse; a core vessel detonates, the shockwave ripping the standing water into a flat sheet and bending the flare into a horizontal streak across frame.
0:10-0:15  Extreme Close-Up on @cathedral: telephoto-compressed view of the disintegrating rig against the sky, steel plate peeling and glowing white-hot, raining burning debris down toward the camera.
CONSTRAINTS: 16:9 anamorphic widescreen. ONE CONTINUOUS SHOT, absolutely NO hard cuts. Telephoto compression during the zoom. No slow-motion. Photoreal throughout.
AUDIO (NO MUSIC): deep structural groan of failing steel, the hiss and slap of water under the hull, tearing-metal screech from above, the rigging-hum and canvas crack of the skiff at speed, wind roar across open flats.

entries.title: H3 Max: 16-bit San Francisco endless-runner gameplay (rules-based prompt)
entries.description: Official prompt written as game rules: only JUMP or DUCK, every obstacle must intersect the path, four parallax layers, an 8-12 frame run cycle, a minimal score HUD, chiptune music and synced SFX, no anti-aliasing.
entries.prompt:
Create a pixel-art side-scrolling platformer gameplay animation, presented as authentic 16-bit / 32-bit retro game footage.
The game is a fast, continuous San Francisco-themed endless runner. A heroic pixel-art adventurer automatically runs from left to right while the camera smoothly tracks the character, keeping the hero roughly centered on screen. The player cannot stop or move around obstacles. Every obstacle that enters the hero's running path must require either jumping over it or ducking underneath it.
GAMEPLAY
Obstacles approach clearly from the right side of the screen with enough visual anticipation to understand what is happening. There are only two ways to avoid hazards. JUMP: used for anything occupying the ground-level running path. DUCK: used for anything crossing directly above the running path at head or upper-body height. Every gameplay obstacle must physically intersect the hero's path if no action is taken.
San Francisco-themed obstacles: a cheerful corgi runs directly across the hero's path and the hero jumps completely over it; a startup founder charges toward the hero holding out a giant term sheet, jump over the person; an autonomous delivery robot rolls into the running path, jump over it; an abandoned electric scooter lies horizontally across the sidewalk, jump over it; a shopping cart rolls into the running path, jump over it; a low-flying delivery drone crosses at the hero's head level, duck underneath it; a flock of pigeons flies across the path at head height, duck underneath them; low construction scaffolding extends across the sidewalk, duck underneath it. Keep obstacles visually distinct and spaced far enough apart that every jump or duck reads clearly as a deliberate gameplay action.
SAN FRANCISCO ENVIRONMENT
Multi-layer parallax scrolling. Foreground: lush grass, sidewalk edges, rocks, flowers, fire hydrants, cable-car rails, fallen leaves, utility covers and small particles moving quickly. Midground: colorful Victorian houses, steep streets, cafes, trees, cable cars, fences, stone walls, staircases, scaffolding and occasional fantasy waterfalls at medium speed. Background: enormous green hills, dense neighborhoods, downtown skyscrapers, the Transamerica Pyramid, distant castle-like silhouettes, the Bay, the Golden Gate Bridge and mountains beyond the city, moving slowly. Very distant atmospheric layer: colorful California sky, enormous clouds, drifting coastal fog, distant birds. Blend recognizable San Francisco architecture with a lush fantasy-adventure world: Victorian houses beside ancient stone ruins, cable-car tracks winding through grassy hills, waterfalls descending beside city staircases, the Golden Gate Bridge appearing dramatically between mountains and fog. Background pedestrians, cars and scenery are decorative only.
HERO ANIMATION
A highly polished 8 to 12 frame running cycle with expressive movement, bouncing hair and clothing, an animated cape or jacket, natural arm and leg motion, and tiny dust particles beneath the boots. Transition cleanly between RUN, JUMP, LAND, RUN, DUCK, RUN. Jump animations must visibly carry the hero completely over each ground obstacle; duck animations must visibly lower the hero enough for airborne obstacles to pass over. Keep the hero's design, face, clothing, colors, proportions and sprite dimensions consistent throughout every frame.
SCORE AND GAME UI
A small, authentic retro-game score counter in the upper-right corner, simple pixel font, continuously increasing as the hero survives, such as SCORE 004820. Keep the interface minimal. No menus, tutorial text or dialogue boxes.
MUSIC AND SOUND
Energetic retro video-game music throughout, like a polished SNES or early PlayStation-era adventure game: upbeat and catchy, chiptune-inspired synths, punchy retro drums, melodic bass and a bright adventurous lead melody. Synchronized retro sound effects: soft rhythmic footsteps while running, a short arcade-style jump sound on each jump, a quick swoosh while ducking, a landing sound on touchdown, drone buzzing as drones approach, pigeon wing flaps, small environmental sounds for passing cable cars, and a subtle point sound after clearing an obstacle. Music stays the dominant layer with effects mixed cleanly underneath.
PIXEL-ART REQUIREMENTS
Crisp hand-crafted pixel art with clearly visible individual pixels, a limited retro palette and extremely detailed sprite work, resembling a premium modern indie pixel-art platformer. No 3D rendering, no vector graphics, no smooth painted edges, no realistic textures, no motion blur, no anti-aliased artwork.
CAMERA
Classic side-view 2D platformer perspective, fixed camera height, smooth horizontal tracking, no zooming, no cuts, no camera rotation. The hero stays approximately centered while the environment moves continuously from right to left.
Format: 16:9 widescreen, side-scrolling 2D gameplay, continuous gameplay, retro soundtrack and sound effects, minimal score HUD, no logos.

entries.title: FLUX 3: bartender's line over a live jazz trio that never stops
entries.description: "plays … continuously from the first frame to the last, never stopping" and "The music keeps playing under and after his words" keep the music bed under dialogue.
entries.prompt: One continuous unbroken real-time ten-second cinematic shot inside a small dim basement jazz club, late set. A live trio — upright bass, brushed drums, and piano — plays a slow, smoky number continuously from the first frame to the last, never stopping. Slow dolly along the bar toward a bartender in a rolled-sleeve white shirt polishing a glass. Over the music, he leans toward a regular seated at the bar and says in a low, warm voice: "Last call was an hour ago. For you, the night is still young." The music keeps playing under and after his words. Audio: the jazz trio constant throughout, murmur of a few late patrons, the soft clink of the glass as he sets it down, and a faint espresso-machine hiss from the back. No on-screen text, no subtitles.

entries.title: FLUX 3: one conductor, one voice, English then German
entries.description: Language labels, an exact order, "the same warm, lightly amused voice" and a slow-paced German line make the language hand-off explicit; aurora light crosses the train windows.
entries.prompt: One continuous unbroken real-time ten-second cinematic shot inside a retro-futurist glass observation train gliding beneath a vivid violet aurora above snow-covered mountains. Medium shot of one conductor standing alone at a brass intercom, clearly visible from the waist up as moving aurora light crosses the curved windows behind her. She looks toward the passengers beside camera and makes one calm announcement in two languages, in this exact order, using the same warm, lightly amused voice. First in English: "Next stop: the northern lights." Then, after a short natural pause, in German, spoken slowly and clearly at a relaxed, unhurried pace with a gentle rest between words: "Bitte halten Sie Ihre Träume fest." She takes her time with the German line and says each line only once with natural pronunciation. No other speech. Audio: steady rail rhythm, soft wind against the glass, one departure bell, and a restrained analog-synth shimmer kept below the voice. No on-screen text, no subtitles.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 "PROP LOCKS" + "STAGING LOCK": grandma, a debt collector and her "cat"
entries.description: Labelled prop locks (PROP-STICK, PROP-BOWL: always in one hand, never dropped), a STAGING LOCK that fixes who enters from where, LOOK with filmic grain and halation, a PACING line, timecoded Korean dialogue, then a long NEGATIVE list (incl. "no attack gore"). Ends on a hard cut to black mid-leap.
entries.prompt:
REFERENCES: Grandma = 95–100-year-old tiny hunched Korean grandmother (exact face, white bun with wooden pin, quilted indigo jeogori, grey knit scarf, plum skirt, gomusin shoes). Thug = very chubby greasy gangster (exact face with eyebrow scar, shiny black puffer jacket open, red-black floral silk shirt, gold chain, gold ring, black track pants, dirty white sneakers). Leopard = giant adult snow leopard (exact smoky grey-white coat, black rosettes, pale icy-blue eyes, long thick ringed tail). Hut = snowy thatched mountain tea hut on a hilltop with a small snowy yard, a footpath winding down the slope toward camera, and vast misty snow mountains on the right. Keep every identity, outfit, marking and set identical to refs throughout. Only these three beings exist in the scene.

PROP LOCKS: PROP-STICK = gnarled dark-brown wooden walking stick, always in Grandma's right hand, she leans on it every moment. PROP-BOWL = small round brown earthenware bowl of raw red meat chunks, always in Grandma's left hand, never dropped, never changes.

STAGING LOCK: Grandma stands in the snowy yard just in front of the Hut doorway, facing the footpath/camera, for the entire scene; she never walks away. Thug comes UP the footpath and stops 2 metres in front of her, his BACK to the footpath and slope. Leopard later comes up that SAME footpath from the slope behind Thug. Snow falling softly throughout.

LOOK: overcast winter daylight, cool blue-white snow, warm amber glow from the hut door, low saturation, low-to-mid contrast, filmic grain, soft halation. Ambient wind, crunching snow.

PACING: natural unhurried Korean delivery, short pauses between lines; never rushed.

0–6s: Opening aerial FPV drone shot: high above vast misty snow mountain ranges, gliding smoothly over frosted pine ridges and drifting clouds, then diving gracefully down the slope toward the tiny snow-covered Hut on the hilltop, slowing and pushing in to a medium shot of Grandma standing in the yard, leaning on PROP-STICK, holding PROP-BOWL.

6–11s: Grandma looks around the hills, calling sweetly and caringly, like to her own son:
Grandma (sing-song, tender): 「우리 아가~ 밥 먹자… 어디 갔니, 우리 아들~」
She calls once more, peering at the ridges, smiling.

11–17s: Heavy crunching steps. Thug stomps up the footpath, panting, chin raised, and stops in front of her.
Thug (rough, ruthless): 「할매, 이번 달 자릿세. 빨리 내놔.」
Grandma looks at him calmly and gives a small sly smirk.
Grandma (humble, gentle): 「잠깐만… 우리 고양이 밥 좀 주고. 그다음에 줄게.」

17–22s: Thug scoffs proudly, pinching his thumb and index finger close together in front of his face to mock something tiny.
Thug (angry, sarcastic): 「그 쪼끄만 망할 고양이 기다릴 시간 없어!」
Grandma's eyes shift past his shoulder to the slope; a happy, satisfied smile spreads.
Grandma (warm): 「아이고… 저기 오네.」

22–30s: Thug (annoyed): 「어디?」 He turns around toward the slope — and freezes; his face drains, eyes bulging, mouth falling open in shock. Reverse shot: the giant Leopard climbs up the snowy footpath toward them, heavy shoulders rolling, head low, snow on its fur, a deep low growl. Slow push-in on Leopard's face, icy-blue eyes locked on Thug. It opens its jaws and lets out a majestic thunderous roar, fangs bared, snow shaking off its whiskers, then explodes forward in a powerful leap toward camera — HARD CUT TO BLACK mid-leap.

NEGATIVE: no extra people, no extra animals, no small house cat, no attack gore, no Grandma walking without stick, no stick or bowl change, no Grandma moving away from the hut, no Thug standing beside Grandma, no leopard coming from inside the hut, no leopard marking change, no cartoon or CGI-game leopard, no face or outfit drift, no fast or rushed speech, no subtitles, no text.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 asset assignment: five sheet ghosts G1-G5 cross in front of a driver
entries.description: Image 1 = fixed opening frame with "No ghosts in the opening frame", Image 2 = look reference; ghosts labelled G1-G5 with an exact count, a fixed order, "Only G5 waves, exactly once", then a windshield jump scare. One fixed driver-POV angle.
entries.prompt:
Asset Assignment:
- Image 1: Fixed opening frame. Preserve the car interior, dashboard, windshield view, road, crosswalk, suburban houses, Halloween decorations, lighting, and camera perspective. No ghosts in the opening frame.
- Image 2: Visual reference only for four small sheet ghosts (G2–G5). G1 is a significantly larger ghost with the same white sheet aesthetic.

Scene: Create a photorealistic, Hollywood-style Halloween comedy in a 15-second, uninterrupted driver-POV night shot.

Timeline:
0–4s: The car approaches an empty zebra crossing and slows down. No ghosts are visible.

4–8s: Five sheet ghosts enter one by one from the left, floating across in single file. G1 is the large leader, followed by G2, G3, G4, and G5. The car stops before the crossing.

8–11s: The first four ghosts continue crossing without stopping. G5 pauses, turns toward the car, raises one hand, waves exactly once, and lowers its hand completely.

11–13.5s: G5 turns forward and hurries to catch up. All five ghosts finish crossing and disappear from the road naturally.

13.5–15s: Just when everything seems peaceful, G5 quickly drifts in from the right edge and stops right outside the front windshield, extremely close to the driver’s view. Its two black oval eyes stare through the glass. Add subtle reflections and realistic fabric details. End on a funny, unexpected jump-scare moment.

Visual Style: Premium photorealistic live action, realistic headlights, soft fabric movement, natural shadows, believable windshield reflections, consistent street perspective, and cinematic Halloween lighting.

Audio: Quiet nighttime ambience, subtle car interior sounds, and one short, playful surprise stinger. No dialogue, narration, music, or exaggerated cartoon effects.

Strict Constraints: One fixed camera angle, no cuts or zooms. Exactly five ghosts. Maintain the order G1 → G2 → G3 → G4 → G5. No teleportation, duplication, flickering, or overlapping. Only G5 waves, exactly once. All five ghosts must finish crossing before G5’s final windshield surprise. Only G5 appears at the end.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 slapstick: a sleeping night watchwoman defeats five thieves
entries.description: Six timecoded shots of sleep-fighting gags with short muttered lines ("Too slow…", "Five more minutes", "Called it") and a reference-image identity lock; "exaggerated but harmless physical gags".
entries.prompt:
Create a cinematic, ultra-realistic slapstick comedy scene. The watchwoman’s face and outfit must match the reference image throughout.

Shot 1 (0–3s): At a warehouse entrance, a night watchwoman sleeps deeply in a chair, feet on a crate, snoring with a half-eaten bag of chips on her lap. Five thieves sneak in, smirking at her.

Shot 2 (3–8s): The thieves try passing her, but her unconscious movements effortlessly clothesline one, trip another into crates, and send a third crashing into a shelf. She keeps eating chips and sleepily mutters, “Too slow…”

Shot 3 (8–13s): The remaining thieves nervously huddle before the leader charges her. Without opening her eyes, she elbows him in the stomach, mumbling, “Five more minutes.” He collapses beside the others.

Shot 4 (13–18s): The last thief attempts to escape, but her outstretched leg trips him into boxes. All five thieves lie scattered across the warehouse while she finishes her chips, tosses the empty bag perfectly into a trash can, and uses one thief as a footrest.

Shot 5 (18–23s): Police sirens approach. She briefly opens one eye, surveys the defeated thieves with a deadpan expression, mutters, “Called it,” and immediately falls back asleep. Her drool resumes as she snores.

Shot 6 (23–30s): Police rush in, find the thieves defeated, and stare at the sleeping watchwoman in disbelief. An officer tries waking her, but she lazily swats his hand away. The final close-up reveals a fresh bag of chips mysteriously resting in her lap as she smiles peacefully in her sleep.

Style: Fast-paced slapstick comedy, exaggerated but harmless physical gags, expressive reactions, consistent character appearance, smooth shot transitions, cinematic warehouse lighting, impeccable comedic timing, and a satisfying punchline.

entries.title: FLUX 3: two astronauts, Spanish then French, tied to suit colours
entries.description: "Give each speaker a language": visible roles (orange-suited / blue-suited astronaut) bind each line and language to a person; short separate turns, no overlap; the roof opens on the last word.
entries.prompt: One continuous unbroken real-time ten-second cinematic shot inside an orbital greenhouse during a meteor shower. Medium two-shot: an astronaut in an orange work suit steadies a glowing irrigation valve on the left while an astronaut in a blue work suit reaches for the petal-shaped roof controls on the right. The orange-suited astronaut speaks first in Spanish, practical and excited: "Las raíces están listas." After she finishes, the blue-suited astronaut replies in French, smiling with quiet wonder: "Alors, ouvrons le ciel." Keep the speakers distinct, the turns short and separate, with no overlap and no other speech. As the French line ends, the glass roof petals open and meteor light sweeps across rows of floating plants. Audio: soft ventilation, water moving through transparent pipes, roof servos, faint radio texture, and distant muted meteor impacts; no music. No on-screen text, no subtitles.

A young woman in her late twenties wearing a deep crimson wool peacoat, hands tucked in the coat pockets, breath faintly visible in the cold air.

Walks briskly down a rain-slicked Manhattan side street at night, her boots clicking on wet asphalt, the camera tracking smoothly alongside her at her own pace.

Rain-slicked Manhattan side street, night. Neon storefront signs, shallow puddles, scattered drifting steam from a manhole cover behind her.

Steady tracking shot, 35mm telephoto, shallow depth of field, sharp on her face, soft bokeh background.

Warm amber backlight skimming her shoulder, cool blue ambient filling the shadows, neon pink and cyan reflections in the puddles.
## Mood
Cinematic, intimate, contemplative.
