Create a breathtaking, ultra-photorealistic luxury bridal fashion film featuring an extraordinarily beautiful blonde bride wearing an intricately embroidered light green couture wedding gown and a magnificent cathedral-length veil.

The bride poses gracefully throughout the perfectly manicured gardens of a grand historic European castle. The film combines intimate beauty portraits, extreme macro shots of exquisite bridal craftsmanship, majestic architectural compositions, and elegant slow cinematic camera movements.

The atmosphere is ethereal, regal, romantic, expensive, and timeless, resembling a high-end European bridal couture campaign.

MAIN CHARACTER — STRICT IDENTITY CONSISTENCY

A stunning 24-year-old European woman @dp with delicate, symmetrical facial features, luminous fair skin, naturally rosy cheeks, striking pale-blue eyes, softly arched eyebrows, a slender straight nose, and naturally full pink lips. blush on her cheeks.

Her long golden-blonde hair is styled in an elegant, slightly loose bridal updo, with delicate wisps framing her cheeks and temples.

Her expression is serene, sophisticated, mysterious, and quietly confident.

Skin realism: Visible natural pores, subtle freckles, realistic skin translucency, natural peach fuzz, and gentle imperfections. Absolutely no plastic skin, excessive smoothing, porcelain appearance, or artificial CGI beauty.

Maintain exactly the same face, eye color, hairstyle, body proportions, and bridal outfit across every shot.

BRIDAL GOWN — STRICT WARDROBE CONSISTENCY

Bodice details:

Structured, fitted corset silhouette with a romantic sweetheart neckline.

Exquisite sheer ivory lace extending across the shoulders and arms.

Delicate off-shoulder illusion neckline.

Intricate floral embroidery and ornate lace appliqués.

Hundreds of tiny pearls, translucent crystals, and hand-sewn beads.

Elaborate symmetrical pearl chains draped across the bust.

A central teardrop-shaped pearl ornament.

Fine silver-thread embroidery and delicate floral motifs.

ENVIRONMENT

A magnificent historic European stone castle with Gothic Revival architecture, imposing towers, ornate windows, crenellated rooftops, grand terraces, and weathered limestone façades.

The castle is surrounded by:

Beautifully maintained formal English gardens.

Perfectly sculpted geometric hedges.

Tall conical topiary trees.

White blooming roses.

Ancient stone balustrades.

Ornamental stone urns and sculptures.

A large reflective ornamental pool.

Symmetrical gravel pathways.

Lighting: Warm late-afternoon golden-hour sunlight coming from behind and beside the bride, creating beautiful rim lighting around her blonde hair, translucent lace sleeves, and enormous veil.

00:00–00:01.2 — ANCIENT GARDEN DETAIL

Camera slowly slides sideways with shallow depth of field.

00:01.2–00:02.5 — THE BRIDE'S REVEAL

Cut to a medium portrait shot of the blonde bride standing gracefully beside tall sculpted hedges.

Her body is turned slightly sideways while her face turns toward the camera.

The sunlight illuminates the edges of her blonde hair, delicate veil, and lace sleeves.

She maintains a calm, regal expression.

00:02.5–00:03.5 — COUTURE MACRO DETAIL

Reveal the intricate pearl chains, symmetrical embroidery, delicate lace textures, tiny crystals, and central teardrop pearl ornament.

00:03.5–00:05.0 — THE CASTLE REFLECTION

The bride stands elegantly beside the large reflective pool, with the enormous historic castle filling the background.

The water reflects the castle architecture and soft golden sky.

Camera slowly tracks sideways, emphasizing the grand scale of the location and the flowing bridal silhouette.

00:05.0–00:06.5 — THE FLOWING VEIL

00:12.0–00:13.5 — THE FINAL BEAUTY CLOSE-UP

Her striking blue eyes, natural rosy cheeks, softly parted lips, and delicate blonde hair strands are sharply detailed.

The bride is centered in the frame beside the reflective pool.

Her magnificent cathedral-length veil stretches several meters sideways and backward, gracefully floating in the golden-hour breeze.

The castle towers rise dramatically behind her, creating an extraordinary royal bridal portrait.

Camera: ARRI Alexa 35, full-frame cinematic lens simulation.

Lenses: 85mm portrait lens for facial close-ups, 100mm macro for embroidery, 35mm for medium fashion shots, and 24mm for castle establishing shots.

Color grading: Soft ivory whites, warm champagne highlights, natural golden skin tones, muted botanical greens, pale limestone colors, and subtle cinematic film grain.

Motion: Natural human movements, realistic fabric physics, physically accurate veil movement, gentle breeze, no artificial slow-motion distortions.

Editing: Elegant cinematic cuts, carefully timed fashion-film pacing, no aggressive transitions.

AUDIO DIRECTION

A luxurious, romantic instrumental soundtrack featuring delicate piano, soft orchestral strings, and gentle cinematic swells.

Subtle ambient sounds of the garden breeze, distant birds, and delicate fabric movement.

No dialogue, no voiceover.

NEGATIVE PROMPT

Cartoon, anime, illustration, artificial CGI, video-game graphics, plastic skin, porcelain face, excessive beauty filters, unnatural facial proportions, inconsistent character identity, changing gown design, missing pearl embellishments, distorted lace patterns, changing veil length, unnatural fabric physics, stiff body movements, deformed hands, extra fingers, distorted architecture, warped castle towers, excessive lens flare, overexposed white dress, unrealistic wind, flickering embroidery, inconsistent lighting, low-resolution textures, excessive camera shake, artificial background blur, subtitles, text overlays, logos, watermarks.

FINAL CREATIVE DIRECTION: Every frame should look like an expensive international bridal couture campaign photographed at a historic European castle. Prioritize extraordinary facial realism, intricate wedding-gown craftsmanship, beautiful golden-hour light, grand architectural compositions, and breathtaking cathedral-veil movement.

entries.prompt:
20 seconds, 16:9, high-end cinematic suspense short film, realistic cinematography, 35mm film look, realistic lighting and physical movement.

Use @Image 1 as the only female protagonist throughout the entire film, keeping her face, blonde hair, body shape, and brick-red silk dressing gown completely consistent. Use @Image 2 as the only private jet cabin and @Image 3 as the only cockpit. The character, aircraft, and spaces must remain consistent throughout. No additional characters, duplicate characters, deformation, or disappearance.

【0–2.5 seconds】

The shot begins with movement already in progress: a luxurious private jet cabin with symmetrical composition along the central axis. The female protagonist walks quickly forward alone along the central aisle, looking natural but slightly alert. The camera smoothly tracks backward, maintaining distance from her. The cabin is illuminated by stable, warm golden artificial lighting, appearing bright, warm, and luxurious. Outside the windows are gloomy blue-gray clouds, with no direct sunlight.

As she walks forward, the cabin ceiling lights and wall lights suddenly begin flickering continuously. The entire cabin alternates between bright and dim due to the electrical malfunction, causing the woman's face and the seats to repeatedly shift between light and shadow. She immediately stops walking and looks up at the lights, her expression instantly becoming alert.

The next moment, the aircraft suddenly jolts violently. Inertia throws her body forward, causing her to stumble one step. She immediately reaches out and grabs the seat beside her. A transparent glass tumbler on the table responds to the aircraft's movement with realistic inertia, sliding across the tabletop toward the edge before naturally falling off and shattering. The glass must maintain continuous, physically realistic movement, without floating, teleporting, or suddenly disappearing.

Hearing the abnormal loud noise, the woman immediately looks toward the cockpit, realizing something is wrong. As the aircraft experiences its first violent shake, the camera suddenly accelerates backward, instantly establishing a strong sense of impact.

【2.5–4.5 seconds】

The aircraft violently loses control again, and the cabin suddenly tilts to one side. The woman immediately turns and rushes toward the cockpit, but after running only a few steps, a violent lateral jolt strikes without warning. She loses her footing, her body is thrown sideways, and she crashes heavily onto the aisle floor.

She does not stop. She immediately reaches out and grabs the base of the nearest seat, trying to get back up, but the aircraft tilts again, throwing her back down through inertia. The camera rapidly tracks backward with slight shaking, continuously following her struggle.

【4.5–7.5 seconds】

Realizing she can no longer stand normally, the woman immediately switches to crawling along the floor toward the cockpit. She alternately grips the bases and armrests of the seats on both sides with her hands, struggling to move forward while being pulled and thrown around by the aircraft's continuous shaking.

A violent jolt makes her slide backward a short distance. She grips the seat tightly to stabilize herself, then continues forward. The aircraft briefly returns to a level position. She immediately pushes herself up, staggers forward, rushes to the cockpit door, and forcefully pushes it open.

The camera follows rapidly from behind her at a low angle, producing realistic handheld shake as she crawls, gets up, and sprints. The cockpit doorframe quickly sweeps across the frame and completely obscures the camera, creating a seamless spatial transition through occlusion rather than using a conventional hard cut.

【7.5–10 seconds】

The camera seamlessly enters the cockpit from behind the door, following the woman from behind. She collapses into the left pilot's seat and grips the control yoke tightly with both hands.

The cockpit combines warm artificial lighting with the cold blue environment outside. Churning black thunderstorm clouds fill the windshield. Instrument warning lights begin flashing. She pulls the control yoke sharply, trying to control the aircraft, but the plane continues tilting violently.

The camera rapidly pushes in from over her shoulder, briefly entering her point of view: thunderstorm clouds rush closer at high speed as the aircraft shakes violently.

【10–14 seconds】

Cut to a close external aerial shot of the aircraft.

The same private jet suddenly loses altitude, and its nose begins pointing noticeably downward. The camera tracks parallel to the aircraft, clearly capturing the complete progression from an uncontrolled tilt into a steep dive.

The aircraft continues descending at high speed, with the dive angle becoming increasingly steep. The wings shake violently in the powerful airflow, and the fuselage visibly jolts up and down. Do not make the aircraft suddenly disappear or crash instantaneously.

Keep the entire aircraft visible in the frame while slightly tracking downward, allowing the audience to clearly feel that the plane is rapidly falling. The thunderstorm clouds remain in the distance as a dark background, with occasional lightning flashes across the sky, but the aircraft must remain clearly visible and must not enter the clouds.

The main focus of this section is to convey realistic high-speed loss of control and a strong sense of vertical descent.

【14–20 seconds】

Instantly return to the cockpit.

Red emergency warning lights continue flashing, with red light repeatedly sweeping across the woman's face. The light fixtures remain intact, with no explosions, shattering, or exaggerated visual effects.

Extreme close-up of her face: her hair is disheveled, her breathing is rapid, and her expression gradually changes from panic to genuine despair. She desperately pulls the control yoke, but the aircraft still does not regain control.

She finally realizes that the aircraft is continuing to descend and that she can no longer save it. She stares forward, briefly losing focus, as all hope disappears from her eyes.

Amid the violent shaking, she screams one desperate “NO!” The scream continues and gradually becomes uncontrollable. The red warning lights repeatedly sweep across her face, and her hair moves slightly with the shaking. She keeps looking forward, unable to do anything, forced to watch helplessly as the aircraft continues descending.

For the final approximately 2 seconds, hold on an extreme close-up of her desperate, terrified face. Let the scream end naturally, then cut off abruptly.

Sound: Roaring engines, continuous electrical malfunction sounds, aircraft turbulence, the glass tumbler sliding and shattering, hurried footsteps, rushing airflow, instrument warning alarms, and the woman's rapid breathing and sustained desperate screaming. No subtitles, text, or logos.

Core requirements: The female protagonist must be moving naturally from the very first frame. Do not leave her standing still and staring for a long time. When the malfunction begins, she must react immediately and appropriately to the situation. entries.prompt: One continuous shot. The camera steadily follows a person in a black coat (refer to Image 1) moving from left to right through six connected rooms, each with a different color palette and atmosphere. Every room has the same structure: white walls, light herringbone wood flooring, French double floor-to-ceiling windows, and white sheer curtains, based on Image 2, but the view outside and the interior atmosphere are completely different. entries.prompt:
Photorealistic live action blockbuster, shot on 65mm IMAX, humid rainforest atmosphere, mist and water droplets on lenses, natural sunlight through haze, kinetic aerial camera. Color grade: deep emerald greens, soft gold sunlight, gray-white mist.  
A colossal praying mantis with an emerald armored body, leaf-like wings, spiked forelegs and glistening compound eyes. A military helicopter with a crew flying over the rainforest.  
SHOT 1: Interior shot, 28mm lens, inside the helicopter cockpit, the pilot banks over the canopy, mist streaking across the windshield, a green shape shifting in the trees ahead.  
SHOT 2: Wide shot matching the reference image, the mantis rises out of the canopy, trees sliding off its back, birds exploding into flight, its head rotating toward the helicopter.

SHOT 4: Slow motion wide shot, 20mm lens, the mantis strikes with its spiked forelegs, the helicopter swerving at the last instant, rotor wash blasting leaves and mist into a vortex.  
SHOT 5: Aerial pull-back, 16mm lens, the helicopter escapes low over the river as the mantis spreads its wings with a loud buzzing hum, hovering above the jungle in the golden haze.  
Rotor thump, radio chatter, jungle birds and insects, cracking branches, a clicking chitinous sound, a deafening buzz of wings, a gust of rotor wind, tense percussion and brass.

GETTING READY FOR HER FIRST JOB INTERVIEW

Create an ultra-realistic personal vlog filmed by a friend using a consumer MiniDV camcorder in South Korea in 2003. A young Korean woman nervously prepares for her first job interview in her modest bedroom, from choosing her outfit to rushing out the door.

She compares two cardigans against her interview clothes, hesitates, chooses the darker one, and gives the camera a nervous smile. A wooden desk, paper calendar, and handwritten interview note establish the year.

SCENE 2 — IRONING (5–10s)

She carefully irons her blouse, struggles briefly with a sleeve, smooths it out, and checks the collar. A corded telephone and household calendar appear in the background. The iron stays safely on the board when not in use.

SCENE 4 — DOCUMENTS (15–20s)

She organizes her résumé and application papers into a folder. One page falls; she retrieves it and puts it back. Seeing the clock, she places the folder in her shoulder bag and checks for her purse and keys.

SCENE 5 — FINAL CHECK (20–26s)

She smooths her blouse, adjusts her cardigan, fixes her collar, and tucks back loose hair. After attempting a confident smile, she notices the time and grabs her bag in a hurry.

SCENE 6 — DEPARTURE (26–30s)

She hurries to the door, checks her keys, slips into her black shoes, and gives the camera one last nervous smile. The camera follows her into the hallway before an abrupt recording cut.

VISUAL STYLE & SOUND

Authentic early-2000s MiniDV footage: soft SD detail, mild video noise, imperfect handheld framing, autofocus hunting, accidental zooms, and brief exposure shifts. Use natural lighting, realistic colors, and period-appropriate Korean apartment interiors. Include fabric rustling, ironing, paper shuffling, faint clock ticking, footsteps, jingling keys, and the door opening. Dialogue is quiet, natural Korean speech.

Avoid modern technology, cinematic grading, fake VHS overlays, exaggerated acting, face morphing, duplicated fingers, teleportation, instant outfit changes, and background music.

entries.prompt:
Create one ultra-realistic cinematic live-action video set in Japan in 2003–2004. The entire story must be shown in a clear chronological sequence with smooth transitions. Do not skip any important action. The same adult Japanese woman and the same adult Japanese man must remain consistent from beginning to end.

SCENE 1 — WALKING ON THE STREET

A Japanese woman walks along a quiet early-2000s Japanese neighborhood street during the daytime. She passes small shops, bicycles, older Japanese cars, utility poles, and period-correct storefronts. The camera follows her naturally from the front and side.

SCENE 2 — THE PHOTOS DROP

A few meters ahead, a Japanese man walks while carrying a small photo folder containing several printed photographs. The folder accidentally opens. The photographs fall onto the pavement.

SCENE 3 — WIND SCATTERS THEM

Before he can collect them, a natural gust of wind catches the loose photographs. Several photos slide across the sidewalk while a few move toward the curb. The man immediately stops and turns around, looking worried.

SCENE 4 — WOMAN NOTICES

The woman sees the scattered photographs and the man's reaction. She immediately stops walking, looks at him, then looks down at the photographs and realizes he needs help.

SCENE 5 — BOTH START COLLECTING

The woman crouches down and begins collecting the photographs one by one. The man also kneels down and collects photographs from another part of the sidewalk. Show their hands picking up individual photos clearly.

SCENE 6 — PHOTO BLOWS AWAY

One photograph remains on the ground. A stronger gust pushes it farther along the sidewalk. The woman notices it immediately and follows it while the man continues collecting the others.

SCENE 7 — SHE SAVES THE LAST PHOTO

The photograph slides close to the curb. Before it can reach the road, the woman quickly but safely catches it with one hand. She looks relieved, then walks back toward the man holding the recovered photograph carefully.

SCENE 8 — COUNTING AND ARRANGING

Both return to the same spot. The woman places her collected photographs beside the man's. They carefully arrange all the recovered photos into one neat stack. The man counts them and realizes that the complete set has been recovered.

SCENE 9 — RECOGNIZING THE MEMORIES

The man slowly looks through the photographs. Close-up shots show printed family and personal memories from the early-2000s era. His worried expression changes into visible relief and emotion.

SCENE 10 — RETURNING THE PHOTOS

The woman gathers the photographs into one neat stack and gently hands them to the man. He accepts them with both hands and immediately places them safely back inside his photo folder.

SCENE 11 — THANK YOU

The man looks genuinely grateful. He gives the woman a respectful Japanese bow and a warm smile. She smiles back and gives a small polite nod, showing that she is happy she could help.

SCENE 12 — FINAL WALK AWAY

The man closes the photo folder securely and walks away with the photographs. The woman continues walking in the opposite direction. The camera slowly pulls back, showing the peaceful early-2000s Japanese street.

0-3s: Fast forward-moving shot just above the car roofs down East 42nd Street: chaotic gridlock of sedans, SUVs, vans, a box truck, a few yellow taxis, motorcycles and cyclists weaving between lanes, people crossing between bumpers, pushing in on CAR stuck in the middle lane beside a city bus. <horns> <idling engines> <a bike bell>

6-7s: Close on the centre screen: a finger of NORA presses a glowing round button. <a soft chime>
7-10s: Low at road level behind CAR beside the bus: the four nozzles flare white, gas blasts onto the asphalt, a cyclist swerves, and CAR rises straight up past the side of the bus, level, the Chrysler Building ahead. <thrusters spooling up into a roar>

Natural understated acting, small real expressions, no mugging. No dialogue. Raw unedited RED camera footage on a real New York street: very shaky handheld camera in every shot, flat overcast daylight, low contrast, low saturation, no grade, real skin. entries.prompt:
concept: 

a candid 30-second clip, 1080p, shot like a real home video. an ordinary summer afternoon with a young korean woman going about her day in a quiet residential area. no title card, no reference image.

the woman: 

early 20s, natural korean features, soft realistic skin with visible texture, barely any makeup. calm and warm, not performing for the camera. long dark hair pulled up into a loose, slightly messy high ponytail with a few strands falling out. pastel blue fitted short-sleeve top, loose cream pajama-style trousers, black sneakers, thin silver necklace. her look, hair and body proportions stay identical across every frame.

where it happens: 

an older, lived-in seoul neighborhood in warm afternoon light. tight concrete lanes, low houses, plant pots on the ground, parked bikes, utility poles, tangled overhead wires, laundry hung outside homes. a small corner shop and a few kids kicking a football nearby. nothing touristy, no logos, no ads, no recognizable brands. everything looks ordinary and worn-in.

how it’s shot: looks like a friend filmed it on a cheap consumer DV camcorder from the early 2000s. shaky handheld movement, slightly off framing, autofocus searching now and then, washed colors, visible compression, light grain, small accidental zooms, natural camera wobble. no gimbal, no drone, no stabilization, no cinematic lighting. imperfect on purpose.

what happens, in order:

she steps out of her front door holding a small reusable shopping bag, pulls the door shut, fixes her ponytail and gives a relaxed smile at the camera. she walks off down the narrow lane, breeze moving her hair. a few neighborhood kids with backpacks come the other way, she recognizes them and steps aside with a smile as they pass. one kid waves, she waves back, keeps walking, no dialogue. further down, kids are playing football in the street and the ball rolls to her feet. a child shouts “noona! kick it!” she stops it gently with her foot and taps it back to them with a little playful kick, then laughs and keeps going. the ball stays in the scene, it does not vanish or reset. she passes a small public tap, stops, cups some water in both hands, splashes it lightly on her face with her eyes closed, water dripping down her cheeks, wipes her face, fixes a loose strand, turns the tap off. she reaches the corner, the kids still playing behind her wave again, she turns, smiles, waves back, looks at the camera and says “have fun!” then walks on as the camera follows behind and she turns the corner. the clip cuts straight to black.

real location sound only. kids shouting and laughing, the football thudding on concrete, footsteps, birds, summer insects, bike bells, far-off scooters, faint neighborhood chatter, running water, breeze, and the small handling noises of the camera. no music, no voiceover. only the two spoken lines above.

Every slipping book must move continuously and visibly. No teleportation, floating, duplicated objects, distorted fingers, self-correcting stacks, stuttering, judder, frame skipping, slow motion, or excessive cinematic movement.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 "Try this Roadster": a 28 s seven-scene flying-car commercial with strict continuity locks
entries.description: A spec car ad for an invented car: a CONTINUITY block fixes the car (silver-white 4.5 m roadster with an "RDSTR" plate, yoke steering, exactly four thin downward vapour jets), then seven timed scenes, a full SFX list with no music, a long NEGATIVE line and a FINAL DIRECTIVE that forbids omitting, repeating or extending scenes.
entries.prompt:
Create a premium Hollywood-style live-action automotive commercial using realistic 35mm cinematography, natural lighting, organic grain, accurate reflections, dynamic tracking shots, and seamless transitions. Real-time speed only. No music.

CONTINUITY: Same silver-white 4.5m Roadster with “RDSTR” plate, identical woman and racer, and consistent locations. The racer wears a plain white-and-silver suit. The woman always drives from the left seat using the same yoke steering control. Every flight or hover uses exactly four thin white vapour jets pointing downward, without flames or glow. Preserve realistic physics, scale, shadows, and reflections.

SCENE 1 — INVITATION (0–7s): In an old stone courtyard, a low tracking shot reveals the Roadster. The man rests his hand on the roof: “Try this Roadster.” She replies, “It looks amazing!” She enters the left driver's seat, admires the yoke, and starts the car.

SCENE 2 — GETAWAY (7–8s): The Roadster accelerates past the camera on a leafy street with realistic tyre noise, rushing air, and brief tyre haze.

SCENE 3 — DESERT FLIGHT (8–12s): About 12 camels react to the approaching car; one groans. Four downward jets lift it above the dusty highway. It completes exactly one nose-to-tail barrel roll above the camels, returns upright, lands softly, and accelerates away.

SCENE 4 — LEAF MAGIC (12–15s): In an autumn suburb, the Roadster hovers beside a street sweeper in an orange safety vest. Four jets scatter dry leaves into a swirling cloud, revealing a clean sidewalk. The sweeper laughs; the woman smiles.

SCENE 5 — APPLE PICKING (15–17s): In a green orchard, the car hovers beside an apple tree. The woman reaches through the open window, picks a red apple, and smiles as the branch springs back.

SCENE 6 — THE DRIVER (17–18s): Interior side profile of the smiling woman driving one-handed with the yoke. Warm sunlight crosses her face, transitioning into sunset.

SCENE 7 — SKYBOUND (18–28s): On a runway, the Roadster accelerates beside an unbranded white private jet. Four jets activate as the car lifts through dust. Both climb toward golden clouds, but the Roadster pulls ahead. It passes through a dense cloud bank, emerges above glowing clouds, and flies among six to eight naturally moving white geese. A goose passes the open window as the woman smiles and waves. Finally, the Roadster tilts nose-down and begins descending through golden clouds as the camera pulls back to a vast cinematic sky. No text or logo.

SOUND: Natural dialogue, footsteps, door thunk, electric hum, tyre noise, wind, camel groan, vapour hiss, sand, landing, leaves, laughter, birdsong, apple snap, jet roar, and goose calls. No music.

NEGATIVE: No cartoon or artificial CGI appearance, flames, explosions, glowing exhaust, incorrect jets, changing car or plate, duplicate characters, wrong steering position, round steering wheel, logos, malformed anatomy, frozen animals, teleportation, blended scenes, extra rolls, flips, slow motion, captions, watermarks, or text.

FINAL DIRECTIVE: Exactly seven scenes, 28 seconds, original order, all essential actions preserved, consistent assets, realistic physics, natural dialogue, and seamless live-action transitions. Do not omit, repeat, or extend scenes.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 over a Cinema 4D blockout: helicopter liftoff over a burning city, rotor timing to the second
entries.description: Video-to-video direction from a colour-coded C4D animation (<<<Video1>>>) plus first-frame, helicopter and pilot reference sheets: an EXTERIOR ONLY camera rule, exact crew count, rotor spin-up timed by the second, and a long "Do not" list for the failure modes the creator hit.
entries.prompt:
A 30-second cinematic sequence, 24 fps, 1080p, in six shots. Photorealistic, gritty military realism, filmed on a real cinema camera.
EXTERIOR ONLY
Every shot is filmed from outside the helicopter, at the same distance and angle as <<<Video1>>> . The camera never enters the cockpit, never cuts to an interior view, and never moves closer to the pilots than <<<Video1>>> does. Never show the instrument panel, switches, displays, or controls. The pilots are only ever seen through the canopy glass from outside, as part of the full helicopter in frame. The whole helicopter is always visible in the frame.
REFERENCES
<<<Image1>>> is the first frame. Match its city, buildings, rooftop helipad, helicopter position, camera distance, and lighting exactly in the opening shot.
<<<Image2>>> is the helicopter reference sheet. Use it for the helicopter's exact design, panel details, decals, wear, vents, and proportions in every shot. Keep the design consistent. Do not redesign it.
<<<Image3>>> is the pilot reference sheet. Use it for both pilots' helmets, visors, flight suits, gloves, and gear.
<<<Video1>>> is the motion and camera reference. Follow its camera moves, timing, shot cuts, and the helicopter's movement exactly. Ignore its flat color-coded parts, plain sky, and placeholder boxes. Those are only guides. Replace them with the realistic materials from <<<Image2>>> and a real burning city. The two landing gear bay doors on the belly are two separate doors. They match the rest of the helicopter's hull exactly, in the same paint and wear as <<<Image2>>> . They never merge, touch, or fuse together.
CREW (every shot where the cockpit is visible)
There are always exactly TWO pilots in the cockpit, seated side by side, one in the left seat and one in the right seat. Both are helmeted, with visors down, and both match <<<Image3>>> . Both are visible through the canopy glass whenever the cockpit can be seen. Never show one pilot, an empty seat, or three pilots.
MAIN ROTOR (the large top propeller) - timed
0.0-3.0 s: The main rotor on top of the helicopter is completely motionless. The four blades hang perfectly still, drooping slightly, with no blur and no movement at all. This is critical. The top rotor must NOT be spinning at the start of the video.
3.0 s: The main rotor begins to turn, very slowly at first.
3.0-8.0 s: It steadily speeds up. By about 5 s the blades are clearly turning. By 8 s it is at full speed.
From 8 s to the end: the four main rotor blades sweep around the mast as a soft motion-blurred disc. The blades are real blades that spin around the hub. They are never a frame, a ring, or a shape sitting behind the helicopter. Do not make them vibrate or flicker in place.
SIDE FANS (spin) - timed
0.0-1.5 s: Both side fans are completely motionless.
1.5 s: Both side fans begin to turn, very slowly at first, and steadily speed up. They reach full speed by about 6.5 s.
From 6.5 s to the end of the video: both side fans spin continuously at full speed and never stop. They are always in motion in every shot. At this speed each fan is a soft, blurry, translucent spinning disc, with the individual blades smeared into a motion blur. The hub stays visible at the center. A fan must never look sharp, still, or frozen after it has started. Even when the fans are tilting, they keep spinning and stay blurred.
SIDE FAN TILT (timed)
The two side fans are mounted on the helicopter's sides and rotate on a pivot as the helicopter flies. Both fans always rotate together and match each other.
0-4 s: Both fans face forward. Their discs stand upright, like airplane propellers.
4-7 s: Both fans rotate 90 degrees, from facing forward to facing straight up. Their discs become flat and horizontal, like lift fans.
7-12.5 s: The fans stay facing straight up for liftoff.
12.5-18 s (during shot 4): Both fans rotate from facing up to a settled angle of about 45 degrees, tilted up and forward, for forward momentum.
18 s to the end: The fans hold that 45-degree angle through shots 5 and 6. They do not return to facing up or facing forward.
SHOT 1 (0-4 s): Establishing
Start exactly on <<<Image1>>> . The helicopter sits on the rooftop helipad, far from the camera, over a burning city. The side fans face forward. The main rotor on top is completely still for the first 3 seconds, with no spinning and no blur. The side fans are still for the first 1.5 seconds, then begin to turn slowly. At 3 s the main rotor begins to turn slowly. The camera drifts slowly forward with subtle handheld movement. Smoke and fire move constantly across the city.
SHOT 2 (4-8 s): Startup, front view
A low front view of the helicopter on the helipad. The main rotor, which started turning at 3 s, keeps speeding up toward full speed. The side fans keep speeding up as well and become blurred. The side fans visibly rotate from facing forward to facing straight up. Dust and debris blow across the roof. Through the clear canopy glass, with no color cast or tint, both helmeted pilots, one in each seat, are plainly visible from the front, and they move constantly throughout the shot. The near pilot reaches up and flips overhead switches, then lowers his hand to the center console and presses buttons in sequence, glancing down at the displays and back up. The far pilot checks the panel in front of him, taps a screen, then raises one hand and gives a short thumbs-up to the near pilot. The near pilot turns his helmet toward him and nods. Both pilots' helmets and shoulders keep turning and shifting as they work, and their gloved hands are always doing something. Cockpit display lights glow and flicker on their faces and gloves. The camera orbits slowly around the nose.
SHOT 3 (8-12 s): Liftoff from behind
The camera is behind the helicopter. The main rotor is at full speed. The side fans face straight up. It lifts off the helipad, rises, and the landing gear begins to tuck. The rotor wash whips smoke and dust. The camera rises with it. The side fans are spinning fast and blurred.
SHOT 4 (12-21 s): Gear up and flyover, one continuous shot
The camera starts low in front of and below the helicopter as it climbs. The side fans face straight up. The landing gear retracts into the body. The two landing gear bay doors on the belly swing open as two separate doors, one on each side, matching the rest of the hull. They stay apart, never touch, and swing closed again after the gear is up. As the helicopter climbs and flies directly over the camera, both side fans visibly rotate from facing straight up to a settled angle of about 45 degrees, tilted up and forward, and keep that angle for the rest of the shot. Then the camera whips around and tracks the helicopter as it continues across the burning city. The helicopter keeps flying away, getting smaller and farther from the camera until the cut at 21 s. The sky is clear of birds and flying objects. Only smoke, and slowly drifting ash and embers, are in the air. Follow <<<Video1>>> exactly. The side fans are spinning fast and blurred.
SHOT 5 (21-26 s): Front three-quarter, exterior
A wide exterior front three-quarter view of the helicopter in flight over the burning city. The side fans are at their 45-degree angle. The camera stays outside and flies alongside at the same distance as <<<Video1>>> for the whole shot. The entire helicopter, with its rotor disc, angled fans, and landing gear area, stays in frame, with the city below. The camera never pushes in to the cockpit and never cuts to an interior view. The canopy glass is perfectly clear and untinted, with no color cast, so both pilots are plainly visible through it. Through the canopy, both helmeted pilots, one in each seat, are visible from outside. They stay seated and are alert, scanning the devastation below. They slowly turn their helmets to look out the side windows, sweep their gaze across the burning city, and glance forward and then out the window again. Their movements are smooth and steady, with their bodies staying seated. Visors stay down. The side fans are spinning fast and blurred.
SHOT 6 (26-30 s): Flyaway
The helicopter flies away from the camera over the burning city and shrinks into the distance among the smoke. The side fans stay at their 45-degree angle. The side fans are spinning fast and blurred.
FIRE AND SMOKE (every shot)
The city has been under attack. Many buildings are on fire. Flames flicker, flare, and shift constantly. Thick black and gray smoke columns rise, billow, twist, and drift with the wind. Embers and ash float through the air. The fire and smoke never stay still and evolve continuously in every shot. Orange firelight reflects on the helicopter's metal body only. The canopy glass stays clear and colorless, with no orange tint.
CAMERA
Subtle handheld shake throughout. Cinematic lens, natural depth of field, slight film grain. Cuts happen exactly at 4, 8, 12, 21, and 26 seconds, matching <<<Video1>>> .
CONTINUITY
Same helicopter, same two pilots, same city, same lighting, and same time of day in every shot. The helicopter's design never changes. The helicopter faces the same direction as in <<<Video1>>> . The two fans always match each other.
DO NOT
Do not have the main rotor on top spinning, blurred, or moving during the first 3 seconds. It is completely still until 3 s.
Do not let the side fans stop, slow down, or freeze after 1.5 s. Once they start, they spin continuously until the end.
Do not show the side fan blades sharp or perfectly still after 6.5 s. They must always be blurred by their motion.
Do not show only one pilot, an empty seat, or more than two pilots. There are always exactly two pilots, one in each seat.
Do not show any interior or cockpit camera shot, in any shot, especially shot 5.
Do not move the camera closer to the cockpit than <<<Video1>>> does.
Do not show the instrument panel, switches, displays, or controls up close.
Do not cut away from the full helicopter in shot 5.
Do not add birds, flocks, flying animals, or flying debris in any shot. Nothing in the sky except smoke, ash, and embers, and nothing may pop in or disappear mid-shot.
Do not have the side fans turning during the first 1.5 seconds.
Do not leave the side fans facing forward or straight up after shot 4. They must settle at the 45-degree angle.
Do not merge, fuse, or melt the two landing gear bay doors together. They are two separate doors.
Do not paint the landing gear bay doors differently from the rest of the hull.
Do not redesign the helicopter or change its markings.
Do not use the flat colors, plain sky, or boxes from <<<Video1>>> .
Do not make the rotor blades vibrate in place, turn into a ring or frame, or freeze.
Do not make the canopy dark or opaque. Do not hide the pilots.
Do not tint the canopy glass orange or any other color. Do not let fire reflections color the glass.
Do not let the fire or smoke stay still or loop.
Do not add text, logos, or watermarks.

The demon cat lowers its head and growls menacingly at the camera. Just then, an owner's hand enters the frame and shakes a colorful candy wrapper. The terrifying monster instantly becomes curious.

The hand tosses a wrapped candy onto the porch. The moment it lands, a magical flash transforms the giant demon cat back into the original tiny black kitten.

End with the adorable kitten sitting innocently beside the candy, looking up with wide amber eyes as if nothing happened.

Visual style: Photorealistic cinematography, realistic feline anatomy, detailed fur, cinematic Halloween lighting, believable shadows, premium commercial quality, and subtle magical effects.

Audio: Natural nighttime ambience, one brief crystal bell chime for each transformation, a short feline growl, and a subtle candy-wrapper crinkle. No background music or narration.

Strict rules: One continuous camera shot, one kitten, consistent environment, smooth transformations, no extra limbs, no cuts, no cartoon effects, and no candy entering the cat's mouth. The candy must trigger the final transformation back to normal.

entries.prompt:
Video Style: Ultra-realistic 3D anthropomorphic animals, adorable Halloween costumes, energetic synchronized dancing, whimsical fantasy atmosphere, vibrant autumn colors, cinematic animation, realistic fur textures, smooth character movements, 9:16 vertical format, 4K quality.

SETTING:

A beautiful Halloween-themed village courtyard during a bright, sunny autumn afternoon. A magnificent Victorian haunted mansion stands in the background, decorated with glowing jack-o'-lanterns, carved pumpkins, hanging lanterns, cobwebs, spooky ornaments, and Halloween decorations. Tall maple trees with brilliant orange, golden-yellow, and crimson-red leaves surround the courtyard. Fallen autumn leaves cover the cobblestone pathway. A vivid blue sky with fluffy white clouds creates a cheerful Halloween atmosphere.

MAIN CHARACTERS:

Five adorable anthropomorphic cats and one large anthropomorphic tiger, all standing upright on their hind legs.

Witch Cat: A fluffy black-and-white cat wearing a pointed black witch hat, a purple witch dress, and a flowing purple cape.

Ghost Cat: An adorable fluffy white cat wearing a flowing white ghost costume with a cute ghost hood and tiny black bow tie.

Skeleton Cat: A fluffy black-and-white cat wearing a black skeleton jumpsuit featuring white bones and a small black Halloween hat.

Pumpkin Cat: A chubby orange tabby cat wearing a bright orange pumpkin costume with a carved jack-o'-lantern face and a small green pumpkin-stem hat.

Frankenstein Tiger: A large, realistic orange-and-black striped tiger standing upright like a human, wearing a green Frankenstein-style monster headpiece, a long dark-green Victorian coat, a purple waistcoat, and dark trousers.

All characters have realistic animal faces, expressive eyes, detailed fluffy fur, and adorable personalities.

SCENE 1 (0–5 seconds): GROUP DANCE INTRO

The camera opens with a wide cinematic shot of the Halloween courtyard.

Four adorable costumed cats stand in the foreground while the giant Frankenstein tiger stands behind them.

All characters begin dancing together to a playful, upbeat Halloween rhythm.

The cats bounce on their hind legs, swing their little paws, wiggle their bodies, and move their heads in perfect synchronization.

The Frankenstein tiger performs exaggerated, funny dance moves behind them.

The camera slowly pushes forward.

SCENE 2 (5–10 seconds): CUTE CAT CLOSE-UPS

A quick transition reveals the fluffy white ghost cat and the black skeleton cat dancing side by side.

Both cats face the camera, raise their front paws near their faces, and perform matching playful paw gestures.

Their costumes bounce naturally as they move.

The ghost cat tilts its head adorably while the skeleton cat gives a confident little pose.

Smooth camera tracking, realistic fur movement, cheerful expressions.

SCENE 3 (10–15 seconds): GROUP DANCE FROM BEHIND

The camera moves behind the dancing cats.

The witch cat's purple cape sways dramatically, the ghost cat's white costume flutters, and the skeleton cat wiggles its hips.

The cats perform synchronized side steps toward the Frankenstein tiger.

The tiger dances enthusiastically in front of the haunted mansion.

Autumn leaves scatter gently across the cobblestones.

SCENE 4 (15–20 seconds): FRANKENSTEIN TIGER SOLO

A medium close-up focuses on the giant Frankenstein tiger.

The tiger performs a hilarious solo dance, crossing its furry arms over its chest, swinging its shoulders, moving its paws rhythmically, and nodding its head.

Its long green coat sways naturally.

The tiger maintains a serious, comical facial expression while dancing.

The camera gently zooms closer, emphasizing the tiger's expressive face and detailed striped fur.

SCENE 5 (20–25 seconds): PUMPKIN CAT TAKES CENTER STAGE

The adorable chubby orange pumpkin cat steps into the center of the courtyard.

It performs a funny bouncing dance, swinging its tiny paws from side to side.

The pumpkin costume jiggles with every movement.

The other cats dance around it while the Frankenstein tiger follows the rhythm in the background.

A quick, playful camera movement emphasizes the energetic choreography.

SCENE 6 (25–30 seconds): FINAL HALLOWEEN DANCE

All five characters gather together for a final synchronized Halloween dance.

The cats perform matching paw waves, little jumps, shoulder movements, and playful head tilts.

The Frankenstein tiger stands behind them, performing exaggerated monster-style dance gestures.

The camera alternates between a wide group shot and a close-up of the tiger.

The video ends with the Frankenstein tiger crossing its furry arms confidently while the cats strike adorable Halloween poses.

CAMERA & VISUAL QUALITY:

Photorealistic 3D animal animation, realistic fluffy fur, expressive animal faces, physically accurate costume movement, cinematic daylight, vibrant autumn colors, natural shadows, detailed Victorian architecture, smooth tracking shots, playful close-ups, energetic choreography, adorable character expressions.

AUDIO:

Upbeat, playful Halloween dance music with a catchy rhythm, funny spooky sound effects, light monster growls, cheerful cat meows, and synchronized dance beats.

IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS:

Maintain identical character appearances, costume designs, fur patterns, and proportions throughout every scene. All animals must remain upright on two hind legs while dancing. Dance movements must be smooth, rhythmic, and synchronized. No character morphing, no extra limbs, no costume changes, no distorted faces, no flickering, no text overlays, no subtitles, and no watermarks.

She stays almost still, gazing calmly to the left with a subtle head turn. Static locked-off camera with a very slight, slow push-in. entries.title: Seedance 2.5 penguin "Milo": a giant apple, one bark slab, a downhill sled ride and a doorway too small
entries.description: A 30 s 3D comedy built entirely on prop physics: every object is sized against the character (apple = torso plus head, bark = twice his length, doorway smaller than the apple), placed before the story starts ("Milo never tears it from a tree"), and given a sound for each contact. The character sheet "defines Milo's appearance only".
entries.prompt:
Create an exactly 30-second 3D animated adventure-comedy in 16:9 horizontal format. Use the attached Milo character sheet as the exact visual reference for Milo. Maintain his identical face, brown eyes, three-feather head tuft, charcoal-grey feathers, cream belly, muted golden neck patches, narrow curved dark beak, long thin flippers, tall pear-shaped proportions, oversized pinkish-grey webbed feet and overall silhouette throughout the entire video. The reference defines Milo’s appearance only.

The story takes place in one continuous sunny autumn forest-edge clearing. An old wild apple tree grows near the upper part of a broad gently sloping grassy hill. One enormous ripe glossy red apple is already lying naturally on the ground beneath the tree before Milo arrives. The apple is approximately the same height as Milo’s torso and head combined. It is far too heavy for him to lift but round enough that he can roll it by pushing. Several meters away lies exactly one naturally detached broad curved slab of tree bark. The bark is approximately twice Milo’s body length, shallowly concave like a natural tray, thick and rigid enough to keep its shape, and wide enough to support the giant apple with Milo sitting behind it. The bark was already detached before the story begins, and Milo never tears it from a tree. A clear grassy trail leads gently downhill from the apple tree. Near the bottom of the hill is one deep pile of loose dry orange and golden autumn leaves positioned directly across the trail. Immediately beyond and slightly beside that leaf pile is Milo’s small round forest shelter entrance built naturally into an earth bank. The entrance is visibly smaller than the giant apple. Keep the apple tree uphill and the shelter downhill for the entire video.

Use a premium photorealistic 3D CGI animated feature-film aesthetic with highly detailed soft penguin feathers, realistic bark, glossy apple skin, dry autumn leaves, lush vegetation, expressive character animation, cinematic warm daylight, vibrant natural colors and exaggerated physical-comedy timing. Maintain realistic gravity, friction, momentum, weight, collisions and object support underneath the stylized animation. Use warm sunny autumn daylight throughout with natural cinematic depth of field. There is no dialogue, no text, no subtitles, no logos, no HUD and no additional characters.

From 0:00 to 0:02, open with a wide low tracking shot. Milo suddenly bursts through a patch of low autumn plants and runs into the sunny clearing. His oversized webbed feet rapidly slap against the grass, his long flippers swing beside him and his three-feather tuft bounces slightly. Milo suddenly stops when he sees the enormous glossy red apple beneath the old tree. Warm sunlight reflects from its surface. Milo’s eyes widen, his beak opens slightly and his expression immediately becomes excited.

From 0:02 to 0:04, move into a medium frontal shot beside the apple. Milo inspects the enormous fruit, then crouches beside its lowest accessible side. He slides both long flippers underneath it as far as physically possible, bends his knees and tries to lift. The apple does not move. Milo strains harder while his oversized webbed feet begin slipping slightly backward through the grass, but the apple remains fully supported by the ground.

From 0:04 to 0:06, use a wide side shot. Milo makes one final enormous lifting effort. His flippers lose their grip against the smooth apple and he falls backward onto the grass. The apple stays completely stationary. Milo lies dazed for a brief moment, raises his head, looks at the apple and then scans the clearing. His eyes stop on the broad curved piece of detached bark lying nearby. He looks at the bark, then at the apple, then back at the bark. His expression changes as he gets an idea.

From 0:06 to 0:08, use a wide side tracking shot that clearly shows Milo’s full body, both webbed feet and the entire bark slab at the same time. Milo quickly runs to one narrow end of the bark and remains completely standing on the grass. He does not sit, stand, kneel or ride on the bark. Milo faces the bark, bends forward and grips the narrow end using both long flippers. Both oversized webbed feet stay firmly on the ground. Milo begins walking backward toward the apple, stepping backward with one foot and then the other. His feet press against the grass and provide the traction that moves his body backward. Because both flippers are gripping the bark, his backward movement pulls the bark across the ground toward him. Most of the bark remains continuously supported by and in contact with the grass. The bark never moves underneath Milo and Milo’s body never rests on it. He drags it all the way to the giant apple and releases it.

From 0:08 to 0:11, use one clear wide side shot showing Milo, the complete apple and the entire bark slab. Milo positions the bark flat on the grass immediately downhill from the apple with its shallow concave surface facing upward. One end lies close to the fruit. Milo walks around to the uphill side of the apple, places both flippers against it and pushes. His webbed feet remain firmly planted on the ground. The apple slowly rotates forward, first one quarter turn and then another, until it rolls directly onto the center of the curved bark slab. Milo immediately stops pushing. The apple settles naturally into the shallow concave center while the bark remains fully supported by the ground.

From 0:11 to 0:13.5, show a wide lateral view. Milo walks behind the loaded bark sled and places both long flippers firmly against its rear edge while both feet remain completely on the grass. He leans his pear-shaped body forward and pushes. The bark begins scraping slowly across the nearly flat ground. His feet visibly push backward against the grass with every step. Milo remains on the ground and does not ride the bark yet. The apple remains nested in the center and moves together with the bark as one loaded sled.

From 0:13.5 to 0:15.5, use a wide side shot clearly showing the ground transitioning from almost flat grass into a gentle downhill trail. Milo continues pushing from behind. The front half of the loaded bark reaches the downward slope. As more of the sled moves onto the incline, gravity begins pulling it forward. Milo notices that it is becoming easier to push. The bark gradually starts moving slightly faster than Milo’s walking pace. Milo removes his flippers from the rear edge and begins running directly behind it.

From 0:15.5 to 0:18, use a dynamic side tracking shot. The loaded bark continues sliding downhill at a moderate speed because of gravity. Milo runs behind it using his oversized webbed feet. He catches up while the sled is still moving slowly enough to board safely. Milo reaches forward and places both flippers over the rear side edges of the bark. He takes two quick running steps, places one webbed foot onto the rear portion of the bark, then the second foot, and immediately lowers his body. Milo sits securely behind the giant apple and grips the bark edges with both flippers. This is the first time in the entire video that Milo sits or rides on the bark.

From 0:18 to 0:21, use a wide cinematic tracking shot moving alongside the trail. The loaded bark sled continues sliding naturally down the gentle hill. Dry leaves scatter slightly underneath the front and side edges. The trail remains completely clear. The bark stays continuously in contact with the ground. The apple remains seated securely in the shallow concave center and does not roll independently. Milo sits directly behind it. At first he looks nervous and grips the bark tightly. After a moment, he realizes the ride is stable. His expression slowly changes from concern to excitement and a delighted smile appears.

From 0:21 to 0:23.5, move into a closer side tracking shot. The downhill trail becomes slightly steeper but remains smooth and safe, causing gravity to moderately increase the sled’s speed. Milo continues gripping the bark edges. His charcoal-grey feathers and three-feather tuft move gently in the rushing air. He looks forward and realizes everything appears under control. His confidence grows. Milo straightens his upper body slightly while remaining securely seated, pushes his chest forward and smiles proudly as though the entire ride was planned.

From 0:23.5 to 0:25.5, use a front-facing tracking shot moving backward downhill. Milo continues riding proudly behind the giant apple. He looks past the fruit toward the bottom of the hill. Camera pulls slightly wider and reveals the enormous deep pile of orange and golden autumn leaves directly across the trail. Beyond and slightly beside the pile is Milo’s small shelter entrance. Milo initially smiles when he sees home, but then notices how quickly the leaf pile is approaching. His expression changes immediately and he grips both sides of the bark more tightly.

From 0:25.5 to 0:27, use one uninterrupted wide side-profile shot. The loaded bark sled enters the deep pile of loose dry autumn leaves. The leaves create strong resistance and friction against the bark, causing the sled to rapidly but smoothly lose speed. A large soft burst of orange and golden leaves sprays outward. The bark remains flat against the ground and never flips. The giant apple stays inside the shallow center and does not launch forward. Milo naturally leans forward because of the deceleration but remains seated safely behind the apple. The sled comes to a complete stop inside the soft leaf pile. Nothing breaks.

From 0:27 to 0:28.5, use a medium shot beside the leaf pile. Milo climbs carefully off the stopped bark sled and steps onto the grass. He looks at the giant apple, then turns toward his nearby shelter entrance. His proud smile returns. Milo positions himself behind the apple, places both flippers against it and pushes. The apple rolls slowly off the bark with one controlled rotation and then another. Milo continues walking behind it and pushing it across the short flat patch of ground toward the shelter.

From 0:28.5 to 0:30, finish with a static frontal comedy shot facing the shelter entrance. The enormous red apple rolls directly toward the small round doorway. Its diameter is clearly larger than the opening. The curved sides of the apple contact the earth around both sides of the entrance and it stops with a low soft thud. Milo continues pushing for one brief moment but nothing moves. He stops, looks at the shelter entrance, looks at the enormous apple, looks back at the entrance, then slowly looks at the apple again. After one small silent beat, Milo calmly walks around the side of the fruit, sits comfortably on the grass, leans toward the apple and takes one enormous satisfied bite. His eyes close happily and he smiles. Cut to black.

Maintain strict Milo consistency throughout all 30 seconds. Never alter his facial structure, brown eyes, three-feather tuft, charcoal-grey feathers, cream belly, muted golden neck patches, dark curved beak, long thin flippers, oversized pinkish-grey webbed feet, pear-shaped body or overall silhouette.

There is exactly one giant red apple. It begins resting on the ground beneath the apple tree and remains the exact same fruit throughout the entire video. It never falls from the tree, teleports, duplicates or changes size. There is exactly one curved bark slab. It begins lying naturally on the grass and Milo physically moves it. The bark never moves by itself before Milo pushes it onto the visible downhill slope. It never floats, flies, flips, changes size, changes shape or behaves like fabric.

Before 0:15.5, Milo must never sit, stand, kneel, balance or ride on the bark. During the 0:06 to 0:08 dragging action, Milo remains entirely on the grass. Both webbed feet must remain clearly visible on the ground while he walks backward and pulls the bark using both flippers. Never depict Milo sitting on the same bark that he is trying to drag. During the apple-loading and pushing sequence, Milo also remains entirely on the ground. Milo boards the bark for the first time only from 0:15.5 onward after gravity has already started moving the loaded sled downhill.

When the apple is on the bark, its full weight remains physically supported by the concave bark surface. The apple never hovers or balances on invisible support. During the downhill ride, the apple stays in direct contact with the bark and does not independently roll ahead or backward. The loaded sled moves slowly across flat ground only while Milo physically pushes it. Continued motion and acceleration occur only once the sled reaches the visible downhill slope and gravity acts on it.

The leaf pile is already present before Milo reaches it and contains only loose dry leaves. There are no hidden rocks, logs or hard objects inside. The increasing friction and resistance of the leaves gradually stop the sled. Milo does not fly out, the bark does not flip and the apple does not launch forward.

The shelter entrance remains exactly the same size throughout the video and the apple remains exactly the same size. The ending works only because the apple was already wider than the doorway. The doorway never shrinks and the apple never grows.

Maintain one continuous uphill-to-downhill geography. The apple tree remains uphill and the shelter remains downhill. Do not mirror or reverse the environment between shots. Once Milo passes a location, it remains geographically behind him. No teleportation, object duplication, object regeneration, invisible supports, spontaneous acceleration, unexplained movement, additional animals or humans.

Use readable cinematic framing throughout. Use wide lateral views whenever physical cause and effect matters. During the bark-dragging sequence, keep Milo’s full body, both webbed feet and the entire bark visible at the same time. During the apple-loading action, clearly show the apple physically rolling onto the bark. During the loaded-sled push, clearly show Milo behind the bark with both feet on the ground. Clearly reveal the terrain becoming downhill before the sled begins moving independently. During boarding, show Milo running behind the sled and physically stepping onto it without hiding the transition. Keep the downhill direction consistent and never use camera rotation to fake sled movement.

Use a playful adventurous orchestral score throughout. Include rapid webbed-foot footsteps during Milo’s opening run, natural autumn forest ambience, soft wind through leaves, comedic effort sounds while he tries lifting the apple, a soft thump when he falls backward, realistic bark scraping over grass as he drags it, clear webbed footsteps during the dragging action, a low rolling sound as the apple moves onto the bark, heavier scraping as he pushes the loaded sled and gradually more adventurous music when the sled reaches the slope. Add rhythmic dry-leaf and bark-sliding sounds during the downhill ride, light wind rush as the speed increases and a triumphant musical feeling as Milo becomes confident. When the leaf pile appears, shift briefly into playful tension. Use a large soft rush and poof as the sled enters the leaves, followed by falling and settling leaf sounds. Add soft apple-rolling sounds near the shelter, a low thud when the apple contacts the doorway, a tiny pushing effort sound, then brief silence as Milo realizes the problem. Finish with one crisp apple bite and one tiny satisfied orchestral note before cutting to black.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 dragon catch: a CONTINUITY LOCK for screen direction, no teleporting and fewer, longer shots
entries.description: A 30 s live-action fantasy chase that opens with a mandatory CONTINUITY LOCK: the chase always moves left to right, the giant is always behind and above, every change of position is shown in continuous motion, and the camera uses fewer, longer motivated moves. Timed beats follow.
entries.prompt: Cinematic 16:9 live-action Hollywood fantasy action short film, 30 seconds, 30fps. Shot like a scene from a big-budget fantasy blockbuster: real actress, real mountain gorge location, photorealistic CGI dragons fully integrated into the plate. Shot on ARRI Alexa 65 with anamorphic lenses, epic scale, natural skin texture, real fabric and hair in strong wind, physically accurate fire, rock debris, mist and water spray. Late-afternoon golden sunlight cutting through mist, filmic color grade, subtle grain, natural motion blur. Intense, thrilling, then emotional and heartwarming. No cartoon, no animation, no Pixar or 3D-render look. No gore.  CONTINUITY LOCK (MANDATORY): - Screen direction never flips: the chase always moves from LEFT to RIGHT of frame. The giant dragon is always BEHIND (left of) and ABOVE her dragon, never in front. - No teleporting. Every change of position is shown on screen in continuous motion. No character can appear somewhere they were not seen moving to. - Fewer, longer shots. The camera follows the action with smooth motivated moves: tracking, drone follow, slow push-in. No random angle jumps. - She is always either on the bridge, falling, or seated on her dragon's back holding his neck spikes, and the transitions between these are shown fully. - Identical faces, outfit and dragon designs in every frame.  Characters: 1) A real young woman in her mid-20s with messy wavy blonde hair, thin round wire glasses, a cream linen blouse with rolled sleeves, a dark brown pinafore apron dress, and a small leather satchel full of herbs. Natural freckles, realistic skin, expressive brave face, believable acting. 2) HER DRAGON: a horse-sized real living dragon. Thick, textured white-cream scales with pink-magenta markings, a crest of soft pink flexible spikes, wide cream wings with pink-tinted membranes, wet glossy amber eyes with vertical pupils. Agile, fast, loyal, with real weight and mass. 3) THE GIANT: a wild dragon five times bigger than hers. Charcoal-black scales, jagged obsidian horns, tattered leathery wings, burning ember-orange eyes, smoke leaking between its teeth. Heavy, slow to turn, terrifying. Each keeps an identical design and scale in every shot.  Setting: A deep misty mountain gorge with a long old rope-and-plank bridge spanning it, a river far below, waterfalls on the cliffs, pine trees on the edges. Further along the gorge to the RIGHT, a narrow natural stone arch spans the canyon, just wide enough for her dragon.  0-3s (HOOK): Wide drone shot. She is halfway across the swaying rope bridge, herb satchel over her shoulder. A colossal black shadow rises out of the mist below the bridge. She freezes and looks down. The giant dragon's burning eyes open in the mist directly beneath her. 3-6s: The giant erupts upward through the mist and smashes through the middle of the bridge behind her. Planks explode into the air, ropes snap. Medium shot: the bridge splits and her half drops away under her feet. She grabs a rope with one hand, swinging, legs dangling over the drop. Her satchel falls; herbs scatter into the wind. 6-9s: Close-up on her hand slipping down the frayed rope, knuckles white. Far away on the RIGHT cliff edge, her dragon's head snaps toward the sound, eyes wide. He launches off the cliff, wings snapping open, diving toward her. 9-13s: The rope tears. She falls. One continuous falling drone shot: she tumbles down through mist and flying planks, hair and dress whipping. Her dragon dives into frame from the upper RIGHT, wings tucked, faster than her, passes underneath her, rolls, and she lands across his back. She scrambles to grab his neck spikes as his wings slam open and he pulls out of the dive just above the river, spray exploding off the water. 13-16s: Low tracking shot following them LEFT to RIGHT along the river at high speed. She clings to his neck, glasses crooked. Behind them on the LEFT and above, the giant dives after them, roaring, its huge wingbeats whipping the river into spray. 16-20s: The giant unleashes a massive blast of fire. Her dragon banks hard to the right and the fire scorches the cliff wall beside them, rock cracking and falling into the river. He weaves between falling boulders. Close-up: she looks back over her shoulder, terrified, then forward, and sees the narrow stone arch ahead. 20-23s: Wide shot. Her dragon folds his wings tight and shoots straight through the narrow stone arch with inches to spare, her hair brushing the rock. The giant, too big, slams its wings out and pulls up hard at the last second, its claws scraping the arch, chunks of stone falling. It roars in frustration, hovering, unable to follow. 23-26s: They burst out the other side of the arch into a wide sunlit valley and glide down toward a soft green meadow. Her dragon lands in a skidding run through the tall grass. Behind them, far away above the arch, the giant turns and flies away into the clouds. 26-30s: She slides down from his back and her legs give way; she sits in the grass, shaking, then laughing with relief. Her dragon lowers his big head to her, breathing hard. She throws her arms around his snout and presses her forehead to his, eyes closed. He purrs and gently curls his wing around her. Slow pull back to a wide golden shot: the two of them small in the meadow, the stone arch and the gorge behind them. Hold.  Style: Photorealistic Hollywood fantasy action blockbuster. Huge scale contrast between the two dragons, real wind and mist, real fire light on rock and water, golden sunlight through mist, cold misty blue in the gorge warming to golden in the meadow. No morphing, no extra limbs, no warped hands, stable glasses and face.  Audio: Quiet wind and creaking bridge ropes at the start, then a deep rumble and an earth-shaking roar. Splintering wood and snapping ropes, her scream, rushing wind during the fall, a heavy wing-boom on the catch, water spray, a huge fire blast, cracking rock. An epic orchestral score with drums and choir building through the chase, then a sudden release as they pass through the arch into soaring emotional strings. Her breathless laughter and her dragon's deep purr at the end.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 "When watermelons go wild": a 30 s single take from inside a car on a wet highway
entries.description: A dashcam-style phone video with realism rules: windshield raindrops, autofocus hunting and imperfect digital zoom; eight timed beats of physical cause and effect (rolling melons, a basket catch, a chain reaction, a harmless landing in cardboard boxes); no cuts and "no teleportation… or impossible trajectories".
entries.prompt:
30-SECOND VIDEO — 16:9

Create one continuous 30-second ultra-realistic smartphone video filmed from inside a moving car on a wet rural highway during daytime. Natural handheld shake, windshield raindrops, autofocus hunting, realistic motion blur, exposure shifts and imperfect digital zoom. No cuts.

0–4s — DISCOVERY The car approaches a stopped farm truck carrying enormous watermelons. Its rear gate suddenly swings open, and dozens of giant watermelons begin rolling onto the wet highway. The camera zooms toward the unfolding chaos.

4–8s — THE GIANT CATCH A huge, heavyset man in a yellow raincoat runs into view carrying an oversized empty laundry basket. He struggles to catch a massive rolling watermelon, which drops into the basket and nearly pulls him off balance.

8–12s — UNEXPECTED CRACK He places the watermelon on the road and attempts to crack it open by dropping another watermelon onto it. The fruit bursts apart, splashing juice and seeds across the asphalt. He slips slightly but regains his balance.

12–16s — DOMINO EFFECT Several loose watermelons roll downhill, collide with one another and bounce off the roadside barrier. Their chain reaction sends a giant watermelon bouncing toward a parked roadside fruit stall.

16–20s — FRUIT EXPLOSION The giant watermelon crashes into stacked melons, triggering a spectacular cascade of rolling fruit. The startled vendor jumps aside as melons tumble across the shoulder. The camera operator instinctively jerks the phone toward the commotion.

20–24s — THE UNLIKELY LAUNCH One enormous watermelon rolls beneath the man's feet. He steps onto it, loses his balance and is launched upward in a believable comedic tumble as the watermelon shoots away beneath him. His yellow raincoat flaps, and his sandals fly off separately.

24–27s — MID-AIR CHAOS The man travels forward in a realistic ballistic arc toward a slowly moving delivery van with its rear cargo doors open. The camera tilts and zooms shakily to follow him.

27–30s — PERFECT LANDING He lands harmlessly in a towering pile of soft empty cardboard boxes inside the van. The boxes collapse around him, the van rocks slightly, and the driver turns around in complete disbelief. One sandal drops onto the road behind the van.

AUDIO: Natural highway traffic, rain, truck gate rattling, heavy fruit rolling, watermelon impacts, splashing juice, cardboard crashing, rushing air and authentic surprised reactions. No music.

REALISM RULES: Maintain one uninterrupted take with continuous physical cause and effect. Realistic gravity, momentum, object weight and collision physics. No teleportation, instant movement, duplicated people, disappearing objects or impossible trajectories. Keep the comedy non-graphic and injury-free. No cinematic cuts, slow motion, subtitles, captions, text overlays, logos, watermarks or artificial CGI appearance.

15-second fast-paced cute clay-animation sketch. Use the exact character designs from the reference: the huge stern blue clay Samurai and the tiny elegant red Oni/Geisha. Handmade stop-motion clay aesthetic, expressive squash-and-stretch, playful physical comedy. No dialogue. No dead time.

0–4 sec: The Samurai dramatically draws his katana with exaggerated seriousness — SHIIING! He strikes an intimidating battle pose. The tiny Oni-Geisha looks completely unimpressed, casually pulls out a small red folding fan and THWACKS the flat side of his sword downward.

He quickly steps in front of her and performs an absurdly elaborate sequence of lightning-fast sword flourishes, sleeves and blue robe whipping around — WHOOSH, SWISH, SWISH! She effortlessly ducks each swing while continuing her tiny graceful walk without even looking at him.

8–12 sec: Frustrated, Samurai commits to one enormous overhead strike. Oni-Geisha simply takes one tiny step sideways. WHAM! His katana gets stuck deep in the clay floor. He pulls desperately; the sword refuses to move. His giant body stretches comically from the effort.

12–15 sec: Oni-Geisha calmly taps the sword handle once with her fan — TOK! The sword instantly pops free, launching Samurai backward into a ridiculous clay tumble. He lands sitting upright, stunned. Oni-Geisha gives him a tiny smug bow and snaps her fan open. End immediately on Samurai’s embarrassed glare.

Audio: energetic cute Japanese-inspired percussion and plucked-string music, tightly synchronized with the comedy; exaggerated clay footsteps, sword unsheathing, metallic swishes, fan thwacks, impact sounds and comedic pops. No speech, no vocals.

entries.prompt:
Create a 15-second cinematic action sequence for Seedance 2.5.
Aspect ratio: 16:9, landscape.
Photorealistic mechanical characters in realistic live-action surroundings.
Extremely fast aerial combat, precise weapon contacts, powerful impacts, and spectacular destruction.

PRIMARY VISUAL RULE — SPARK-FREE MECHANICAL COMBAT
Do not generate flying sparks or glowing particle trails anywhere in the sequence.
Show weapon contact through physical recoil, brief camera vibration, metallic sound, and a small cool-white daylight reflection confined to the contacting metal surfaces.
This reflection does not scatter, spray, or leave a trail.

All flying debris must look like solid manufactured material:
silver metal fragments, dark steel pieces, white ceramic chips, recognizable gears, brackets, and electronic components.
Fragments have hard edges, visible thickness, rigid rotation, and gravity-driven trajectories.
Avoid clouds of tiny luminous specks.

Keep destruction effects neutral in color.
No red, orange, yellow, pink, or brown particle effects.
No liquid-like jets, splashes, droplets, dripping, or wet textures.
Dust is pale gray, dry, thin, and slowly settling.

SETTING
Times Square, New York City, in bright midday daylight.
Giant LED billboards, tall commercial buildings, glass storefronts, projecting signs, maintenance platforms, streetlights, and broad intersecting streets.
Blue sky, strong natural sunlight, crisp shadows, and neutral daylight color grading.
The combat area is deserted.

The fighters repeatedly move between street level and several stories above the intersection.
Use walls, columns, billboard frameworks, and elevated platforms as physical rebound surfaces.
Keep the streets visible below during aerial exchanges.

Maintain consistent geography and accumulating damage.
Broken buildings, fallen signs, glass, craters, and rubble remain damaged throughout the sequence.

REFERENCE ASSIGNMENT

REFERENCE IMAGE 1 = A, THE CYBERNETIC ONI SAMURAI.
Preserve the reference silhouette and appearance: tall black horns, ivory-colored armored helmet, red electronic eye details, mechanical respirator, purple and acid-yellow armor, decorative chest plates, exposed machinery, hoses, heavy boots, and mechanical backpack.
The helmet and chest ornamentation are manufactured armor.
A carries two katana matching the reference.

A moves through explosive jumps, wall rebounds, rapid pivots, ballistic momentum, and physical combat.
A never teleports or transforms into mist.

REFERENCE IMAGE 2 = B, THE MECHANICAL REAPER.
Preserve the exact reference silhouette, proportions, color arrangement, markings, hanging fabric, chains, and enormous curved scythe with its suspended vessel.

B is an entirely mechanical construct.
The deer-skull-shaped face is an ivory-colored ceramic mask mounted over a metal head assembly.
