entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second ultra-realistic fictional personal home-video featuring a clearly adult Korean woman, age 28, enjoying an ordinary summer afternoon in an older Seoul residential neighborhood.

CHARACTER:
A fictional adult Korean woman, age 28, with long straight black hair tied casually in a low ponytail and a natural everyday appearance. She wears a bright coral-red crop top, relaxed high-waisted white denim shorts, simple casual sneakers, a small shoulder bag and a delicate bracelet. Bold colorful summer streetwear with a casual everyday feel. Keep the same adult character, hairstyle and outfit consistent throughout the entire video.

IMPORTANT VIDEO INSTRUCTION:
Every interaction must show the complete physical action clearly. Do not skip object handling. Whenever she buys or uses something, visibly show her reaching for the object, picking it up, holding it, exchanging money, receiving the object and physically carrying it afterward.

SCENE 1 — LEAVING HOME
She opens the front door of an older Seoul apartment building and steps outside. She pulls the door closed behind her, checks that it is shut, adjusts the strap of her small shoulder bag and walks through the metal gate into the narrow residential lane.

She notices the person filming, smiles naturally and continues walking.

SCENE 2 — SMALL NEIGHBORHOOD SHOP
She approaches a tiny old-fashioned neighborhood shop.

She opens the refrigerator door with her right hand, reaches inside and physically takes out one chilled bottled fruit drink. She holds the bottle clearly in front of her, looks at it briefly, then closes the refrigerator door.

She walks to the counter while holding the bottle. She opens her small shoulder bag, takes several coins out with one hand and places the coins directly into the shopkeeper's hand.

The shopkeeper gives her a small amount of change. She takes the change, puts it into her bag and keeps the bottled drink in her other hand.

She walks out of the shop carrying the drink.

SCENE 3 — FRUIT STAND
She reaches a small outdoor fruit stand.

She stops and looks over the fruit. She extends her hand toward the display, physically picks up one peach and lifts it to chest level. She turns the peach slightly in her hand and examines it.

She decides to buy it. While continuing to hold the peach, she reaches into her shoulder bag with her other hand, takes out several coins and hands them to the vendor.

The vendor accepts the coins and gives her a small paper bag. She takes the paper bag with one hand, places the peach inside it herself, closes the top of the bag and puts it carefully inside her canvas shopping bag.

She picks up her bag and continues walking.

SCENE 4 — OLD PHOTO BOOTH
She notices a small old-fashioned photo booth beside a neighborhood shop.

She walks toward it, pulls the curtain open with her hand and steps inside. She takes a small printed photograph from the machine, looks at the photograph and smiles.

She holds the photograph up briefly toward the camera, then puts it safely inside her shoulder bag.

She closes the curtain and walks back into the street.

SCENE 5 — BICYCLE VENDOR
She hears a bicycle bell and turns her head.

A bicycle vendor slowly rides past her. She steps to the side to let the bicycle pass, watches it continue down the lane and then takes the bottled drink from her hand.

She twists the bottle cap open, raises the bottle to her mouth and takes a natural drink. She lowers the bottle, closes the cap and puts the bottle into the side pocket of her shoulder bag.

SCENE 6 — OUTDOOR WATER TAP
She reaches an old outdoor water tap beside a residential building.

She places her shopping bag carefully on a nearby concrete ledge. She reaches toward the tap, turns the handle and visibly starts the water.

She places both hands underneath the running water, washes them briefly and then splashes a small amount of water onto her face.

She laughs naturally, wipes her face with the back of her hand, turns the tap off, picks up her shopping bag from the ledge and continues walking.

SCENE 7 — FINAL WALK
She walks slowly down a quiet sunlit residential lane carrying her shopping bag.

The camera follows behind her for a moment, then moves around to face her.

She stops briefly, reaches into her shopping bag and physically takes out the peach. She holds it in one hand, smiles toward the camera and takes one bite.

She laughs softly, gives a small wave with her free hand and says:

“Bye bye!”

She lowers the peach, turns around and walks away down the lane until she disappears around the corner.

CAMERA:
Authentic early-2000s consumer MiniDV/DV-camera footage recorded casually by a friend or family member.

Handheld camera shake, imperfect framing, occasional shaky walking movement, autofocus hunting, automatic exposure fluctuations, slightly blown highlights, soft digital detail, mild CCD noise, subtle compression artifacts, natural motion blur and occasional awkward zooms.

The camera operator should sometimes fail to perfectly center her, making the recording feel spontaneous and genuinely amateur.

VISUAL ENVIRONMENT:
Older Seoul residential neighborhood with weathered apartment buildings, narrow concrete lanes, utility cables, small local shops, old signs, parked bicycles, leafy trees, concrete walls and ordinary neighborhood clutter.

Natural summer daylight only.

AUDIO:
Authentic location sound only: footsteps, bicycle bells, refrigerator hum, shopkeeper conversations, coins, paper bags, distant traffic, birds, children playing, running water and light wind.

No music.
No narration.
No subtitles.
No text overlays.
No beauty filter.
No CGI.
No fantasy elements.
No slow motion.
No dramatic camera movements.
No professional commercial cinematography.
No polished advertising aesthetic.

The final footage should feel like a genuine forgotten personal MiniDV recording from the early 2000s, spontaneous, imperfect, casual and completely believable.

**0–2 seconds:** The cat starts in a relaxed, confident standing pose. It performs a smooth shoulder roll, subtle chest isolation, and controlled side-to-side hip movement while maintaining eye contact with the camera.

**2–4 seconds:** The cat executes clean, stylish footwork, stepping right and left while moving its arms rhythmically across the torso. Natural wrist movements, relaxed elbows, and controlled upper-body grooves.

entries.description: A 30 s practical-effects horror short: a man notices his carved pumpkin behaving strangely; the beats escalate in 5 s steps and the sound plan ends with "sudden silence before the final reveal". entries.prompt:
30 seconds | 16:9 | 4K Ultra HD | 30 FPS | Ultra-photorealistic live-action Halloween horror short.

A terrifying Halloween night unfolds on a rain-soaked wooden porch, where a real adult man discovers that his carved jack-o'-lantern is behaving strangely. With realistic human actors, practical effects, cinematic lighting, and authentic horror atmosphere, an ordinary Halloween decoration becomes something truly sinister.

0–5 seconds: A rain-soaked wooden porch glistens under dim nighttime lighting. A flickering jack-o'-lantern sits beside the front door. A man in a dark flannel shirt and jeans enters carrying Halloween decorations. Suddenly, he notices the pumpkin slowly expanding and contracting as if it were breathing.

5–12 seconds: The camera slowly pushes toward the pumpkin. Its jagged carved smile subtly widens before returning to normal. The internal candle flickers in sync with the movement. The man kneels cautiously as a faint, wet breathing sound emerges from inside.

12–21 seconds: The pumpkin's light abruptly goes out. Complete silence. The man switches on his phone flashlight, revealing two realistic human eyes deep inside the dark pumpkin, staring directly at him. Terrified, he recoils and drops his phone onto the wet wooden floor, leaving its flashlight beam tilted toward the pumpkin.

21–27 seconds: The man slowly reaches toward the pumpkin again. Before he can touch it, the jack-o'-lantern rotates several inches toward him on its own. Its carved smile remains perfectly still. Frozen with disbelief, he slowly backs toward the door.

27–30 seconds: Extreme close-up of the pumpkin. Its internal light suddenly switches back on. A tiny, fresh handprint gradually appears in condensation across its outer surface. Before the viewer can understand what has happened, the screen cuts instantly to black.

Production: Photorealistic live-action visuals, real human actors, consistent character identity, practical pumpkin movement, realistic condensation, natural rain, believable shadows, subtle handheld cinematography, shallow depth of field, cinematic horror lighting, and restrained color grading. Sound design includes rainfall, distant wind, wooden footsteps, soft breathing, subtle fabric movement, a low suspenseful musical rise, and sudden silence before the final reveal.

Negative prompt: No animation, cartoon visuals, CGI-looking characters, artificial environments, changing faces, inconsistent clothing, distorted anatomy, unrealistic pumpkin movement, exaggerated jump scares, gore, dialogue, narration, subtitles, text, logos, watermarks, black bars, or abrupt transitions before the final cut.

Photorealistic, high-budget cinematic action scene inside a modern urban subway car. A stylish young East Asian woman with long blonde hair, wearing a brown cropped hoodie and matching sweatpants, stands holding a ceiling hand strap. A man in a yellow bomber jacket attempts to snatch her luxury designer shoulder bag. Instantly reacting, the woman locks his arm in a swift martial arts joint-lock, sweeps his legs, and forces him down onto the train floor. As a second assailant wearing a dark green hoodie and black cap lunges forward, she dodges, delivers a lightning-fast high kick stopping millimeters from his nose, and leaves him paralyzed in fear. The subway passengers watch in stunned silence. High-contrast interior subway lighting, dynamic handheld camera movements, seamless motion blur, dramatic close-ups, crisp sound design, hyper-realistic physics, cinematic color grading, 4K resolution.
Detailed Shot-by-Shot Prompt Breakdown
Shot 1: The Setup and Attempted Theft
Framing and Camera: Medium shot, steady camera tracking inside a subway car.
Action: A stylish blonde woman in a brown lounge set stands near the center pole, holding a grab strap. A man in a yellow jacket discreetly reaches toward her luxury bag, reaching into it.
Lighting and Atmosphere: Cool fluorescent subway overhead lights, authentic train passenger atmosphere.
Shot 2: The Counter-Attack and Takedown
Framing and Camera: Close-up transitioning rapidly to a wide tracking action shot.
Action: The woman grabs the thief's wrist with precision, pivots her weight, sweeps his foot, and slams him flat onto the floor. She maintains a wrist-lock on his arm while looking up at the second attacker.
Visual FX: Dynamic motion blur, exaggerated impact physics, realistic clothing movement.
Shot 3: The High Kick and Standoff

Action: The second attacker in the dark green hoodie charges in. The woman swiftly executes an elevated high kick, stopping the sole of her shoe precisely in front of his nose. The attacker's eyes widen in intense shock and terror.
Focus and Depth: Shallow depth of field focusing sharply on the attacker's reaction and the shoe, blurring the background passengers.
Shot 4: The Exit
Framing and Camera: Wide shot facing the subway doors.
Action: The woman coolly adjusts her hoodie, slings her bag back over her shoulder, and walks out through the opening subway doors, leaving the two attackers defeated on the floor.

entries.prompt:
Create a 10-second ultra-photorealistic cinematic video in 16:9 widescreen, recreating Newton’s famous apple discovery with precise timing, expressive acting, realistic physics, and spectacular golden scientific visual effects.

Character: A beautiful young woman with a unique face, natural skin texture, and an elegant hairstyle. She wears a historically inspired European outfit consisting of a navy-blue jacket, cream ruffled blouse, brown corset, and long brown skirt. She sits beneath a large, leafy tree in a peaceful, sunlit meadow.

Scene-by-Scene Sequence

0–1 Second | The Apple Falls
A shiny red apple detaches from a tree branch and falls directly onto the TOP OF THE WOMAN’S HEAD. Capture the impact with realistic physics and a brief, natural reaction. Use a cinematic medium shot with warm sunlight filtering through the leaves.

1–3 Seconds | The Discovery Begins
The apple bounces off the top of her head and lands visibly on the grass beside her. She flinches, gently touches her head, looks down in surprise, and picks up the apple with a curious expression. Maintain natural body movements and believable apple motion.

3–5 Seconds | A Scientific Revelation
She raises the apple near her face and examines it thoughtfully. Glowing golden mathematical equations, physics formulas, orbital diagrams, and geometric patterns gradually materialize around her. The atmosphere transforms into a dramatic amber-gold scientific fantasy, with luminous particles floating through the sunlight.

5–6 Seconds | From Sketch to Hologram
A vintage pencil-sketch illustration of the woman holding the apple appears briefly, then seamlessly transforms into a radiant golden holographic outline. Fine luminous lines trace her silhouette and the apple, creating an elegant transition between historical illustration and futuristic science.

6–7 Seconds | The Power of Discovery
An extreme close-up reveals her face as her eyes emit a subtle white-gold glow. Intricate scientific equations and delicate golden symbols swirl around her face in a controlled, mesmerizing motion. Preserve her natural facial features and realistic skin texture.

7–9 Seconds | Gravity Defied
The red apple rises and levitates above her open palm. Two additional red apples float gracefully near the tree branches. She slowly looks upward in amazement as golden particles spiral around the levitating fruit. Use a smooth cinematic camera movement and convincing three-dimensional depth.

9–10 Seconds | The Astonishing Finale
Cut to an extreme close-up of her widened eyes and slightly open mouth, capturing genuine astonishment. Golden reflections shimmer in her eyes as the scientific symbols glow softly in the background. End on a dramatic, polished cinematic frame.

Visual Style

Ultra-photorealistic historical fantasy, premium cinematic filmmaking, natural sunlight, realistic skin and hair, detailed period-inspired clothing, shallow depth of field, smooth camera transitions, physically believable apple movement, sophisticated golden holographic effects, volumetric lighting, subtle atmospheric particles, and high-quality 4K visuals.

Strict Continuity and Physics

- The first apple MUST strike the TOP OF HER HEAD before falling onto the grass.

entries.prompt:
PART 1 (30 seconds)

CHARACTER
Use @image 1 and @image 2 as the Master Identity Lock. Keep her face, hair, skin tone, outfit (cream knit cardigan, sage-olive cargo pants, white sneakers, beige bucket hat, tan backpack) and body proportions exactly the same throughout. No identity drift.

LOCATION
Use @image 3 as the environment reference: a windy volcanic hilltop on a Korean island with golden silver-grass, low black stone walls, and a wooden lookout over the sea. Soft late-morning sunlight, light sea breeze, gentle clouds. Keep the same light and weather for the whole video.

STYLE
A spontaneous travel vlog filmed by a friend following just behind and beside her, with slight natural shake, smooth reframing, and candid expressions. Realistic live action, not stylized.

VOICE AND PERFORMANCE
Native Korean speech, natural conversational tone, accurate lip-sync. Every line is performed with visible emotion: the eyebrows, eyes, mouth, and breathing all react to what she feels. Her expression should change before, during, and after each line, with no flat or robotic delivery.

TIMECODE AND SCENES

00:00–00:04 | The Trailhead
She walks along a stone-wall path through tall silver-grass. She glances at the lens, eyes lighting up, eyebrows lifting, and says with bright, bubbly excitement and a rising pitch: "정상이 나를 부르고 있어!" (The summit is calling me!) She ends with a proud, wide grin and a small fist pump. Camera follows from the front at a medium shot.

00:04–00:08 | The Wobble
She tries a slow, cool model walk. Her sneaker catches a small pebble and she wobbles slightly. Her eyes go wide for a split second, then she freezes in a proud “ta-da” pose, holding a stiff, tight smile with flushed cheeks. She says in a deadpan whisper through the smile, eyes darting sideways: “…의도한 거야.” (…I meant to do that.) Camera drifts closer to catch her face.

00:08–00:12 | The Pony
A brown Jeju pony grazes beside the path. She crouches to take a selfie with it, but the pony calmly turns its back to her. Her jaw drops in mock offense, her lower lip pushes into a pout, and she says in a wounded, dramatic tone: "진짜? 얼굴도 안 보여 주는 거야?" (Seriously? You won’t even show me your face?) Then she bursts into helpless laughter, shoulders shaking. Camera: low angle, then a quick pan to her reaction.

00:12–00:17 | Grass Tunnel
The path narrows into tall silver-grass. She pushes through, disappears behind it, then pops out making hand-binoculars and scanning the horizon with a squinted, ultra-serious explorer face. She gasps softly, thrilled, as if she has spotted something. Camera follows from behind, then swings around to the front.

00:17–00:22 | The Wind Hits
She climbs a few stone steps to the crater rim and spreads her arms, eyes closed, face lifted in blissful relief. A gust throws her hair across her face. She pulls a strand from her mouth, scrunches her nose, and laughs. Wide shot, then a medium close-up.

00:22–00:27 | The Seagull
She flaps her elbows like a seagull with a goofy, beaming face. She stops, points at the lens with a playful, challenging look, chin lifted and eyebrows raised, and says in a teasing sing-song voice: "너도 해 봐!" (You try!) Camera circles in a gentle quarter turn, with the sea visible behind her.

00:27–00:30 | Final Frame (hold exactly)
She steps onto the small wooden lookout. A sudden gust blows her hat off and she catches it in mid-air with a surprised gasp and wide eyes. She crouches beside the rope railing, holding the hat against her knee, looking into the lens, laugh fading to a breathless, happy smile. Medium shot, slightly low angle, ocean and soft clouds behind her, camera steady for the last second.

AUDIO
Wind across the grass, soft footsteps on gravel, fabric rustle, pony snort, distant waves, spontaneous laughter. No background music.

NEGATIVE
No face or outfit changes, no real falls, no dangerous actions, no teleporting, no location jumps, no body distortion, no glitches, no CGI look, no stiff movement, no flat or emotionless dialogue, no lip-sync mismatch, no neon or glowing colors.

FORMAT: 16:9 | 30s | 4K | 24 FPS | Ultra-realistic live action | Natural handheld

PART 2 (15 seconds)

Use the very last frame of Part 1 as the first frame / @image 4.

CONTINUITY LOCK
Start from exactly the frame in @image 4: she is crouched beside the rope railing on the wooden lookout, holding her hat, looking into the lens with a fading smile. Same pose, same camera angle, same light, same wind, same background. No cut, no reset. Keep the identity from @image 1 and @image 2 and the outfit identical.

VOICE AND PERFORMANCE
Native Korean speech, natural tone, accurate lip-sync, with emotion visible on her face and in her breath for every line.

TIMECODE AND SCENES

00:00–00:03 | Picking Up
Without a cut, she stands up, puts the hat back on, and tilts her head toward the steps with a cheerful, bouncy energy. She says in a light, breathless voice: "내려가면 간식이다, 가자!" (Snacks are waiting downhill, let’s go!) Camera stays at her medium shot and follows.

00:03–00:07 | The Balance Beam
Back on the trail, she steps onto a low black stone wall and walks along it with arms out like a gymnast, tongue slightly between her teeth in concentration. She keeps it low and safe, then hops off with a small, proud landing and a triumphant “yes!” face. Camera follows from the side, then moves behind her.

00:07–00:11 | Snack Review
She sits on the wall, takes a triangle kimbap from her backpack, and bites in. She closes her eyes, chews slowly, savoring it, and nods with solemn drama like a food critic. Her eyes open wide and she turns to the lens, saying in a hushed, awestruck voice: "별 다섯 개." (Five stars.) Wind ruffles her hair. Close-up, then medium shot.

00:11–00:15 | The Quiet Ending
She stands, walks toward the camera with a mischievous half-smile, leans in, puts a finger to her lips, and whispers with sparkling, conspiratorial eyes: "비밀이야." (It’s a secret.) She gently tilts the lens up toward the open sky and soft clouds, and the shot slowly settles as the wind fades into silence.

AUDIO
Wind, footsteps on gravel, kimbap wrapper crinkle, distant waves, soft laughter, ending in quiet ambience. No background music.

NEGATIVE
No cut or reset at the start, no face or outfit changes, no location or lighting change, no dangerous balancing, no glitches, no CGI look, no flat or emotionless dialogue, no lip-sync mismatch, no neon or glowing colors.

entries.description: A 30 s post-apocalyptic short with a four-slot reference lock (two characters, a city layout, a rust-red muscle car), story beats in 5-7 s blocks and a look line of "burnt rust red, weathered sand gray, charcoal, dusty gold sunlight, textured blacks, subtle film grain".
entries.prompt:
30s, 16:9, ultra-realistic post-apocalyptic ruin-punk cinematic short. Dense visuals, grounded physics, natural performances, and clear action continuity. The story: Alin enters Ston’s territory to recover a stolen ignition key, provokes him into revealing its location, and escapes with it after a tense confrontation.

Reference lock: Ref 1 = Alin, Ref 2 = Ston, Ref 3 = ruined city layout, Ref 4 = rusty red-brown modified muscle car. Preserve their identities, proportions, and designs. Do not inherit reference backgrounds or poses.

0–5s — Arrival: Start inside the moving car. Tight shots of Alin’s hands, eyes, and calm side profile as she drives through a ruined city toward a collapsed industrial courtyard. Dust and wreckage pass naturally outside. She spots Ston standing beside a wrecked watchtower and slows. No dialogue.

5–10s — The provocation: Alin drives into the courtyard and performs two controlled drift circles around Ston, throwing up dust and gravel. Ston tracks the car, becoming increasingly aggressive but remaining grounded and physically believable. The car stops directly in front of him. Alin exits calmly, holding his gaze.

10–16s — The reveal: Ston gives one deep roar and steps toward her. Alin does not retreat. She points toward the watchtower. Ston glances back for a moment, revealing a small metal key hanging from a chain around his neck. Alin’s eyes briefly confirm it. Ston notices her attention and grips the chain.

16–23s — The confrontation: Ston lunges. Alin sidesteps the attack and uses the car door as a barrier. Ston slams into the metal, denting it with realistic weight. Alin pulls the chain free during the impact, stumbles back, regains balance, and runs toward the driver’s side. Ston recovers and charges after her. Keep the action continuous, with no teleporting or impossible movements.

23–30s — The escape: Alin reaches the car, starts the engine, and reverses sharply as Ston grabs the rear of the vehicle. The tires regain traction, the car pulls free, and she accelerates through the courtyard exit. Ston remains standing in the dust, roaring as the car disappears into the ruined streets. End on a brief rear view of the car leaving, then cut to Alin’s calm eyes in the mirror as she closes her hand around the stolen key.

Cinematography: Motivated cuts only, clear screen direction, realistic vehicle weight, natural dust lag, believable impacts, subtle handheld movement, no excessive shaky cam. Medium-low saturation, burnt rust red, weathered sand gray, charcoal, dusty gold sunlight, textured blacks, subtle film grain.

Sound: Continuous engine load, tire friction, gravel, metal impacts, wind, car-door mechanics, and one final roar. No dialogue, subtitles, watermarks, extra characters, glowing eyes, exaggerated facial expressions, or AI-looking motion. End with the story completed, not mid-action.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 umbrella fight in one continuous take: seven opponents, one prop, two chained parts
entries.description: A 45 s wuxia-style street fight in two parts (30 s + 15 s), each "ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE | NO CUTS BETWEEN BEATS". The umbrella is the whole choreography: opened in a face as a blind, as a parachute mid-flip, as a shield against a thrown stool, flat overhead in a knee slide. Part 1 ends on a written FINAL FRAME LOCK and Part 2 opens on a START-FRAME LOCK; exclusions forbid weapon switching, a second umbrella and gore.
entries.prompt:
PART 1 (30 seconds)

Attach: @image1, @image2 (umbrella), @image3 (opponents).

[30 SECONDS | 16:9 | 24 FPS | ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE | NO TRANSITION EFFECTS | NO CUTS BETWEEN BEATS]

[REFERENCE LOCK]
@image1: Han Seo-yeon, the main fighter. Keep her face, hair, jacket, trousers, sneakers and thumb ring identical in every frame.
@image2: her umbrella, a large matte black umbrella with a brushed brass hook handle, steel shaft and steel ferrule tip. It is the same single object in every beat, and it is the only weapon.
@image3: seven opponents. Keep each face, outfit and build consistent. They attack in staggered groups of two or three, never fully surrounding her.

[POSITIVE LOCKS]
- The umbrella is always matte black fabric with a brass hook handle, never glowing, never changing color, no patterns.
- It is opened and closed only on the beats written below. It is closed by default.
- She controls it mostly one-handed, with short two-handed grips only on blocks.
- Her ponytail, sage jacket and white-soled sneakers stay unchanged, getting wetter and muddier only naturally.

[LOCATION & ATMOSPHERE]
A hanok-style courtyard market in an old Korean town at dusk, just after rain. Wet grey flagstones with shallow puddles, dark timber pillars, curved tiled roofs, plaster walls, canvas-covered produce stalls, stacked bamboo crates, a stone well in the center, and a stone staircase on the left leading up to a lantern-lit lane. Paper lanterns and hanging bulbs give warm amber light against cool slate-blue ambient dusk. Light mist rises off the stones. Palette is muted indigo, slate, amber and earth tones. Absolutely no neon, no glowing signs, no colored light.

[CINEMATIC STYLE]
Premium photorealistic action cinema, 35 mm anamorphic look, 40° field of view on wide shots and 28° on close shots, organic grain, natural motion blur, soft highlight roll-off, realistic skin, wet cloth, fabric, metal and stone textures. Natural, restrained color grade. No glossy CGI finish.

[ACTION & CAMERA]
0–5s: Wide, low, front-facing tracking shot. Seo-yeon walks slowly down the stone staircase with the closed umbrella in her right hand, its steel tip tapping each step. Seven opponents wait in the courtyard below. Opponent 7 (charcoal coat) says in a low, amused tone: "You walked into the wrong market tonight." She tilts her head slightly and answers calmly: "Then I'll leave it a little tidier." Opponents 1 and 2 charge. She steps off the last stair, flicks the umbrella around so the brass hook catches Opponent 1's ankle, and pulls sharply. He drops flat on the wet stone with a splash. Camera drops with the pull.

5–10s: Opponent 2 swings a wild haymaker. She ducks and snaps the umbrella open right in his face. The canopy bursts open with a spray of rainwater and blinds him. From behind the canopy she lands a spinning heel kick on his shoulder, sending him sliding across a puddle. She snaps the umbrella shut in one motion. Camera orbits 180° around the canopy burst in one smooth arc, catching water droplets in the air.

10–15s: Opponents 3 and 4 flank from the market stalls. She burst-steps forward in one explosive sprint, a streak of water spraying from her sneakers, and reappears between them. A short jab with the steel tip into Opponent 3's raised forearm, then the brass hook catches Opponent 4's collar and she swings him sideways into a stack of bamboo crates, which tumbles lightly. Camera whip-pans left, then right, and settles behind her shoulder.

15–20s: Opponent 5 (rust coverall) charges like a bull. She runs at the plaster wall, takes two steps up it, flips backward over his head, and opens the umbrella mid-flip so she drifts down behind him in a soft, controlled landing. She closes it as her feet touch and drives the shaft into the back of his knees. He falls forward into a canvas stall, which sags and splashes rainwater from its tarp. Camera follows the wall-run in a tight vertical tilt, then drops to the landing.

20–25s: Opponent 6 (olive bomber) hurls a wooden stool at her. She snaps the umbrella open as a shield and the stool bounces off the canopy and clatters away. She spins the open umbrella once, flinging a wide arc of trapped rainwater into Opponents 6 and 3's faces, then snaps it shut and blocks Opponent 6's punch with the shaft held crosswise in both hands. She twists and flicks her away with a sharp one-handed rotation. Opponent 6 slides back across the wet stone. Camera pushes in tight on the shield-open, then pulls wide.

25–30s: Seo-yeon sprints and slides on her knees across a long puddle, umbrella held flat overhead, passing under a swinging blow from Opponent 1. She springs up at the stone well in the center of the courtyard, steps onto its rim, and plants the closed umbrella's tip beside her foot. Water streams off the canopy. Opponents 7 and 1 stand ahead of her, breathing hard, while the others recover behind. She is breathing steadily, eyes locked forward. HOLD this exact final frame for the last half second.

[FINAL FRAME LOCK: END OF PART 1]
Medium-wide frame, 40° field of view, camera at chest height in front of her at about 5 m. Seo-yeon stands on the stone well rim at center frame, right hand gripping the CLOSED umbrella by its brass hook handle, steel tip planted beside her right foot. Her weight is slightly forward, ponytail swaying to the left. Opponent 7 (charcoal coat) is on the left at about 4 m, Opponent 1 on the right at about 3 m, the rest staggered behind them. Wet flagstones, amber lanterns in the background, mist on the ground.

[AUDIO]
No music. Dialogue exactly as written. Footsteps on wet stone, umbrella snap-open and snap-shut, canopy whoosh, steel tip taps, water splashes, grunts, tarp rustle, bamboo clatter.

[EXCLUSIONS]
No neon or glowing light. No wooden weapon, no staff, no bat. No second umbrella, no weapon switching, no change of umbrella color or pattern. No smoke teleport. No morphing faces. No extra characters. No large structural destruction.
STEP 3: PART 2 (15 seconds)

Pehle frame ke liye Part 1 ka last frame use karo, plus @image1, @image2, @image3.

[START-FRAME LOCK]
The video opens on the exact final frame of Part 1: Seo-yeon standing on the stone well rim at center frame, CLOSED umbrella planted tip-down beside her right foot, Opponent 7 on the left, Opponent 1 on the right, the others behind. Same camera position, same field of view, same wet flagstones, same lantern light, same mist. No reset, no new angle, no jump. Motion starts naturally from this pose.

[REFERENCE LOCK]
@image1: Han Seo-yeon, same face, outfit and ponytail, now damp and slightly muddy. @image2: the same matte black umbrella with the brass hook handle. @image3: all seven opponents, same faces and outfits, some now wet, scuffed or limping.

[POSITIVE LOCKS]
- The umbrella stays matte black fabric with a brass hook handle, a single object. Closed by default, opened only on the beats below.
- Opponents' injuries stay subtle and consistent (scuffed knees, ruffled hair), nothing gory.
- Lighting stays warm amber lantern light against cool slate dusk. No neon, no colored glow.

[LOCATION]
Same hanok courtyard market, now with a few tumbled bamboo crates, a sagging canvas stall and scattered puddles. Light drizzle begins falling halfway through, visible against the lantern glow.

[CINEMATIC STYLE]
Same look as Part 1: photorealistic, 35 mm anamorphic feel, 40° wide / 28° close, organic grain, natural motion blur, muted natural grade.

[ACTION & CAMERA]
0–3s: Opponent 7 steps forward and says coldly, "Everyone gets one lucky night." Seo-yeon glances at the umbrella, a small smile at the corner of her mouth, and replies, "Then spend yours wisely." Opponent 1 lunges. She plants the umbrella's steel tip on the well rim and uses it like a vaulting pole, swinging over his lunge and landing behind Opponents 1 and 4 as they collide. Camera follows the vault in a slight upward arc.

3–6s: Opponents 2, 4 and 6 charge together. She catches a hanging paper-lantern rope with her free hand (the lantern stays intact and swinging) and swings across the gap in a wide arc, kicking Opponent 4 in the chest mid-swing. Releasing the rope, she lands in a crouch and sweeps the closed umbrella low through Opponents 2 and 6's legs, dropping both in a splash. Camera tracks her swing, then drops low with the sweep.

6–9s: Opponent 3 jumps in with a flying kick. She snaps the umbrella open overhead and the kick lands on the canopy, which flexes and bounces her backward in a burst of water spray. She snaps it shut and strikes Opponent 3's raised guard with the shaft, sending her skidding. Opponent 5 grabs the umbrella from behind. She releases it, spins, and delivers a hard elbow strike to his ribs, then catches the umbrella as it falls and flips the brass hook forward into her grip. Camera orbits tightly around the grab and release.

9–12s: Only Opponent 7 and Opponent 1 remain standing, both furious. They rush together. She kicks a bamboo crate into Opponent 1's path, making him stumble, then faces Opponent 7 alone. They exchange three fast shaft-and-forearm blocks. Rain falls harder, glinting in the amber light. She hooks the brass handle around Opponent 7's leading ankle, yanks, and drops him into a shallow puddle. Camera does not cut, whip-pans to the fall, then settles tight on her face.

12–15s: Seo-yeon straightens and says quietly, "Next time, ask before you block the stairs." The seven opponents lie or kneel scattered around the courtyard, groaning. She snaps the umbrella open over her head against the drizzle and walks calmly toward the stone staircase, rain pattering on the black canopy. The camera slowly pulls back and rises to a wide shot of the whole courtyard with lanterns glowing in the drizzle. She climbs the first few steps and disappears into the lantern-lit lane under the open umbrella. Hold the empty wide shot for the last second.

[AUDIO]
No music. Dialogue exactly as written. Rain on fabric, wet footsteps, umbrella snaps, impacts, grunts, bamboo clatter, rope creak, water splashes.

[EXCLUSIONS]
No neon or glowing light. No wooden weapon, no staff, no bat. No second umbrella, no weapon switching, no change of umbrella color or pattern. No smoke teleport. No morphing faces or outfit changes. No scene reset at the start. No gore. No structural destruction.

entries.title: MiniMax H3 couture casting tape: the laugh runs too long, then stops mid-note
entries.description: Horror carried entirely by performance: a fixed-frame casting tape where a warm laugh keeps going "past funny, past polite" while the eyes stop laughing, then cuts off "MID-NOTE" into two seconds of dead silence and one quiet line. Written like an actor's brief (Premise, Objective, Obstacle, Tactic, Subtext, Voice recipe, Micro-behaviour) with prosthetic and EYE LOCKs and "Fine 35mm film grain".
entries.prompt:
Chartreuse-yellow seamless paper, flat even studio light, locked-off camera at eye level with the faintest handheld breath, medium close-up, shallow depth of field.

The performer:  [📷 Image1]  [📷 Image2] a Black male model in his twenties with deep ebony skin, natural realistic skin with visible pores and fine texture, a huge soft black afro, sculpted magenta-purple painted brows and lilac-purple painted shadow across both lids, a gold septum ring and a thin gold ring in the left nostril, glossy coral-red lips, four long curved ivory tusk-fangs — two rising from the lower jaw, two descending over the lip — long sculpted hot-pink stiletto claw-nails with carved rococo ridges on every finger, coral drop earrings, a pink toile-de-Jouy puff-sleeved garment printed with pastoral figures, a hot-pink fur stole at the shoulders. The tusk-fangs and pink claw-nails are prosthetic couture pieces and remain exactly as in the start frame in every moment — never vanish, never multiply. His face, hair, makeup, prosthetics, costume, body type and identity never change — he is exactly the man in the start frame. EYE LOCK: his natural irises exactly as in the start frame, NEVER glowing, never changing colour — only wet surfaces catch the chartreuse light.

Premise — NOT FINISHED: the beautiful thing tried to leave the fitting early, and made a small joke of it at the door. He is laughing at the joke. The reader is just left of the lens, never into the camera. Objective: to bring them back to the chair. Obstacle: the laugh keeps going past where a human laugh would stop. Tactic: let the wrongness do the work. Subtext: the door was never the way out.

Voice recipe: warm, unravelling, then dead flat. A deep baritone laugh with too much air in it.
Performance: he opens already laughing — head tipped back a little, tusks catching the light, claws loosely spread on the fur stole, and for the first two seconds it is a genuinely warm, delighted laugh. It keeps going. Three seconds. Four. Five — past funny, past polite, the laugh continuing at exactly the same warmth while his eyes, open now, have stopped laughing entirely and are fixed on the eyeline. Six seconds. THE PEAK: the laugh stops MID-NOTE — cut off instantly, no trailing off, no echo — and his face drops in the same instant to perfectly flat, perfectly still. Two full seconds of dead silence. Then, quiet and even, each word placed: "Sit down. We're not finished." Aftermath: one slow blink, the head levelling, a claw gesturing — once, small — toward the unseen chair. Cut before it resolves.

Micro-behaviour: blink-rate change, jaw tension, hands tighten and release, chin lift.

Diegetic sound only: the laugh, its instant stop, room hum, his level voice.
Cinematic realism, raw casting-tape energy, natural understated acting with real dread — masterful slow-burn horror-film pacing, unhurried, never camp. Fine 35mm film grain, realistic skin detail. The couture stays immaculate: fashion-editorial polish inside the dread. No transformation, no VFX morphing, no creature growth — the horror is entirely in the performance. No music. No overacting, no melodrama, no trailer energy, no montage, no plastic smooth skin, no exaggerated cartoon expressions, no design changes, no added worldbuilding. EXACTLY ONE person in frame throughout, exactly two hands. The reader is NEVER visible; no part of their body or belongings ever enters the frame.

entries.prompt:
THE RED LIGHT: WE USED TO BE US

DURATION: 30 SECONDS
ASPECT RATIO: 16:9 LANDSCAPE
STYLE: Ultra-realistic live-action romantic drama, premium cinematic photography, Japanese romance film atmosphere, natural performances, subtle 35mm film grain, realistic skin texture, cinematic color grading.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:
@image1 = Male protagonist, the woman's former boyfriend.
@image2 = Female protagonist, the man's former girlfriend.

STRICT IDENTITY LOCK:
Preserve both characters' exact facial identities, facial structures, hairstyles, and recognizable features throughout every scene. Their clothing may change naturally between present and past, but their faces must remain consistent. No face swapping, identity mixing, or character duplication.

STORY:
Two former lovers unexpectedly encounter each other at a busy city intersection. A brief exchange of glances triggers a rapid montage of their happiest memories. When the traffic light turns green, reality returns. They pass each other silently and continue in opposite directions.

SCENE 1 — AN UNEXPECTED ENCOUNTER
00:00–00:05

Late afternoon at a busy Japanese urban intersection. Red traffic lights, waiting pedestrians, passing cars, storefront reflections, and soft sunlight create a realistic cinematic atmosphere.

Begin with a wide establishing shot, then slowly push through the waiting crowd toward @image1. He looks across the street and suddenly freezes.

POV shot: @image2 stands on the opposite side. She recognizes him at the same moment.

Alternate close-ups of their faces. Their expressions shift subtly from surprise to quiet recognition. They maintain eye contact without speaking.

The surrounding traffic sounds become slightly muffled.

TRANSITION:
Push toward @image2's eyes. As she blinks, use a precise match cut to the same eye movement in a memory of her laughing at @image1 in a sunlit coffee shop.

SCENE 2 — THE FIRST MEMORY
00:05–00:09

FLASHBACK: A cozy coffee shop with warm afternoon sunlight, amber highlights, soft shadows, and subtle analog film texture.

@image1 slides a drink across a wooden table. @image2 takes a sip, mischievously steals his drink, and laughs. He pretends to be annoyed before smiling.

Use intimate handheld medium shots and close-ups of their natural expressions.

TRANSITION:
The coffee cup fills the frame and match cuts into the circular surface of an umbrella during a rainy-day memory.

SCENE 3 — MEMORIES IN MOTION
00:09–00:19

A rapid, sweet nostalgia montage. Each memory lasts approximately 0.5–1 second. Use seamless match cuts, natural movement, foreground objects, and coherent visual transitions.

MEMORY 1 — SHARING AN UMBRELLA:
@image1 holds an umbrella over @image2 while walking through light rain. His shoulder gets wet. She notices, moves closer, and laughs.
Transition: A raindrop on the umbrella match cuts into sunlight reflected on a train window.

MEMORY 2 — THE TRAIN RIDE:
They sit beside each other on a moving train, sharing earphones. @image2 rests her head on his shoulder. He glances at her with a gentle smile.
Transition: The train enters a dark tunnel, creating a natural full-frame transition.

MEMORY 3 — COOKING TOGETHER:
In a small home kitchen, @image1 struggles with a simple meal. @image2 laughs and playfully teases him. He jokingly defends his cooking.
Transition: A kitchen towel briefly covers the lens before revealing the next memory.

MEMORY 4 — THE BEACH:
They run along a beautiful beach during golden hour. @image2 runs ahead, turns around, and invites him to catch up. He follows, laughing.
Use a low-angle tracking shot of their feet in the sand, followed by a wide coastal shot.
Transition: A wave rushes toward the camera until water and foam fill the entire frame.

MEMORY 5 — THE NIGHT FESTIVAL:
Warm lanterns illuminate their faces. @image2 grabs @image1's hand and pulls him toward colorful festival stalls. They turn toward each other and laugh.
Use handheld tracking, warm bokeh, and candid close-ups.
Transition: A glowing lantern passes directly in front of the lens, briefly obscuring the entire frame.

MEMORY 6 — THE LITTLE MOMENT:
They sit together on a park bench at sunset. @image2 rests her head on his shoulder. @image1 gently moves a loose strand of hair away from her face. They exchange warm smiles.

This is the montage's most intimate memory.

TRANSITION BACK TO PRESENT:
Sunlight reflecting on their faces match cuts into the red traffic signal reflected on a passing car window. Warm colors instantly return to the cooler palette of the present.

SCENE 4 — THE YELLOW LIGHT
00:19–00:24

Back at the intersection. @image1 and @image2 are still looking at each other.

City ambience gradually returns. The traffic light changes from red to yellow.

Alternate close-ups show quiet affection, recognition, and restrained sadness.

@image2 gives a barely noticeable smile. @image1 gently returns it.

Insert one final flashback lasting approximately 0.5 seconds: the couple walking hand in hand beneath golden sunlight, laughing together.

Immediately match cut back to the present, where their hands hang separately at their sides.

No dialogue. No tears. Let the contrast tell the story.

SCENE 5 — THE GREEN LIGHT
00:24–00:30

The traffic light turns green. Pedestrians begin crossing from both sides.

@image1 and @image2 walk toward each other among the moving crowd.

Use a controlled lateral tracking shot, keeping both characters visible as they approach.

They pass each other. Their shoulders nearly touch, but they do not make contact.

For a brief moment, their expressions soften with recognition. Neither stops. Neither speaks. They continue in opposite directions.

ENDING SHOT:
The camera remains stationary as the crowd gradually separates them.

@image1 disappears into the crowd on one side. @image2 disappears into the crowd on the other.

Hold the wide composition as ordinary pedestrians continue crossing and the city resumes its rhythm.

End naturally without a fade to black, title card, or text.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
Present day: cooler, restrained colors, realistic city lighting, slightly desaturated tones.
Flashbacks: warm golden sunlight, soft highlights, subtle 35mm film grain, natural colors, intimate handheld cinematography.

CAMERA:
Wide establishing shots, controlled dolly-ins, intimate close-ups, lateral tracking, natural handheld movement, shallow depth of field, realistic motion blur, and seamless match cuts.

All flashbacks must feature the same recognizable characters. Their past clothing may differ from their present clothing, but their identities must remain unchanged.

AUDIO:
NO BACKGROUND MUSIC.
Use natural city traffic, footsteps, cafe ambience, rain, train sounds, kitchen ambience, waves, and distant festival sounds. Connect memories with brief natural sound bridges. Restore the city ambience when the traffic light changes to green.

No narration, no dialogue, no lyrics.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS:
No identity drift, face swapping, duplicate characters, artificial expressions, robotic movement, excessive slow motion, fantasy portals, random transitions, plastic skin, exaggerated crying, text overlays, subtitles, logos, or watermarks.

FINAL EMOTIONAL GOAL:
The audience should feel the sweetness of a relationship returning through a few seconds of memory, followed by the quiet realization that the two people can no longer return to the life they once shared.

The memories should make the audience smile. The ending should leave a gentle ache without explaining everything.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 Korean apartment horror: hallway lights switching off one by one, in 1.5 s beats
entries.description: A retention-first horror short: an "Immediate hook" in the first 1.5 s, then 1.5-2 s beats (first anomaly, impossible movement, invisible approach, false safety, reflection horror, an unsettling call) and a camera note to "leave negative space in corridors so subtle silhouettes and background movement can be noticed".
entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second ultra-realistic cinematic Korean apartment horror short in 16:9 widescreen, specifically designed to grab attention within the first few seconds and maintain escalating tension until the final frame.

CORE CONCEPT: A young woman returns home late at night and notices that the automatic hallway lights are switching off one by one behind her. At first she thinks it is a faulty lighting system. Then she realizes something is using the darkness to get closer.

SEQUENCE

0–1.5s — Immediate hook:
Wide cinematic shot of a quiet Korean apartment corridor late at night. A young Korean woman walks toward her apartment carrying a small grocery bag. The fluorescent light directly behind her suddenly switches off. She stops and looks back.

1.5–3s — First anomaly:
She continues walking. Another ceiling light farther behind her flickers twice and turns off. For a single instant, a tall human-like silhouette is visible underneath the next remaining light. It does not move.

3–4.5s — Impossible movement:
She cautiously looks back again. The corridor appears empty. She takes one step backward. Another light shuts off. When the light goes dark, the silhouette is suddenly several meters closer when the next light comes on.

4.5–6s — Fear reaction:
Close-up of her face as she realizes something is wrong. Her breathing becomes tense. She slowly raises her phone and activates the flashlight.

6–7.5s — Empty corridor:
Her flashlight sweeps across the hallway. Nothing is there. The camera follows the beam naturally. She starts to relax—then notices a single wet footprint directly in front of her.

7.5–9s — Invisible approach:
More wet footprints slowly appear on the floor one after another, moving toward her from the darkness. No creature is visible. She freezes.

9–10.5s — Escape:
She suddenly runs toward her apartment. Controlled handheld camera follows behind her. Corridor lights extinguish sequentially in her direction, creating the impression that darkness is chasing her.

10.5–12s — Door struggle:
She reaches her apartment, hurriedly searches for her keys and unlocks the door. Her hands tremble naturally. She enters and immediately turns around.

12–13.5s — False safety:
She looks down the hallway. It is completely empty. She slowly closes and locks her apartment door.

13.5–15s — Something is inside:
The apartment is quiet. She takes several steps away from the door. The hallway light inside her apartment flickers. In the glass of a nearby cabinet, a dark human silhouette can be seen standing behind her.

15–17s — Reflection horror:
She notices the reflection and slowly turns around. Nothing is there. She looks back at the glass. The silhouette is now much closer to her reflection.

17–19s — Reality breaks:
She spins around again. The apartment remains empty. Her phone suddenly begins ringing.

19–21s — Unsettling call:
Extreme close-up of the phone screen. The incoming call appears to be coming from her own phone number. She hesitates before answering.

21–23s — Sound reveal:
She answers. No voice comes through. Instead, she hears the unmistakable sound of footsteps coming from her apartment hallway—matching the exact rhythm of the footsteps she made earlier.

23–25s — Final reveal begins:
Her front door slowly opens by itself. Beyond it is the dark apartment corridor. At the far end stands a figure that looks almost identical to her, facing away from the camera.

25–27s — Unnatural turn:
The woman remains frozen inside her apartment. The distant figure slowly rotates its head toward the camera while its body remains completely motionless. The movement is subtly unnatural and unsettling, but no gore or extreme deformation.

27–28.5s — Darkness:
Every light in the corridor suddenly switches off simultaneously. Complete darkness for a brief moment. Hold the silence.

28.5–30s — Replay-worthy ending:
The lights suddenly return. The corridor is empty. The woman is no longer visible. The camera remains inside the apartment, staring toward the open doorway. After a brief pause, the door slowly closes by itself.

CUT TO BLACK immediately.

VISUAL STYLE

Ultra-realistic Korean apartment complex at night, authentic modern residential architecture, narrow corridor, realistic fluorescent lighting, subtle reflections, natural skin texture, believable clothing and hair movement, realistic phone illumination, cinematic shadows, atmospheric darkness, restrained psychological horror, sophisticated body-horror influence without gore, realistic environmental physics, cinematic film grain, natural motion blur, high dynamic range, premium horror-film cinematography.

CAMERA & COMPOSITION

16:9 widescreen cinematic composition. Use the wide frame intentionally: leave negative space in corridors so subtle silhouettes and background movement can be noticed by viewers. Combine wide establishing shots, controlled handheld tracking shots, medium shots and occasional close-ups.

Keep camera movement tense but controlled and physically believable. Avoid excessive shaking, random zooms, unnecessary cuts, or disorienting camera movement. Maintain clear geography of the apartment and hallway throughout the entire video.

CONTINUITY & QUALITY CONTROL

Maintain the exact same woman, face, hairstyle, clothing, grocery bag, phone, apartment door, corridor architecture and lighting environment throughout every shot.

Ensure:

- Consistent facial identity
- Correct human anatomy and proportions
- Natural hands and fingers
- Realistic walking and running physics
- Realistic reflections
- Correct shadows and lighting direction
- Consistent object placement
- No duplicated characters
- No disappearing or changing clothing
- No warped faces
- No extra limbs or fingers
- No floating objects
- No changing apartment architecture
- No inconsistent doors or hallways
- No random camera transitions
- No accidental text or subtitles
- No gore
- No blood
- No cartoonish monster design

The horror should come primarily from anticipation, darkness, reflections, impossible positioning and subtle movement, keeping the entity mysterious rather than showing it constantly.

SOCIAL-MEDIA RETENTION

Make the first 1–2 seconds visually intriguing, introduce a new unsettling event approximately every 1–2 seconds, and progressively increase the tension. Avoid slow filler shots.

The final reveal should be subtle enough that viewers may want to rewatch the video to find the exact moment the entity appeared, making the ending highly suitable for social-media sharing.

OUTPUT: 16:9 widescreen, 30 seconds, photorealistic cinematic horror, premium film quality, coherent continuous story, polished professional cinematography, realistic motion, no text, no subtitles, no watermark.

entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second ultra-realistic live-action Korean historical film set in a Joseon-era village in the late 1800s. High-budget Korean cinema style, natural acting, realistic environments and emotional storytelling.

CHARACTERS:
Mother: 68-year-old Korean woman, wrinkled gentle face, grey-black hair in a traditional low bun, faded beige jeogori and dark-brown chima.

Son: 28-year-old Korean man, lean face, short black hair, light stubble, exhausted eyes, worn dark-blue Joseon soldier robe, traditional fabric armor and muddy shoes.

SCENE 1 (0–5s): At dusk, the elderly mother sits outside her traditional wooden house holding an oil lantern, staring at the empty village road, waiting for her son who left for war. Autumn leaves blow gently in the wind.

SCENE 2 (5–10s): She walks slowly to the village entrance, searching the deserted dirt road. Seeing no one, she presses a folded piece of cloth to her chest and returns home with tearful eyes.

SCENE 3 (10–15s): Inside her dimly lit house at night, she prepares to extinguish her oil lamp when she hears exhausted footsteps outside. She freezes, turns toward the wooden door and notices a shadow beneath it.

SCENE 4 (15–20s): She slides open the door and finds her long-lost son standing outside, exhausted and covered in dust. He whispers emotionally in Korean, “Eomeoni…” (Mother). She stares at him in disbelief, her eyes filling with tears.

SCENE 5 (20–26s): She touches his cheek with trembling fingers, realizes he is real and embraces him tightly. He rests his head on her shoulder, silently crying. She whispers, “I knew you would come home.” Warm lantern light illuminates their emotional reunion.

SCENE 6 (26–30s): Inside the house, mother and son sit together sharing a simple bowl of warm rice. She holds his hand and rests her head against him, smiling through tears. The camera slowly pulls back through the doorway as the lantern flickers against the cold autumn night. End on this peaceful reunion.

VISUAL STYLE: Ultra-photorealistic live-action, authentic Joseon architecture and clothing, realistic skin texture, natural facial expressions, cinematic 35mm film look, subtle film grain, realistic depth of field, cool moonlight contrasting with warm lantern light, smooth camera movements and consistent character faces throughout.

AUDIO: Gentle wind, distant village ambience, footsteps on dirt, sliding wooden door and subtle emotional orchestral music. Natural, clear Korean dialogue.

entries.prompt: SCENE CONTEXT A 15 second comic scene inside a vintage car actively traveling along a country road at 40 km/h. The car is already moving in the first frame and continues moving through the final frame. A terrified blonde passenger helps steer while the composed brunette driver applies lipstick. ACTIVE REFERENCE : starting-frame reference for both adult women, their exact faces, hairstyles, white clothing, seating positions, vintage car, and warm film look. Blonde passenger on screen left; brunette driver on screen right. Match their appearance 100% to the reference. FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING Begin with the reference composition already in motion. The blonde leans across with her hand gripping the upper-left steering wheel. The brunette holds red lipstick against her lower lip, with her other hand resting on the lower-right wheel. Both faces remain clearly visible. CAMERA One continuous shot, 63° field of view, matching the reference perspective. Camera mounted outside on the front of the moving car, facing inward through the windshield. Its position stays fixed relative to the car while the landscape moves continuously outside. Gentle chassis vibration passes through the camera. VISIBLE CAR MOVEMENT Through the side windows, nearby fence posts, grass, and trees sweep backward with clear parallax: nearby objects pass faster than distant fields. Through the rear window, the road visibly recedes. Moving tree reflections slide over the windshield. Bands of sunlight travel across the women’s faces and clothing. The rearview mirror trembles slightly; earrings and loose hair sway with the car’s vibration. Maintain these movement cues throughout every line of dialogue and the ending. ACTION AND DIALOGUE 0.0–3.0 seconds: The blonde tightens her grip, staring forward with wide eyes. BLONDE, sharply: “Watch the road!” The brunette finishes a short lipstick stroke and moves the lipstick away from her mouth. 3.0–6.0 seconds: Still inspecting herself in the rearview mirror, the brunette answers casually. BRUNETTE: “You are. I’m multitasking.” She presses her lips together once. 6.0–9.0 seconds: The wheels cross a small uneven patch. Both women bounce gently with the suspension. The blonde makes a small steering correction, shoulders tense. BLONDE: “We’re going to die!” 9.0–12.0 seconds: The brunette holds the lipstick beside her cheek and studies her reflection with a tiny head tilt. BRUNETTE, completely composed: “Does this shade wash me out?” 12.0–14.0 seconds: The blonde briefly gives her an incredulous sideways look. BLONDE: “The funeral lighting might!” 14.0–15.0 seconds: The brunette slowly lowers the lipstick, shifts her eyes to the road, and tightens her grip on the wheel. The blonde faces forward with her jaw clenched. Hold their contrasting reactions as scenery continues sweeping past. PERFORMANCE / PHYSICS Natural English conversation, one speaker at a time, with synchronized mouth movements. Blonde voice: breathless, tense, increasingly incredulous. Brunette voice: relaxed, dry, matter-of-fact. Allow brief reaction pauses between lines. Preserve realistic skin texture, eye movements, finger anatomy, and continuous hand contact with the wheel. Steering corrections stay small and physically plausible. LIGHTING / COLOR Warm directional afternoon sunlight, fixed 5600K white balance. Preserve the reference’s yellow-green vintage grade, golden skin highlights, creamy white lace, vivid red lipstick, and deep teal-green cabin shadows. Soft highlight bloom and fine photographic grain. AUDIO Clearly audible continuous engine rumble, tire-on-road hiss, wind through a slightly open window, and faint dashboard rattling. A soft suspension thump accompanies the bump at 6 seconds. Mix dialogue clearly above the environmental sounds. The soundtrack consists of conversation and location sounds. OUTPUT 15 seconds, 16:9 landscape, photorealistic, real-time motion, one uninterrupted take. CONTINUITY LOCKS Same two women, faces, wardrobe, car interior, and prop positions throughout. The brunette retains the lipstick in her original hand. Both women retain their respective steering-wheel grips. Keep the car visibly traveling forward for the entire 15 seconds, including the final reaction.

entries.title: Pika H3 Flex balcony orbit: one continuous crane/orbit visiting three stacked balconies, 1970s pastel film palette
entries.description: Official text-to-video camera-control showcase: three people stretch on three identical stacked balconies while one uncut move orbits ~40 degrees, pushes in on the middle balcony, booms up, booms down fast and reverse-orbits back to the opening wide. Every stretch is written as "three to four seconds to flow into"; each person's knitwear or tracksuit colour is named so the camera can find them; sound is diegetic only with an explicit list of what must not be heard.
entries.prompt:
A tall white modernist apartment tower against a soft pale-blue sky with faint streaky cirrus cloud. The building sits on the right half of the frame; the left half is open sky. Smooth off-white render facade with small square windows in thick white frames. Three identical cantilevered concrete balconies are stacked vertically on the building's corner, each a thick white slab with an angled, wedge-shaped underside and a thin white metal railing of vertical balusters. Crisp, graphic, minimal, soft 1970s film palette: chalky whites, powder blue, muted pastels.

Three people are doing a slow, calm morning stretch routine, one per balcony. They are always gently in motion, never frozen, but every movement is slow, smooth and controlled, like yoga or tai chi: each stretch takes three to four seconds to flow into, eases gently at the end, and flows unhurried into the next. No fast, jerky, snapping or flailing movements. Graceful, deliberate, meditative.
Top balcony: a young woman with dark hair pulled back, in a lilac fluffy knit jumper and matching lilac wide-leg knit trousers. She slowly reaches both arms high overhead, then gradually leans her upper body into a long side bend to the left, eases back to centre, and slowly leans to the right.
Middle balcony: a man with short dark hair in a rust-red tracksuit. He hangs in a deep forward fold with palms on the floor, then slowly rolls up through his spine to standing, and lifts his arms in one wide, slow circle overhead.
Bottom balcony: an older woman with short silver-grey hair in a cobalt blue short-sleeved polo and loose cream trousers. She holds a wide warrior lunge with arms stretched out to each side, slowly shifts her weight from one bent knee to the other, and gently sweeps one arm up and over her head into a side bend.
Each person moves at their own unhurried rhythm, slightly out of sync with each other, with full-body range of motion: knitwear and trousers stretching and settling, real balance and weight.

Camera, one continuous shot with no cuts:
0-3s: Wide establishing frame. The camera begins a slow, smooth orbit around the corner of the tower, arcing about 40 degrees, with strong parallax between the balconies, building face and sky.
3-5s: Still moving, the camera pushes in hard on the middle balcony until the man in the red tracksuit fills the frame alone, waist-up, mid-stretch, railing in the foreground.
5-7s: A steady vertical boom up the face of the building, past the concrete underside of the slab above, revealing the lilac woman mid-side-bend.
7-10s: A fast, controlled boom straight down past the middle balcony to the bottom one, revealing the older woman shifting through her lunge.
10-13s: Smooth pull back and reverse orbit, landing on the opening wide composition, all three still actively stretching.

Soft diffused daylight, gentle soft shadows under each slab, no hard sun. 35mm film look with fine grain. Stabilized crane/drone motion, never jittery.

Sound: natural diegetic location sound only — light wind gusting past the building, distant city hum, faint birds, soft fabric rustle. No music, no score, no singing, no melody, no rhythm track. No speech, no voices, no talking, no dialogue, no murmuring, no vocal sounds of any kind.

entries.description: Official ComfyUI reference template in the six-field Ref2VA format: subject_definitions list each reference's features "to follow exactly" (and drop the pilot photo's grey background), retention_analysis marks fully_preserved / attribute_transfer / weak_reference, and the description carries the camera from orbit into the bay (black frame at the threshold, lights coming up in rows) to a stop on the pilot at 4.5 s.
entries.prompt:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the station exterior in <Picture 2>. Reference role: form and material anchor. Features to follow exactly: a wide white saucer-shaped upper hull with visible panel seams and small antennas on top, a lit yellow-orange window band running around the rim, a cluster of white cylindrical modules hanging beneath the saucer with thin antenna spars at the bottom, weathered white paint with dark seams between plates, and the blue limb of a planet with white cloud bands behind it.
<Subject 2> is the pilot in <Picture 1>. Reference role: identity and gear anchor. Features to follow exactly: a dark matte flight helmet with a wide glossy black visor, one thin orange glowing ring on the left side of the visor and two horizontal orange glowing bars on the right side, a segmented metal collar ring under the jaw, and a bulky dark flight suit with a soft padded cowl. Do not carry over the light grey studio background of <Picture 1>.
<Subject 3> is the station interior, invented to match <Subject 1>: a dark rectangular hangar bay with ribbed white-metal walls, deep structural ribs, a grated catwalk running across the middle distance, small cargo clamps along the walls, and orange strip lights recessed between the ribs that match the colour of the pilot's visor glow.

summary:
[reference generation] A five-second single continuous shot: the station of <Picture 2> hangs in orbit, the camera pushes in toward its saucer rim, the bay mouth opens and the camera travels inside, where the hangar lights come up to reveal the pilot of <Picture 1> standing on the catwalk. Exterior and interior are one move, no cut.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - saucer hull, panel seams, yellow-orange rim band, hanging module cluster, antenna spars.
<Subject 2> (appears at the end of [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - helmet silhouette, glossy visor, the orange ring and two orange bars, collar ring and padded cowl.
<Subject 3> (appears at the end of [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - the ribbed white-metal language and window-band orange of <Subject 1> are carried inside as hull ribs and strip lights; the bay layout itself is new.
<Picture 1> background: weak_reference only - its light grey studio backdrop is discarded entirely.
No audio reference is used in this generation.

detailed_description:
Refined retro-futurist cinematography in a single unbroken move, cold blue ambient outside against warm orange interior light, deep blacks in both halves, fine grain and no lens flares; the camera is the only thing that travels and it never cuts.

[Shot 1] Wide establishing frame: the station of <Subject 1> hangs in the black, centred and slightly below eye level, the planet's blue limb and white cloud bands filling the lower third behind it. The saucer's rim band glows a soft orange, the hanging module cluster underneath reads as a dense white cylinder mass with thin spars, and the hull plates are weathered white with dark seams. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed, straight toward the saucer rim, and the station grows until the window band fills the upper half of the frame.

At about one and a half seconds a rectangular bay mouth opens in the rim below the band: two armour plates slide apart, spilling a warm orange rectangle of light into the vacuum, and a faint haze of vented gas drifts out of it. The camera does not stop and does not slow down; it continues into the opening, the frame going completely black for a beat as it crosses the threshold, then the interior lights of <Subject 3> come up in rows from the far end toward the lens, stripping in along the ribs one section at a time.

At about three seconds the camera is inside, gliding down the length of the ribbed hangar at chest height, the grated catwalk beneath it, cargo clamps and rib shadows sliding past on both sides, and the orange strip lights drawing long converging lines toward the far bulkhead. The camera decelerates and comes to rest at about four and a half seconds, framing <Subject 2> standing on the catwalk in three-quarter profile: dark helmet, glossy black visor with the orange ring and the two orange bars lit, padded cowl, suit reading as a soft dark mass against the white ribs. The last beat holds completely still while the pilot turns their head a few degrees toward the lens and the visor glow spills a thin orange edge onto the nearest rib.

overall_soundscape:
Deep vacuum silence outside with only a low sub-bass hum from the station's structure, then a hard change as the camera crosses the threshold: pressurised air rushing past the lens, the hydraulic whine of the bay plates closing behind, distant bulkhead clanks, the hum of the hangar settling into a steady tone, and one soft suit life-support hiss from the pilot at the end.

non_diegetic_music:
A slow retro synthwave pad that holds one low chord through the exterior, drops to near silence for the threshold crossing, and returns as a warm rising two-note figure as the hangar lights come up, ending on the held final frame.

entries.prompt:
DURATION: 15 SECONDS  
ASPECT RATIO: 16:9  
GENRE: Photorealistic cinematic science fiction / Mystery

VISUAL STYLE:

Ultra-photorealistic live-action science fiction, indistinguishable from a high-budget Hollywood film shot on ARRI Alexa 65 with anamorphic lenses. Physically accurate lighting, realistic human anatomy, natural skin textures, subtle film grain, atmospheric volumetric lighting, detailed metallic surfaces, realistic reflections and cinematic depth of field. No CGI-looking imagery, no animation, no stylization.

SCENE:

Deep inside an enormous abandoned alien spacecraft, a female astronaut in a weathered white exploration suit discovers a mysterious ancient machine. Her transparent helmet reveals a realistic human face, illuminated by the faint blue glow of her equipment. The vast alien architecture is covered in dust, strange geometric structures and dormant machinery.

0–3s: THE DISCOVERY

Wide cinematic tracking shot following the astronaut as she cautiously walks into a colossal dark chamber. Her helmet flashlight cuts through floating dust particles. The camera slowly moves around her, revealing the extraordinary scale of the alien architecture. Her footsteps echo across the metallic floor.

3–6s: THE SIGNAL

Close-up of the astronaut's face through her helmet visor. Her eyes widen as a faint blue light suddenly appears behind her. She turns naturally toward the source. Cut to an over-the-shoulder shot revealing an enormous circular alien machine beginning to glow in the darkness.

6–9s: THE ACTIVATION

The astronaut approaches the machine and carefully places her gloved hand against its surface. Thousands of intricate alien symbols illuminate beneath her fingers. A deep mechanical vibration travels through the chamber. Dust begins to rise from the floor as massive concentric rings slowly rotate overhead.

9–12s: THE AWAKENING

Suddenly, the entire chamber comes alive. Towering columns of blue-white energy ignite in sequence, illuminating the enormous alien structure. The camera rapidly pulls backward, revealing the astronaut as a tiny human figure beneath a gigantic rotating mechanism. Powerful atmospheric lighting, realistic debris and intense mechanical movement.

12–15s: THE REVELATION

An enormous alien eye opens at the center of the machine, its intricate biological iris contracting as it focuses directly on the astronaut. Extreme close-up of her terrified expression reflected in the helmet glass. Final wide shot: the colossal living machine watches her silently as the chamber pulses with cold blue light.

CINEMATOGRAPHY:

Sophisticated Hollywood camera language. Smooth dolly movements, precise rack focus, natural handheld micro-movements, realistic motion blur, dramatic wide-angle compositions and seamless spatial continuity. Physically believable interactions between the astronaut, machinery, lighting and environment.

AUDIO:

Deep atmospheric science-fiction sound design. Subtle breathing inside the astronaut's helmet, metallic footsteps, distant mechanical echoes, low-frequency vibrations, enormous rotating machinery and a powerful cinematic bass crescendo. No dialogue, no narration.

CRITICAL:

Maintain the exact same female astronaut, spacesuit and helmet throughout. Consistent spatial geography of the chamber and alien machine. Realistic human proportions, natural movement, accurate reflections and physically plausible lighting. The astronaut never removes her helmet. No duplicated characters, no morphing, no cartoon effects, no text, no subtitles.

entries.prompt:
DURATION: 15 SECONDS  
ASPECT RATIO: 9:16 VERTICAL  
MODE: TEXT TO VIDEO  
GENRE: Neo-noir anime / Gun-fu / Crime action

VISUAL STYLE:

Spectacular high-budget 1990s Japanese seinen anime OVA. Authentic hand-drawn 2D cel animation, gritty urban noir atmosphere, sharp expressive ink linework, dramatic shadows, richly painted backgrounds, sophisticated character animation and explosive sakuga action.

A stylish combination of grounded martial arts, realistic gunplay and dynamic cinematic editing. Deep midnight blues, warm amber lighting, crimson accents, subtle film grain and beautifully animated muzzle flashes.

SETTING:

A narrow, dimly lit apartment hallway in Tokyo at night. Flickering fluorescent lights, wooden doors, scattered debris, rain visible through a window at the far end.

CHARACTERS:

The protagonist is a lean Japanese hitman in his thirties, with messy black hair, sharp facial features, a black suit, loosened tie and white shirt. He carries a black semi-automatic pistol.

Two armed assassins wearing dark tactical clothing confront him inside the corridor.

0–3s — THE FIRST SHOT

Extreme close-up of the protagonist's narrowed eyes.

A sudden gunshot tears through the silence.

Smash cut to a dramatic low-angle shot: the protagonist twists sideways as a bullet shatters the wooden doorframe beside his head.

He immediately raises his pistol and fires twice toward the first attacker.

Brilliant muzzle flashes illuminate the narrow corridor.

3–6s — CLOSE-QUARTERS GUN-FU

The second attacker rushes toward him.

The protagonist deflects the attacker's pistol arm with his left forearm, steps inside his guard and delivers a brutal elbow strike to his face.

Without breaking the movement, he grabs the attacker's jacket, pivots and throws him against the corridor wall.

Dynamic lateral tracking shot, sharp anime impact frames, convincing physical contact.

6–9s — THE COUNTERATTACK

The first attacker fires again from the far end of the corridor.

The protagonist ducks behind the fallen attacker, then slides sideways across the wooden floor.

A spectacular low-angle tracking shot follows him as he fires two precise shots while sliding.

Bullets strike the wall behind his opponent, sending wood splinters flying.

The first attacker staggers and falls out of frame.

9–12s — THE FINAL EXCHANGE

The second attacker recovers and lunges at the protagonist.

A rapid sequence of beautifully choreographed close-ups: a wrist grab, a blocked punch, a sharp knee strike.

The protagonist spins behind his opponent, forces the attacker's gun arm downward and delivers one final close-range shot toward the floor, narrowly missing him.

The attacker drops his weapon and collapses to his knees.

12–15s — THE SILENCE

Sudden silence.

Low-angle close-up of the protagonist, breathing heavily, his black hair falling across his eyes.

Smoke rises from his pistol.

The camera slowly pushes toward his face as he adjusts his loosened tie with his free hand.

Behind him, the corridor lights flicker and finally go dark.

A final flash of lightning illuminates his silhouette.

Cut to black.

CINEMATOGRAPHY AND EDITING:

Extremely dynamic cinematic montage with aggressive whip pans, dramatic low angles, extreme close-ups, fast lateral tracking shots and powerful perspective changes.

The 9:16 vertical composition must be used creatively: dramatic full-body shots, strong foreground-background separation, narrow architectural framing and intense vertical camera movements.

Fast, readable action with exceptional timing, momentum and visual clarity.

No slow motion. Every second must feel energetic and purposeful.

ANIMATION DIRECTION:

Premium hand-drawn sakuga animation with convincing body mechanics, expressive facial acting, sharp silhouettes, powerful impact frames, realistic weapon recoil and fluid transitions between shooting and martial arts.

Every physical interaction must have clear cause and effect.

AUDIO:

Sharp, powerful gunshots with realistic indoor echoes, metallic shell casings hitting the floor, heavy footsteps, brutal physical impacts, splintering wood and intense industrial percussion.

The soundtrack stops abruptly for the final three seconds.

No dialogue.

CRITICAL:

Strict 9:16 vertical framing throughout.

Exactly three characters: one protagonist and two attackers.

Maintain consistent character designs, clothing, weapons and spatial relationships.

The protagonist carries exactly one pistol throughout the entire sequence.

No duplicated characters, no extra limbs, no teleportation, no disconnected strikes, no floating weapons.

Authentic traditional 2D Japanese anime only. No CGI, no 3D rendering, no photorealism, no text, no subtitles.

entries.prompt: Low quality raw phone video, natural indoor lighting, handheld with slight shake, casual unpolished home-video color grading. A man sits on a couch holding a plate of fried chicken, a small tan chihuahua sitting upright directly in front of him on the cushion, staring fixated at the food. The man lifts a piece of chicken slowly and takes an exaggerated bite just inches from the dog’s face, then deliberately turns his head away, chewing with a smug expression, fully ignoring the dog. The chihuahua’s eyes track the chicken with unblinking intensity, ears pinned forward, front paws lifting off the cushion in small desperate hops. The man glances down, smirks at the dog, and holds another piece just above its nose — then pulls it back sharply at the last second before the dog can grab it. The chihuahua lunges forward with a quick snap of its head, missing the chicken by a fraction, and freezes mid-air with an outraged, betrayed expression. It immediately erupts into a burst of rapid, high-pitched indignant barks, spinning in a tight frustrated circle on the couch. The man laughs, clearly enjoying the tease, taking another bite while the dog continues staring up at him with pure betrayal.
