entries.title: Seedance 2.5 DV gym comeback vlog: tape-camcorder selfie under overhead fluorescents, mirror rule and a 10-cut storyboard
entries.description: The same DV vlog template applied to a first gym session after months away. CAMERA bans the camcorder from the frame and from the mirror reflection, and turns going hands-free into the picture swinging and settling. LOOK asks for faint tape noise, mild highlight bloom under the overhead lights, subtle auto-exposure flicker and muted contrast. The FINAL INSTRUCTION fixes the ending ("the recording ends on her face … never cuts away to an empty room").
entries.prompt:
CAMERA:
DV tape camcorder handheld aesthetic. A woman films herself directly by hand in selfie-cam and first-person style through her first gym session after months away. Keep realistic hand shake, slightly crooked framing, delayed autofocus, awkward zoom-ins and zoom-outs, occasional motion blur, and small framing mistakes where part of her face briefly slips out of frame. Mix handheld selfie footage with fixed external shots. ABSOLUTE RULE: no camera, camcorder, phone or recording device ever appears in the frame, in her hands, on any surface, or in the mirror reflection — her hands are always empty of equipment. Everything is seen from the recording camera's own point of view. When the shot becomes hands-free, do NOT show her putting anything down: the IMAGE ITSELF swings, tips and settles on a surface, and we understand what happened purely from what the picture does. When switching from handheld to a fixed external angle, use a clean jump cut as if the camera had already been positioned before the shot began. The camcorder itself is never visible on screen.

LOOK:
Soft digital tape camcorder look with subtle vintage DV character. Slight blur, faint tape noise, mild highlight bloom under the overhead lights, subtle auto-exposure flicker, muted contrast, realistic skin texture, believable indoor lighting. The room is an ordinary everyday gym and nothing in it is designed or boutique — the colour does all the work: warm sodium overhead strip light, one crimson exercise mat on black rubber flooring, cobalt-blue padded equipment, a single bright yellow towel. Saturated primaries sitting inside a completely plain room.

STYLE:
A realistic late-night gym vlog. The tone is dry, sheepish, slightly breathless and very natural. She is charismatic and funny about herself, but it must read as a genuine self-recorded vlog and never as a commercial or a fitness advert. Clean jump cuts, strong continuity, natural body language, no dead moments.

CHARACTER:
The woman in @Image1. Keep her face, hair and wardrobe exactly as shown: a French-Algerian woman in her mid-thirties, warm olive skin, a sharp jaw, a small scar through one eyebrow, deep-set dark eyes, hair scraped back into a low ponytail, no makeup, visible skin texture, wearing a plain black long-sleeve athletic top and black leggings, white trainers, and a bright yellow towel over one shoulder. She is distinctive and real — never a smoothed or symmetrical face.

SETTING:
An ordinary municipal gym late at night, almost empty. The main floor with its mirror wall, dumbbell rack, flat bench, crimson mat and water bottle is @Image2. The plain entrance corridor with lockers and double doors is @Image3. Nothing boutique, nothing branded. No trainer, no crowd, no other people.

IMPORTANT CONTINUITY RULES:
The same woman remains fully consistent in every shot: same face, same low ponytail, same black top and leggings, same yellow towel. No duplicated limbs, no broken hands, no broken gym equipment, no impossible movements. The water bottle stays on the bench until she picks it up at cut 7. The dumbbells she picks up at cut 4 are the same pair she puts down at cut 5. Her breathing gets progressively heavier from cut 5 onward and never resets, and from cut 7 she is visibly sweating, with the sweat and flush increasing through to the final frame. No camera visible, no camera setup shown, no other people.

STORYBOARD (30 seconds total, 10 cuts):

1. (~3s, arm's-length selfie) She walks in filming herself, shoulders slightly hunched, sheepish. Dialogue: "Right. First time back in… we don't say the number out loud."

2. (~3s, handheld pan across the room and back to her) The camera drifts across the dumbbell rack, the mirror wall and the empty floor, then returns to her face. Dialogue: "Nobody here. Which is exactly how I planned it."

3. (~4s, handheld arm's-length selfie at the mirror) She stops at the mirror holding the camera herself at arm's length, reaches up with her free hand and tightens the ponytail, and catches her own eye in the glass. Then, on the last word, the IMAGE ITSELF swings down, tips over and settles at a wonky angle resting on the end of the bench, still running — she has freed up both hands. No camera is ever seen. Dialogue: "I look like someone about to make a mistake."

4. (~3s, from the wonky resting angle on the bench) Continuing from where the image came to rest. She steps back into frame, picks up two dumbbells and tests the weight in one hand before committing. No dialogue.

5. (~4s, same resting angle) She performs a short set of presses. It is visibly harder than she expected: the first rep is clean, the second slows, and the third she has to grind out, arms shaking slightly at the top. She drops the weights down to her chest and then to the floor, doubles over her knees and laughs at herself while completely out of breath. The line is broken up by real effort — grunting, gasping and a breathless laugh between the words, not delivered cleanly. Dialogue, breathless and grunting through it: "Whoo— (grunts) okay. Okay, that's— (huffs) that's it. Too much. (breathless chuckle) Whew."

6. (~3s, handheld walking selfie) Back in selfie mode, towel over one shoulder, walking it off, breathing noticeably harder. Dialogue: "My arms have filed a complaint."

7. (~3s, tight handheld close-up) She picks up the water bottle, drinks, lowers it and exhales in relief. Dialogue: "This is the part I'm actually good at."

8. (~3s, fixed external wider shot facing the mirror) Jump cut to a fixed shot. She does a short stretch, catches her own reflection, and laughs at herself, looking away from the lens to do it. Dialogue: "Stretching. So it counts as a real session."

9. (~3s, handheld close selfie, extreme close on her face) She is visibly worked: skin shining with sweat, a damp hairline with short strands stuck to her temples and the back of her neck, deep colour high in her cheeks, chest still moving with her breathing, one bead of sweat at the jaw. She pushes a stuck strand of hair off her forehead with the back of her wrist, tired and quietly pleased. Dialogue: "I said twenty minutes. It's been fifty."

10. (~3s, arm's-length selfie ending) She walks out through the corridor still filming herself, still flushed and damp, and gives a small genuine smile straight into the lens. She stays in frame for the whole shot — the film ends on HER face, never on an empty room. Dialogue: "Same time Thursday. Probably. Night."

ACTING NUANCE:
The sheepishness at cut 1 lives in her shoulders, not in her voice. At cut 4 she genuinely weighs the dumbbell in one hand before she commits to it. Cut 5 is the honest beat of the whole film: the effort is real and it beats her, her arms shake on the last rep, and the breathing is LOUDER than the words — she is fighting to get the sentence out between gasps rather than speaking over the top of them. The laugh at the end of it is genuine self-mockery, aimed at nobody. At cut 8 the laugh is at herself and she breaks eye contact with the lens to do it. At cut 10 the smile is small and real, not a performed sign-off. The sweat and the flush do not disappear between cuts 9 and 10 — she is still recovering right through the last frame.

AUDIO:
Trainers squeaking on rubber flooring, a small dull knock as the recording is rested on the bench at cut 3, the heavy clack of dumbbells hitting the floor at cut 5, the dull clack of dumbbells being set back on the rack, a constant low air-handling hum, her breathing getting progressively heavier from cut 5, the crackle of a plastic bottle, a distant door closing somewhere in the building, and the slight room reverb of a large empty space. Her voice is close and slightly clipped by the camcorder's own microphone. No music of any kind: this is a self-recorded vlog and it does not score itself. Do not add any instrumental score, soundtrack or background music.

FINAL INSTRUCTION:
The result must feel like a real self-recorded late-night gym vlog in an ordinary gym. Prioritise realistic handheld motion, strong continuity, believable pacing, natural breathing and subtle imperfection. The ending is complete, not cut off: she delivers the final line to the lens, holds her own gaze for a beat, and the recording ends on her face. This is a selfie vlog, so it never cuts away to an empty room. No subtitles.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 DV "first morning in a new flat" vlog: autofocus that hunts and settles, exposure breathing between window and shade, saturated set colour
entries.description: A shorter version of the DV vlog template. The LOOK block links the camera behaviour to the light: "subtle auto-exposure breathing as she moves between the bright window and the shaded room" and highlight bloom "where hard morning light enters". Colour comes from the set, not a grade (crimson bedroom wall, cobalt bathroom tiles, one acid-yellow chair, terracotta floor; "Colour is the emotional temperature of the film"). It has a 10-cut storyboard and ends on a held beat at the balcony railing.
entries.prompt:
CAMERA:
DV tape camcorder handheld aesthetic. A woman films herself in selfie-cam and first-person style through her first morning in a flat she has just moved into. Keep realistic hand shake, slightly crooked framing, delayed autofocus that hunts and then settles, occasional motion blur, and small framing mistakes where part of her face briefly slips out of frame. Mix handheld selfie footage with fixed external shots. Never show her placing, adjusting or setting up a camera. When switching from handheld to a fixed external angle, use a clean jump cut as if the camera had already been positioned before the shot began. The camcorder itself is never visible on screen.

LOOK:
Soft digital tape camcorder look with subtle vintage DV character. Slight blur, faint tape noise, mild highlight bloom where hard morning light enters, subtle auto-exposure breathing as she moves between the bright window and the shaded room, muted contrast, realistic skin texture, believable interior colour. Saturated primaries carried by the set itself against a domestic interior: a deep crimson bedroom wall, glossy cobalt bathroom tiles, one acid-yellow kitchen chair, warm terracotta floors. Colour is the emotional temperature of the film.

STYLE:
A realistic first-morning-in-a-new-flat vlog. The tone is warm, a little tired, self-deprecating and completely natural. She is charismatic and talks to the lens like a friend, but it must read as a genuine self-recorded vlog and never as a commercial. Clean jump cuts, strong continuity, natural morning movement, no dead moments.

CHARACTER:
The woman in @Image1. Keep her face, hair and wardrobe exactly as shown: a Spanish woman in her early thirties, olive skin, a strong prominent nose, a wide gap-toothed smile, thick untamed brows, hair in a slept-in bun with strands escaping, no makeup, a small mole on one cheek, wearing an oversized man's white shirt over cotton shorts, barefoot. She is distinctive and real, with visible skin texture — never a smoothed or symmetrical face. The slept-in hair stays flattened on one side for the whole film and is never fixed.

SETTING:
A small apartment on moving-in day, still half unpacked. The bedroom is @Image2, the bathroom is @Image3, the kitchen is @Image4, the balcony is @Image5. Cardboard boxes, newspaper wrapping and bare shelves throughout. Warm morning light. No other people anywhere in the film.

IMPORTANT CONTINUITY RULES:
The same woman remains fully consistent in every shot: same face, same slept-in bun, same white shirt, same bare feet. No duplicated limbs, no broken hands. The boxes stay in the same places. Once she is dressed at cut 8 she stays dressed. The coffee pot she finds at cut 4 is the same one on the hob at cut 5 and the same cup in her hand at cuts 9 and 10. No camera visible, no camera setup shown, no other people.

STORYBOARD (30 seconds total, 10 cuts):

1. (~3s, arm's-length selfie, bed) She wakes among boxes, hair flattened on one side, squinting, and pushes herself upright. Dialogue: "Okay… first morning here officially."

2. (~3s, handheld) She pulls a bedsheet down off the window it was pinned over and hard morning light floods the crimson wall. Dialogue: "Bedsheet as a curtain for now... we'll figure it out tomorrow." She says as she chuckles.

3. (~3s, mirror) Bathroom, cobalt tiles. She is brushing her teeth and does NOT stop or take the brush out to speak — she talks around it with a mouthful of foam, so the line comes out thick, muffled and half-swallowed, genuinely hard to make out. Dialogue, garbled through toothbrush and foam: "I still don't know which tap is hot."

4. (~3s, fixed external, kitchen) Jump cut to a fixed shot already in place. She is at the counter digging through an open box, newspaper spilling out. Dialogue: "Somewhere in here there is a coffee pot."

5. (~3s, same fixed shot) She lifts the coffee pot out, sets it on the hob, lights it, and leans back against the counter to wait. Dialogue: "Found it. This flat is forgiven."

6. (~3s, handheld walking) She moves through the room pushing windows open and nudging a box aside with her bare foot. Dialogue: "Right. Let's make it look like someone lives here."

7. (~3s, frontal shot facing her) She sits on the floor against the acid-yellow chair, framed head-on from the front, and unwraps a single framed photograph from its newspaper. She stops moving completely and her voice drops. Then she turns the photograph around and holds it up toward the lens to show it to the camera, looking over the top of it. Dialogue: "This one goes up first. Always."

8. (~3s, fixed external, bedroom) Jump cut to a fixed shot. She is already dressed, flattening the duvet with both hands, then sits down on it and looks around the room. No dialogue.

9. (~3s, close selfie at the window) Coffee in hand, light across her face, a slow real smile arriving. Dialogue: "Yeah. I think this is going to be alright."

10. (~3s, arm's-length selfie, balcony) She steps out, leans on the iron railing, looks down at the street for a beat, then back to the lens. Dialogue: "New street. Same me. Let's go."

ACTING NUANCE:
The flattened hair is never fixed. At cut 3 she talks through the toothbrush and does not stop to spit. Cut 7 is the only moment in the film she stops moving, and the camera goes still with her. She unwraps carefully, looks at the photograph for a beat before anyone else can see it, and only then turns it out to the lens — the showing is a small act of trust, not a presentation. At cut 9 the smile arrives late, a beat after she starts speaking. At cut 10 she looks down at the street first and only then delivers the line — the line is a decision, not a reaction.

AUDIO:
Room tone with the slightly hollow echo of an empty flat. Packing tape peeling off cardboard, bare feet on tile, the gas hob ticking and then catching, a coffee pot gurgling and rising to a hiss around 15 seconds, newspaper crumpling at cut 7, window latches, and street noise arriving from outside only when the balcony door opens at cut 10. Her voice is close and slightly clipped by the camcorder's own microphone, with the level jumping when she turns toward it. At cut 3 the words are genuinely obstructed by the toothbrush and foam — thick, wet and indistinct rather than clean speech, with brushing sound continuing underneath the whole line. No music of any kind: this is a self-recorded vlog and it does not score itself. Do not add any instrumental score, soundtrack or background music.

FINAL INSTRUCTION:
The result must feel like a real self-recorded first-morning vlog. Prioritise realistic handheld motion, strong continuity, natural speech pacing, authentic home ambience and subtle imperfection. The ending is complete, not cut off: she leans on the railing, delivers the final line, and the recording holds on her for a full beat before it ends. No subtitles.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 locked-off vintage-pool film: 35 mm colour-negative texture, exactly two cuts and one handbag-placement insert
entries.description: A 20-second piece about edit discipline: one locked-off master, one close-up insert of a burgundy handbag being placed on a bench, then back to the identical wide for the rest. The texture is written as "Photorealistic 35mm color-negative film texture: fine organic grain, gentle contrast, soft highlight roll-off, subtle halation". The closing paragraph locks the count ("Exactly two clean cuts … no camera movement") and keeps the bag still once placed.
entries.prompt:
Use Image 1 for the vintage indoor pool, centered bench, architecture, lighting, and colors. Use Image 2 for the adult woman’s identity, dark teal athletic one-piece swimsuit, ivory swim cap, bare feet, and burgundy handbag. Do not reproduce the character sheet’s white background or multiple views.
20 seconds, 16:9. A locked-off master shot with one handbag-placement close-up insert. Exactly two cuts: into the close-up, then back to the original wide shot. Everything after returning to the wide shot plays continuously without further cuts or camera movement.
Photorealistic 35mm color-negative film texture: fine organic grain, gentle contrast, soft highlight roll-off, subtle halation around bright windows, restrained saturation, and natural skin tones. Muted mustard walls, creamy whites, and turquoise water.
The master camera is locked on a tripod across the pool, facing the central bench. Water fills the foreground, with the bench and dry walkway behind it. Preserve the exact framing, camera angle, and focal length when returning from the close-up. No zooms, pans, tilts, tracking, or dolly movements.
0–3s — Fixed wide shot:
Already wearing her swimsuit and ivory swim cap, the woman enters from screen left, barefoot, carrying the burgundy handbag by its short handle in her left hand. She walks to the central bench without sitting down. She brings the handbag just above the seat, preparing to set it down.
3–5s — Handbag-placement close-up:
Cut on the lowering action to a fixed close-up of her hands, the handbag, and the wooden bench seat. Her left hand holds the handle while her right hand steadies the bag’s side. entries.prompt:
Create a 10-second, 16:9 retro fashion-editorial film with five shots in this exact order: wide shot → facial close-up → medium shot → oar-blade close-up → wide shot.

REFERENCE MAPPING
Use  only for the woman's identity, long chestnut waves, cobalt-blue pantsuit, ivory top and oxblood shoes. Show one woman, never the character-sheet layout.
Use  for the distant, left-facing boat, boathouse architecture, lighting and rich colors. Treat it as a location reference; the woman is already seated and rowing in the opening shot.

VISUAL STYLE AND CAMERA
Rich golden-ochre plaster, dark-green shutters, petrol-teal water and cobalt-blue tailoring. Soft directional daylight, tactile wool and varnished wood, subtle color-negative film texture. Maintain consistent color and exposure across cuts.

Shoot every shot from the SAME SIDE of the boat. Keep the camera perpendicular to the boat’s length: strict side profile, including a profile view of her face. Do not orbit, cross the action axis, or switch to frontal or three-quarter angles.

The pointed bow faces SCREEN LEFT. The boat travels LEFT, parallel to the facade. She sits on the central fixed rowing bench facing the stern, SCREEN RIGHT, opposite the direction of travel. Track left alongside the boat to keep the subject centered. Change shot size through cuts, not zooms.

ROWING ACTION
She rows continuously with confident, brisk strokes, approximately one complete cycle every two seconds. Use natural real-time motion, not accelerated playback. Both oars pivot in fixed oarlocks: blades enter together, push water toward the stern, lift clear, feather flat, then recover.

Her feet remain braced and the seat stays fixed. Arms and a controlled forward-backward torso hinge provide the effort. Show visible leftward travel and a wake trailing right. Cuts continue the ongoing action rather than restarting each stroke.

0.0–2.0s — DISTANT WIDE SHOT
Show the complete boat in strict side profile, occupying approximately 38% of the frame width, centered slightly below the middle. Establish the broad ochre facade and generous foreground water. She is already rowing briskly. Track left at the boat’s speed, keeping it centered as the windows slide right behind her. Begin immediately with a crisp splash, warm bass and a 120-BPM vintage percussion groove.

2.0–3.2s — PROFILE EXPRESSION CLOSE-UP
Hard cut to her face in clear side profile from the same side. Continue tracking left with the boat. She looks screen-right with focused eyes and a relaxed mouth, exhaling lightly with the effort. Long hair moves gently toward the stern. Her shoulders continue the rowing motion; she never pauses to pose or turns toward the camera. The ochre wall passes softly behind her.

3.2–5.4s — SIDE MEDIUM SHOT
Hard cut to a strict side medium shot including her head, torso, hands, handles and central seat. Track left alongside her. Show a brisk rowing cycle: arms extend, blades catch, handles draw toward her lower ribs, torso hinges slightly backward, hands lower to lift the blades, then arms extend into recovery. The blue jacket folds naturally at elbows and shoulders. Continue smoothly from the previous shot.

5.4–7.0s — OAR-BLADE CLOSE-UP
Hard cut to the near-side blade and water, lowering the camera while remaining on the same side. Track left with the boat. The blade catches firmly, pushes water toward the stern, raises a compact splash, then lifts and feathers as droplets fall. Show believable water resistance and movement around the fixed oarlock. Emphasize the synchronized entry and release sounds; briefly lower the music beneath them.

7.0–10.0s — RETURN TO DISTANT WIDE SHOT
Hard cut back to the opening side-profile wide composition, the boat again approximately 38% of frame width. Continue tracking left at matching speed. She keeps rowing briskly without resting. The facade moves right behind her and a longer, finely rippled wake trails the stern. End with a clear blade entry and a musical accent while the boat remains in motion.

Use clean hard cuts connected by continuous action and water sounds. Preserve the same face, long hair, suit, boat, two oars and leftward direction. No dialogue, captions, logos, additional people, orbiting camera, frontal portrait, slow motion or speed ramps.

entries.description: A 12k-character fashion advertisement with one adult model in every shot. entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second, 16:9 high-fashion Neo-Chinese fashion advertisement. The entire film features only one adult female model, and the model must appear in every shot.
Strictly separate the functions of the reference images:
@Image1 simultaneously and exclusively defines the model’s identity, face shape, facial features, skin tone, original freckle density, original makeup, lip color, refined center-parted black hair, low looped bun, and the large asymmetric hand-blown glass headpiece and nails on the same side. However, the nails should preferably remain understated and not overly visible.
Preserve the face and original makeup from @Image1 completely. Do not add green or pink eyeshadow, intensify the blush, or change the eyebrows, eye shape, or lip color. Do not copy the clothing or background from @Image1.
@Image2 exclusively defines the complete outfit and footwear: a straight black velvet Neo-Chinese qipao, high Mandarin collar, black frog closures, asymmetric dark-green jacquard overlay and draping, restrained water-lily embroidery, and black velvet square-toe flats. Lock the exact same garment structure, embroidery placement, draping, dress length, and shoes throughout the film.
@Image3 exclusively defines the minimalist contemporary Chinese courtyard.
@Image4 exclusively defines the small circular platform in the lake and its surrounding rocky landscape.
@Image5 exclusively defines the overhead water-lily pond, including the water surface, flower shapes, and evenly spaced arrangement.
@Image6 exclusively defines the realistic three-dimensional structure, thickness, curled edges, and moist material of the giant water-lily interior.
The environmental reference images must not alter the model’s identity, makeup, hairstyle, headpiece, nails, or clothing.
The large glass headpiece must retain exactly the same shape, scale, position, and materials throughout the film: translucent smoky-green tendrils, clear curved spikes, pale tea-amber droplets, dark-red glass spheres, trapped air bubbles, and molten folds. The headpiece must always remain clearly visible, but it must never cover the eyes, nose, or mouth.
Editing language: powerful yet restrained high-fashion advertising. Use direct hard cuts between scenes, alternating extreme wide shots, medium shots, facial close-ups, fabric macro shots, and embroidery macro shots. Use fast but controlled handheld tracking, short push-ins, 20–30-degree short-arc orbits, and low-angle upward camera movement.
Avoid prolonged exploratory camera movement, bullet time, freeze frames, and flash transitions. The model performs clear, independent, readable editorial cover poses. She does not dance or perform a continuous series of strange poses. Every shot must clearly display at least one of the following: the clothing, headpiece, nails, or footwear.
Editing language: forceful high-fashion advertising. Use direct hard cuts between scenes, alternating extreme wide shots, medium shots, facial close-ups, fabric macro shots, and embroidery macro shots. Use fast but controlled handheld tracking, whip pans, rapid push-ins, short parallax orbits, and low-angle rush-ins.
Do not use empty establishing shots. The model must already be visible in the first frame of every new scene. Do not use freeze frames, rigid pauses, dissolves, flash transitions, or slow continuous exploratory camera movement. The model performs clear, independent, readable editorial cover poses. She does not dance or perform a continuous series of strange poses. Every shot must show the clothing, headpiece, nails, or shoes.
0.0–3.0 seconds｜Water-lily pond
The model stands at the center of the dark-green water-lily pond from @Image5, viewed from directly overhead.
Numerous ivory-white water lilies with pink centers bloom rapidly and simultaneously in concentric circles radiating outward from her. The movement of the water follows realistic physical behavior.
The aerial camera descends rapidly and pushes toward her. She looks upward and quickly opens both arms once, clearly revealing the qipao silhouette and asymmetric draping.
3.0–5.5 seconds｜Water-level portrait
Hard cut to a handheld three-quarter close shot at water level.
The camera performs one fast clockwise short-arc orbit, fully revealing the dramatic glass headpiece. She quickly shifts her gaze toward the camera while her right hand sweeps from the high collar to the shoulder line within 0.6 seconds.
Her nails remain clearly visible and consistent in appearance.
5.5–9.0 seconds｜First fashion montage
@Image1 + @Image2.
Begin with two fast close-ups: the transparent nail extensions quickly pass over the frog closure at the collar, followed by both hands sweeping outward once across the dark-green waist area.
Then begin the first rapid fashion montage. Alternate direct hard cuts lasting 0.3–0.5 seconds:
Eyes and lips → transparent fingertips and nails → dark-green jacquard overlay → water-lily embroidery → black square-toe flats stepping through shallow water.
Do not repeat the stroking action. The face, hands, fabric, and embroidery should create a clear visual rhythm.
9.0–13.0 seconds｜Inside the giant flower
@Image1 + @Image2 + @Image6.
The model is already reclining diagonally inside the giant flower from @Image6, resting on petals that transition from ivory white to pale pink.
A low-angle camera rapidly rushes toward her, then shifts into a fast 25-degree orbit. She turns toward the camera while one hand quickly travels from the high collar, across the black velvet bodice, and toward the waist draping.
Hard cut: she is now standing at the center of the flower. Her weight shifts to one side, one hand rests at her waist, and the other creates a clean, graphic line beside her face.
At this moment, the petals expand once in a slow, breathing motion.
Cut again to a two-thirds side angle. She lifts her chin and looks directly into the camera.
Directly hard-cut between a low-angle wide shot, a side medium shot, and a steep overhead shot. Her movements should resemble an editorial fashion shoot rather than a dance or a simple sequence of touching the clothing.
13.0–14.0 seconds｜Transition montage
A rapid transitional montage of four short hard cuts:
Frontal face → glass headpiece → water-lily embroidery → black flats.
14.0–18.0 seconds｜Small platform in the lake
@Image1 + @Image2 + @Image4.
14.0–15.0 seconds: A strictly symmetrical 24mm extreme wide shot with the camera completely locked.
The model stands facing forward and performs one slight shoulder turn. Preserve natural breathing and subtle movement in the fabric and draping. The small circular platform is surrounded by dark-green lake water and warm-toned rocks.
15.0–16.2 seconds: Hard cut on the action to a 50mm three-quarter medium close shot.
The handheld camera moves laterally from the model’s left side to directly in front of her. At the same time, she shifts her weight to one side, turns her shoulders into a three-quarter angle, and places one hand at her waist, creating a sharp editorial pose.
16.2–17.0 seconds: Hard cut to an 85mm close-up of her face and glass headpiece.
The camera rapidly pushes in and then stops immediately. She raises her chin slightly and turns her gaze directly toward the lens.
Preserve her original makeup. Do not add new green or pink eyeshadow. The complete glass headpiece remains clearly visible without covering her facial features.
17.0–18.0 seconds: Hard cut to a slightly low-angle medium close shot.
The camera rapidly pulls backward as she takes one step toward the lens. The black velvet qipao, dark-green draping, and embroidery move with realistic weight and physical behavior.
18.0–30.0 seconds｜Chinese courtyard
@Image1 + @Image2 + @Image3.
The model remains in the shallow water in front of the moon gate, maintaining exactly the same face, original makeup, glass headpiece, transparent nail extensions, outfit, and courtyard environment.
18.0–19.4 seconds: Symmetrical wide shot.
With her back toward the camera, she walks through the shallow water toward the moon gate. The fabric and reflections on the water move subtly with each step.
19.4–20.8 seconds: Hard cut to a side medium shot.
She continues walking along the water’s edge as the camera rapidly tracks laterally beside her. She then partially turns back and looks directly into the camera.
20.8–22.0 seconds: Hard cut to an over-the-shoulder medium close shot.
She initially faces away from the camera, then turns her eyes and chin back toward the lens. The camera remains behind her shoulder, and the complete glass headpiece stays visible.
22.0–23.0 seconds: Frontal knee-up medium shot.
Her transparent nail extensions quickly move from the high collar across the frog closures and slide toward the asymmetric waist overlay. The camera follows the hand diagonally downward.
At the end of the movement, she turns into a three-quarter angle.
23.0–25.0 seconds｜Rapid close-up and wide-shot montage
Each shot lasts approximately 0.25 seconds. Use direct hard cuts, alternating close-ups with wide shots containing the model.
The model may hold editorial poses with subtle, natural movement. Every shot must use a different angle and composition. Do not use @Image5.
@Image1 frontal facial close-up → @Image4 symmetrical extreme wide shot of the model on the lake platform → @Image1 side facial close-up with transparent nail extensions visible → @Image3 wide shot of the model in the moon-gate courtyard → @Image1 close-up of the face and complete glass headpiece → @Image6 low-angle full-body wide shot of the model inside the giant water lily → @Image1 facial close-up → @Image3 symmetrical wide shot of the model centered inside the moon gate.
Maintain the same model, original makeup, glass headpiece, and clothing. Every wide shot must contain the model. Do not repeat shots or merge the environments.
25.0–27.5 seconds｜Return to the courtyard
Return clearly to the Chinese courtyard from @Image3.
Rapidly push from a low-angle full-body shot into a waist close-up. Her transparent nail extensions quickly trace downward along the water-lily embroidery as the camera moves synchronously toward the hem.
Ivory-white water lilies bloom evenly across the dark-green water surrounding her. The flowers must not be too dense or obscure the clothing.
27.5–30.0 seconds｜Final cover portrait
Perform one tight, short-distance orbit around her face and glass headpiece.
Finish by returning to a frontal, knee-up editorial cover composition. Her weight shifts slightly to one side. One hand rests at her waist while the other forms a simple, clean line. She looks directly into the camera.
Preserve subtle movement in her breathing, clothing, water, and petals, then freeze the frame.
Visual style
A Hasselblad medium-format 120-film fashion editorial. Slightly underexposed with clean, restrained contrast and fine, irregular film grain.
Creamy ivory highlights, warm beige stone walls, gray sage-green and dark-green midtones, and dense black velvet shadows. The skin, glass, water, embroidery, transparent nails, and fabric textures must appear physically realistic.
The overall rhythm is fast while keeping the clothing information clear and readable.
Music
Restrained modern minimalist electronic music at 110 BPM.
Soft low-frequency pulses, sparse wooden percussion, airy analog synthesizer drones, and very occasional short glass-like tones.
The rapid editing may follow the beat subtly, but do not add a strong accent to every hard cut.
No guqin, traditional Chinese opera melodies, grand orchestral music, or vocals.
Environmental sound
Extremely subtle water ripples, velvet and jacquard fabric movement, flat shoes contacting the ground, delicate resonance from the glass headpiece, and soft moist friction as the petals open.
The sounds should feel intimate, restrained, and realistic.
No exaggerated impacts, enormous whooshes, dramatic risers, or dialogue.
Avoid
Empty shots, additional people, duplicated models, outfit changes, missing or reduced headpiece, headpiece covering the face, inconsistent nails, bare feet, furniture, malformed hands, duplicated limbs, slow motion, dancing, magical particles, freeze frames, text, subtitles, or a generated logo.

entries.prompt:
FILM 15 — Sundial Silk — She Measures the Sun

References: @Image1 defines the exact same single North African–Italian fashion figure, her distinctive face, amber eyes, silver-streaked long curls, turquoise drop earrings, terracotta silk cape dress, cream geometric belt and leather sandals. Its three panels are views of one person, never three people or a sheet layout inside the film. @Image2 defines the exact terracotta modernist courtyard with cream stone, turquoise pool, sculptural pine, agave, wooden doors, hard blue sky and sharp architectural sunlight. @Image3 defines the exact turquoise-tiled rooftop garden with cream pergola, terracotta pots, roses, sea horizon and central stone sundial at golden hour. All references lock identity, wardrobe, architecture, palette, materials and sunlight character. The only new hero object is one consistent pair of sculptural translucent amber acetate sunglasses with smoke-brown lenses, subtle upswept geometry, no visible logo and physically plausible hinges. Pinterest-derived end-card direction: restrained 1960s Italian optical-ad typography, one refined high-contrast modern serif, generous tracking, asymmetrical negative space and no decorative badge.

Subject: A high-fashion sunglasses reveal in which every preceding image studies a different behaviour of the sun: reflection, architecture, shadow, heat, translucency, time, glare and horizon. The same woman follows a causal path made by sunlight from the midday courtyard of @Image2 to the golden-hour sundial terrace of @Image3. Sunlight controls the film until the final product reveal lets her look back at it calmly. The sunglasses remain completely unseen before the final reveal. Fine tactile 35mm grain, natural mature skin, shaped blacks, sun halation, terracotta silk, turquoise water, cream stone, amber light and deep smoke-brown lenses; no generic resort imagery.

Action: The camera discovers the white sun reflected as a perfect circle in the turquoise pool. A ripple divides it and the circle reforms. Match cut to the real sun framed by a courtyard opening; its sharp shadow line advances across terracotta architecture. The woman crosses the moving beam, her dress changing from muted copper to molten orange while her face remains partially concealed. She lifts one translucent silk edge and sunlight passes through it, projecting a warm red plane onto cream stone. That triangular projection match-cuts to the moving triangular shadow on the rooftop sundial. The shadow reaches one exact engraved mark. She notices, follows the indicated line and moves beneath the pergola toward the open terrace. Alternating bars of sunlight and shade travel across her uncovered eyes; her gaze narrows slightly under the increasing glare. At the terrace edge she faces the low sun. The camera moves around her silhouette until a natural lens flare fills the frame. The flare resolves inside the camera-right smoke-brown sunglass lens, and a slow pullback reveals the same woman now wearing the exact translucent amber sunglasses for the first time. Across the entire pair there is only one small subdued sun highlight near the outer edge of the camera-right lens; the camera-left lens carries only a soft sea-and-sky gradient. Never show two mirrored suns or repeated circular reflections. She turns from the sun toward camera; tension around her eyes and jaw releases, chin lifts and a restrained self-possessed half-smile arrives. entries.title: Seedance 2.5 courtroom chocolate commercial: "who ate the last chocolate", played straight, with a matte-only title lockup and a [Text law] block
entries.description: A 30-second ad written in bracketed sections ([风格与氛围] style and mood in Chinese, then English [Reference layer], [Generation goal], [Camera], [Motion law], [Performance], six timed [Stage] blocks, [Audio], [Text law]). The prop is fixed in its story state ("almost empty, with exactly ONE chocolate left … every other case empty and creased"), and the box carries the same chocolate every time. The closing lockup is a white-on-black image used as a matte: "Take ONLY the letterforms … The black is a matte and is never reproduced." [Text law] limits the picture to the exact named strings.
entries.prompt:
[风格与氛围]
快节奏庭审类型叙事、电影级木质法庭美学：以举证、认罪与一次开盒制造高密度悬念，同时保持法庭深胡桃木与包装深金红、单一高窗侧逆光、自然肤色、粗粝 35mm 颗粒与无柔化。

[Reference layer]
@Image1 defines the judge. @Image2 defines the prosecutor. @Image3 defines the accused. @Image4 defines the chocolate box, and it is shown in its story state: almost empty, with exactly ONE chocolate left in its paper case and every other case empty and creased. Its lid must read exactly COLLIER'S CHOC and that last chocolate's domed shape must be distinctive and legible. The box carries this same single remaining chocolate every time it appears in the film. @Image5 defines the courtroom. @Image6 is the closing lockup, supplied as white type on a pure black field. Take ONLY the letterforms from it and SUPERIMPOSE them over the live final shot, centred in the frame. The black is a matte and is never reproduced: the film does not cut to a black card, never cuts to a solid colour card, and never shows a lower-third banner or any box, bar or panel behind the type.

[Generation goal]
Generate a 30-second commercial for a chocolate maker, staged as a full courtroom drama about who ate the last chocolate. The genre is played completely straight at every moment.

[Global setting]
A wood-panelled courtroom: deep walnut, a raised bench, a gallery of onlookers, dust turning in a shaft of high side-light. Deep gold and red packaging is the only warm colour against the walnut.

[Camera]
Full courtroom-drama coverage played with total sincerity: low angles on the bench, a long walk-and-stop for the prosecutor, tight ECUs on the accused, reaction cuts to the gallery, and one rack focus at the end. Hard cuts, dense and escalating.

[Motion law]
Every shot plays at normal speed from first frame to last. The picture is never held, still-framed, slowed or stopped, and there is no freeze-frame anywhere. When a character stops moving, the CAMERA keeps living — stillness belongs to a performer, never to the image. Where the film calls for calm at the end, that calm comes from the action genuinely finishing, never from footage slowing down.

[Performance]
Every performer plays it as if a serious crime is being tried. Nobody winks. The accused is genuinely frightened. The gallery genuinely gasps.

[Stage 1] 0-4s
Initial state: a courtroom in session.
Primary event: full coverage — panelling, a low angle on the bench, a gavel, dust in a shaft of light.
Dialogue language: British English, formal and completely serious.
The judge says: {Would the defendant please rise.}
End state: the accused stands.

[Stage 2] 4-9s
Primary event: evidence is presented. A closed chocolate box is held up in a gloved hand for the room to see.
The prosecutor says: {Exhibit A. The box, as found.}
End state: the box is set on the evidence table.

[Stage 3] 9-13s
Primary event: ECU on the accused — and there is a smear of chocolate at the corner of his mouth, which he does not know about. He swallows.
Acting nuance: his eyes go to the box and come back. He does not touch his face.
End state: held on him, guilty and unaware.

[Stage 4] 13-18s
Primary event: the prosecutor walks the full length of the room and stops.
The prosecutor says: {How do you plead?}
A long silence. Then, very small:
The accused says: {…Guilty.}
End state: the room absorbs it.

[Stage 5] 18-24s
PIVOT.
Primary event: the box is opened and turned to face the room — and there is ONE LEFT. A genuine dramatic gasp goes round the gallery. Then two or three beats of the room whispering behind hands, heads leaning together. Cut to one old woman in the gallery mouthing, barely voiced: {How dare he leave exactly one piece…} Then cut to the lid, held up, legible, reading exactly COLLIER'S CHOC.
End state: everybody in the room is staring at one chocolate.

[Stage 6] 24-30s
收. Primary event: the gavel falls. The accused is led away, soft and out of focus in the background, wailing over his shoulder: {PLEASE, your honour — the chocolate was just too good—} and the camera RACKS FOCUS off him onto the evidence table in the foreground, landing sharp on the open box and the last chocolate sitting in it.
End state: held on the chocolate, with the closing lockup superimposed over the live frame — white type reading exactly COLLIER'S CHOC / Worth the trial. The film never cuts to a solid colour card.

[Maintain consistency]
Same courtroom, same three principals, same box throughout. The chocolate smear stays at the corner of the accused's mouth for the whole film.

[Audio]
(Full courtroom-thriller strings played completely straight, cutting dead the instant the box is opened; one comic pizzicato figure under the rack focus, resolving and decaying to near silence.)
<a gavel> <a large wood-panelled room's reverb> <a gloved hand on cardboard> <a box lid lifted> <a genuine collective gasp from a gallery> <whispering behind hands> <footsteps walking the length of a hard floor> <a door at the back of a courtroom>

[Text law]
The only words that may appear anywhere in the picture are the exact strings named above. Spell each one exactly as written, correctly and legibly. No other lettering, signage copy, captions, labels, numbers or watermark appears anywhere in the film.
No subtitles.

Create a 10-second, 16:9 synchronized-sound pure brand fragrance film titled BLUE–GREEN FREQUENCY. Show no person, body part or human silhouette. The concept is that fragrance is an invisible frequency made visible through color, water, directional light and refraction. Build one practical tabletop architecture from old-mint plaster walls, powder-blue glazed tiles, a narrow sage-green glass corridor, shallow cobalt water channels, brushed-chrome rails and one narrow rectangular daylight slot. entries.prompt:
One continuous 30-second low-altitude chase shot, a single unbroken take with no cuts, shot at greyhound speed. On a vast muted-green lawn a distinguished older man in a cream golf outfit lines up a putt at a banana lying on the grass; a slender grey greyhound wearing a knitted cream balaclava snatches the banana at the exact moment of the putt and bolts; the camera drops to ten centimeters off the ground and chases the dog flat-out for the rest of the film.
0-5s: the theft: club swings, the dog's jaws close on the banana mid-stroke and it accelerates away in three strides, ears flat inside the balaclava; the golfer watches it go without any expression; the camera whips down and after it, grass streaking past the lens.
5-11s: across the lawn at full sprint, weaving between motionless cream sheep who do not react; the dog leaps a low hedge, the camera vaulting it a half-beat behind.
11-17s: through a butter-yellow doorway into a whitewashed coastal street, claws skittering on cobblestones, laundry lines whipping overhead; the dog cuts left as a red city bus sweeps past behind it as one long streak of motion blur.
17-23s: out of the street straight into a blush-pink world flooded ankle-deep with glassy water: the dog charges through in sheets of spray, past an elegant woman standing in a red paper boat who turns her head slowly to watch it pass, spray hanging in pink light.
23-27s: up an ochre steppe slope, petals and dust kicked up in its wake, the camera swinging wide alongside as the dog bounds onto a single rounded black boulder at the top.
27-30s: the dog places the banana carefully on the very top of the boulder like a trophy, sits bolt upright beside it, perfectly still, and stares into the lens, deadpan, balaclava slightly askew. Far below on the lawn, the tiny figure of the golfer raises his putter once in salute.

Lens 35-50mm, stabilized low tracking, level horizon even at speed. Generate a single shot, one continuous take.

Style: editorial, refined, fashion-forward, deadpan surrealist fashion film with high kinetic energy. Grade: slightly desaturated, lifted blacks, compressed milky highlights, low contrast while colors stay legible, light 35mm film grain, faint halation on highlights only, matte print-like finish, warm cream as the neutral instead of pure white. ABSOLUTELY NO on-screen text, no titles, no captions, no logos, no typography of any kind anywhere in the frame. A small old barbershop in a single sage-green world: sage painted walls, cream wainscoting, worn terracotta tile floor, one bentwood waiting bench, glass bottles of green tonic on a shelf, soft morning light through the shopfront glass.
In the barber chair, wearing the full striped barber cape, sits a large leafy TOPIARY BUSH. Behind it stands the barber: an older heavyset man, white moustache, putty smock, sleeves rolled. On the bench a middle-aged man in a sage cardigan waits with a potted fern on his lap, reading a folded newspaper. Everyone treats all of this as completely ordinary.
0-6s: static wide; the barber shakes out the cape, tucks it at the bush's 'neck', pumps the chair up twice with two heavy clunks, and asks flatly: "The usual?" — the bush answers with one small polite rustle. The waiting man turns a page.
6-13s: the camera begins its slow half-circle; the barber mists the bush from a brass atomizer — close on the leaves beading with droplets — then combs it with a wide wooden comb, the foliage parting in neat tracks like hair.
13-20s: the trim: precise scissor-work in a quick confident rhythm, leaf clippings falling into a tidy cone on the terracotta tiles; close on the scissors flashing; close on the barber's unhurried, professional squint; the fern on the bench trembles very slightly, watching.
20-26s: the reveal: the barber spins the chair to face the mirror — the bush has been trimmed into a PERFECT POODLE silhouette, pom-poms and all; a held beat of silence; then the poodle-bush shakes itself exactly like a wet dog, shedding two leaves, and settles proudly.
26-30s: the barber whisks the cape off with a matador snap, sweeps once with a broom, and looks at the waiting bench. The man lowers his newspaper, looks down at his own fern with mild concern, and the fern's fronds droop shyly. The barber, deadpan: "Next." Hold on the fern.
Audio: cape shake, two chair-pump clunks, mist puffs, comb strokes through leaves, then the scissors settling into a light waltz rhythm that becomes the score; the dog-shake rustle; broom strokes; total silence before "Next."; one page-turn after it.
Lens 40-50mm, level, unhurried; sage single-hue world with the terracotta pot and floor as the only warm accent; the joke is never acknowledged by anyone.

Art direction (Pika R3): colors soft but vibrant, true to subject, cream as the neutral instead of pure white; lighting one enormous soft source, shadows filled so every texture reads; grade natural and restrained, low-to-moderate contrast, open detailed shadows, subtle fine 35mm film grain, faint halation on highlights only, matte print-like finish, no color cast, no teal-and-orange, no HDR, no crushed blacks, no neon saturation. Every impossible event is physically real and practical-looking — NO glow, NO sparkles, NO particle magic, NO fantasy effects. All faces deadpan, composed, never mugging or winking at the joke. ABSOLUTELY NO on-screen text, no titles, no captions, no logos, no typography anywhere.

entries.title: Wan 3.0 hand-painted gouache short: "ART STYLE — hold this exactly in every frame, it is the contract", with no outlines at all
entries.description: A 30-second animated short (a man climbs to a single grave at golden hour). The style block comes first and is called a contract: thick opaque pigment, brush marks "left unblended", palette-knife strokes that follow the terrain, atmospheric perspective, and "NO outlines and NO line work at all". Nine named shots alternate story beats with B-roll (grass, birds, breath), and the only dialogue is one line at the end: "Hey, it's been a while." A second binding block (ANIMATION STYLE) asks for frame-by-frame painting on twos at 12 fps so "the whole image BOILS", and bans smoothing, interpolation and motion blur ("the judder and the boil ARE the style").
entries.prompt:
Generate a 30-second, 16:9 hand-painted gouache animated short: a man climbs a hill at golden hour and reaches a single grave at the summit.

ART STYLE — hold this exactly in every frame, it is the contract: hand-painted gouache landscape painting. Thick opaque pigment, every brush mark visible and left unblended. Directional flat-brush and palette-knife strokes that follow the slope of the terrain. Saturated emerald and spring-green hillside against cool slate-blue and lavender haze; white flecked wildflowers scattered through the grass; deep forest-green shadow masses. Strong atmospheric perspective — distant cliff walls flatten into pale blue mist. NO outlines and NO line work at all: form comes entirely from brush mark and value. Matte pigment throughout, no gloss, no gradient blending, no airbrush, no digital smoothing, no photorealism, no text or watermarks. The figure stays small and simplified, a painted silhouette rather than a rendered character.

ANIMATION STYLE — this is equally binding: hand-painted frame-by-frame traditional animation running at 12 frames per second, on twos. Every frame is a separately painted gouache painting, so the surface never sits still — the whole image BOILS. Every 2 to 4 frames the brush texture, edge placement and pigment grain visibly shift and re-form, because a human repainted them. Outlines of hills, clouds and the figure wobble and breathe frame to frame. Colours flicker very slightly between adjacent frames as pigment density varies. This boil must be constant and present in every single shot, including the still ones. Do NOT smooth, interpolate, stabilise or motion-blur between frames — the judder and the boil ARE the style. No 24fps smoothness, no CG tweening.

CHARACTER: Image 1 is the world and the style authority. The climber is a lone man in a dark coat, small in frame, painted as a simplified silhouette with no facial detail except in the two close-ups described below.

Shot 1 [0-4s]: THE START. Wide. The man begins climbing the steep green slope, tiny against the vast misty valley and pale cliff walls behind him. Late golden light rakes across the grass.
Shot 2 [4-7s]: B-ROLL — GRASS. Extreme close-up. Wind ruffles through the grass blades and white wildflowers, stems bending and springing back, painted marks reshaping with every frame.
Shot 3 [7-10s]: THE CLIMB. Medium-wide. He works his way up the slope, leaning into the gradient, one hand steadying against the ground. The valley falls away behind him.
Shot 4 [10-12s]: B-ROLL — BIRDS. Medium shot of the pale sky. A loose scatter of birds crosses the frame, painted as quick dark strokes, wheeling once.
Shot 5 [12-15s]: B-ROLL — BREATH. Extreme close-up on the climber's mouth and jaw. He is breathing hard and open-mouthed, warm breath faintly visible in the cooling air, a strand of hair stuck to damp skin.
Shot 6 [15-18s]: THE LAST PUSH. He crests the final ridge, pushing off his own knee with one hand, head down, then slowly straightens up.
Shot 7 [18-22s]: THE REVEAL. Reverse angle. At the summit stands a single weathered stone grave marker, alone on the grass — and behind it the sun is setting low, the whole sky glowing in soft amber, apricot and rose, warm light haloing the edges of the stone. He stands motionless.
Shot 8 [22-26s]: THE SIT. Wide shot. He holds still for a beat, just taking it in, the wind moving the grass around his legs. Then he walks slowly forward and sits down on the ground in front of the grave marker, facing it. The sky glows on, gold fading gently into rose.
Shot 9 [26-30s]: THE GREETING. Close-up on his face in three-quarter profile, the only time we see him clearly — weathered, tired, eyes glistening, the warm evening light soft on his cheek. He looks at the stone, and a small, tender smile finds him. Quietly, warmly, his voice low and catching slightly, he says: "Hey, it's been a while." He breathes out and keeps his eyes on the stone. Hold on his face to the final frame.

CAMERA: patient and mostly locked, letting the painted frames do the work — a slow drift with him on the climbing shots, static for the three b-roll inserts, a steady hold on the wide of him sitting, and a slow, gentle push-in on his face for the final line that settles and holds. No handheld shake, no fast moves.

AUDIO: no music until the reveal at 18s, then a single sustained cello line that swells gently, softens to almost nothing under his words, and resolves on the final frame. Wind moving through grass, boots on soil, laboured breathing in the breath close-up, distant birdcalls, and the deep quiet of high open ground. The only dialogue in the entire video is his single quiet line at the end, in his own voice, low, gentle and sentimental: "Hey, it's been a while."

entries.prompt:
Format & duration: archived 2003 network reality-TV broadcast footage, shot handheld on a consumer MiniDV camcorder. 4:3, standard definition, interlaced. 30 seconds, fast-cut multi-location montage, cut on the music beat.

Image references: Image1 — the only recurring character. No location references; every location is built from this prompt.

Scene geography: six public locations in a sunny American city, one per segment. A mall with a skylit escalator. A supermarket aisle under fluorescent tubes. A stone plaza fountain in harsh midday sun. A city bus stop on a bright street. A grassy park with a jogging path. An electronics store with a wall of chunky CRT TVs. Each location is shown wide enough to read in its first second.

Immutable character facts: Image1 is a heavyset adult man, 173 cm tall, with exactly the build and proportions on his reference sheet. Short curly dark hair, flushed cheeks, grey crew-neck tee, navy bike shorts, dark grey sneakers. Same face, hair, body and outfit in every location. He is the only person who appears in more than one segment.

Dramatic goal: one fearless guy brightens an ordinary day by turning every public place into his stage. Strangers go from staring to laughing along with him. The comedy comes from his total commitment, never from his body.

Continuous timeline:
0:00–0:04.3. Mall. Image1 rides the down escalator backwards, arms flung wide like an opera singer, holding one long note. Shoppers on the up escalator twist to stare; one woman covers her mouth laughing.
0:04.3–0:08.1. Supermarket. He shoves a shopping cart into a sprint, hops onto the rear bar gripping the handle, and glides down the aisle arms out. A stock clerk in a green apron flattens against the cereal shelf and cracks up.
0:08.1–0:11.6. Fountain. He sits on the stone edge, both feet in the water, shoes beside him, and kicks a SPLASH toward a college couple who shriek and run off laughing.
0:11.6–0:16.8. Bus stop. Down on one knee with a silver boombox on his shoulder, he serenades a grey-haired woman holding a newspaper. She stares flat for two beats, then cracks and SWATS his shoulder with the rolled paper.
0:16.8–0:21.5. Park. He races a jogger in a headband across the grass, dead serious, then DIVES into a belly slide over a chalk finish line while a group of college-age friends cheers.
0:21.5–0:26.4. Electronics store. He robot-dances in front of the CRT wall. An employee in a red polo glances around, then joins in, and they lock eyes doing the same arm-pop.
0:26.4–0:30. Back outside. The camera operator's hand reaches into frame; Image1 SMACKS a high five, then leans into the lens, out of breath and grinning.

Dialogue, spoken exactly as written:
Supermarket clerk: "Whoa whoa whoa!"
Image1, at the bus stop: "Ma'am, this one's for you."
Image1, at the end: "Same time tomorrow?"

Micro-expressions & performance: Image1 plays everything completely straight — eyes squeezed shut on the escalator note, cheeks puffed on the cart, tongue between his teeth on the splash, hand on heart and pleading eyebrows at the bus stop, jaw set and fists pumping in the race. The joke lands because he never breaks until the last shot, where he finally grins wide and sweaty. Every bystander is a different adult with a different reaction: stunned stare, shriek, deadpan that breaks, reluctant joining-in.

Camera workflow: one handheld operator running alongside him, part of the fun, not a crew. Operator stumbles backward down the escalator filming upward. Whip pan with a late reframe in the supermarket. Snap zoom across the plaza with autofocus hunting through the spray. Crouched low and tilting at the bus stop. Bouncing run-along in the park. Snap zoom in the store. Final shot pushes past the lens's limit into blurry digital zoom on his face, with a one-frame stutter on his grin.

Look & artifacts: low dynamic range, so skies, skylights and water clip to flat white and shadows crush to black. CCD vertical smear — a white streak straight up and down the frame — from the skylight, sun glints and the fountain. Heavy saturated colour with slight bleed on reds and blues. Interlace combing on whip pans. Exposure pumps when the camera swings from shade into sun. Fluorescent white balance lags blue in the store, then corrects. Scan-line flicker on the CRT wall.

Sound: original 2003-style pop-punk instrumental, fast palm-muted guitar and snare, dropping under every spoken line. Built-in camcorder mic throughout — clipped shouts, wind buffeting outdoors, handling thumps, his escalator note cracking, cart wheels rattling, the splash, boombox hiss, the landing thump, CRT whine, the operator laughing.

Hard prohibitions: no text, subtitles, timestamps, REC icon or logos. No smartphones, LED screens or anything made after 2006. No minors. No jokes about his weight or body. No property damage and no one getting hurt. No change to Image1's face, hair, build or outfit. No gimbal smoothness, no stabilisation, no film look, no shallow depth of field, no modern colour grade.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 storm-bridge stunt: a REALISM block of wet-skin, rust and rain-on-lens specifics for 8 shots in 15 s
entries.description: An action short whose REALISM block is the reusable part: "Real heavy rain, real wet skin with pores and water drops on the lashes, real soaked leather, real rusty steel rails … sparks from steel on steel", flat grey storm daylight, headlights burning through rain, "a fine film grain, drops of rain on the lens", and "Everything moves at real speed, no slow motion". Eight shots carry the story (a woman stops a train with one palm at a collapsed bridge). The safety and continuity negatives close the prompt (the train keeps eight cars, no injuries, five fingers).
entries.prompt:
15s / 8 shots / vertical 9:16 / real live-action footage, Hollywood film shot on a cinema camera

REALISM
This is real live-action footage, a photorealistic shot from a big-budget Hollywood film, filmed with a real cinema camera, real actors, real light and practical effects. Not 3D, not CGI, not animation, not a render, not a video game, not cartoon, no plastic or glossy look. Real heavy rain, real wet skin with pores and water drops on the lashes, real soaked leather, real rusty steel rails and dark wet wooden sleepers, real gravel, real sparks from steel on steel, real steam. Flat grey storm daylight, soft shadows, the train headlights still burning white through the rain, slightly overexposed sky, a fine film grain, drops of rain on the lens. Everything moves at real speed, no slow motion.

STORY
In the afternoon in a storm, a span of an old railway bridge over a deep gorge has collapsed, and a passenger train is racing toward the gap. One young woman stands alone on the rails five meters in front of the broken edge, facing the train. She raises one open palm, the train slams into it, and she is pushed back along the rails until her heel stops a few centimeters from the edge. A drone rises and reveals the whole picture: the long train stopped dead on the bridge, the tiny woman in front of it, and nothing behind her but the gorge.

SHOT LIST
Shot 1 (0-2s): Extreme close-up of the woman's wet face in the rain. A white light grows in her eyes. She does not blink.
Shot 2 (2-4s): Wide side view of the bridge. She stands alone on the rails. Out of the fog a train with blazing headlights comes straight at her.
Shot 3 (4-5.5s): Close-up on the train wheels locking, a shower of sparks, the horn screaming.
Shot 4 (5.5-7s): Close side profile, the train looming huge in front of her on the LEFT. She raises her RIGHT palm toward it.
Shot 5 (7-9.5s): Side medium shot. The train nose hits her palm. The rain blasts sideways, she slides back along the rails.
Shot 6 (9.5-11s): Low close-up at her boots. Her heel stops at the torn edge of the bridge, gravel falls into the deep gorge.
Shot 7 (11-13s): From behind her, over the edge. She stands with her palm on the stopped train, breathing hard.
Shot 8 (13-15s): A drone rises fast. The whole bridge, the stopped train, the tiny woman, and the missing span behind her over the gorge.

SUBJECT
The woman: an adult woman, 28 years old, about 172 cm tall, a striking, strong look, an athletic curvy figure with a full bust and strong shoulders. Oval face with high cheekbones, thick dark straight brows, intense grey green eyes, full lips without lipstick, light olive skin with visible pores, wet with rain, drops on her lashes and chin. Long dark brown hair, soaked, falling in heavy wet strands past her shoulders and sticking to her neck and cheeks. She wears a black leather biker jacket, zipped up to the collar, wet and shining with water, over a black high-neck top; dark grey straight jeans soaked dark; black leather lace-up ankle boots with thick rubber soles. Her face is calm and focused the whole time, jaw set, no screaming, no fear.
The train: a long passenger train of eight cars, dark blue with one thin silver stripe, a rounded front with two bright white headlights low on the nose and one above the windshield, a black rubber front buffer at the center of the nose. The passenger windows reflect the grey sky and are streaked with rain, so no faces are visible inside. The driver is only a dark blurry silhouette behind the rain-covered windshield. No logos, no numbers, no text.
The same woman and the same train in every shot, nothing about them changes.

WORLD
An old steel truss railway bridge over a deep green rocky gorge in the afternoon, under low dark grey storm clouds. One track of two rusty rails on dark wooden sleepers with gravel between them, steel truss girders on both sides. The train comes from the far end of the bridge. The woman stands between the rails five meters in front of the near end, where the last span of the bridge has collapsed: behind her the rails are torn and bent down over empty air, broken sleepers hang in the air, and far below, about 100 m down, a fast grey-green river runs between pine-covered rocks. Fog drifts in the gorge, rain falls hard and slanted, wind pushes it from LEFT to RIGHT. Light: soft grey daylight from the overcast sky, everything clearly visible, plus the bright white train headlights. Palette: cold grey sky, dark green pines and wet brown rock, rusty steel, the dark blue train, her black jacket, the white headlights as the accent. Anchors that never change: the steel truss, the two rails, the broken edge behind her, the river far below.

LOOK
Shot on a real cinema camera with anamorphic lenses: shallow depth of field in the close-ups, horizontal flares from the headlights, a fine film grain, natural daylight contrast, a slightly blown-out grey sky, real rain drops and streaks on the lens that the camera does not wipe. Colors true-to-life, cool and muted, no glossy grading. Close-ups at eye level, wide shots from the side at a distance, the last shot from a real drone climbing in the rain, the gorge fully visible in daylight. The camera shakes from the vibration and jolts at the impact. No slow motion, no speed ramps.

MOTION
Everything moves at real speed. The train is enormous and heavy: it comes fast, its nose dips when the brakes lock, sparks spray from the wheels, and when it hits her palm the whole train stops in a long violent jolt that runs back through all eight cars one after another, each car rocking on its springs. The woman stands with her feet apart between the rails, knees slightly bent, weight forward, her RIGHT arm straight and locked toward the train, her LEFT arm pulled back for balance. At the impact she does not fall: she is pushed straight back along the rails, her boots sliding on the wet sleepers and gravel, her knees bending deeper, her whole body leaning into the train, until she stops. Her wet hair whips back and her leather jacket ripples from the blast of air and rain. After the stop she breathes hard: her shoulders and chest rise and fall, water runs down her face. She blinks against the rain.

SHOTS IN DETAIL
Shot 1 (0-2s): Camera at eye level, 50 cm from her face, a very slow push-in on a dolly with a slight tremor. Extreme close-up of her face filling the frame, rain running down her forehead and cheeks, wet strands of hair stuck to her skin. In her eyes a small white point of light reflects and slowly grows brighter. She does not blink, rain drips from her chin. Behind her head the grey sky and rain, softly out of focus. Sounds: <heavy rain on steel> <wind howling in the gorge> <a distant train horn, far away>.
Shot 2 (2-4s): Camera wide from the side, far from the bridge, at the height of the rails, locked-off. The bridge crosses the lower third of the vertical frame, the storm sky above it and the gorge below it; the woman is a small figure standing between the rails on the RIGHT part of the frame, facing LEFT. On the LEFT, two white headlights burst out of the fog: the train is coming straight along the bridge toward her, horn blaring, the truss shaking. The broken end of the bridge behind her is hidden behind the RIGHT edge of the frame. Sounds: <the train roaring closer> <a long train horn> <wind in the gorge>.
Shot 3 (4-5.5s): Camera low beside the track, close to the front wheels as they pass. The steel wheels lock and scream on the wet rails, a thick shower of orange sparks sprays out sideways, steam and spray rise, the rail vibrates. Sounds: <a deafening steel screech> <the horn screaming> <hissing sparks in the rain>.
Shot 4 (5.5-7s): Camera at chest height, three meters from her, exactly at her side, locked-off: a close profile of her face and upper body on the RIGHT of the frame, facing LEFT, and the oncoming train with its blazing headlights on the LEFT of the frame, growing bigger every moment. She looks straight at the light, squints slightly, and in one steady motion raises her RIGHT arm straight forward to shoulder height, palm open toward the train, five fingers together, elbow locked. Her LEFT arm swings back for balance. Rain bounces off her raised arm and runs off her fingers. Her wet hair starts to lift back in the wind of the approaching train. Sounds: <the roar of the train filling everything> <the screech of brakes> <rain hammering the leather jacket>.
Shot 5 (7-9.5s): Camera at the side, at waist height, 6 m away, a short handheld pan following her backward. At 7.2s the black rubber buffer at the center of the train nose meets her open palm. A shockwave of air blasts the rain sideways in a white sheet, her wet hair snaps back, her jacket ripples. The train keeps pushing and she is driven straight back along the rails toward the RIGHT of the frame, toward the broken edge: her boots slide on the wet sleepers, gravel and water spray up from under her soles, her knees bend deeper, her body leans hard into the train. The camera shakes hard. At 9.3s the train stops. Sounds: <a huge metal thud> <gravel scraping under her boots> <the long groan of the cars jolting one after another>.
Shot 6 (9.5-11s): Camera low on the rails, a close-up at her boots, looking toward the edge. Her rear boot, the RIGHT one, slides back and stops; the heel ends a few centimeters from the torn end of the rail. Beyond the heel there is nothing: the bent rails hang down into empty air, a small piece of gravel and a loose bolt tip over the edge and fall away toward the river far below. Sounds: <a bolt clinking and falling> <wind rising from the gorge> <the train hissing>.
Shot 7 (11-13s): Camera behind her and slightly above, as if hanging over the gorge, locked-off, looking past her back toward the train. She stands at the edge, her RIGHT palm still flat against the buffer of the train, her LEFT hand at her side. The two headlights glow around her, steam rises from the front of the train, rain falls between them. Her shoulders rise and fall with hard breaths. The stopped train stretches back along the bridge. Sounds: <her hard breathing> <the hiss of brakes> <rain>.
Shot 8 (13-15s): A real drone starts 5 m above her and rises fast straight up and back, the rain streaking past the lens. The frame opens to reveal the whole scene: the long bridge across the gorge, the eight dark blue cars of the stopped train, the tiny woman standing at its nose, and right behind her the missing span: the bridge simply ends and the bent rails hang over the gorge, the green river far below, pine forest on both slopes. The last frame holds on this view. Sounds: <wind> <the river far below> <the rain>.

HARD MOMENTS
7-9.5s RISK: the train hitting a person can look fake, pass through her, or she can fall or get crushed. Step by step: 7.0s her RIGHT arm is straight and locked, palm open, five fingers together, the buffer 20 cm away. 7.2s the buffer touches her palm, her hand stays flat, the train does not pass her hand. 7.3s her body is pushed back as one piece, the train nose stays exactly at her palm. 7.5-9.2s she slides back about five meters in a straight line, both boots stay planted and slide on the wet sleepers, never lifting off, her body angle stays the same. 9.3s everything stops. MUST NOT: her hand must not sink into the train, her arm must not bend backward, she must not fall, fly, be crushed or go under the train, the train must not shrink, change shape or color, no explosion, no fire, no blood.
9.5-11s RISK: the heel at the edge. Only her RIGHT boot is in close-up, the heel stops on the last sleeper a few centimeters from the edge. MUST NOT: the boot must not go over the edge, she must not slip or fall, no extra foot, the edge stays in the same place.
5.5-7s RISK: raising the arm. One steady arc forward to shoulder height, shoulder and chest turn slightly, the palm opens. MUST NOT: no extra arm or fingers, no fused fingers, the arm must not stretch longer.
13-15s RISK: the drone reveal with many cars. Exactly one train of eight dark blue cars, all on the rails, in one straight line behind her. MUST NOT: the cars must not multiply, bend off the rails or melt together, no second train, no people on the bridge, the woman must stay at the nose of the train, the gap must stay behind her.
0-2s RISK: extreme close-up of the face. Real skin, pores, rain drops running down, no beauty filter. MUST NOT: the face must not change between shots, no waxy skin, eyes stay natural.
4-5.5s RISK: sparks and steam. Sparks are short orange streaks that fly outward and die in the rain within half a second, steam rises and is torn away by the wind. MUST NOT: sparks must not turn into fire or flames, the wheels must not leave the rails.

CONTINUITY
The same woman in the same black leather jacket, black high-neck top, dark grey jeans and black boots, soaked, in every shot. She always raises the RIGHT arm. The train always comes from the far end of the bridge toward the broken edge, and in every shot after 7.2s its nose is pressed against her palm. The broken edge is always behind her: five meters behind her until the impact, a few centimeters behind her heel after she slides. Rain, wind direction, the grey daylight and the white headlights stay the same in every shot. After each cut her position continues from the end of the previous shot. In every side view the train is on the LEFT of the frame and the broken edge on the RIGHT, the camera never jumps to the other side of the track. In the side profile shot she faces LEFT toward the train; from behind, the train is in front of her and the gorge is at the bottom of the frame. She stays soaked, never dry.

AUDIO
Only real sounds of the place: heavy rain, wind in the gorge, the train roaring, the horn, the steel screech of brakes, the metal thud of the impact, gravel scraping, the cars groaning, hissing steam, her hard breathing. No dialogue. No music, no narrator.

KEEP
Only one woman and one train, the driver only as a blurry silhouette, no faces in the windows, no other people anywhere. Five natural fingers on each hand. The train keeps the same size, color and eight cars. She never falls and is never hurt. No blood, no injuries, no explosion, no fire. No logos, no numbers, no signs, no subtitles, no text, no watermark. Real live-action footage filmed in real life. Not 3D, not CGI, not animation, not a render, not a video game, not cartoon, no plastic or glossy look.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 "Change the camera only" re-shoot: an extreme wide, eye-level, locked-off camera applied to every cut of an existing clip
entries.description: Pika's camera-director app writes a reusable edit prompt for Seedance 2.5: "Edit @Video1.
