entries.title: Seedance 2.5 30 s kaiju blockbuster over a fictional New York: a suited man transforms into a 700 m armored giant and fights a horned monster from Times Square to the Brooklyn Bridge
entries.description: A 12k-character action spec built on a 30-beat timeline ("00-01:" … "29-30:"). It says outright that the one-second intervals are "choreography beats, not a requirement to cut every second." Reference sheets get named roles plus overrides ("Override the reference-sheet height: his transformed height is 700 meters"; "Use the sheets for appearance only; never show their layouts, panels, labels"). It locks energy colours per character ("Do not swap colors"), fixes the screen direction ("SERAPH advances from screen left… Preserve this action axis"), and keeps scale cues like taxis, buses and street-level humans with "Never shrink the giants to fit a building." The very first frame has to open mid-action, with no opening pose. Separate SOUND and EXCLUSIONS blocks follow.
entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second, 16:9, photorealistic live-action blockbuster kaiju battle. Bright sunny midday in a fictional cinematic New York: Times Square, Manhattan skyscrapers, and the Brooklyn Bridge. Hard sunlight, blue sky, realistic materials, enormous weight, violent acceleration, layered destruction, atmospheric depth.

Action movie camera work continues every 1 second.
Maintain purposeful action-movie camera movement in every one-second interval. The intervals are choreography beats, not a requirement to cut every second. Keep contact, trajectories, and cause-and-effect readable.

REFERENCE ASSIGNMENT AND CONTINUITY
Reference image 1 = THE DIRECTOR, the human before transformation. Preserve his exact face, short hair, goatee, dark sunglasses, navy double-breasted suit, gold details, watch, rings, and polished shoes. He remains approximately 1.88 meters tall until transforming. The transformation adds a luminous crimson V-shaped sigil shining through his suit at the sternum.
Reference image 2 = SERAPH-DELTA / SERAPH-Δ, the same man after transformation. Preserve the off-white ceramic armor, black biomechanical frame, crimson internal details, curved horns, long trailing black cables, clawed hands, and reference foot/sole construction. Override the reference-sheet height: his transformed height is 700 meters.
Reference image 3 = GORGON. Preserve the bulky gray-green armored body, huge crescent-shaped head crest, tusks, porous shoulders, tooth-lined chest mouth, claws, and long spiked tail. Override the reference-sheet height: his height is 700 meters. His attack beam comes from the mouth in his HEAD, not his chest mouth.

GORGON's attack energy is poisonous fluorescent green. SERAPH's transformation and attack energy are deep vivid crimson. Do not swap colors. GORGON emits crimson internally only during the final overload caused by SERAPH's beam.
Use the sheets for appearance only; never show their layouts, panels, labels, or measurement graphics. Keep the two giants distinct. THE DIRECTOR becomes SERAPH; do not leave a separate human duplicate.

SCALE AND STAGING
Both giants remain 700-meter class, matched in height; GORGON is broader and heavier-looking. Honor the requested exaggerated below-knee city scale by staging nearby towers below their knees. Retain detailed windows, tiny yellow taxis, buses, and street-level humans as scale cues. Never shrink the giants to fit a building.
Use deliberately compressed movie geography, connecting the Times Square battle corridor to the East River and Brooklyn Bridge. Show travel and destruction between locations; no unexplained teleportation.
From the collision onward, SERAPH advances from screen left toward GORGON on screen right; the river and bridge lie behind GORGON. Preserve this action axis. Reveal whole bodies at decisive impacts. Accelerate limbs and attacks sharply while bodies, tails, cables, dust, and debris retain immense inertia.

ONE-SECOND ACTION AND CAMERA TIMELINE

00-01:
The VERY FIRST FRAME already shows a continuous poisonous-green beam firing from GORGON's head-mouth into distant Manhattan towers. No opening pose or charging shot. The camera races backward beside the beam as glass facades erupt along its path.

01-02:
Continue the rapid reverse tracking along the beam toward its source, widening through layers of skyline. GORGON sweeps his head horizontally; successive buildings explode across a lateral line, with the destruction visibly following the beam.

02-03:
The pullback reaches an extreme wide shot containing GORGON's entire 700-meter body and the whole collapsing row of towers. Buildings buckle and fall while debris hangs at different depths. His feet, knees, skyline, and beam remain legible together.

03-04:
Cut to pavement-level lateral tracking through Times Square. Crowds flee toward the foreground between abandoned taxis, looking upward. Falling glass and masonry strike the street behind them; the moving camera threads past a vehicle wheel.

04-05:
Tilt sharply upward while continuing the low tracking move. GORGON's gigantic spiked tail passes overhead like a moving elevated wall, casting a vast shadow over the fleeing crowd. Keep people and street fixtures at the bottom of frame to establish scale.

05-06:
Cut inside a news helicopter, looking through the cabin window. Window framing and vibrating cabin edges establish its tiny scale as GORGON's enormous face fills the view. The camera pushes toward the glass; his eye turns toward the helicopter and his head-mouth swings into firing alignment.

06-07:
Cut outside at the instant the green mouth-beam strikes the helicopter. The complete aircraft bursts into a fireball; rotor and fuselage fragments separate. Whip-tilt down with a distinctive burning fuselage section falling toward the avenue. No visible injured occupants.

07-08:
Match the falling wreckage into a low frontal tracking shot of THE DIRECTOR standing alone in the dusty avenue. The same burning fuselage crashes behind him and explodes. He does not turn or flinch; flames roll behind his intact silhouette.

08-09:
Push into a low three-quarter close-up as he removes his sunglasses in one deliberate movement and looks up at GORGON. A crimson V-shaped sigil ignites through the chest of his existing suit. The camera begins tilting upward with his gaze.

09-10:
Continue into a rapid upward-and-backward camera move as a vertical crimson light column surrounds him. His silhouette visibly enlarges and reference-matched armor unfolds into SERAPH. Horns and cables resolve above the skyline; both feet descend. Complete the transformation and make first ground contact at exactly 10.0 seconds.

10-11:
Track low beside SERAPH's feet as the landing releases an expanding pressure ring, throwing abandoned cars into the air and peeling debris outward. Before the shockwave settles, he pushes off into a forward charge, leaving the spreading dust behind.

11-12:
A low, wide side-tracking two-shot shows SERAPH slamming bodily into GORGON. Show actual torso and shoulder contact before the shockwave erupts. GORGON recoils; nearby building windows burst outward in a simultaneous glittering wave.

12-13:
Truck sideways at torso height as they lock into a chest-to-chest strength contest. Their feet grind trenches through the street grid. SERAPH lowers his center of gravity while GORGON presses against his shoulders; both bodies remain visible.

13-14:
Move into a clear three-quarter wide shot. SERAPH changes to a scoop grip: one arm beneath GORGON's thighs, the other supporting his upper back. SERAPH drives upward through bent legs; GORGON's feet visibly leave the ground.

14-15:
Boom upward with the lift. SERAPH raises GORGON horizontally above his own head, back facing the ground. Show both complete silhouettes against the blue sky, with the skyline far beneath them and GORGON's heavy tail hanging downward.

15-16:
Pull wider along the same side. Briefly reveal the overhead peak, then SERAPH drives GORGON downward in a huge back-first body slam toward a cluster of skyscrapers. Keep the grip, downward arc, and intended impact zone visible.

16-17:
A steep aerial pullback captures GORGON's back hitting the towers. Buildings collapse outward in a domino sequence, slabs and facade sections separating before dust engulfs them. A dense dust wave races along the streets from the impact center.

17-18:
Track laterally above the dust line. GORGON staggers back to his feet with the river corridor behind him. In the same wide frame, SERAPH immediately starts a running approach; broken towers separate the two giants.

18-19:
Use a fast low side-tracking shot as SERAPH accelerates, jumps, turns his torso nearly horizontal, and extends BOTH legs toward GORGON's face. Show the reference-matched soles, the full airborne body, and the target in one readable composition.

19-20:
Both soles strike GORGON's face simultaneously in a clear wide side view: a true two-foot dropkick. Use only a brief quarter-second slow-motion impact accent as ivory fang fragments snap away, then return to full speed. GORGON's head recoils before his whole body launches backward. No blood.

20-21:
Pull into a sweeping aerial wide shot following GORGON's backward trajectory through the compressed city corridor toward the Brooklyn Bridge. SERAPH recoils in the opposite direction, tucks his legs, and lands in a braced crouch on the avenue at screen left.

21-22:
Continue the aerial tracking as GORGON crashes back-first across the Brooklyn Bridge. The bridge splits into two collapsing sections; suspension cables snap and the deck folds into the East River. Huge water columns rise around his body, leaving his upper torso and tooth-lined chest mouth exposed.

22-23:
Cut to a low frontal push toward SERAPH rising from his crouch into a firm stance. He brings both hands forward together, palms facing GORGON. Crimson charge runs through his horns and trailing cables, then gathers between his aligned palms.

23-24:
Move to a wide over-the-shoulder view as an extremely thick, concentrated crimson beam erupts from both hands. Keep SERAPH's firing pose, the beam's continuous path, and GORGON at the broken bridge visible together.

24-25:
Race alongside the crimson beam toward its impact in GORGON's TOOTH-LINED CHEST MOUTH. His upper body is pinned against the shattered bridge remains. Crimson light spreads beneath his armor and begins leaking from the pores across his shoulders and torso.

25-26:
Pull rapidly away as the crimson leaks intensify across GORGON's body. His silhouette remains recognizable for an instant, then erupts into an enormous crimson-white explosion, scattering armored fragments and vapor. The destruction is energetic and non-graphic.

26-27:
Reach an extreme aerial wide shot. A gigantic mushroom-shaped fire-and-smoke cloud rises above the river while a visible pressure front expands across Manhattan, swallowing streets and buildings in rolling dust. Preserve readable city scale rather than covering the entire image with white light.

27-28:
Cut to the FINAL, continuous rear ultra-low-angle shot of SERAPH, the blast beyond him. Glide forward behind his feet and tilt upward along his armored back toward his horned silhouette. He stands solidly against the enormous fire cloud.

28-29:
Continue the same rear shot with a restrained low lateral arc. The blast wind reaches him, lifting and streaming his long horn-associated cables and back cables sideways. Armor stays rigid while cables whip with delayed, heavy motion.

29-30:
Continue the low upward camera move and settle into a monumental rear composition: SERAPH's horns, shoulders, and streaming cables silhouetted against rolling flames and the mushroom cloud, with blue daylight still visible above. End on moving fire and cables, without a fade or freeze-frame.

SOUND
No BGM or musical score. Environmental sound and synchronized cinematic effects only: city ambience, nonverbal crowd panic, sirens, rotor blades, green-beam roar, helicopter explosion, falling wreckage, glass cascades, transformation resonance, massive footsteps, armor strain, body impacts, crumbling concrete, snapping bridge cables, rushing river water, crimson energy charge, beam discharge, and the final deep blast.
Make the overhead lift creak with immense weight. Give the dropkick one sharp, clear impact followed by the rolling bridge collapse. Briefly duck surrounding effects before the final detonation, then release a huge bass pressure hit and long debris rumble. Finish with wind, crackling fire, cable movement, and distant collapse. No dialogue or narration.

EXCLUSIONS
No subtitles, captions, speech balloons, title cards, news graphics, watermarks, or added logos. Preserve the characters' existing costume insignia and the requested transformation sigil. Times Square screens use abstract imagery without readable slogans.
No blood, gore, exposed organs, or close-ups of injured people. No character redesign, swapped abilities, extra giants, duplicated limbs, detached floating feet, toy-like city scale, cartoon rendering, prolonged slow motion, excessive camera spins, or smoke concealing decisive contact.

entries.prompt:
Macro cinematic push-in on a cyberpunk mechanical fly, beginning as a clean product-style beauty shot, then transitioning into an invasive, surgical exploration of its internal clockwork systems.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 vs Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, same prompt: a year-2000 Mini DV walk along West Lake's Bai Causeway with a garment-level outfit and hair-clip lock
entries.description: A same-prompt model comparison (top Seedance 2.5, bottom Omni 1.2 Flash) built on a Mini DV home-video brief. entries.prompt:
10秒，横屏16:9。2000年初夏，家用 Mini DV 手持家庭录像，像同行的朋友随手拍下在杭州西湖散步的片段。上午晚些时候，地点始终在白堤靠孤山的一侧。湖边垂柳拂过浅灰石岸，隔着北里湖能看见宝石山，山脊上露出细瘦的保俶塔，远处一只木桨船划过。
全片是同一位二十多岁的杭州女孩，虚构成年角色。她穿靛蓝底浅米色小碎花短袖连衣裙，浅圆领，腰间两道省缝自然收腰，裙摆到膝下，走动时布料轻轻摆动。棕色一字带露趾平底凉鞋，后跟有细搭带。及肩黑直发做半扎发。头顶上半层从左右太阳穴一起梳向脑后，在后脑正中央合成一小束，由一枚茶色一字横夹横着扣住。下半层直发从横夹下面自然垂到肩头，两层分明。耳侧没有发夹。自然肤色与皮肤纹理，四段保持同一面孔、衣着、鞋和发型。
0–2秒。柳荫下，她坐在湖边低石阶上。朋友从斜后方拍到她半扎的齐肩发和后脑正中央的茶色横夹。焦点从柳枝回到横夹时，她抬手在后脑按一下横夹，放下手，脸微侧着低头抿笑。画面里有湖水。
2–5秒。朋友在身后徒步跟拍，她沿临湖石径走几步，见一只狸花猫趴在步道内侧的矮石台上，便蹲下轻摸它的背。柳叶漏下的光扫过衣袖，镜头稍微跟慢半步，走动时带到她的鞋和下装。
5–8秒。湖边树下，她坐矮木凳朝湖面看，手边放一杯清透的西湖龙井，玻璃杯底有几片舒展的茶叶。她把被湖风吹到脸侧的散发顺到耳后，侧面手持构图微微漂移，远处木桨船从山影前缓缓经过。
8–10秒。她拿起茶杯，回头看向拍摄的朋友，笑一下，轻轻点头，转身沿白堤的柳荫往前走。还在迈步时骤切黑，像朋友按下停录键。
可见手抖、偶尔跑焦、树荫和水面之间轻微曝光跳动、低反差暖色、细颗粒和少量早期数字压缩。声音只有湖水轻拍石岸、柳叶风声、脚步、猫呼噜和玻璃杯轻碰木凳。无对白、旁白、配乐、字幕、水印、航拍或慢动作。画面里无智能手机、无线耳机或二维码。

entries.prompt: Late-1970s American supernatural slasher-film atmosphere, Halloween night, 1978.  CRITICAL VISUAL AUTHENTICITY: The footage must convincingly look PHYSICALLY PHOTOGRAPHED ON 35MM FILM IN 1978, NOT like a modern digital movie with a retro filter.  Authentic late-1970s low-light film photography: prominent organic 35mm grain, slightly soft resolving detail, mild analog color instability, subtle exposure breathing, crushed shadow detail, imperfect blacks, restrained dynamic range, slightly muted autumn colors, cool blue nighttime exterior illumination mixed with weak warm tungsten household light.  NO modern HDR. NO ultra-clean digital image. NO modern teal-and-orange grading. NO razor-sharp 4K appearance. NO glossy contemporary horror cinematography. NO stabilized gimbal movement.  The entire sequence is FIRST-PERSON POV and feels like an unseen person physically walking toward and entering an old two-story suburban house.  The POV person is NEVER seen except for one brief natural glimpse of a hand opening the back door.   [00:00–00:03]  Halloween night. Completely deserted.  Begin outside beside an old two-story American suburban house surrounded by darkness, bare tree branches, bushes, grass and scattered autumn leaves.  FIRST-PERSON POV CAMERA is stopped near the side/front corner of the property and tilted upward, staring toward a SECOND-STORY WINDOW.  A weak warm tungsten bedroom light glows behind the upstairs window.  Hold on it.  The upstairs light suddenly SWITCHES OFF.  The window instantly becomes black.  AT THE EXACT MOMENT THE LIGHT SWITCHES OFF: Hear one sudden sharp ELECTRICAL SNAP/POP from the house.  Immediately afterward, all exterior ambience abruptly disappears for approximately HALF A SECOND, creating a brief unnatural dead silence.  Then the soft crickets, faint wind and natural nighttime ambience return.  The camera remains staring at the now-dark window for a brief unsettling beat.  Then the POV slowly tilts downward toward normal human eye level.   [00:03–00:10]  At eye level, the camera now faces along the SIDE OF THE HOUSE.  The POV begins WALKING slowly forward through the grass.  One continuous handheld first-person movement.  The movement has subtle natural human walking motion: gentle vertical sway, tiny lateral corrections, imperfect framing and slight handheld instability. Controlled and deliberate, NOT violently shaky.  IMPORTANT: Walking produces NO audible footsteps. Do not emphasize walking sounds.  The camera passes close beside the old house exterior.  Deep darkness surrounds the property. Sparse moonlight catches portions of siding, windows, bushes and dead autumn leaves.  Nobody is outside.  No pedestrians. No trick-or-treaters. No cars passing. No visible POV body.  The house feels unnaturally isolated.  Crickets continue softly in the darkness.  Occasional dry leaves scrape across the ground in the wind.  Continue slowly approaching an old BACK DOOR.   [00:10–00:12]  Without stopping, the POV reaches the back door.  A hand briefly enters the bottom edge of frame naturally.  The old metal doorknob quietly TURNS.  Clearly hear the subtle mechanical movement of the old door hardware.  The hand slowly pushes the door inward.  The old wooden door gives a long, restrained CREEEAK as it opens.  The camera crosses the threshold directly into the house.  NO CUT.   [00:12–00:15]  The POV takes several cautious steps into a nearly black interior.  The camera movement becomes slightly slower and more cautious.  NO audible footsteps.  The outdoor crickets, wind and leaves become naturally MUFFLED behind the POV after entering the house.  Most of the room ahead disappears into deep grainy shadow.  However, from a hallway opening OFF TO THE LEFT comes an eerie DARK BLUE / PALE BLUE nighttime illumination.  The cold blue light weakly spills across part of the floor and one wall while the rest of the house remains nearly black.  The POV subtly turns toward that blue-lit hallway.  The interior is extremely quiet.  Only subtle old-house sounds remain: faint wood settling, the final residual movement of the old door, and extremely soft interior room tone.  Do NOT reveal anyone.  Do NOT reveal a monster.  Do NOT create another jump scare.  Do NOT reveal the source of the blue light.  End while the POV silently stares into the ominous blue hallway, as though something may be somewhere deeper inside the house.   overall_soundscape:  The scene relies entirely on realistic environmental sound and uncomfortable silence.  EXTERIOR: Persistent but restrained nighttime CRICKETS. Soft cold wind moving through trees and bushes. Occasional dry autumn leaves softly scraping across the ground.  NO FOOTSTEP SOUNDS. Walking movement remains visually natural but silent.  The natural ambience becomes increasingly sparse and uncomfortable as the POV approaches the house.  UPSTAIRS LIGHT: At the exact instant the second-story light switches OFF, hear one sudden sharp ELECTRICAL SNAP/POP from the house.  Immediately afterward, the crickets, wind and exterior ambience abruptly stop for approximately HALF A SECOND.  Complete unnatural dead silence.  Then the soft crickets, faint wind and natural nighttime ambience return.  BACK DOOR: Clearly audible old metal doorknob TURNING. Small mechanical latch movement. Slow restrained wooden DOOR CREAK as the door opens.  INTERIOR: As the POV crosses inside, exterior crickets, wind and leaves become naturally muffled behind the camera.  Extremely subtle old-house room tone. Occasional faint wooden settling. Final subtle residual movement of the opened door.  NO footsteps inside or outside. No voices. No dialogue. No screaming. No breathing directly into the microphone. No additional jump-scare effects.   non_diegetic_music:  NONE.

One CONTINUOUS FPV shot, no cuts, EXTREME kinetic speed through the fight. The footage NEVER reverses. NO slow motion except one half-second beat at the reveal, then an instant snap back to full speed. GHOST CAMERA: INVISIBLE, no drone or reflection in frame. The camera ORBITS the fighters at street level and DIVES in on every strike — always moving, never climbs. GEOMETRY LOCK: the two face each other along the street, resetting after every exchange; blows land OFF-axis past the lens.

REFERENCES: @Image1 is the LOCATION — match it exactly. @Image2 is BIG BRO — 185 cm, massive round heavy build, topknot and braids, teal jacket, shoulder sensor; match him exactly. @Image3 is LITTLE SIS — 160 cm, slim and quick, bun and braids, crimson sash, teal trousers; match her exactly. Her head reaches his shoulder. Render everything in the references' painterly cinematic style, fully animated.

The market is alive: steam, swaying lanterns, chickens pecking between stalls, laundry overhead. At a bun stall the vendor sets down the LAST fat steaming bun, and two hands slap onto it at the same instant — Big Bro's huge palm and Little Sis's gloved fingers. He snatches it first, stuffs it into his orange belt pouch and smirks; she narrows her eyes. A few stalls down, an old man on a stool slurps noodles, watching. Their fight drives them down the street toward him. She FIRES snapping kicks at his head; he swats them aside and palm-shoves her back, chickens SCATTERING squawking from her boots. She rolls under a fruit cart; the camera dives on her flurry grabbing at his pouch — he BOUNCES her off his belly with a laugh into a stall awning, tipping a startled cat off its edge, and she rebounds feet-first back at him. She steps off his shoulder, VAULTS his topknot and slaps the back of his head. A kid cheers; the old man keeps slurping as a stool cartwheels past. His backfist splinters a crate; she ducks and drives three palms into his chest. THE REVEAL: half-second slow motion — her flying knee slipping past his blocking palm toward his waist, dust hanging — then an INSTANT SNAP back to full speed as her knee SLAMS his belt pouch and the bun POPS out, tumbling through the air, bouncing off an awning, then a lantern. Both EXPLODE after it at once, the fight now a frantic scramble beneath it: she cartwheels over a cart, he barrels through baskets, stalls collapsing like dominoes, a water barrel bursting across the stones, ducks flapping out of a toppled crate, shoving and tripping each other, the camera tearing low between them. The bun drops toward the old man's stool; both launch a final full-length dive — and an inch from their fingers his chopsticks catch it in midair. They crash face-first into the wet dust at his feet. He takes a huge bite and chews, a chicken settling on his knee. The siblings look at each other, nose to nose in the dirt — and both burst out laughing as the clip cuts.

Sound: palm thuds, a rubbery BOING off his belly, squawking chickens, a yowling cat, splintering wood, a driving wuxia score of drums, erhu and pipa — dropping to one held breath of near-silence at the midair clash, then a MASSIVE concussive impact, then sustained escalating chaos — collapsing stalls, splashing water, quacking ducks, crashing lanterns, drums racing — cut to sudden silence on one sharp chopstick CLICK, a big chewing bite, then the siblings' laughter and a final playful drum hit.

Global style lock: painterly cinematic wuxia matching the references; @Image1, @Image2 and @Image3 match exactly, heights and proportions locked; the camera never visible, never climbs; the bun is one single object; every animal and onlooker REACTS and keeps moving, close, never frozen; every strike reads clean; playful, no injuries; no dialogue; no subtitles, no watermarks. 16:9.

Four 3–4 s beats follow, and the first and last share a device: a "circular fisheye peephole on black" that opens the film into a whip pan and returns at the end. In between come a low-angle flame toss with a speed ramp, precise slicing and tweezer plating, and a "stacked split-screen of eyes and hands". The output keeps the tungsten/teal 500T palette and grain throughout. A ready-made structure for chef, craft or maker spots.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 · 1998 Sony MiniDV rainy-weekend family vlog in a traditional Korean house: tea at the window, hotteok, cassette tapes, floor-table dinner
entries.description: A cosy-mood piece in an eight-scene format. The rain is the throughline ("Rain continues from morning to evening"), and the family's small domestic tasks are the action: tea at a rain-streaked window, cooking hotteok with her mother, folding blankets, finding handwritten cassette tapes and playing one, tea with her father and his newspaper, then dinner on floor cushions. The prompt adds an order-of-events block ("Pancakes before breakfast, cleaning after breakfast, cassette listening before dinner"), period exclusions ("No modern phones, smart TVs…") and a one-line FINAL GOAL. The output holds all three characters and the house across the scenes.
entries.prompt:
A RAINY WEEKEND AT HOME | KOREA, 1998 🌧️

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic live-action home vlog set in a traditional Korean family house in 1998. Make it look like authentic Sony MiniDV family footage.

CHARACTERS:

- Main girl: 21-year-old Korean woman with shoulder-length dark brown hair and bangs, wearing a cream knitted sweater and brown trousers.
- Mother: Short dark hair, floral apron.
- Father: Short black hair, grey sweater and dark trousers.

Keep faces, hairstyles and outfits consistent.

EXACT 8-SCENE SEQUENCE:

1. RAINY MORNING (0–4s): The girl sits beside a rainy window, holding warm tea and watching raindrops fall over the quiet Korean neighbourhood.

2. MAKING PANCAKES (4–8s): In the traditional kitchen, she mixes dough, adds brown sugar and cinnamon filling, and cooks golden homemade hotteok while her mother smiles nearby.

3. BREAKFAST (8–11s): She enjoys a freshly cooked pancake and tea beside the rainy window.

4. CLEANING (11–15s): She folds blankets, arranges cushions, wipes the wooden table and sweeps the floor while her mother folds laundry.

5. OLD CASSETTE TAPES (15–19s): She discovers handwritten cassette tapes in an old drawer, inserts one into a vintage cassette player and listens with a nostalgic smile.

6. FAMILY TEA TIME (19–22s): Her father joins with a newspaper. The girl serves tea, and all three share smiles and laughter.

7. PREPARING DINNER (22–26s): Mother prepares Korean rice, kimchi, doenjang-jjigae and grilled fish. The daughter helps arrange everything on the low dining table.

8. COZY EVENING (26–30s): The family enjoys dinner together on floor cushions. They chat and laugh naturally. The girl smiles at the camcorder. End with rain falling outside the window.

VISUAL STYLE:
Photorealistic live-action, authentic 1998 Sony MiniDV footage, soft resolution, subtle tape noise, faded warm colours, handheld camera shake, imperfect framing and natural exposure changes.

AUDIO: Rain, cooking sounds, cassette player clicks, family conversations, laughter and dinner ambience. No background music, narration or subtitles.

STRICT CONTINUITY: Same characters, outfits, house and objects throughout. Pancakes before breakfast, cleaning after breakfast, cassette listening before dinner. Rain continues from morning to evening.

No modern phones, smart TVs, teleportation, duplicated characters, outfit changes, distorted hands or artificial CGI.

FINAL GOAL: A peaceful, cozy and nostalgic family memory that feels like a genuine rainy weekend recording from Korea in 1998. Include all 8 scenes in exact order within 30 seconds.

entries.prompt:
**15 sec, 16:9, text-to-video only. Exactly 6 scenes, 2.5 sec per scene. Every scene transition is a clean hard cut with no effects. Zero reference images, start frames, or storyboard inputs. Include generated natural sound.**
**【Art Style】**
Original Japanese-style hand-drawn 2D cooking animation. A fully hand-drawn look. Soft yet crisp pencil outlines with subtle line-weight variation and retained hand-drawn wobble. Thin, warm lines for food; lines one grade thicker for hands and tools. Clean 2–3-tone full-color cel shading in warm mid-tones, with no black-crushed shadows. A lived-in kitchen showing brush strokes, shallow atmospheric perspective, restrained analog film grain, and slight color bleed along cel edges. Strong specular highlights only on the ganache and wet dough. Do not imitate the distinctive look of any existing studio, artist, film, or character.
**【Subject and Rules】**
Subject: cocoa chocolate loaf bread. Make a cold ganache sheet from dark chocolate and fresh cream, knead the cocoa dough, and proceed through the first proof.
Only the forearms below the elbows and the two hands of one skilled adult woman appear. Ivory linen sleeves, warm peachy-beige skin, short unpainted nails, five fingers on each hand, no accessories. No face, head, torso, full body, or second person. Only the food and the cooking process are the subject. Each scene has exactly one main action, and ingredient states progress forward only. Never show the finished loaf, baked bread, formed log, or interior chocolate.
**【Scene Breakdown】**
**Scene 1 — 0.00–2.50**
Camera: high overhead close-up looking almost straight down at a worn oak cutting board, very slow push-in. Start: one unwrapped block of dark couverture and one knife with a pale oak handle. Action: the left hand holds it steady while the right hand makes four separate cuts, lifting the blade fully each time. Change: a pile of small, even pieces. Texture: dry, sharp cut faces and tiny crumbs, neither melting nor glistening. Link: all of these same pieces go into Scene 2.
**Scene 2 — 2.50–5.00 ★ Texture showcase scene**
Camera: low side macro just above the bowl rim, moving very slowly to the right. Start: the pieces from Scene 1 melting from the edges in hot fresh cream. Action: a dark brown silicone spatula stirs three widening circles from the center outward. Change: the pieces vanish into a black, uniform ganache, and the final mark slowly closes. Texture: heavy viscosity that does not slosh like water, with narrow bright highlights. Link: butter and cake flour are mixed into this same ganache, spread to 3 mm, and chilled.
**Scene 3 — 5.00–7.50**
Camera: fixed high 45-degree medium shot looking down at the work surface. Start: one chilled ganache sheet, 22×8 cm and 3 mm thick, on natural-colored parchment paper. Action: two hands grip both ends of the parchment and lift once. Change: the sheet bends gently but neither sags nor cracks. Texture: a cold, flexible solid with a narrow, firm sheen. Link: this same single sheet is kept cold in reserve.
**Scene 4 — 7.50–10.00**
Camera: fixed overhead close-up near the rim of a stainless steel bowl. Start: uniform brown dry powder with a cold dairy liquid in the center. Action: a spatula folds four times from the bottom upward. Change: one lump of rough, torn, shaggy cocoa dough with almost no loose flour. Texture: dark wet patches, a lumpy surface, small dry flour at the edges. Link: this same dough and one block of butter go to Scene 5.
**Scene 5 — 10.00–12.50 ★ Texture showcase scene**
Camera: fixed low side medium shot at work-surface height. Start: one block of butter in the center of the shaggy dough. Action: two hands push forward and fold inward three times. Change: the butter marks and cracks disappear into a smooth, elastic, deep-cocoa dough, and one thin edge lets light pass through without tearing. Texture: elastic sheen rather than wet gloss, with gluten resistance. Link: this same dough proofs in the same bowl to roughly double in size.
**Scene 6 — 12.50–15.00**
Camera: high 45-degree macro toward the center of the bowl, very slow push toward the indentation. Start: the same dough as a smooth dome risen to roughly double. Action: one index finger presses the center and withdraws completely. Change: only the edges slowly spring back partially, while the center mark remains shallow. Texture: fine fermentation bubbles and soft elasticity, no baked crust. Link: end at this proof-complete state.
**【Camera】**
Change at least two of distance, angle, and height in every scene. Within a scene, hold still or use only the specified extremely slow movement. No whip pans, handheld shake, rotation, or sudden zoom. What is touching what must always be readable. The tightest macros are used only in Scenes 2 and 6.
**【Texture and Movement】**
The progression chocolate pieces → heavy emulsion → cold flexible sheet, and dry powder → shaggy dough → smooth gluten → risen dough, must read in distinct stages. Hands carry weight and follow-through after each motion; liquids and dough obey viscosity, elasticity, and gravity. No sudden morphing or reversion of state.
**【Light and Stage】**
One clean, warm-morning home kitchen. White quartz worktop and a worn oak cutting board. Soft golden key light from a window at the upper left of frame, a weak cool fill on the opposite side, and grounded shadows in the same direction beneath every hand, tool, and ingredient. Only objects named in the current scene appear.
**【Physical Continuity】**
Maintain the same full quantity of couverture, the same single batch of ganache and one sheet, the same single lump of cocoa dough, and the same hands, sleeves, bowl, kitchen, and light source. The number, size, and material of tools and ingredients do not change. Obey the real cooking sequence and gravity.
**【Sound】**
Low home-kitchen room tone and on-screen contact sounds only: dry chopping, wet spatula friction, parchment rustling, bowl resonance, dough-sticking sounds, a small finger-stick sound. No BGM, dialogue, narration, or human/animal voices.
**【Negative】**
On-screen text, titles, captions, subtitles, numbers, labels, logos,

entries.title: Seedance 2.5: 15-shot floating-bed dream comedy that ends on a match cut from a scream in the clouds to the same scream in a plane seat
entries.description: A 30-second, 15-shot montage (every shot exactly 2.0 s, listed as S1 0–2s … S15 28–30s) about a woman who wakes on a bed floating in the clouds, gets served a plain sandwich by a skydiving waiter, sees a jet burst through the clouds, and screams. The payoff is S14, a match cut: "same head position, same angle, same screaming expression" now in a plane window seat, with "the scream carries over the cut" so the audio bridges the edit. The prompt writes the lens as field of view plus focal length on every shot ("18°/100mm close-up", "84°/22mm wide"), fixes screen geometry (sun upper left, birds right to left, window screen-left), gives a colour budget ("~70% soft white and sky blue, ~25% warm sun gold, ~5% chrome glint"), allows only scripted lines, and ends with a LOCKS line that restates the event order. Useful for any dream→reality or fantasy→product reveal where the cut has to land on matching action.
entries.prompt:
15 shots across 30 seconds, montage, every shot 2.0s: S1 0–2s, S2 2–4s, S3 4–6s, S4 6–8s, S5 8–10s, S6 10–12s, S7 12–14s, S8 14–16s, S9 16–18s, S10 18–20s, S11 20–22s, S12 22–24s, S13 24–26s, S14 26–28s, S15 28–30s. Hard cuts. Real-time, no slow motion.

Style: 8K photoreal live-action fantasy comedy, large-format film, organic grain. NOT a 3D render, NOT a game engine, NOT a game cutscene, NOT a cartoon. Pore-level skin. 24fps, 180-degree shutter, real motion blur, no warping, no morphing.

NO ON-SCREEN TEXT — CRITICAL: no captions, subtitles, titles, logos or watermarks at any point.

THE SCRIPT — CRITICAL: only these words are spoken, by the woman, nothing improvised: S7: "Ooohh... Nooo!!". S8: "Am I dreaming??". S13 and S14: a wordless scream only. Nobody else speaks.

THE TONE — CRITICAL: gentle comic fantasy. Her reactions are real, never mugging; the waiter stays dead serious and elegant.

LIVING SKY — CRITICAL: the bed floats in open sky surrounded by gathered white clouds, drifting slowly downward but never falling. Clouds drift at different speeds, vapor slides over the bed edge, wind gusts in uneven pulses lifting the duvet hem, her hair and the waiter's coat tails.

ASSETS:

@Image 1 = the woman, 100% match to reference face, hair and wardrobe.

@Image 2 = the waiter, full formal restaurant uniform: black tailcoat, white shirt, black bow tie, white gloves, slim black backpack with a pull cord on its left side.

GEOMETRY: a white-sheeted double bed centred in frame, sky and clouds on all sides, sun upper left. The waiter lands on the foot of the bed, she sits at the head. Birds travel screen-right to screen-left. S14–S15: she sits in a window seat, window on screen-left, passengers on screen-right.

FIRST FRAME: tight close-up on her sleeping face, no empty hold.

ACTION (montage, every cut on the 2-second mark):

S1 (18°/100mm close-up, gentle handheld): asleep, uneven breathing; birdsong grows loud off-frame, her brow knits, she groans and turns her head on the pillow, eyes shut.

S2 (29°/85mm, side angle): a wind gust whips her hair across her face; eyes still closed, she swats it away.

S3 (34°/65mm, high angle over the bed): she yanks the duvet up to her chin; warm sunlight crawls onto her face and she squeezes her eyes tighter, annoyed.

S4 (crash zoom): she sits bolt upright, duvet sliding off; the lens snap-zooms into an extreme close-up of her eyes flying wide open.

S5 (zoom out to 63°/30mm medium wide): reveal the bed floating in the middle of the clouds, golden sun flaring soft.

S6 (84°/22mm wide): a flock of birds enters frame-right, chirps loudly at centre frame and exits left; her head follows them, mouth open.

S7 (47°/50mm medium, handheld): she grabs her head with both hands: "Ooohh... Nooo!!"

S8 (18°/100mm close-up): utterly bewildered, head tilting, eyes darting around the clouds, lips parted, she mutters: "Am I dreaming??"

S9 (63°/30mm medium wide): a waiter drops from above in freefall and lands on the foot of the bed, mattress compressing.

S10 (47°/50mm): he lifts a polished chrome dome off a plate like a grand banquet course: just a plain sandwich. He pulls the cord on his backpack side and is yanked straight up out of frame top.

S11 (47°/50mm medium): still wrapped in the duvet, she bites the sandwich, chews, and smiles wide, savouring it.

S12 (84°/22mm wide, low behind her shoulder): a deep roar; a passenger jet bursts through the clouds, its nose filling the frame, heading straight at her.

S13 (fast horizontal orbit ending at 47°/50mm): the camera swings around her and lands on her face as she screams.

S14 (match cut, 47°/50mm, aircraft cabin): same head position, same angle, same screaming expression, now in casual travel clothes in a window seat. The scream carries over the cut; nearby passengers jolt and turn to stare.

S15 (47°/50mm): she freezes, cheeks flushing, covers her face with both hands and turns toward the window.

PHYSICS: real gravity on landings, mattress compressing and rebounding, coat tails lagging, the cord yank jolting his body upward. Only the bed floats.

ACTING: she is invested in one task: figure out where she is. Her eyes hunt the sky, the birds and the waiter, checking if this is real; in S14–S15 they dart to the staring passengers, then escape to the window. Natural blinks, never a frozen stare. The waiter keeps polite focus on her.

LIGHT & COLOUR: warm morning sun upper left, bright cloud bounce. ~70% soft white and sky blue, ~25% warm sun gold on skin, ~5% chrome glint from the dome. S14–S15: soft cool daylight through the cabin window.

AUDIO: birdsong, wind gusts, duvet rustle, mattress creak, chrome dome lift, cord snap and whoosh, jet roar, her lines, cabin hum and murmurs. No music, no score, no swell, no drone.

LOCKS: order holds — sleep, disturbed, sits up, birds, disbelief, waiter's sandwich, she savours it, jet, match cut to plane, hides face. Same face and hair throughout. No CGI look, no gimbal glide, skin never plastic.

Then it times every event to the millisecond: woman frozen with a misty white edge glow, "rapid white flash at 00:00.850", hard cut to the man at 00:01.000, flash, back to her with "a brief ghosted afterimage overlay", glow swells and fades to black by 00:04.000. entries.title: Seedance 2.5: 2004 MiniDV found-footage elevator prank, one 24 s handheld take with a full camcorder-fault spec
entries.description: The strongest camcorder-texture spec in the library so far, in a mandatory block: "about 480 lines upscaled: soft image, interlacing combing on fast motion, mild sharpening halos, low dynamic range, ceiling lights and steel reflections blown to white, shadows crushed to black with chroma noise, warm yellow white balance, slow auto-exposure and autofocus", plus what to leave out (no HDR, no phone sharpness, no grading, no shallow depth of field, no REC or date overlay). Operator behaviour is written as a separate block (shake that grows with emotion, late reframes, overshooting zooms, the operator and camera never seen, even in steel doors). The timeline uses sound to carry the off-screen event (bang, cable snap, a brake screech that travels downward, a distant crash) and closes on a prop payoff (the torn "OUT OF ORDER" sign falling out of a pocket). The continuity block rules out blood, bodies and injuries. Reusable as a template for any found-footage or UGC camcorder piece.
entries.prompt:
FORMAT
Exactly 24 seconds, vertical 9:16, one continuous uninterrupted take, no cuts. Authentic found footage: a real prank filmed at night in 2004 on a cheap consumer MiniDV handycam. Fast, punchy pacing with no dead pauses. It must look like a genuine home recording, not a film and not a modern phone video.

CAMCORDER IMAGE (MANDATORY)
Standard-definition MiniDV look, about 480 lines upscaled: soft image, interlacing combing on fast motion, mild sharpening halos, low dynamic range, ceiling lights and steel reflections blown to white, shadows crushed to black with chroma noise, warm yellow white balance, slow auto-exposure and autofocus. No HDR, no smartphone sharpness, no cinematic grading, no shallow depth of field. People, skin, fabric, steel, and concrete look physically genuine through this imperfect image. No REC text, date stamp, or any overlay.

HANDHELD OPERATION
Held by an unseen friend. Natural hand shake that grows with emotion: sway while hiding, bouncing while laughing, violent jolts during the fall, trembling at the reveal. Tilted horizon, framing that drifts and corrects late, focus that hunts before locking, clumsy zooms that overshoot, heads sometimes cut off by the frame edge. The operator, his hands, body, shadow, reflection, and the camcorder NEVER appear on screen, including in steel doors and walls. Only his voice is heard, close to the mic.

LOCATION
Old apartment building corridor at night, 2004: yellowed beige walls with scuffs, worn grey tile floor, warm ceiling lights, one fluorescent tube flickering down the hall. Brushed steel elevator landing doors with a steel sill. On the wall right of the doors: a call button and, taped above it, a white A4 sheet with large bold black letters "OUT OF ORDER". Above the doors: a small red digital display showing "7". Cabin interior: scratched brushed steel walls, cold white ceiling light, rear handrail, button panel on the right front wall.

CHARACTERS
OPERATOR: never seen, voice only, young man, excited whisper, loud laugh.
FRIEND B: man, about 24, blond curly hair, denim jacket, white T-shirt, grey jeans, a silver flip phone in his right front pocket.
JAKE: man, about 25, short dark hair, light grey hoodie, black backpack on one shoulder, white sneakers, wired earbuds, texting on an open silver flip phone.
Ordinary real-looking people, natural skin with imperfections, consistent faces and clothing throughout.

THE PRINT
A thin vinyl sticker cut to exactly the size of the cabin floor, wall to wall, no white border, nothing extending into the corridor. It shows a photo of a shaft looking down and from a distance convincingly looks like a missing floor. Up close, gloss and faint creases reveal it is flat. The image stays identical whenever visible.

THE REAL SHAFT
Seen only at the end: irregular and physically real, rough stained concrete, a steel guide rail with rusty brackets, snapped greasy cables, dust. Never symmetrical, never a repeating tunnel, no visible bottom, no lit end. Completely unlike the print.

TIMELINE
0.0-2.5 seconds:
Shaky shot straight into the open elevator: the floor seems missing, a deep shaft below. The operator giggles. Friend B steps into frame, plants one foot on the "void", the vinyl crinkles, he bounces once and grins at the lens: "Looks real, right?" He steps back out into the corridor.

2.5-4.5 seconds:
The camera whips to the wall right of the doors; focus locks on the "OUT OF ORDER" sheet. Friend B rips it off, crumples it, and stuffs it into his right front pocket: "Can't have that ruining it." He presses the call button to hold the doors open, and both flatten against the wall left of the doors. The camera settles beside the doorway, aimed into the cabin.

4.5-8.0 seconds:
Jake walks in from the right, texting on his flip phone, and steps into the cabin. His foot lands on the printed shaft: he screams "WHOA!", stumbles back two steps, and slams his back and backpack into the rear wall, grabbing the handrail. On that impact the whole cabin drops about ten centimeters with a heavy metallic CLUNK and tilts slightly, leaving a clear visible step between the cabin floor and the corridor sill. The cabin light flickers. Jake freezes, wide-eyed. No frozen T-pose, no arms held out straight.

8.0-11.0 seconds:
The operator bursts out laughing, thinking the clunk was part of the joke; the camera bounces. Friend B points into the cabin: "Bro, your face!" A clumsy zoom on Jake overshoots and cuts off his head. Jake sees it is a sticker, goes red, and slaps a button: "You guys are idiots." The doors slide closed and meet fully. The display still shows "7".

11.0-12.0 seconds:
Only after the doors are fully closed, the display changes to "6" with a motor hum. Friend B mimics Jake's scream.

12.0-15.0 seconds:
A massive metallic BANG behind the doors; the doors shudder in their frame. A sharp crack of a snapping cable, then the whip of loose cable. The display goes black. Instantly a piercing continuous steel-on-steel SCREECH: the cabin's emergency brakes grinding on the guide rails as it falls. It starts harsh right behind the doors, making them vibrate, then travels rapidly downward, more muffled, lower in pitch, hollow and echoing, with irregular knocks of the cabin hitting brackets. The corridor lights dip. The camera is thrown toward the tile, the mic clipping, then swings back to the doors, out of focus.

15.0-16.5 seconds:
The screech ends far below in a deep heavy CRASH; the floor shudders. A short echo rolls up the shaft, then silence except the fluorescent buzz and shaky breathing. Focus finds Friend B's face, half cut off by the frame, pale. Operator whispers: "Dude..."

16.5-18.5 seconds:
Friend B jams his fingers into the door seam and drags the doors apart with his whole body, sneakers slipping on tile. They grind open to shoulder width. Behind them: pure black.

18.5-20.5 seconds:
A click: the camcorder's small built-in light switches on, a harsh cold beam with fast falloff. The camera pushes to the gap over Friend B's shoulder. No cabin. The beam shows only the nearest few meters: stained concrete, a rusty bracket, snapped cables swaying and knocking the wall, dust in the beam, grit sprinkling onto the lens. The camera tilts down: the light dies after two floors, below is total black.

20.5-24.0 seconds:
Friend B pulls his flip phone from his right front pocket; the crumpled sign comes out with it, drops onto the tile beside the sill, and half unfolds. The camera tilts down and focus locks on the bold words "OUT OF ORDER". Above frame, Friend B flips the phone open, dials, and whispers: "...Jake?" A beat. From deep in the black shaft, faint and echoing, a silly polyphonic cartoon quacking ringtone starts playing. The camera stays on the sign at the edge of the shaft, trembling. The ringtone keeps playing. Take ends. No title, no further event.

PHYSICS AND REALISM
Real weight and inertia: Jake's stumble and backpack impact, the cabin's sudden ten-centimeter sag and tilt, laughter shaking the camera, finger strain and heavy door resistance, sneaker slip. Crumpled paper falls and unfolds naturally. Cables sway with decaying momentum; dust and grit fall with gravity. Light comes only from corridor practicals, the cabin light while the cabin is present, the camcorder light, and the phone screen.

AUDIO AND DIALOGUE
Camcorder onboard mic: close, thin, compressed, handling rustle, faint tape hiss, clipping on loud sounds. Vinyl crinkle, paper ripping and crumpling, whispers, footsteps, scream, backpack on steel, the cabin clunk, echoing laughter, button click, door motor, lift hum, the bang, cable snap and whip, the long brake screech traveling down with echo and knocks, the deep crash, fluorescent buzz, doors grinding, hollow shaft air, creaking cables, grit on the lens, and the distant echoing ringtone. The ringtone is an original simple quack melody, not any existing song. English dialogue only, naturally lip-synced: "Looks real, right?" / "Can't have that ruining it." / "WHOA!" / "Bro, your face!" / "You guys are idiots." / "Dude..." / "...Jake?" No music, narration, subtitles, or laugh track.

STRICT CONTINUITY
Two visible people plus the unseen operator. Jake is never seen after the doors close. The sticker stays in the cabin and leaves with it. The sign is torn off once, stays in the pocket, and falls out only at the end. The display changes only after the doors fully close and stays black after failing. One sag, one fall, one door opening. The cabin never returns. The real shaft never resembles the print. Nobody steps into the shaft. No smartphones, only flip phones. No blood, no bodies, no injuries, no visible sparks, no explosions, no extra people, no duplicated limbs. The operator and camcorder never appear in reflections or shadows.

entries.title: MiniMax H3: rainy-night Japanese train platform, one locked long take as a passing commuter train's light washes across a woman's profile
entries.description: An 8,500-character single-take prompt that treats light as the main performer. The headlights grow "extremely gradually", the cool headlight glow turns into the warm carriage glow "over about a second, brightness roughly unchanged, only cool-to-warm", and a gust arrives in the same instant as the train's nose. A long paragraph of light physics forbids the usual AI failures: "no window-shaped light patches sweeping across her face", no flicker, exposure locked, light landing on umbrella, rain, tiles and coat at once "never only on her face". The skin rules are strict too: matte, "No skin oil, sweat, water shine, specular spots… or droplets on the face." Blocking keeps a clean right profile the whole time, and the smile comes only at the end. It's a very complete realism checklist for any moving-light-on-face shot.
entries.prompt:
A single continuous live-action long take on a Japanese elevated train platform at night in the rain. One woman waiting alone, camera locked in place at her right side, filming her right profile down the length of the platform. It runs from her small waiting fidgets, through a commuter train arriving and passing in front of her, to the train nearly stopping and a soft side-profile smile. One take, camera fixed with only slight handheld breathing, no cuts, no zoom, no push-in. Normal real-world speed throughout, no slow motion.

Shot 1 — 0.0s: Realistic cinematic, real-camera rainy-night platform, one continuous long take, medium shot from mid-thigh up, camera fixed at her right at chest height looking down the platform's depth. Right side of frame is the wet-bright yellow tactile paving, the platform edge, and two steel rails converging into the distance, with the arched glass windscreen beyond; left side is the platform interior and orange glowing shopfront boxes; cool fluorescent tubes recede overhead; red-blue-green neon bokeh at the far end; tiles wet-black and reflective. Riria stands center-slightly-left inside the yellow paving, facing the tracks, her right profile to the lens, shopfront orange rimming her back and bun. The right-side rail is empty, no train yet. She is already mid-action: tilting the umbrella back a little, looking up past its rim at the night sky beyond the canopy, reaching her right hand forward toward the track side past the umbrella rim, palm up, holding a beat to test whether it's still raining, a few drops landing in her palm.

Shot 1 continues — 1.5s: She pulls her hand back, rights the umbrella back over her head, lets out a soft breath, and shifts her weight from one foot to the other.

Shot 1 continues — 2.0s: Two small, soft cool-white headlights light up at the far end of the right-side rail. She leans her upper body slightly forward (feet not crossing the yellow paving), peering toward the far end of the tracks, body still squared to the rails. The headlights grow larger and brighter extremely gradually along the right rail, the steel, the standing water, and the platform edge lighting up bit by bit.

Shot 1 continues — 3.5s: She straightens up, steps back half a step, grips the umbrella handle again with her left hand, her gaze following the approaching train. The light keeps rising slowly and evenly — first catching the side-profile edge of her forehead, nose bridge, and lips, then washing softly onto her face. The same light also falls on the droplets on the umbrella, the rain, the wet tiles, and her coat, no hard edges, no flicker. Her skin is only softly brightened overall, still matte, no shine spot. She squints slightly and tucks her chin a little into the turtleneck.

Shot 1 continues — 5.5s: A silver stainless-steel commuter train with a green waistline reaches her along the right-side rail, wheels on the rails, body tight to the platform edge, the nose passing in front of her and exiting frame right. In the same instant a gust blows in from the depth of frame: bangs and side hairs pressed to her cheeks, coat hem, lapels, and back belt lifting, umbrella tilting about a hand's width and trembling. Her left hand steadies the umbrella, her right hand lifts to gather the blown-open coat front at her chest, still facing the tracks. The cool-white headlight glow transitions smoothly into the warm-white carriage glow over about a second, brightness roughly unchanged, only cool-to-warm. Carriages run past in front of her on the right with motion blur, the warm-white light a long steady even band on her face, coat front, and umbrella rim, no flicker. Her feet stay planted, sharp, normal speed, no slow motion.

Shot 1 continues — 7.0s to 10.0s: The train visibly decelerates, carriages resolving back into distinguishable windows, inside them only defocused warm-white light and blurred shapes, but the warm light on her stays constant. The wind eases, hems settle, hair slowly drops. Around 8.5s she releases the coat front and uses her right fingertips to tuck the strands stuck to her cheek behind her ear, revealing the pearl stud, then lets her right hand fall naturally.

Shot 1 continues — 10.0s: The train glides slowly toward a near-stop, settling on the right-side rail, the warm-white light still steady and soft on her face.

Shot 1 continues — 10.5s: Her head turns only slightly toward the lens side, feet and shoulders still toward the tracks, still a clean right profile in frame, at most the far corner of her eye and mouth just showing, never a three-quarter front or full face. Her gaze slants gently toward the lens side, not direct to camera. Framing stays mid-thigh-up medium, no push-in.

Shot 1 continues — 12.5s: The corner of her mouth slowly lifts into a soft, restrained closed-lip smile on the profile, cheekbone rising a touch, eye corner curving, never a toothy grin or a posed frozen smile. The smile holds on the profile, she blinks once and breathes out softly, a strand of hair still swaying in the leftover wind, the train completing its last short glide at walking pace with doors staying shut. The image ends while these tiny motions are still underway, never a freeze frame. Live throughout — rain keeps falling, droplets slide and pool on the umbrella, the turtleneck collar rises faintly with her breath, flyaways drift, puddle ripples shimmer, distant neon glows steady, the handheld frame breathing lightly.

All light changes are continuous, slow gradients, never blinking: no flicker, strobe, or on-off pulsing, no per-frame brightness jumps, no sudden light on or off, no hard-edge pools or stage-spotlight circles, no window-shaped light patches sweeping across her face. The windows are large and the carriage light diffuse, so what lands on her is one steady sheet of warm light. The headlights are just two softly growing points, never direct into the lens, the frame never flashes white. The same light lands on the umbrella, the rain, the wet tiles, the platform edge, and her coat at once, never only on her face. Fluorescent tubes and distant neon glow steady, never flickering. Camera exposure locked the whole time, no auto-brightening or darkening. The whole clip brightens smoothly only once, then holds steady, never bright-then-dark-then-bright. The nose passing in front of her and the gust lifting her hair and hems happen in the same instant (around 5.5s), never wind-before-train or train-already-past-before-wind.

Prohibited

No subtitles, watermark, logo, or overlay text; platform light boxes, billboards, and train destination displays appear only as defocused glowing color blocks, never any readable text. No dialogue or narration. No standing still before the train or woodenly posing before it; no flicking water off the hand. No light blinking, flickering, strobing, or on-off pulsing; no bright-then-dark-then-bright; no sudden light on or off; no headlight flaring white into the lens; no window-shaped light patches sweeping across her face; no stage-spotlight circles or hard light beams; no light landing only on her face; no exposure wavering; no flickering tubes or neon. No standing with her back to the tracks; no facing the shopfronts, platform interior, or lens; no chest toward frame left. No rail on the left side of frame; no train driving onto the platform; no train on the left or shopfront side; no train crossing the frame; no train floating or off the rails; no train passing behind her; no train between her and the lens; no train coming from behind the camera, driving off into the distance, or reversing. No push-in, pull-out, zoom, or orbit. No chest-up close-up or face close-up. No full face to lens, three-quarter front glance back, or direct eye contact. No turning the shoulders or turning around. No early smile. No skin oil, sweat, water shine, specular spots, wet reflection, or droplets on the face. No rubbery, silicone, waxwork, or plastic skin, no smoothing, no freckles vanishing. No grey studio backdrop. No triptych, split-screen, or a second Riria. No other passengers or staff on the platform. No doors opening or anyone getting off. No slow motion or slowed hair drift. No umbrella flipping inside out, flying from her hand, or the shaft crossing her face; no right hand covering her face. No features drifting into a similar-looking different person — it is this person from the reference. No toothy grin. No global amber or teal-orange filter. No CG, anime, over-sharpening, or HDR look. No freeze frame. No third hand or finger distortion.

entries.description: A fashion film written like a music-synced storyboard: a 4-part rhythm map (silence → build → drop at 8 s → poster), then 30 half-second beats. The wardrobe rule is the clever part: "Any new colors must only appear through watercolor gradually absorbing into the fabric", so the white high-neck dress picks up pale cyan, crimson lake and smoky violet over the take. The camera follows one path with "No hidden transitions" (droplet macro → pull back → orbit → paper gallery → through dimensional type → overhead poster). entries.prompt:
## Concept
AQUARELLE No.7 — an avant-garde haute couture film where watercolor becomes a living medium.

15-second cinematic sequence.

The rhythm controls the visual world:
0–4s: restrained silence and negative space
4–8s: gradual density buildup
8s: drop moment, expanding into fluid long-form motion
12–15s: transition into a final fashion poster composition

## Character Identity Lock

Maintain the exact same female character throughout the entire video.

Identity:
- Young woman
- Long black hair
- Calm and refined facial features
- White high-neck pigment dress
- Black wide belt
- Pigment heels

Strict consistency:
- Same face
- Same hairstyle
- Same age
- Same body proportions
- Same garment structure

Any new colors must only appear through watercolor gradually absorbing into the fabric.

Core concept:
Her fingertips can extract transparent watercolor ribbons from the air.

These watercolor ribbons can:
- Pull the camera through space
- Transform the environment
- Shape physical typography
- Interact with depth and materials

The world follows real cinematic physics:
water, paper, fabric, light, shadows, and depth of field must feel physically believable.

## Camera Direction

Strict one-take shot.
No cuts.
No teleportation.
No hidden transitions.

Camera journey:

Macro shot of a floating water droplet →
watercolor ribbon emerges →
camera pulls back to reveal the woman →
camera circles around her →
enters a paper art gallery →
passes through dimensional typography →
rises into a final overhead fashion poster.

## Typography

Only allow these words:

LET SILENCE BLOOM

AQUARELLE No.7

WEAR THE UNSEEN

Typography is not a flat overlay.

Letters must have:
- Physical depth
- Wet watercolor reflections
- Paper fiber edges
- Shadows
- Occlusion
- Material interaction

## Visual Style

Avant-garde fashion editorial.

Inspired by:
- Museum catalog composition
- Handmade ivory paper
- Sculptural negative space
- Elegant Didone serif typography
- Translucent watercolor calligraphy

Color palette:
- Pale cyan
- Crimson lake
- Smoky violet
- Ink black

## Motion Language

Every movement follows the music:

Kick:
Camera movement and paper folding.

Wooden snare:
Paper structures physically fold and transform.

Sub-bass:
Changes the perception of spatial scale.

##  Storyboard

30 beats, 0.5 seconds each.

01 0.0–0.5
Macro shot: A transparent water droplet floats in the air, reflecting a blurred silhouette of a black-haired woman.

02 0.5–1.0
The droplet stretches with the breath-like vocal, becoming a pale cyan watercolor thread.

03 1.0–1.5
Camera travels backward along the thread as paper fibers slowly emerge into focus.

04 1.5–2.0
The thread wraps around the lens. Focus shifts to her raised fingertip.

05 2.0–3.0
Camera continues pulling back, revealing her face and white high-neck dress.

06 3.0–4.0
She moves her wrist. The watercolor thread guides a smooth camera arc.

07 4.0–8.0
Additional watercolor colors emerge from her movement.
Paper folds, typography begins forming, and the phrase "LET SILENCE BLOOM" appears as a physical object.

08 8.0–12.0
The camera passes through a transparent paper flower structure.
The environment expands into an endless ivory paper gallery.

Her dress absorbs watercolor naturally.
The ribbons create sculptural forms around her body.

09 12.0–15.0
Camera cranes upward.

The composition transforms into a luxury fashion advertisement poster.

Typography appears:

AQUARELLE No.7

WEAR THE UNSEEN

Final frame:
A museum-level fashion editorial poster.
The woman remains centered, calm, and elegant.
A final watercolor droplet remains suspended in the air.

## Negative Prompt

No:
- Cuts
- Scene changes
- Identity change
- Face swap
- Extra limbs
- Deformed hands
- Random costume changes
- Explosive paint effects without physical cause
- Incorrect typography
- Chinese characters
- Extra subtitles
- Extra logos
- Watermarks

Style: prestige historical war-era drama, quiet and devastating. 35mm film look, Kodak Vision3 500T, fine grain, soft halation on the window, muted earthy palette, cold dawn light from the window as the only key light, deep shadows, slow restrained camera. Aspect ratio 2.39:1 widescreen. Performances are subtle and naturalistic: small breaths, hesitations, eyes avoiding each other.

Story: Before dawn, the son is leaving for the war. The father has never known how to say goodbye.

0–4s: Static wide shot exactly like Image 1. Steam rises slowly from the cups. Silence, a ticking wall clock, distant birds. The father rubs his thumb against his knuckles. The son stares at his cup without drinking.

4–8s: Slow push-in toward the father, medium close-up. He breathes in to speak, stops, looks at the window. His jaw tightens. The father says quietly, in a low rough voice: "Your mother would've known what to say."

8–12s: Reverse medium close-up on the son. He keeps his eyes down, a faint sad smile. The son says softly: "You don't have to say anything, Dad."

12–17s: Close-up of the father's weathered hands. He slowly unbuckles an old worn leather wristwatch from his wrist and slides it across the table, past the coffee pot, until it stops in front of the son's hands. The ticking of the watch becomes audible.

17–21s: Close-up on the son's face. His eyes fill with tears; one tear runs down his cheek. He looks up at his father for the first time. The father says, almost a whisper: "It brought me home once. It'll bring you home."

21–23s: Back to the same wide shot and same kitchen layout as Image 1. The son stands up slowly, puts on the wristwatch, and rests his right hand firmly on his father's left shoulder for one long second. The father does not look up; he only closes his eyes.

23–25s: The son walks to the wooden back door on the left wall, turns the handle, opens it and steps outside. Cold blue dawn daylight falls across the floorboards through the open doorway, with no light beams or rays in the air. He closes the door behind him. The son stays solid and fully physical the whole time and is visible until the door closes. Outside, an old truck engine starts and slowly fades away.

25–30s: Very slow push-in on the father, now alone at the table. The steam from the son's untouched cup thins and disappears. The father reaches out and places his hand around the son's cup, holding it as if it were still warm. His shoulders tremble once. Hold on his silhouette against the white window. Cut to black at the 30-second mark.

Sound: no BGM until 21s; only room tone, wall clock, cups, breathing. From 21s, a single low solo cello note enters and swells gently until the cut to black. Dialogue in English, natural and quiet.

Do not add subtitles.

entries.description: A five-scene 30-second animated short written like a mini film bible: ART STYLE ("soft rounded shapes… pastel colors… Not photorealistic or anime"), MAIN CHARACTER (round cream body, blue cap, yellow backpack, "Maintain exactly the same appearance throughout"), SETTING, five timed scenes, then CONTINUITY written as a count ("One delivery worker, one paper airplane, one yellow backpack, and one rainbow container") and AUDIO with a no-existing-music rule. entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second cute, polished 3D animated short film titled "The Cloud Delivery Service."

ART STYLE:
Charming stylized 3D animated movie aesthetic, soft rounded shapes, adorable character design, expressive facial animation, fluffy clouds, pastel colors, beautiful lighting, detailed miniature environments, and smooth cinematic animation. Whimsical, warm, and visually delightful. Not photorealistic or anime.

MAIN CHARACTER:
A tiny cloud delivery worker with a round cream-colored body, short arms and legs, rosy cheeks, large expressive eyes, a small blue delivery cap, and a bright yellow backpack. Maintain exactly the same appearance throughout.

SETTING:
A magical sky village above the clouds. Small colorful houses sit on separate floating islands connected by tiny bridges. The sky is bright blue with fluffy white clouds and warm sunlight.

SCENE 1 (0–5s):
Wide shot of the floating village. The tiny delivery worker stands beside a giant folded paper airplane at a small delivery station. They check a little parcel, place it carefully inside the yellow backpack, and climb aboard the airplane.

SCENE 2 (5–11s):
The paper airplane glides smoothly between floating houses. The worker steers with excitement, waving to a tiny character on a balcony. The camera follows alongside the airplane as clouds drift past.

SCENE 3 (11–17s):
The worker arrives at a small pink house on a floating island. They land gently, take out the parcel, and leave it beside the front door. A tiny fluffy resident opens the door and happily receives it. The worker waves goodbye and returns to the airplane.

SCENE 4 (17–23s):
As the airplane flies toward the next island, the backpack suddenly glows. The worker looks confused, opens it, and discovers a tiny glass container with a miniature rainbow swirling inside. Its colorful light reflects across their face.

SCENE 5 (23–30s):
The container opens slightly. A beautiful glowing rainbow grows out of it, stretching across the sky and connecting the floating islands. The village residents look up in amazement. The delivery worker smiles proudly as the paper airplane glides through the rainbow. End with a beautiful wide shot of the colorful sky village.

CONTINUITY:
One delivery worker, one paper airplane, one yellow backpack, and one rainbow container. Maintain consistent character design, clothing, and proportions. Keep the village layout coherent. The airplane must remain the same throughout. No duplicate characters, random objects, sudden transformations, or unexplained scene changes.

CAMERA:
Smooth cinematic tracking, wide establishing shots, expressive character close-ups, and gentle aerial movements. Keep the important actions clearly visible.

AUDIO:
Cheerful original orchestral-style instrumental with gentle bells and playful percussion. Soft wind, paper airplane flutter, and magical sparkling sound effects. No dialogue, lyrics, or recognizable existing music.

entries.prompt:
A top-down stop-motion style video of four hands assembling a detailed dragon head sculpture on a clean white surface using only natural materials.
Start with four hands holding and positioning bare brown twigs and branches, carefully arranging them into the basic outline of a dragon’s head, neck, and curved spine with small protruding sticks for spikes.
Next, hands place large pieces of rough textured tree bark to form the dragon’s face, snout, and jaw, carefully fitting the pieces so the bark grain creates natural scales and ridges. Yellow lichen spots appear on the forehead and cheeks. Small sharp wooden shards are inserted as teeth.
Then hands add layers of thin bark strips and light-colored wood pieces along the neck to create overlapping scale armor. Fresh green moss is packed into the upper neck and crest area. Dried brown and golden autumn leaves are carefully layered in a flowing mane along the side of the neck.
Hands continue refining: placing two curved wooden sticks as horns, adding small pinecones as decorative spikes, inserting a realistic glass eye into the socket, and tucking pine needles into the mouth and around the head like whiskers and eyebrows.
Final shot: the completed dragon head sculpture sits alone on the white background — a fierce yet elegant nature-made dragon with bark scales, moss crest, leaf mane, wooden horns, sharp teeth, and a single glowing eye. entries.title: MiniMax H3: analog practical title sequence on film, a domino chain on a walnut floor that, seen from above, spells FALL
entries.description: A practical-effects title card: "Analog practical title sequence shot on real film… warm tungsten light, shallow depth of field, a polished dark walnut floor." A fingertip tips the first domino, the camera tracks low with the chain as it branches, cranes up to an overhead, and the fallen dominoes spell "FALL". The text rules are strict ("Only the four letters F, A, L, L. No other text, no logos") and the output spells the word legibly. A strong template for any campaign word or product name built from a chain reaction.
entries.prompt:
Analog practical title sequence shot on real film, photorealistic, warm tungsten light, shallow depth of field, a polished dark walnut floor.

[0-3s] Extreme close-up, low to the floor: a single black domino with white pips stands at the start of a long curving line of dominoes. A fingertip taps it. It tips over.

[3-9s] The camera tracks low alongside the chain reaction as it races forward, hundreds of black dominoes falling one after another in a fast rippling wave with crisp clicking sounds. The line curves and splits into several branching paths.

[9-13s] The camera cranes smoothly up and back to a high overhead view as the final branches fall. The fallen dominoes have been laid out so that, seen from above, the lines of toppled black dominoes spell the single word FALL in large clean block capital letters across the floor.

[13-15s] Hold perfectly still on the overhead view. The word FALL is sharp, legible and correctly spelled, made only of fallen dominoes. The last domino settles. Silence.

Only the four letters F, A, L, L. No other text, no logos, no people except the single fingertip at the start.

entries.description: A documentary-realism prompt in field-report form: EXPEDITION, EXPLORERS (crampons, helmets, headlamps), a SHOOT WINDOW ("7:05 AM – 7:20 AM… Cold blue daylight enters through the cave entrance"), RECORDING STYLE ("First-person expedition footage mixed with a second camera operator"), five timed beats, AUDIO, and a REALISM DIRECTIVE: "Ice must behave like real compressed glacier ice, not glass. entries.prompt:
EXPEDITION:
Two glaciologists enter a newly formed ice cave to document its internal structure before seasonal melting changes it.
EXPLORERS: Two researchers, both wearing crampons, helmets and headlamps, carrying compact measurement equipment.
SHOOT WINDOW: 7:05 AM – 7:20 AM Early morning outside. Overcast sky. Cold blue daylight enters through the cave entrance.
LOCATION: Glacial valley, massive blue ice formation, narrow cave entrance, translucent walls, frozen water flowing beneath the surface.
RECORDING STYLE: First-person expedition footage mixed with a second camera operator. Headlamps create moving pools of light across the ice. Natural breathing and footsteps remain prominent.
15-SECOND EXPLORATION:
00:00–00:03 → Researchers squeeze through the narrow entrance.
00:03–00:06 → Camera reveals deep blue translucent ice walls surrounding them.
00:06–00:09 → One researcher notices water suddenly moving beneath a transparent ice floor.
00:09–00:12 → Both carefully step backward and examine the changing surface.
00:12–00:15 → They mark the location and begin retreating toward daylight.
AUDIO: Boots scraping ice, dripping water, distant cracking, breathing, muffled voices.
REALISM DIRECTIVE: Ice must behave like real compressed glacier ice, not glass. Light scatters through the walls naturally. No fantasy formations, supernatural elements or impossible cave geometry.

entries.title: MiniMax H3 Image (official): overhead farm-to-table feast on a weathered wooden table, from the repo's prompt-expansion workflow
entries.description: The official text-to-image example from MiniMax's open-weight H3 Image release (2026-11-10/11). The input was one line ("A rustic, overhead shot of a farm-to-table feast…"); H3-Image-Context-IR expanded it into the stored prompt, which places every item by region ("In the center, a large woven basket… To the left… On the right side… At the upper right… In the lower left…") and ends with one light direction that explains the shadows ("coming from the upper left and casting soft, long shadows to the lower right"). That region-by-region layout plus a single light vector is the official H3 Image style, and it suits food and tabletop prop shoots. Use the result as a first frame for a Seedance 2.5 overhead push.
entries.prompt: The image is an overhead, top-down photograph of a rustic farm-to-table feast spread across a weathered, dark brown wooden table with visible grain, knots, and a worn finish. In the center, a large woven basket holds a freshly baked rustic loaf of bread with a cracked golden-brown crust and scattered flour, alongside a halved loaf. To the left, a large dark ceramic plate presents an assortment of colorful seasonal vegetables, including bright orange carrots, deep red heirloom tomatoes, purple cabbage, and a mound of vibrant green leafy kale and arugula. On the right side, a wooden board displays artisanal cheeses: a wedge of sharp aged cheddar, a round of creamy brie with a rind, a soft blue cheese, and a few scattered almonds and walnuts. Below the bread in the lower center, a shallow bowl contains roasted root vegetables, including golden potatoes and beets, sprinkled with fresh rosemary sprigs. At the upper right, a glass jar of golden olive oil stands beside a smaller jar of honey with a wooden dipper. In the lower left, a rustic cloth napkin holds a silver knife and fork. At the upper left, a bunch of purple and red grapes rests near a small bowl of black olives. Scattered herbs, including fresh thyme and sprigs of oregano, decorate the table. The lighting is natural and warm, coming from the upper left and casting soft, long shadows to the lower right, enhancing the texture of the bread, the moisture of the vegetables, and the overall cozy, bountiful atmosphere of the meal.
