entries.title: Seedance 2.5 4K: eight hard-cut macro shots of one tiger walking through a sunlit jungle (official sd25-pe section format, inline sound tags)
entries.description: A 30-second, 4K wildlife film written in the same bracketed structure the official sd25-pe skill uses: [Generation Goal], [Reference Material Roles], [Subjects and Relationships], an [Event Script] of eight numbered stages joined by "Hard cut.", and [Maintain Consistency]. Each stage is one primary event plus one camera instruction (eye macro, ground-level paw macro, side-on flank tracking, water-level drinking shot), and each ends with its own sound cues in angle brackets ("<a soft heavy pad on damp earth> <a twig cracking>"). The output holds stripe pattern and eye colour across all eight cuts with very fine fur and whisker detail. It is a clean template for a premium nature, pet-food or outdoor-brand film built from macro inserts.
entries.prompt:
[Generation Goal]
Generate an intimate wildlife sequence in eight shots joined by hard cuts. The central subject is one tiger, and the primary event is the tiger walking through a sunlit jungle while the camera explores it in extreme close-ups.

[Reference Material Roles]
<<<image_1>>> defines the tiger and the look: its face, vivid orange fur, crisp black stripes, white cheeks and amber-gold eyes, the deep green jungle, the clear side light, and the sharpness of every hair and whisker.

[Subjects and Relationships]
There is exactly one tiger and it is the only animal in the film. It is calm, powerful and unhurried, a photoreal living animal with believable weight and muscle. The jungle is empty of people.

[Event Script]

[Stage 1] Opening state: the composition of <<<image_1>>>, the tiger's face filling the frame, looking into the lens. Primary event: it blinks slowly, its ears turn, and it begins to walk forward. Camera: a steady close-up moving backward at the tiger's walking pace. <a deep slow breath> <leaves rustling> <distant insects>

Hard cut.

[Stage 2] Primary event: extreme close-up of one amber eye; the pupil tightens as a shaft of sun crosses it, the fibres of the iris and the fine lashes sharp. Camera: a macro shot level with the eye, moving with the tiger. <soft footfalls> <a low rumble in its chest>

Hard cut.

[Stage 3] Primary event: a huge paw lowers onto wet earth and moss, the toes spreading, tiny grains of soil pressed outward, a claw tip just showing. Camera: a ground-level macro shot beside the paw, then the paw lifts and leaves the frame. <a soft heavy pad on damp earth> <a twig cracking>

Hard cut.

[Stage 4] Primary event: close-up along the tiger's shoulder and flank as it walks, the muscles sliding under the striped fur, each hair catching the sun, a few water droplets shaking loose. Camera: a side-on close-up travelling with the shoulder. <fur brushing against leaves> <steady breathing>

Hard cut.

[Stage 5] Primary event: close-up of the nose and whiskers; the pink nose twitches as it scents the air, the white whiskers tremble, and its lips part to show the edge of its tongue. Camera: a tight three-quarter close-up from just below the muzzle. <a sharp sniff> <a soft huff>

Hard cut.

[Stage 6] Primary event: the tiger pushes through large wet leaves, which bend around its face and spring back, droplets flying off in sharp sparkling beads. Camera: a close front shot from inside the foliage, leaves parting toward the lens. <wet leaves slapping and dripping>

Hard cut.

[Stage 7] Primary event: the tiger lowers its head to a clear stream and drinks, its tongue lapping, rings spreading across the water, its reflection trembling. Camera: a low shot at water level from the far bank, the eyes just above the surface. <rhythmic lapping> <trickling water>

Hard cut.

[Stage 8] Primary event: the tiger lifts its head, water dripping from its chin, and looks straight into the lens, then gives one long slow blink. Camera: a slow move closer to its face, ending on both eyes. End state: the tiger's eyes filling the frame, held. <water dripping> <a deep contented rumble> <jungle ambience>

[Maintain Consistency]
Keep the tiger's stripe pattern, eye colour and fur identical in every shot. Motion is real-time. No on-screen text.

The visuals feature extreme photorealism with ultra-high-definition detail: tack-sharp focus, crisp micro-contrast, every hair, whisker and water droplet finely resolved, clean noise-free image, vivid orange, amber and deep green, brilliant highlights and clean deep blacks.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5: "The Mushroom House Makeover", a tiny woodland builder turns a red mushroom into a lantern-lit cottage (30 s 3D short, timed scenes)
entries.description: A cosy 3D-animated short in five timed scenes (0–5s, 5–11s, 11–17s, 17–23s, 23–30s). The prompt stops the model from cheating the build: "All additions must be physically carried and installed by the builder. Once placed, doors, windows, chimney, balcony, steps, flowers, and lanterns remain in their exact positions." It also locks the base object ("Keep the mushroom in exactly the same position and shape throughout") and specifies the style negatively ("Not photorealistic or anime"). The output builds up the house step by step and ends on a dusk lantern reveal. It works as a template for a progressive product or set build where every added piece must persist.
entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second cute, polished 3D animated short film titled "The Mushroom House Makeover."

ART STYLE:
Charming high-quality 3D animated movie aesthetic. Soft rounded shapes, adorable character design, expressive facial animation, rich pastel colors, detailed miniature environments, warm sunlight, and smooth cinematic animation. Cozy, whimsical, and visually delightful. Not photorealistic or anime.

MAIN CHARACTER:
One tiny woodland builder with a round cream-colored body, short arms and legs, rosy cheeks, large expressive eyes, a small green leaf-shaped hat, and a brown tool belt. Maintain exactly the same design and proportions throughout.

SETTING:
A peaceful woodland clearing with soft green grass, colorful wildflowers, tiny mushrooms, and tall trees. In the center stands one oversized red mushroom with a wide spotted cap and a plain cream-colored stem. Keep the mushroom in exactly the same position and shape throughout.

SCENE 1 (0–5s):
Wide shot of the clearing. The tiny builder walks toward the large ordinary mushroom carrying a little wooden toolbox. They look up at it, rub their chin thoughtfully, then smile and open the toolbox.

SCENE 2 (5–11s):
The builder places a small round wooden door at the front of the mushroom stem, carefully fits a tiny circular window above it, and adds two miniature wooden steps leading to the entrance. Show each item being carried into place and attached by hand. The mushroom itself does not change shape.

SCENE 3 (11–17s):
The builder climbs a small ladder and carefully attaches two glowing windows to the mushroom cap. They add a tiny chimney on the left side of the cap and a little wooden balcony beneath it. The builder climbs down and proudly examines the progress.

SCENE 4 (17–23s):
The builder decorates the entrance with colorful flowers, places two small lanterns beside the steps, and lays a winding stone pathway through the grass toward the door. Each decoration is placed deliberately. The house now looks warm and inviting.

SCENE 5 (23–30s):
As evening light begins to glow, the builder switches on the lanterns. Warm golden light shines through the windows. The camera slowly pulls back to reveal the finished mushroom cottage surrounded by glowing fireflies and colorful flowers. The builder sits happily on the front step, admiring the completed home. End on a beautiful wide shot.

CONTINUITY:
Exactly one builder and one mushroom house. Preserve the mushroom's original size, red spotted cap, and position. All additions must be physically carried and installed by the builder. Once placed, doors, windows, chimney, balcony, steps, flowers, and lanterns remain in their exact positions. No disappearing objects, duplicate characters, sudden transformations, or random decorations.

CAMERA:
Smooth cinematic camera movements, wide establishing shots, medium construction shots, and expressive close-ups. Clearly show the builder performing each task. Keep the mushroom house visible during the makeover.

AUDIO:
Soft woodland ambience, birds chirping, gentle footsteps, tiny hammer taps, wood placement sounds, and magical sparkling effects when the lights turn on. No dialogue, lyrics, or recognizable existing music.

entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic cinematic commercial for a fictional premium travel luggage brand called VELA.
A stylish young Korean woman with long, sleek dark hair and natural glowing makeup travels through a modern international train station carrying one premium VELA hard-shell suitcase.
She wears a bold contemporary fashion look: a structured deep burgundy leather jacket worn over a fitted black asymmetric top, high-waisted wide-leg charcoal trousers with a dramatic tailored silhouette, pointed black ankle boots, sculptural silver earrings and a sleek black shoulder bag. entries.prompt: 15-second, 16:9 vertical, continuous single-take video that looks like authentic smartphone footage accidentally captured by a passerby in a city park. Overcast natural daylight, subtle handheld shake, limited phone stabilization, occasional autofocus adjustment, and realistic smartphone compression. The absurd event is filmed with a completely serious, unscripted documentary feeling.  0–3s: [Handheld medium shot] A middle-aged man wearing a dark business suit and tie crouches beside the stone edge of a pond. With a completely serious expression, he slowly scatters pieces of bread from a paper bag to several ordinary koi. Small ripples spread across the water as the fish gather in front of him.  3–7s: [Camera instinctively moves closer] An abnormally huge orange-and-white koi suddenly surges out of the murky water, briefly lifting its upper body above the surface and biting down on the entire bread bag in the man’s left hand. The man loses all support and pitches forward into the pond, creating one heavy, realistic splash. The camera quickly tilts downward while keeping the center of the pond visible. The man resurfaces with duckweed covering his head and his wet tie stuck across his face. The giant koi calmly swims past him with the remains of the bread bag still in its mouth. The koi must retain the same orange-and-white markings and enormous size. The pulling, sliding, loss of balance, and fall must show believable weight, inertia, traction, and water displacement. entries.prompt:
Create a 15-second photorealistic live-action video, horizontal 16:9, in one continuous shot. A real ginger house cat is watching a model railway on a wooden table. For the first half, the camera is so low inside the miniature street that the scene looks like a full-sized city with a gigantic cat behind it. The change in camera position reveals the true scale.

CAMERA AND LOOK

DV 16mm tape camcorder handheld feel. Begin at rail height, looking along a gently curving track. Blue-hour light, warm apartment windows, a bright red two-car Japanese commuter train with lit headlights. A little handheld drift, subtle tape grain, believable motion blur. Keep the train, the cat’s eye and the paw large enough to read on a phone.

0–4 seconds. Open with the red train already rounding the bend toward us. In the gap between two buildings, a huge green cat’s eye is watching it. The eye tracks the train as it passes the lens from left to right. A ginger ear twitches above the roofline.

4–8 seconds. The camera pans right with the train. As the last carriage clears the bend, one broad ginger paw comes down into the newly empty space just behind it. A soft tap. The paw misses. The train carries straight on along the same track.

8–12 seconds. In one physical movement, lift the camera above the rooftops and pull back past the front edge of the wooden table. Now we see the entire model railway in a lived-in apartment and the ordinary-sized ginger cat sitting on a chair behind it. The same red train is still moving around the loop.

12–15 seconds. Hold the wider view. The cat draws back the paw it just used and gives it two slow, casual licks. The red train rolls past again in the foreground. Cut on the second lick.

AUDIO

A steady wheel-on-rail rhythm, the soft tap of the paw and quiet room tone. As the camera pulls back, the little electric motor becomes audible. No dialogue, music, captions or logos.

Natural sound of breathing, quiet sobbing, rain and room tone layered under a slow, melancholic piano and strings score that never stops. No gore, no self-harm. No text overlay inside the video. No watermark.
>
> **[0-2s]** Extreme close-up: his eyes open in a dim room, blue dawn light, tears already tracking sideways across his face.
> **[2-3s]** Wide shot: he sits on the edge of an unmade bed, shoulders curved, the room cluttered with dishes and clothes.
> **[3-4s]** Over-the-shoulder: he stares at an empty chair across from him, imagining a faint, blurred figure sitting there and fading away.
> **[4-5s]** Close-up: his hand trembles pouring a glass of whiskey, the bottle clinking against the rim.
> **[5-6s]** Low-angle shot: he sits on the floor against a wall, smoke curling from a cigarette in dim light.
> **[6-7s]** Close-up: he puts on his headphones and closes his eyes, silent sobbing, shoulders shaking.
> **[7-8s]** Whip-pan: his phone buzzes on the table with a name he ignores, and he turns the screen face-down.
> **[8-9s]** Handheld: he storms around the room and throws a plate against the wall, the pieces scattering across the floor.
> **[9-10s]** Wide shot: he slumps into the wreckage and holds his head in his hands.
> **[10-11s]** Close-up: he lies on his back on the bed staring at the ceiling, tears running into his hair.
> **[11-12s]** Slow dolly shot through a doorway: a quiet knock at the apartment door and he doesn't move, avoiding the person outside.
> **[12-13s]** Time-lapse montage cut: the same man, hair and beard visibly longer, curtains still closed, dust in the light.
> **[13-14s]** Close-up in the bathroom mirror: he stares at his unkempt reflection, his breath fogging the glass.
> **[14-15s]** Low-angle shot: shower water pounds on his bowed head, eyes shut, steam filling the frame.
> **[15-16s]** Close-up: he brushes his teeth slowly in the mirror, hollow-eyed.
> **[16-17s]** Close-up: he trims his beard in a few slow strokes, still staring at himself.
> **[17-18s]** Wide shot: he sits alone on a green playground bench at sunset, wind blowing his hair across his face, swings moving faintly behind him.
> **[18-19s]** Close-up: he watches a child laugh far across the field, a flicker of a smile fading.
> **[19-20s]** Overhead drone shot: a tiny figure on a bench in a huge green field, nobody else nearby.
> **[20-21s]** Close-up: he lowers his headphones and for the first time listens to the silence and the wind.
> **[21-22s]** Night, alone by his apartment window: he rests his forehead on the glass, rain streaking the city lights.
> **[22-23s]** Close-up: he finally lets go, a full, shuddering cry, hands over his face.
> **[23-24s]** Slow orbit shot: he slides down against the wall, small in the empty room.
> **[24-25s]** Extreme close-up: his phone lights the dark room with a call from "Maa". He stares at it, thumb hovering.
> **[25-26s]** Close-up: his thumb presses answer and he lifts the phone to his ear, unable to speak.
> **[26-27s]** Close-up: tears fall again, but this time his shoulders loosen, a long exhale.
> **[27-28s]** Wide shot: he opens the curtains and morning light floods the room for the first time.
> **[28-30s]** Final close-up: his face in warm light, eyes red and exhausted but open, the faintest breath of a smile. Cut to black.

entries.description: A resolution ladder for one prompt: the creator renders the same eight-shot, 15-second Seedance 2.5 wildlife sequence at 480p, 720p, 1080p and 4K, and also on Seedance 2.5 Flash at 720p, then edits them side by side. The prompt uses the official sd25-pe skeleton ([Generation Goal], [Reference Material Roles] with <<<image_1>>>, [Subjects and Relationships], an [Event Script] of eight "[Shot N | start–end s]" blocks with inline <sound> tags and "Hard cut.", [Maintain Consistency]). It ends with anatomy rules for a mythical animal ("Preserve exactly two feathered wings and one continuous serpentine body. No legs, arms or bat-like membranes") and "Show the entire wing opening in one shot with no cut, zoom or reframing." Use it to see how much scale, feather and water detail each tier adds.
entries.prompt: [Generation Goal] Generate an exactly 15-second photoreal wildlife sequence in eight shots joined by hard cuts. Quetzalcóatl is a living animal, a long feathered serpent with a fierce reptilian face and one pair of broad feathered wings. It slithers through a humid, sunlit jungle, crosses a shallow stream, then raises its head and spreads both wings in a clearing. The camera begins with intimate close-ups and ends on an uninterrupted full-body shot of the wing display. [Reference Material Roles] Use <<<image_1>>> to match Quetzalcóatl’s anatomy, proportions and coloration throughout the sequence. Preserve its angular scaled snout, amber slit-pupil eyes, swept-back crest, emerald and teal plumage with bronze accents, and broad belly scales. The jungle is the environment in all eight shots. [Subjects and Relationships] Exactly one Quetzalcóatl. Its elongated, legless body moves with the weight and lateral undulation of a large snake. One pair of feathered wings attaches just behind the neck. The wings stay folded against its upper body until the final shot. No other visible animals or people. [Event Script] [Shot 1 | 0.0–1.5 s] Tight frontal close-up at head height. Quetzalcóatl stares into the lens, flicks its forked tongue once and begins to glide forward. The camera tracks backward at the same pace. <soft breathing, distant jungle insects> Hard cut. [Shot 2 | 1.5–2.5 s] Eye-level macro of one amber eye. A shaft of sunlight crosses the iris and the vertical pupil narrows. Fine scales and tiny feather barbs around the brow catch the light. <soft rustle of foliage> Hard cut. [Shot 3 | 2.5–4.0 s] Ground-level macro beside the body. A wave of muscle travels along the serpent as its belly scales slide over wet earth and moss. The soil compresses under its weight and a small twig rolls aside. <damp scales sliding, twig crack> Hard cut. [Shot 4 | 4.0–5.5 s] Side-tracking close-up along one folded wing. The layered flight feathers shift slightly as the serpent bends around a root. A bead of water runs down an emerald feather and falls. <feathers brushing a fern, single water drop> Hard cut. [Shot 5 | 5.5–7.0 s] Tight three-quarter shot from inside the foliage. The scaled snout parts two broad wet leaves. They bend around the head, then spring back as the feathered crest passes, scattering droplets in the sunlight. <wet leaves snapping back> Hard cut. [Shot 6 | 7.0–8.5 s] Low shot at water level. The serpent glides through a shallow stream, pushing a small wake ahead of its belly. The folded wing feathers stay above the surface while the tail draws a narrow ripple behind it. <water displaced by the body, soft trickle> Hard cut. [Shot 7 | 8.5–10.0 s] Medium side shot in a sunlit clearing. Quetzalcóatl stops, settles its long body into a loose S-curve and lifts its head and upper neck. It turns its gaze toward the camera and parts its jaws just enough to show two curved fangs. Both wings remain folded. <body settling on damp leaves, low reptilian hiss> Hard cut. [Shot 8 | 10.0–15.0 s] Stable full-body three-quarter shot with clear space around the crest, both wingtips and the entire tail. From 10.0 to 13.0 seconds, both wings lift from their folded position and open outward in one continuous, anatomically believable motion. The overlapping flight feathers separate progressively, revealing their full span and texture. The long serpentine body stays planted in its S-curve. From 13.0 to 15.0 seconds, hold on the fully spread wings. The outer feathers settle with a small shiver while Quetzalcóatl keeps its eyes on the lens. <deep feather rustle, jungle ambience> [Maintain Consistency] Keep the same head shape, eye color, fangs, crest, feather pattern, body length and wing attachment points in every shot. Preserve exactly two feathered wings and one continuous serpentine body. No legs, arms or bat-like membranes. Real-time motion throughout. Show the entire wing opening in one shot with no cut, zoom or reframing. Render individual feather barbs, overlapping scales, wet foliage and water droplets with sharp photoreal detail. Natural SFX only. No music, voiceover or on-screen text.

entries.prompt:
ULTRA REALISTIC 15 SECOND PERSONAL HOME VIDEO. 1080p 16:9 widescreen render of mid 1990s Hi8 camcorder tape footage. Single continuous handheld take, no cuts. Dialogue driven, Korean. Title: GASOLINE DREAMS.

CONCEPT
1997. A borrowed car at a rural highway petrol station outside Seoul, dusk in late autumn. Three hours still to drive. She is waiting for the tank to fill and her friend is filming instead of reading the map. Nothing happens. The tape is just running.

SUBJECT LOCK
Korean woman, early twenties. Realistic skin with visible pores, faint under eye shadow, minimal makeup, nose and ears pink from the cold, breath faintly visible. Dark brown hair loosely tied back, front strands loose, flattened on one side from sleeping against the car window. Oversized cream knit sweater with stretched cuffs pulled down over her hands, blue jeans, white sneakers scuffed at the toe. Same face, hair and outfit for the full 15 seconds. Slouched, stiff from sitting, stretching her back.

SECOND VOICE LOCK
The friend holding the camcorder is never seen, not a hand, not a shadow, not a reflection in the car glass. Voice only, young female, close to the mic, sleepy and unbothered. Never addresses an audience. A station attendant in a padded work jacket is visible at a distance but never speaks.

SETTING
Small rural petrol station on a two lane highway outside Seoul, late autumn dusk, 1997. Two pumps under a concrete canopy with one flickering fluorescent tube, a stack of oil cans, a plastic stool, a beige sedan with the fuel flap open and the passenger door hanging open. Beyond the canopy, bare rice paddies, a line of poplars, low grey hills, a truck passing, sky going orange to deep blue. Lived in and unstyled. No visible brands, no logos, no readable signage, no Hangul text anywhere in frame.

FRAMING
16:9 widescreen throughout, treated as a later widescreen transfer of the original tape. The extra width is used badly, not compositionally. She sits low and off to one side with dead empty space filling the other half of the frame. Horizon slightly tilted. Nothing centred on purpose.

CAMERA
Raw handheld Hi8 camcorder at chest height, operator leaning on the car. Autofocus hunting between the pump, the car glass and her face, repeatedly grabbing the wrong thing. Exposure pumping hard as the lens drifts from the bright sky to the shade under the canopy. One lazy unmotivated zoom that overshoots past her shoulder and corrects. She drifts out of frame once and the operator is late to follow. Analogue tape noise, chroma bleed on the orange sky, mild tracking wobble at the frame edges, one dropout glitch. No stabilization, no gimbal, no cinematic choreography.

BEATS
0:00 to 0:04 She climbs out of the passenger door mid stretch, arms up, yawning, and walks toward the pump. The camera swings after her too slowly and catches empty canopy for a beat.
0:04 to 0:08 She stands at the open fuel flap watching the numbers on the pump. The exchange, overlapping, both half laughing.
0:08 to 0:12 Dead air. She sits sideways on the car bonnet, feet not reaching the ground, a hot can held against her cheek, watching a truck pass. Nobody speaks for four full seconds. The fluorescent tube flickers.
0:12 to 0:15 A horn from the road. She slides off the bonnet, says the last line without turning around, and the camera is still pointed at the empty bonnet when the tape cuts.

DIALOGUE
Spoken language locked to Korean, casual banmal between friends, flat and unprojected, thinned by the camcorder mic.
0:05 She says Gadeuk chaewoya dwae, apeuro amugeotdo eopseo
0:07 Friend off camera says Neo don isseo
0:08 She says Dangyeonhi eopji
0:13 She says Gaja, got eoduwojinda
Visible mouth movement with bilabial closure on the m, b and p sounds. Friend line off camera only, closer to the mic. No other speech, no narration.

AUDIO
Diegetic only. Fuel pump motor humming, nozzle clicking off, fluorescent ballast buzz, a truck passing with a doppler horn, wind across open paddies, a can tab, her sneakers on grit, faint hand noise on the camcorder body. No music, no score, no radio, no added ambience beds.

STYLE RULES
Nothing dramatic happens on purpose. No posing, no road trip montage energy, no wind in hair, no golden hour beauty lighting, no hero framing. Realism comes from the cold, the flat delivery and the four seconds of dead air nobody bothered to cut. She is talking to her friend, not to viewers. If she performs for the lens the illusion breaks.

NEGATIVE
No music. No subtitles. No captions. No watermark. No timestamp burn in. No slow motion. No colour grading. No lens flare. No shallow depth of field. No visible second person. No brand logos. No readable text.

LAST FRAME
Wide crooked frame of the empty car bonnet under the flickering fluorescent tube with the dark highway filling the right half, image tears with one frame of tape distortion, then hard cut to black. Absolutely no on screen text, no title card, no lettering, no numbers, no logo, no signage of any kind in the final frame.

entries.prompt:
ULTRA REALISTIC 15 SECOND PERSONAL HOME VIDEO. 1080p render of 4:3 early 2000s MiniDV tape footage. Single continuous handheld take, no cuts. Dialogue driven, Hinglish. Title: EK MOMBATTI.

CONCEPT
A birthday with no cake. One candle stuck into a pastry from the corner shop, lights switched off in a small room, one friend filming and singing badly. Twelve seconds later the lights are back on and it is over.

SUBJECT LOCK
Indian woman, early twenties, warm medium brown skin, realistic pores, minimal makeup, face lit almost entirely by a single candle flame from below so the shadows are unflattering and the highlights blow out. Dark brown hair loosely tied back with strands falling loose. Oversized cream knit sweater with stretched cuffs, blue jeans, white sneakers scuffed at the toe. Same face, hair and outfit for the full 15 seconds. Sitting cross legged on the floor, embarrassed, hands in her sleeves.

SECOND VOICE LOCK
The friend holding the camcorder is never seen, not a hand, not a shadow. Voice only, young female, close to the mic, singing off key with no shame. Never addresses an audience.

SETTING
Small rented room at night with the ceiling light switched off. A single pastry on a steel plate on the floor with one thin candle in it, a mattress on the floor, a plastic chair with clothes on it, a curtain with street light leaking around the edge. Lived in and unstyled. No visible brands, no logos, no readable signage, no decorations.

CAMERA
Raw handheld MiniDV camcorder held low and close, sitting on the floor across from her. Severe exposure pumping in near darkness, the candle flame blooming into a smeared vertical streak, her face crushed to noise then recovering. Autofocus hunting constantly and never locking. One clumsy zoom in on the candle. Heavy low light tape grain, interlace combing, one dropout glitch. No stabilization, no gimbal.

BEATS
0:00 to 0:05 She is sitting in the dark behind the candle looking mildly embarrassed while the friend sings the birthday song off key. No lyrics needed, humming and improvised words.
0:05 to 0:09 The exchange about the wish, quick, overlapping, both laughing.
0:09 to 0:12 She blows the candle out. Total darkness on tape for two full seconds, only sound, image reduced to noise and a faint window edge. Nobody bothers to fix it.
0:12 to 0:15 The ceiling light snaps on, the frame blows out white then settles on her squinting, and the tape cuts.

0:13 Friend off camera says Light on kar diya, sorry

STYLE RULES
Nothing dramatic happens. No posing, no celebration montage, no hero framing, no warm candle glamour lighting. Realism comes from the bad singing, the two seconds of black, and the harsh light at the end. If she performs for the lens the illusion breaks.

NEGATIVE
No music. No subtitles. No captions. No watermark. No timestamp. No slow motion. No color grading. No lens flare. No shallow depth of field. No visible second person. No brand logos. No readable text.

LAST FRAME
Her squinting into the newly switched on ceiling light, overexposed and off center, smoke still rising from the candle, one frame of tape tear, hard cut to black. Absolutely no on screen text, no title card, no lettering, no numbers, no logo, no signage of any kind in the final frame.

entries.title: MiniMax H3: "ENDLESS STEP", black-and-white Op Art staircase loop with optical-illusion ripples, impossible gravity and a Möbius return to the first shot
entries.description: A Japanese-language, cut-by-cut spec (CUT1–CUT8) for a 15-second monochrome Op Art / surrealist film. Each cut has Visuals, Camera (lens and aperture, e.g. "24mm / F4", "70mm / F2.8"), Motion, Lighting, VFX, SFX, Emotion and a Transition trigger ("Transition｜足が次の段へ触れた瞬間にCUT2", cut when the foot touches the next step). It bans neon, heavy glitch and particles ("ネオン・派手なグリッチ・大量の粒子は禁止") and asks for geometry, illusions, architecture and body only, ending in a seamless loop back to CUT1. The output delivers striped stairs, concentric-circle floors, a face that becomes architecture, and impossible walkers on walls.
entries.prompt: タイトル：ENDLESS STEP / 終わらない階段 尺：15秒 ジャンル：現代アート / Op Art / Surrealism 画面：16:9 カラー：白黒モノクロ中心 BGM：なし コンセプト：「進み続けているのに、どこにも辿り着いていない」 演出方針：前半は空間の異常、中盤は物理法則の崩壊、後半は人間と空間そのものの境界を崩す。ネオン・派手なグリッチ・大量の粒子は禁止。幾何学、錯視、建築、人体の融合だけで見せる。 CUT1｜0.0–1.8秒 Visuals｜何も存在しない真っ白な巨大空間。中央に一本だけ細長い黒い階段が奥へ伸びている。黒いミニマルな衣装の主人公が背中を向け、ゆっくり階段を上る。階段の表面だけが細い白黒ストライプになっている。最初は完全に静かな世界。 Camera｜24mm / F4。床ギリギリのローアングル。主人公を中央固定した完全シンメトリー構図。ゆっくり前方へドリーイン。 Motion｜主人公の歩行のみ。1歩につき約0.7秒。最後の0.5秒から階段表面のストライプがごく僅かに波打つ。 Lighting｜巨大な白いソフトボックスで空間全体を均一照明。人物と階段の下だけにシャープな黒い影。 VFX｜非常に弱い水平波状ディストーション。まだ異常だと断定できない程度。 SFX｜乾いた靴音「コツ、コツ」。極低音のルームトーン。 Emotion｜静寂。整いすぎていることへの違和感。 Transition｜足が次の段へ触れた瞬間にCUT2。 CUT2｜1.8–3.3秒 Visuals｜足元の極端なクローズアップ。靴底が階段へ触れるたび、白黒ストライプが水面のように沈み込み、波紋となって階段全体へ広がる。階段自体は固体なのに、模様だけが液体のように反応する。 Camera｜70mm / F2.8。階段より少し低い位置から足を追うローアングルトラッキング。 Motion｜足が接触 → 模様が沈む → 円状波紋が広がる → 次の一歩。足の動きはリアル、模様だけ非現実。 Lighting｜白背景を飛ばし気味にし、靴とストライプの黒を強調。 VFX｜Optical ripple、局所的なストライプ変形、軽いレンズ屈折。 SFX｜足音の直後に低い「ブゥン」という短い共鳴音。 Emotion｜世界が人物の存在に反応し始める。 Transition｜波紋が画面いっぱいへ広がりCUT3。 CUT3｜3.3–5.0秒 Visuals｜主人公の横顔ミディアム。背後の真っ白な壁に、横方向へ伸びる黒い階段がいつの間にか存在している。その階段を、もう一人の人物が壁面に対して垂直に歩いている。さらに天井には逆さになった人物が歩く。主人公本人はまだ気づいていない。 Camera｜50mm / F2.8。主人公の横顔にフォーカス。約0.7秒後、背景の異常な階段へラックフォーカス。 Motion｜主人公、壁の人物、天井の人物は全員まったく同じ歩行周期。ただし方向だけ異なる。 Lighting｜全人物へ同じ方向から光が当たっている。重力方向と影の方向が一致しない。 VFX｜Impossible perspective、非ユークリッド建築、重力不一致。 SFX｜正面の足音に、左・上方向から別の足音が薄く加わる。 Emotion｜「何かがおかしい」が明確になる瞬間。 Transition｜主人公が次の一段へ足を置く瞬間、低音と同時にCUT4。 CUT4｜5.0–6.7秒 Visuals｜足が一段に着地した瞬間、巨大空間全体が突然90°回転する。床が右側の壁へ変わり、天井だった面が床になる。しかし主人公は何事もなかったかのように同じ階段を上り続ける。階段の白黒ストライプが一気に巨大な同心円へ変形。 Camera｜18mm / F5.6。主人公正面寄りの超広角。空間回転と完全同期してカメラも90°ロール。その後、主人公だけ水平に見える角度で固定。 Motion｜空間：高速90°回転。主人公：速度一定。同心円：主人公から外側へ膨張。 Lighting｜回転開始時に0.1秒だけ光量低下。回転後は光源方向だけ元の位置を維持し、不自然な影を作る。 VFX｜90° spatial rotation、同心円ディストーション、短いモーションブラー、パース破綻。 SFX｜重い「ゴォン」＋低周波スイープ。 Emotion｜重力のルールが完全に壊れる。 Transition｜同心円の中心へカメラが吸い込まれCUT5。 CUT5｜6.7–8.5秒 Visuals｜超広角全景。上下左右、斜め、天井、壁へ無数の階段が伸びる巨大な不可能建築。人物は複数存在するが大量には増やさず、5〜7人程度。それぞれ異なる重力方向で歩いている。階段同士は交差しているように見えるが、実際には接続していない。中央の主人公だけが正常方向にいる。 Camera｜14mm / F5.6。空間中央を中心に高速オービット約100°。少しだけロールを加える。 Motion｜階段は静止。人物は一定速度で歩行。背景のストライプのみ逆方向へゆっくり移動。 Lighting｜完全モノクロ。白背景、黒い階段。影だけが異なる方向へ伸び、現実感を壊す。 VFX｜Non-Euclidean architecture、forced perspective、figure-ground ambiguity。 SFX｜異なる方向から足音が重なり、リズムが少しずつズレる。 Emotion｜空間そのものが巨大な錯視装置になった感覚。 Transition｜オービット中、主人公の顔がフレーム中央へ入りCUT6。 CUT6｜8.5–10.2秒 Visuals｜主人公の正面クローズアップ。主人公が初めて立ち止まる。顔の右側が模様になるのではなく、頬の表面そのものがゆっくり内側へ折れ始める。皮膚が建築物の壁のように変形し、顔の内部へ何百メートルも続く小さな白黒階段が現れる。片目、鼻、口の位置は正常なまま。顔の内部だけが巨大空間になっている。 Camera｜85mm / F2。顔正面。0.8秒かけてゆっくりドリーイン。最後の0.4秒で顔内部の階段へ急速接近。 Motion｜主人公は完全静止。まばたき一回。顔表面が紙を内側へ折るように段階的に陥没。内部階段の小さな人物だけが歩き続ける。 Lighting｜顔中央に柔らかい正面光。顔内部の空間はCUT1と同じ白い美術館照明。 VFX｜Face-to-architecture morph、recursive geometry、skin folding、深度拡張。顔への単純な模様貼り付けは禁止。 SFX｜周囲の足音が突然消える。顔が開く瞬間に紙を折るような乾いた音＋低い吸引音。 Emotion｜人体と建築の境界が崩れる。 Transition｜カメラが顔内部の階段へ完全に突入してCUT7。 CUT7｜10.2–12.5秒 Visuals｜顔内部の階段を歩く小さな主人公を追う。カメラが180°回転すると、これまで階段だと思っていた巨大な構造が、実は横向きになった人間の顔の輪郭だったと判明する。鼻梁が階段、唇の輪郭が通路、眼窩が巨大な円形空間になっている。さらにもう一度角度が変わると、再びただの階段に見える。「顔」と「建築」が視点によって交互に切り替わる。 Camera｜18mm / F4。人物後方から高速プッシュイン → 180°カメラロール → 一瞬静止 → ゆっくりドリーアウト。 Motion｜小さな主人公は歩行継続。巨大構造は動かさず、カメラ角度だけで顔と階段の認識が反転する。 Lighting｜均一な白黒照明。輪郭にだけ薄いサイドライトを入れ、顔として認識できるギリギリまで強調。 VFX｜Figure-ground reversal、anamorphic perspective、face/architecture ambiguity。モーフではなく「見る角度で意味が変わる」錯視を優先。 SFX｜短い逆再生音。顔として見えた瞬間だけ人間の呼吸音が一度入る。 Emotion｜「見えているものが何なのか分からない」状態。 Transition｜階段の最上部にある巨大な黒い円へ主人公が近づきCUT8。 CUT8｜12.5–15.0秒 Visuals｜主人公が階段の頂上へ到達。正面には巨大な完全な黒い円。その向こうは見えない。主人公が黒い円へ足を踏み入れる。瞬間、カメラが真上へ高速ドリーアウト。巨大な階段構造全体が一度ねじれ、メビウスの輪のようにつながっていることが判明。さらに引くと、先ほどの黒い円は実はCUT1で主人公が最初に踏み出した「階段の一段目」の黒い面だったことが分かる。構図がCUT1と完全一致。主人公が再び最初の一歩を踏み出す。 Camera｜35mmから開始。黒い円への短いプッシュイン → 真上視点へ急上昇 → 14mm相当の超ワイド → CUT1と同じ24mmローアングル構図へシームレス変形。 Motion｜階段全体がゆっくり180°ねじれてメビウス構造になる。主人公は止まらず歩き続ける。最後の0.5秒はCUT1と完全同一の動き。 Lighting｜最後まで完全モノクロ。白と黒のみ。ループ直前に一瞬だけ白黒を反転し、すぐ元へ戻す。 VFX｜Möbius topology transformation、recursive space、black-white inversion、seamless loop。 SFX｜黒い円へ入る直前に音が完全停止。CUT1の構図へ戻った瞬間、最初と同じ「コツ」という一歩目の足音。 Emotion｜「15秒間進んでいたのに、実は最初の一歩から抜け出せていなかった」。 END｜暗転なし。文字なし。ロゴなし。CUT1へ完全に戻るシームレスループ。 最重要生成ルール｜  1. 主役は常に同一人物。同じ黒い衣装・髪型・体格を固定。 2. 世界は白・黒のみ。サイバーパンク、未来都市、ネオンは禁止。 3. 階段の形状と白黒ストライプを全CUTで共通モチーフとして維持。 4. CUT6は「顔に模様を貼る」のではなく「顔内部が巨大建築空間になる」。 5. CUT7は単純な顔モーフではなく、視点によって顔と階段の認識が反転する錯視。 6. CUT8は必ずCUT1へ物理的につながるメビウス構造にする。 7. グリッチは使わない。AIらしい溶け・崩れ・余計な手足・余計な人物生成を避ける。 8. オプ・アートらしい幾何学的精度、直線、反復、同心円、白黒コントラストを優先する。

entries.title: MiniMax H3: "INK AFTER DARK", 1960s pulp-noir screen-print title sequence with torn-paper wipes, typewriter panels and a burnt-red palette
entries.description: A sectioned title-sequence prompt ([FORMAT], [IDENTITY], [BEATS], … [NEGATIVE]) for flat hand-inked 2D animation "with rough screen-print texture, imperfect paper grain, and slightly uneven ink edges". Transitions are physical: the frame "opens sideways like torn paper", a paper ribbon "becomes a graphic wipe", and one key strike splits the screen into "three bold rectangular panels". The negatives defend the look ("No 3D CGI, photorealism, anime styling, glossy modern motion graphics… smooth vector-clean surfaces") and the title is rendered once ("Render \"INK AFTER DARK\" once only"). The output nails the cream / black / burnt-red 1960s graphic style and lands the title.
entries.prompt:
T2V Hailuo MinimaxH3 Prompt

[FORMAT]
Create a 15-second, 16:9 retro graphic opening-title sequence titled "INK AFTER DARK".
A stylish 1960s pulp-noir animation about a mysterious night writer. Bold, minimal, elegant, slightly dangerous, with dry visual wit.

[IDENTITY]
Keep one female writer visually consistent throughout: sharp angular bob haircut, narrow almond-shaped eyes, long black turtleneck, high-waisted trousers, slim silhouette, black leather gloves, calm expression, upright self-assured posture, and hard graphic highlights along one side of her face.
Use flat hand-inked 2D illustration with rough screen-print texture, imperfect paper grain, and slightly uneven ink edges.

[BEATS]
[0–3 seconds] Extreme close-up of the writer's face emerging from near-total black. A narrow cream-colored strip of light slides across her eyes. The frame abruptly opens sideways like torn paper, revealing her full silhouette walking across a burnt-red background while loose sheets of paper trail behind her like a long ribbon.

[3–6 seconds] The paper ribbon sweeps across frame and becomes a graphic wipe. Reveal her in profile at a desk. She strikes one typewriter key. On impact, the screen fractures into three bold rectangular panels: her gloved fingers, the metal typebar snapping forward, and a giant black ink letter striking paper.

[6–9 seconds] Rapid rhythmic close-ups: spinning typewriter ribbon spool, carriage return lever snapping sideways, black ink spreading through rough paper fibers. Thin cream lines cut diagonally across the screen and reorganize the images into an asymmetric editorial collage.

[9–12 seconds] Pull wide. The writer stands alone beside an enormous abstract typewriter rendered as a black geometric silhouette. She pulls one endless page upward. The rising page becomes a full-frame cream vertical wipe while scattered black letters tumble downward like physical debris.

[12–15 seconds] The letters rapidly assemble into the exact title "INK AFTER DARK" centered large on a burnt-red paper field. The writer's small black silhouette crosses beneath the title and exits frame. The title appears through sharp letter-by-letter mechanical impacts over 0.5 seconds, holds completely still through the ending. No bouncing, spinning, stretching, or fly-in typography.

[CAMERA]
Use aggressive graphic changes in scale: extreme facial close-up → full-body silhouette → macro mechanical inserts → monumental wide composition.
Camera movement should feel designed rather than realistic: fast lateral pushes, sudden graphic crops, one rapid pull-out, and precise locked compositions. Avoid conventional cinematic orbit shots.

[LIGHT]
Limited palette only: burnt red, aged cream, deep black, with tiny muted silver highlights on typewriter metal.
Hard noir side-lighting translated into flat graphic shapes. Rough vintage print stock, subtle paper scratches, coarse ink grain, slight registration offsets, and occasional frame jitter.

[EDIT]
Fast editorial rhythm with hard cuts, paper wipes, diagonal panel slices, oversized object masks, and split-screen recompositions.
Transitions must be motivated by paper, ink, typewriter mechanisms, or moving silhouettes. No soft dissolves.
Make every shot feel newly composed rather than simply zooming into the previous image.

[AUDIO]
Audio: dry typewriter key strikes, paper slides, ribbon-spool clicks, carriage-return snaps, faint room hum, and one heavy mechanical impact when the final title locks.
BGM: an original 15-second cue, 65% noir suspense and 35% cool jazz. Upright bass, brushed snare, muted vibraphone, sparse low piano, and short clipped brass accents. Begin almost empty, introduce bass at 3 seconds, rhythmic percussion at 6 seconds, a brief brass accent at 10 seconds, then freeze the final 2 seconds on one bass note and the mechanical title hit. Do not imitate an existing melody.

[NEGATIVE]
No subtitles, extra on-screen text, watermarks, platform logos, or stickers.
Do not introduce Chinese text, garbled characters, misspellings, or additional title variations. Render "INK AFTER DARK" once only.
No 3D CGI, photorealism, anime styling, glossy modern motion graphics, neon cyberpunk aesthetics, or smooth vector-clean surfaces.
Never a slideshow. Maintain active graphic motion, physical visual transitions, and continuously evolving compositions.

Male lead: early 30s, tailored dark 1930s suit, shirt & tie. Voice deep, hesitant, guilty, lost for words. Blocking: She sits left on leather sofa; he stands front-right of sofa. Fixed 180° axis, eye contact locked.
Shot Breakdown
00:00–00:03｜Opening: Female face close-up Table lamp side light half-shadows her face. Eyes brimming with tears, lips trembling, staring steadily at him. Rain patters on glass.
00:03–00:07｜Reverse cut, male close-up + her off-screen line He listens, brow furrowed, uneasy. Her soft tearful voice: “If you cared for me, you wouldn’t hurt me like this.”Cut back to her close-up, glistening tearful eyes. Hard cut, no dissolve.

00:11–00:15｜Final two-shot close-up, static hold ending Cut back to her face, slight sad head shake. He drops his gaze, overwhelmed by guilt. Rain hums in background. Frame freezes, end directly, no fade, no black screen.
Sound Rules

English dialogue, strict lip sync matching lines.
Voice tone: female soft breathy sob; male hesitant, weary, guilty.
Only ambient sound: rain tapping window, faint fabric rustle, quiet breathing, room natural reverb.
NO music, BGM, subtitles, narration, extra sound effects.

Visual Constraints
No text, watermarks, logos. No over-smoothing / over-beautification. No wild gestures, screaming, fancy camera movement, slow motion, flashy transitions. Keep facial features consistent, no face distortion.

entries.prompt:
CHERRY BLOSSOM PICNIC IN KOREA 🌸 | A PERFECT SPRING DAY

Create an exactly 30-second ultra-realistic live-action travel vlog set in Seoul, South Korea, during peak cherry blossom season.

MAIN CHARACTER: A young Korean woman with long wavy dark brown hair, natural makeup and realistic skin. She wears the same cream cardigan, white top, pastel pink long skirt, white sneakers and beige shoulder bag throughout the video. Maintain perfect face and outfit consistency.

SCENE 1 (0–3s) — SPRING MORNING
Inside a cozy Korean apartment, she opens the curtains and smiles at the beautiful cherry blossoms outside.

SCENE 2 (3–6s) — FOOD PREPARATION
In the kitchen, she prepares homemade gimbap, washes strawberries and packs the food neatly into a lunchbox.

SCENE 3 (6–8s) — PACKING
She packs the lunchbox, strawberries, sandwiches, lemonade and camera into a woven picnic basket, then leaves home.

SCENE 4 (8–11s) — JOURNEY
She walks along Seoul streets lined with blooming cherry trees as pink petals gently fall around her.

SCENE 5 (11–14s) — PICNIC SETUP
She finds a peaceful spot beneath a large cherry blossom tree, unfolds a pastel picnic blanket and arranges her basket.

SCENE 6 (14–17s) — PHOTOGRAPHY
She photographs the blossoms with her digital camera, then smiles as a friend takes her picture.

SCENE 7 (17–21s) — PICNIC LUNCH
She opens her lunchbox, enjoys gimbap, strawberries and lemonade, smiling naturally.

SCENE 8 (21–24s) — SPRING MOMENT
She relaxes on the blanket, looking up at the blossoms as petals drift gently around her.

SCENE 9 (24–27s) — EVENING WALK
She packs her belongings and walks along a quiet blossom-covered pathway in warm golden sunlight.

SCENE 10 (27–30s) — FINAL SHOT
She turns toward the camera with a gentle smile, then walks away as pink petals float through the evening light.

VISUAL STYLE: Authentic handheld travel vlog footage, photorealistic 4K quality, natural expressions, realistic skin and movement, beautiful spring lighting, detailed food shots and natural camera focus. It must feel like a real day filmed by a friend, not an advertisement or AI video.

AUDIO: Only natural sounds such as birds, kitchen activity, footsteps, gentle wind, park ambience and camera shutter. No narration, dialogue or background music.

STRICT CONTINUITY: Keep the same woman, face, hairstyle, outfit and accessories in every scene. Maintain the exact story order and realistic progression from morning to evening. Keep the picnic basket, food and blanket consistent. No teleportation, duplicate people, outfit changes, distorted hands, artificial transitions or cartoon effects. Include all ten scenes within exactly 30 seconds.

entries.prompt:
Create a breathtaking 30-second photorealistic cinematic spiritual film inspired by the Islamic hope of Jannah. The entire film must feel emotionally overwhelming, peaceful, heavenly and profoundly beautiful. It should make viewers feel the weight of their struggles in this temporary world and the hope of eternal peace.

SCENE 1 | 0–6 SECONDS: THE WORLD WE LEFT BEHIND

Open with an extraordinary cinematic aerial shot of an endless, beautiful landscape at the final moments of sunset. A lone modestly dressed person stands beside a quiet river, seen only from behind. A gentle breeze moves through the surrounding trees. Tiny reflections of golden light dance across the water. The atmosphere is emotional, silent and deeply peaceful. Slowly transition away from the earthly landscape into an imaginative, ethereal garden.

SCENE 2 | 6–13 SECONDS: A BEAUTY BEYOND WORDS

Reveal an immense garden of extraordinary beauty. Crystal-clear rivers flow naturally through lush green meadows, surrounded by magnificent trees, delicate flowers and breathtaking landscapes. Sunlight passes through delicate leaves, creating thousands of tiny golden reflections. Soft mist floats above the water. Birds move peacefully through the distant sky. Every detail feels impossibly beautiful yet natural. The camera glides forward in one seamless cinematic movement.

SCENE 3 | 13–21 SECONDS: THE REUNION

Two modestly dressed human figures, representing loved ones reunited, walk slowly towards each other beside the river. Show them from behind and in elegant silhouettes, without identifiable facial details. One gently places a hand on the other's shoulder. They embrace quietly. No exaggerated acting, no dramatic crying. Just the indescribable emotion of finally being together again. The surrounding breeze becomes still, flowers gently move and warm sunlight surrounds them.

SCENE 4 | 21–30 SECONDS: NO MORE GOODBYES

The camera slowly rises above the reunited figures, revealing an enormous breathtaking garden with rivers extending towards the horizon. The golden light becomes softer and more beautiful. The figures sit beside the river, looking towards the endless garden. The camera continues pulling away into an extraordinary aerial view.

At the final moment, display elegant white typography against the beautiful landscape:

"One day, we will sit beside a river in Paradise, laughing about the sorrows we experienced in this world."

VISUAL DIRECTION: Ultra-photorealistic cinematography, extraordinary environmental detail, natural volumetric lighting, realistic flowing water, delicate atmospheric particles, rich emerald landscapes, soft golden illumination, cinematic depth, seamless transitions, sophisticated camera movements, realistic human proportions, 4K film quality. 

SOUND DESIGN: Begin with gentle wind and distant water. Gradually introduce a deeply emotional, soft instrumental-free atmospheric ambience, flowing water and subtle natural sounds. Keep the sound peaceful, spiritual and moving.

IMPORTANT: This is a respectful artistic interpretation inspired by Islamic hope and longing. Do not depict Allah, prophets, angels or make literal claims about the unseen. Avoid religious symbols used decoratively, exaggerated fantasy elements, horror, sadness at the reunion or anything disrespectful. The emotional message must remain rooted in hope, patience, love and eternal peace.

entries.prompt:
Create a finished 30-second realistic social-media UGC advertisement for a fictional AI camera app called LENSO.

The entire video must look like an authentic creator-made smartphone advertisement that could realistically be posted on TikTok, Instagram Reels, or X.

It must NOT look like a polished traditional commercial, movie, music video, CGI demonstration, or AI-generated video.

MAIN CREATOR:
A fictional attractive Korean woman in her mid-to-late 20s.
Naturally beautiful, realistic Korean facial features, healthy natural skin texture, expressive dark brown eyes, dark medium-length straight hair, subtle natural makeup, neat eyebrows, natural lips, warm and confident personality.

She should look attractive and stylish without looking artificially perfect or resembling any real celebrity or identifiable person.

WARDROBE:
Bold contemporary Korean fashion styling:
a fitted black leather-look cropped jacket over a rich burgundy fitted top, high-waisted charcoal wide-leg trousers, tasteful silver earrings and a minimal necklace.
Modern, confident, fashionable and eye-catching, but completely appropriate for a lifestyle creator.
The outfit should look like something a real Korean fashion/tech creator would wear.

SETTING:
A beautiful but believable modern apartment in Seoul-style urban surroundings.
Natural daylight coming through a large window.
Real furniture, books, plants, coffee cup and ordinary lived-in details.
No luxury mansion.
No futuristic interior.
No visible brands or logos.

CAMERA STYLE:
The creator is filming herself primarily with a realistic modern smartphone.

Natural handheld smartphone framing.
Small natural hand movements.
Subtle autofocus adjustments.
Realistic exposure changes.
Natural smartphone dynamic range.
Occasional tiny framing imperfections.
Natural facial expressions and blinking.
Natural hair movement.
Realistic skin texture.

Do NOT make the footage excessively stabilized or cinematic.
Do NOT use impossible camera movements.
Do NOT make it look like a professional film crew shot it.

The result must feel like a real person spontaneously recording a recommendation for her followers.

PRODUCT:
LENSO is a fictional AI camera app that transforms ordinary smartphone footage into polished cinematic-looking footage while keeping the original subject and environment realistic.

No recognizable existing app interface.
No Apple, Samsung, Google, Instagram, TikTok or other real brand references.
Do not generate complex readable UI text.
The phone screen can show a simple believable generic camera interface with a single obvious LENSO capture control.

STORY:

0–5 SECONDS — HOOK

The creator holds her smartphone in selfie mode and speaks naturally directly to the camera.

She gives a small surprised smile.

DIALOGUE:
"Okay, I didn't expect this to actually work."

Natural conversational delivery.
No exaggerated influencer acting.

She quickly turns the phone toward herself and the apartment.

5–10 SECONDS — DEMONSTRATION

She says:

"I've been testing LENSO on completely normal phone footage."

She records herself walking a few steps toward the window.

The footage initially looks like ordinary smartphone video.

Natural room ambience.

10–16 SECONDS — RESULT

She taps the fictional LENSO capture control.

Show a believable visual transition into the processed result.

The exact same woman, clothing, apartment and lighting remain consistent.

The footage becomes noticeably more cinematic through:
better natural-looking exposure,
subtle depth separation,
cleaner motion,
beautiful but realistic color,
natural highlight rolloff,
and more polished camera movement.

Do NOT change her face, clothing, apartment layout or identity.

The transformation must look like realistic computational photography, not magic.

She reacts naturally:

"Look at that."

16–22 SECONDS — SECOND TEST

She turns the phone toward herself again and walks toward the apartment window.

She records a second short shot.

The result shows her standing near the window with natural daylight, realistic hair movement and subtle cinematic depth.

She looks genuinely impressed rather than overly excited.

DIALOGUE:
"And that's literally just my phone."

22–26 SECONDS — CREATOR REACTION

Return to authentic handheld selfie framing.

She looks directly into the camera.

Natural smile.

DIALOGUE:
"If you're making content, you need to try this."

Her delivery should sound spontaneous, friendly and believable.

26–30 SECONDS — SIMPLE CTA

She raises the phone slightly toward camera.

Natural close-up.

She says:

"LENSO. Make your everyday footage look cinematic."

End naturally with her smiling and lowering the phone.

Do NOT create a giant advertising end card.

Do NOT use floating graphics.

Do NOT use holograms.

Do NOT use futuristic effects.

Clear natural female Korean-English-accented conversational voice speaking fluent natural English.

Subtle room tone.
No copyrighted or recognizable music.

DIALOGUE MUST BE SYNCHRONIZED:

No missing words.
No unnatural pauses.
No robotic voice.
No exaggerated facial expressions.

CONTINUITY REQUIREMENTS:

Keep her face, hairstyle, outfit, body proportions and accessories consistent.
Keep the same apartment layout throughout.
Keep the same smartphone throughout.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5: 24-second 3D-animated dock comedy, a pelican swallows a pufferfish and its throat pouch inflates into a spiky ball
entries.description: A polished feature-animation-style short: at a sunrise dock, a plump cartoon pelican scoops a tiny pufferfish, its throat pouch balloons into a translucent spiky ball, it coughs the fish out, and ends wet with a slack, wrinkled pouch while the pufferfish floats away. The 15,000-character prompt (written with Opus 5.5, per the creator) is a lesson in state locking: every character has named states (pouch normal / stretched into a ball / stretched out and saggy; pufferfish normal / puffed) with the exact shots where each applies and a rule that the pouch never returns to normal. It also specifies water physics ("No jelly-like slabs of water… no slow-motion splashes"), quiet background life, no music or speech, and bans live-action, cel-shaded or game looks. Use it for mascot and character-animation briefs.
entries.prompt:
Characters and setting:
Pelican — a stylized cartoon big white pelican, eighty centimeters tall when standing, round and plump, white feathers all over with black wingtips; a thick, long neck; a small tuft of messy feathers sticking back on top of its head; round yellow eyes with black pupils, a ring of pink skin around each eye; a very long beak, the upper beak flat and grey-pink with a small hook at the tip, and an orange-yellow throat pouch hanging under the lower beak — the pouch is a thin, stretchy layer of skin; short orange legs and very large webbed feet. It is the same pelican throughout the film, with its pouch in three states:
  Pouch normal — the pouch is tucked up against the underside of the lower beak. This is the state in Shots 1 to 3.
  Pouch stretched into a ball — the pouch is stretched by the pufferfish inside into a perfectly round ball bigger than the pelican's head, hanging in front of its chest, the skin thin, tight, translucent and shiny, with a dozen or so small points poking out from inside across the surface; the beak is forced open and cannot close; what is inside cannot be seen, only the points poking out. This is the state from Shot 4 until it coughs out the pufferfish in Shot 8. The ball is the pouch skin itself stretched out, attached to the lower beak — it is not an object held in the mouth.
  Pouch stretched out and saggy — the pouch has been stretched loose into a big slack, wrinkled sheet of orange-yellow skin, deflated and full of folds, hanging from the lower beak down past the chest; all its feathers are wet, clumped in strands and beaded with water. This is the state from after it coughs out the pufferfish in Shot 8 through Shot 12; the pouch never goes back to normal.
Pufferfish — a stylized cartoon little pufferfish, the same one throughout the film, in two states:
  Normal — only the size of a ping-pong ball, short and round; pale sandy-yellow back with small dark-brown round spots, creamy white belly; smooth skin with no raised spines; two very large round eyes, a little dopey; a tiny pouting mouth showing two little buck teeth; small translucent fins.
  Puffed into a ball — its body is inflated into a perfectly round ball four or five times its normal size, covered all over with short sharp spines; color, spots, eyes, mouth and fins are the same as normal, and the eyes, mouth and fins stay their original size, looking tiny on the big round ball.
Dock (one location, seen from two directions) — a seaside in the early morning. An old wooden piling covered in barnacles stands in clear shallow seawater, two or three steps away from a wooden dock; the top of the piling is flat and stands more than a meter above the water; the piling has weathered wood grain, and the section around the waterline and below is covered in grey-white barnacles and a little green seaweed; the water is very clear, a pale blue-green, with the sand and stones on the bottom visible.
  Facing the sea — behind the piling is open sea all the way to the horizon; ove the horizon, low, with a golden streak of reflection on the water; the skygoes from orange-pink at the horizon to pale blue above, with a few wisps of thin cloud; in the distance, one or two tiny fishing-boat silhouettes and an orange buoy. Shots 1, 2, 3,
7, 8, 9, 10 and 12 use this side.
  Facing the dock — behind the piling is the side of the wooden dock: a row of thick wooden posts at uneven heights holding up an old plank walkway, with shrimp traps, mooring rope
and an old wooden crate on it, and old tires hanging along its edge; farther 's huts on shore; the sun is not visible, and warm golden sunlight comes frombehind the camera. Shots 4, 5 and 11 use this side.

⚠️ Characters: there is only one pelican and one pufferfish in the whole film. Pouch normal, stretched into a ball, and saggy are three states of the same pelican; normal and puffed
are two states of the same pufferfish; two pelicans or two pufferfish never a
⚠️ Scale: the pufferfish is normally only the size of a ping-pong ball — a single one of the pelican's webbed feet is bigger than it; when puffed up it is a ball slightly bigger
than the pelican's head. The pelican stands eighty centimeters tall.

Premium technology-commercial finish, controlled reflections, realistic shadows, shallow depth of field, crisp surface detail, stable product shape, no hands, no distortion, no onscreen text.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 Flash test: a paint flick explodes into a living painted world, a camera flight through a brushstroke canyon, and a pull-back into a gallery frame
entries.description: A 15-second one-idea world-building transition posted on Seedance 2.5 Flash launch day as a same-prompt test of Seedance 2.5 Flash, Seedance 2.0 and Wan 3.0. A loaded brush touches a blank canvas, a burst of red, blue, yellow and violet paint explodes toward the lens and morphs into birds, waves and mountains; the camera flies through the colour into a painted canyon with glowing boats and villages lighting up, and the final pull-back reveals the whole world hanging as a framed painting in a gallery. The prompt is a "World Hook" line plus a chain of plain beats ending in a reveal, and it closes with a sentence saying what the shot should prove (fluid detail, pigment texture, saturated colour, seamless world-building). Strong for art-supply, paint, museum or creativity-brand openers.
entries.prompt: Paint Explosion World Hook: An artist flicks a brush—and the paint becomes an entire living world. Extreme close-up: a loaded paintbrush touches a blank canvas. A violent burst of red, blue, yellow, and violet paint explodes toward camera. Paint morphs into birds, waves, mountains, and clouds. Camera flies through the colour explosion into a painted landscape. A painted river carries glowing boats through a canyon. Villages made from brushstrokes light up one by one. A child on a hill flicks their wrist, sending colours across the sky. Final pull-back: the whole world is inside a framed painting in a gallery. Why it shows 4K: fluid detail, pigment texture, saturated colour, and seamless world-building.

entries.title: Rapid-fire 25-second couple argument in a lamp-lit living room: eight overlapping lines on a locked 180-degree axis, tight close-up / reverse cuts, 35mm grain
entries.description: A grounded dialogue-performance test on MiniMax H3 (run locally with a Turbo LoRA at 6 steps): a couple in their late thirties argue about parenting in an ordinary suburban living room lit by one table lamp. Eight timed lines alternate wife / husband in hard-cut close-ups on a fixed 180-degree axis, with very short gaps, breathing and tight lip sync, and the clip ends on a static hold of her glare with "no fade out, no black screen". The prompt is a compact performance spec: a "Core tone" line (nonstop overlapping debate, fast snappy replies, minimal silence), a character lock with delivery notes per actor, blocking, a per-line timecode script, a sound-design block (no music) and visual constraints (no slow motion or flashy transitions). Useful for testing dialogue pacing, family-insurance or education spots, and drama coverage.

entries.prompt:
Ultra-Realistic Cinematic Wildlife Documentary – The Little Bird's Mud Home

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic wildlife documentary showing a small warm-brown bird carefully building a rainproof mud nest on a natural tree branch, one tiny mud pellet at a time.

SCENE 1 – Collecting the Mud (0–4 seconds)

Begin with a cinematic macro close-up of a small brown-orange bird standing on a rough tree branch in a peaceful green natural environment. The bird carefully carries a round, moist ball of dark reddish-brown mud in its beak and places it onto the branch. Show the bird's delicate beak movements and realistic feather details. The mud must look wet, heavy and naturally textured.

SCENE 2 – Building the Foundation (4–9 seconds)

The bird repeatedly brings small mud pellets and carefully attaches them together. Show realistic construction behavior as it presses, shapes and joins each piece with its beak. Gradually, the mud develops into a thick, rounded nest foundation attached firmly to the tree branch. Use detailed close-up shots to capture the natural building process.

SCENE 3 – Shaping the Nest (9–16 seconds)

Show the bird continuing to add layers of wet mud, gradually raising the walls and shaping a rounded, enclosed dome. The bird carefully smooths the exterior with its beak, leaving subtle natural cracks, uneven textures and tiny pieces of dried grass embedded in the mud.

A small circular entrance gradually forms on the front side of the dome. The nest must look handmade by a real bird, not manufactured or artificially perfect.

SCENE 4 – The Completed Mud Homes (16–23 seconds)

Transition into a wider cinematic wildlife shot revealing two neighboring rounded mud nests attached to the same natural tree branch. Both structures have thick mud walls and small circular entrance holes.

The little brown bird inspects its completed nest, approaches the entrance and carefully moves its head inside. Show realistic bird movements, natural balance and delicate interactions with the nest.

SCENE 5 – Rainproof Shelter (23–30 seconds)

The atmosphere gradually changes. Dark grey rain clouds gather behind the tree branches. A gentle breeze moves the surrounding green leaves.

Rain begins falling naturally, becoming a steady rainfall. Show realistic water droplets running down the rough exterior surfaces of both mud nests. The two birds remain safely visible inside their respective circular entrances.

End with a beautiful cinematic wide shot of both rounded mud homes on the branch during rainfall, emphasizing the contrast between the wet natural environment and the sheltered birds.

VISUAL STYLE & REALISM

- Photorealistic wildlife documentary cinematography.
- Natural bird anatomy, accurate proportions and authentic feather textures.
- Physically realistic wet mud, individual mud pellets and natural surface imperfections.
- Realistic beak movement and believable nest-building behavior.
- Soft natural daylight transitioning into overcast rainy weather.
- Shallow depth of field in close-up shots.
- Smooth, professional camera transitions.
- Natural green forest background with subtle environmental movement.
- Highly detailed 4K visual quality.
- Authentic wildlife documentary color grading.
- Realistic rain physics and water droplets.

CONTINUITY REQUIREMENTS

Maintain the same bird appearance, feather color, body proportions, tree branch, mud texture and environmental setting throughout the video. The nest must develop gradually through visible construction actions. Preserve the circular entrance design and the final two-nest composition.

NEGATIVE PROMPT

entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second cute, polished 3D animated short film with a charming family-friendly 3D animation aesthetic, soft rounded shapes, detailed textures, expressive character animation, pastel colors, and cinematic lighting.

CHARACTER:
A tiny lavender penguin with a white belly, orange beak and feet, round dark eyes, and a mint-green knitted scarf. Keep its design identical throughout.

SETTING:
A miniature ice cream shop inside a transparent snow globe. The shop has a pastel pink roof, wooden counter, ice cream freezer, and a window overlooking a tiny snowy village with three little cottages. The globe rests on a circular wooden base.

STORY:
The village lights have gone out in the cold snow. The penguin makes a magical glowing ice cream to bring the village back to life.

SCENE 1 (0–5s):
Inside the shop, the penguin looks through the window at the three dark cottages outside. Snow falls steadily. The penguin notices the unlit cottages, looks concerned, then turns toward the ice cream freezer with an idea.

SCENE 2 (5–10s):
The penguin opens the freezer and takes out a small tub of pale yellow ice cream. It scoops one round ball into a waffle cone, then adds a second smaller pink scoop on top. It carefully places the cone into a small golden serving holder on the counter.

SCENE 3 (10–16s):
The penguin sprinkles tiny golden sugar crystals over the ice cream. The crystals glow softly. The ice cream begins emitting a warm golden light. The penguin's eyes widen with delight. Keep the cone stable in the holder.

SCENE 4 (16–22s):
The penguin carries the cone outside the shop to a small stone pedestal in the snowy village square. It gently places the glowing cone upright on the pedestal. The golden light spreads across the snow-covered path toward the three cottages. One by one, the cottage windows light up warmly. Snow continues falling.

SCENE 5 (22–30s):
The penguin steps back and watches the village glow. The cottages are now warmly lit, and the snow-covered square has a cozy golden atmosphere. The penguin smiles proudly. The camera slowly pulls back to reveal the entire miniature winter village inside the transparent snow globe, with the glowing shop and cottages visible.

CONTINUITY:
One penguin, one shop, one snow globe, one ice cream cone, and exactly three cottages. The cone must remain the same waffle cone with pale yellow and pink scoops. The penguin must carry the cone from the counter to the pedestal. The cone stays upright on the pedestal. The golden light spreads from the cone to the cottages in sequence. No teleporting, duplicate objects, random transformations, or sudden scene changes.

AUDIO:
Soft original whimsical instrumental music, gentle snowfall ambience, freezer opening, ice cream scooping, delicate sparkling sounds, and warm magical chimes as the cottage lights turn on. No dialogue or lyrics.

entries.prompt:
Create one continuous cinematic shot with no visible cuts.

Begin with an extreme macro close-up of a human eye at night. The eye fills the entire frame. The skin, eyelashes, moisture, and iris feel completely real. A tiny desert under a black, star-filled sky is reflected inside the pupil.

The camera slowly pushes forward and passes through the pupil. Without cutting, the darkness becomes the night sky above that desert. We emerge at ground level, moving inches above the sand.

Every grain of sand begins floating upward in slow motion. The grains gather in the air and form a massive spiral staircase that climbs through the clouds. The camera follows the staircase upward, moving faster as the world opens around it.

A colossal translucent blue whale swims silently through the sky above us. Its body bends the starlight like glass. Inside the whale is a glowing futuristic city with tiny buildings, moving lights, and rivers flowing through its body.

As the whale turns, gravity rotates with it. The horizon slowly tilts ninety degrees. The desert becomes a vertical wall beside the camera while a vast ocean pours upward across the sky.

Follow one water droplet as it separates from the ocean and floats toward the lens. Inside the droplet is a miniature version of the entire scene: the desert, the staircase, the whale, and the vertical ocean.

The camera dives into the droplet. The miniature world expands around us until we are moving through the original desert again. Continue forward into the reflection of the same human eye from the opening shot.

End on the exact opening composition. The eye blinks once, creating a seamless loop.

Everything should feel photorealistic, cinematic, enormous, and physically connected. Use deep blue starlight, warm golden sand, volumetric clouds, realistic reflections, controlled depth of field, and natural motion blur. Keep the camera movement smooth and intentional. Every transformation should happen inside the shot rather than through a cut.

No text, logos, subtitles, jump cuts, flickering, duplicated objects, broken anatomy, random scene changes, or visible transition effects.

entries.prompt:

00:00–00:03 — RAW INGREDIENTS → 2D INGREDIENTS

A hand brings a light-blue stylus into frame and touches the ramen noodles.

The moment the stylus touches them, the noodles instantly transform from realistic food into black-and-yellow 2D hand-drawn noodles, with the transformation spreading outward from the exact contact point.

The raw cartoon noodles, chicken, mushrooms, corn, and vegetables instantly transform into cooked ramen ingredients. Animated broth appears and begins bubbling dramatically. Black-and-yellow motion lines emphasize the cooking action.

The stylus touches the surface of the broth.

Reveal a premium hero shot: glossy ramen noodles, sliced chicken, mushrooms, corn, finely chopped green onions, chili oil droplets, and a perfectly cut soft-boiled egg in a dark ceramic bowl.

entries.prompt:
30-second SINGLE CONTINUOUS SHOT, 16:9. NO CUTS, NO DISSOLVES - one unbroken take containing EXACTLY 15 transformations, one every 2 seconds. No text anywhere in frame.

STYLE: photoreal natural-history cinematography, large-sensor camera, water-housing lens. Rapid kinetic energy - the animal is always mid-action, never posing. Real muscle, blubber, wet hide, spray, silt, bubbles, shafts of sun through water. BBC realism, never a video game.

SUBJECT: ONE animal, first frame to last. Never replaced, never cut away from, never leaving frame. Its dark eye stays at roughly the same point in frame the whole time - the thread the viewer follows. Every change is CONTINUOUS PHYSICAL DEFORMATION of this same living body: bone lengthening under skin, limbs shrinking into the torso, muscle rebuilding mid-stroke. Never a cut, never a dissolve, never a replacement. Changes are FAST and violent, not gentle.

MASK RULE (critical): EVERY transformation is hidden by water. The animal drives into a splash, foam, a silt cloud, a bubble curtain, spray or its own blow, and comes out the other side as the next form. It enters white water as one animal and leaves it as the next. NEVER morph in clear open water.

COUNTERS - these change in this exact order and never reverse: LEGS four, then two, then none. TAIL furry rope, then thick muscular trunk, then a wide horizontal fluke. NOSTRILS at the snout tip, then mid-skull, then a blowhole on top of the head. LENGTH 1 metre, then 5, then 18, then 30.

PACING: each 2-second stage is split in half - roughly one second holding the new form in clear open motion so it reads, then one second driving hard into the next mask. The animal is never still and never drifts. All 15 forms must be individually recognisable across the 30 seconds, not a continuous blur.

CAMERA: one single continuous move - the camera is PULLING BACK for the entire 30 seconds, retreating steadily as the animal grows, so it always fills the frame. Never locked off, never still until the end.

LIGHT AND PALETTE: a continuous slide from warm shallow green-brown river light, through silt and turquoise coastal water, into deep cold blue ocean, ending in bright open sunlit surface. Never jumps.

STORY: 50 million years of whale evolution - a furry four-legged land animal walks into a river and never comes out, becoming the largest animal that has ever lived.

BEATS - hit all 15, one every 2 seconds:
00:00-00:02 [1/15] Pakicetus: a wolf-sized furry four-legged predator with hooved toes wades into a shallow river, drinking.
00:02-00:04 [2/15] It plunges under. SPLASH. Legs shorten, feet splay and web, the snout flattens forward.
00:04-00:06 [3/15] Ambulocetus: sprawled crocodile-shaped body undulating through brown shallows, silt boiling around it.
00:06-00:08 [4/15] It powers through a SILT CLOUD - the body doubles in length, the hips loosen, the tail thickens.
00:08-00:10 [5/15] Rodhocetus: hind legs collapse to short paddles, the thick tail now drives the whole body.
00:10-00:12 [6/15] It breaches into SPRAY - forelimbs flatten into smooth flippers, fur thins away to bare grey skin.
00:12-00:14 [7/15] It exhales a hard BLOW of vapour; through it, the nostrils crawl backward up the skull.
00:14-00:16 [8/15] White water off the tail - two hindlimbs shrink to buried nubs and a wide horizontal FLUKE snaps open.
00:16-00:18 [9/15] Dorudon: fully aquatic, streamlined, driving downward with vertical fluke strokes into darker water.
00:18-00:20 [10/15] Through a BUBBLE CURTAIN the body elongates violently into an 18-metre serpent - Basilosaurus, sinuous.
00:20-00:22 [11/15] A PLANKTON CLOUD swallows it; it re-emerges shorter, massively thicker, blubber swelling the silhouette.
00:22-00:24 [12/15] Lunging through a KRILL SWARM the skull broadens and the jaw widens enormously.
00:24-00:26 [13/15] Teeth recede into the gums and dark BALEEN plates unfurl down from the upper jaw like a curtain.
00:26-00:28 [14/15] A lunge-feed water SURGE - long throat pleats carve down the underside and the whole body balloons.
00:28-00:30 [15/15] Blue whale, 30 metres, rising into sunlight. It blows once. The camera stops moving for the first time.

AUDIO: diegetic sound only - NO music, NO narration, NO voices. Wading and splashing, heavy wet breathing, muffled underwater pressure, rushing water over the body, bubble roar, the deep boom of a fluke stroke, distant whale groans and clicks, krill hiss, one huge wet blow at the end.

NEGATIVE: no cuts, no jump cuts, no dissolves, no cross-fades, no fade to black; no text, no captions, no logos, no watermark; no humans, no boats, no other animals except distant krill; no second whale in frame; no morph flicker, no ghosting, no double exposure, no detaching limbs; no video-game or CGI look, no slow motion, no locked-off camera, no gentle slow morphing.

entries.title: 1970s home-documentary on 16mm: an old man records rain, bicycle wheels and a kettle, then plays the one tape he saved for last
entries.description: A 30-second experimental short from Seedance 2.5 (via Krea) in an authentic 1970s documentary look: 16mm film grain, slightly faded colour, handheld framing and imperfect exposure on an elderly man who records ordinary sounds on a reel-to-reel machine (rain on a window, bicycle wheels, a kettle, birds); shelves fill with labelled reels, then years later, in a nearly empty apartment, he plays one final tape and a woman's laugh is heard. The creator frames it as thirty seconds of "a man recording ordinary things and one tape saved for last" where the woman on the tape is never seen. The prompt is short and timed, makes the recordings the soundtrack, and forbids showing the woman or explaining the relationship, so it shows how far a single film-stock line plus mundane inserts can carry period texture. Good for heritage, memory, audio or archive brand films.
entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second cinematic experimental short film styled as an authentic 1970s documentary, 16mm film grain, slightly faded colors, handheld camera, natural imperfect exposure, real-world locations, observational editing, practical analog recording equipment, emotionally restrained, no subtitles.

CHARACTER:
One elderly man who collects recordings of ordinary sounds.

0–4s:
Close-up of a reel-to-reel tape recorder.
He presses RECORD.

4–7s:
Rain hits a window.
The tape records it.

7–10s:
He records bicycle wheels rolling over pavement.

10–13s:
He records a kettle boiling.

13–16s:
He records birds outside his window.

16–19s:
Rows of labeled tape reels fill shelves in his small apartment.

19–22s:
Years later.
The apartment is nearly empty.
The elderly man sits beside the recorder.

22–25s:
He chooses one final tape.
He presses PLAY.

26–28s:
We hear a woman's laughter.
The man closes his eyes.

28–30s:
He smiles.
The tape continues playing.

Cut to black.

SOUND:
The sound recordings ARE the soundtrack. Rain, bicycle wheels, kettle, birds and finally the woman's laughter. No conventional music.

IMPORTANT:
Do not show the woman. Do not explain the relationship. The final laugh should clearly sound like a real recorded memory, not a supernatural voice.
