entries.title: Deadpan elevator comedy, locked camera: the doors open on a medieval battle and a passing whale while a man never looks up from his phone
entries.description: A 17-second Seedance 2.5 static-camera gag built on a performance rule: the man "NEVER looks up from his phone at any point, no matter what happens, until the final seconds". The doors open on a cavalry battle (an arrow thunks into the wall and stays there for the rest of the film), then onto a wall of ocean with a humpback whale drifting past, then onto a grey office corridor, where he finally sighs, pockets the phone and trudges out. The timeline gives each door cycle its own sound design and a continuity rule (the arrow persists). Use for telecom, streaming, coffee or "Monday" brand spots.
entries.prompt:
Single continuous static shot, fixed camera, no cuts, no camera movement whatsoever for the entire duration. The camera never moves. Cinematic film comedy, muted color grade, 35mm film grain.

SCENE: The exact elevator interior from the start frame: warm wood-paneled walls, dark lower panels, brushed steel doors, red LED floor indicator above the doors counting down. A tired man in his mid-30s with dark tousled hair, stubble, and a grey-blue tweed blazer stands at the left, leaning against the wall, head bowed, scrolling his smartphone with one thumb, face lit by the phone glow. His expression is bored, dead-eyed, completely indifferent. He NEVER looks up from his phone at any point, no matter what happens, until the final seconds.

TIMELINE:
0.0s-2.0s: Quiet elevator hum. He scrolls lazily. A soft elevator ding.
2.0s-6.0s: The steel doors slide open, revealing a full medieval battlefield in daylight: hundreds of armored knights charging through mud, banners, smoke, arrows flying, swords clashing. The deafening roar of battle floods into the elevator. A single arrow flies in through the open doors and embeds itself with a sharp thunk in the wood panel of the back wall, close to the man, still quivering. He does not flinch. He keeps scrolling, motionless, utterly uninterested. The doors slide closed and the battle sound cuts off instantly, back to soft hum. The arrow stays embedded in the wall for the rest of the film.
6.0s-7.0s: Quiet. He shifts his weight slightly. Ding.
7.0s-11.0s: The doors slide open onto the deep ocean: a sheer vertical wall of dark seawater stands impossibly at the threshold like invisible glass, not one drop spilling in. A massive humpback whale is already mid-passage as the doors part, its enormous body filling the doorway, drifting slowly from right to left, its eye passing close to the threshold. Shimmering blue caustic light ripples across the elevator walls and the man's face. Muffled deep underwater sound. He keeps scrolling. He does not look up. The doors slide closed on the whale still passing, sound cuts back to hum.
11.0s-12.0s: Quiet. Ding.
12.0s-15.0s: The doors slide open onto a completely ordinary grey office corridor with flat fluorescent lighting and beige carpet. The man finally reacts for the first time: a small tired sigh, shoulders dropping, he pockets his phone and trudges out of the elevator into the office with the weary walk of a man going to work. The doors begin to close behind him. End.

The man's appearance, wardrobe and the elevator interior stay perfectly consistent throughout. The doors always open and close at the same mechanical speed. Everything beyond the doors is rendered photorealistically. No text, no captions, no camera shake, no cuts.

entries.title: Pre-interview stillness: a scientist sits, adjusts her mic and glasses, settles, then lifts her eyes to the lens and says "Alright. I'm ready."
entries.description: A 15-second observational-documentary performance test (Seedance 2.0) about restraint: a locked 50mm interview frame, slow deliberate settling actions (stool, blazer, lavalier cable, glasses), a reverse over-the-shoulder showing the crew's light, tripod and monitor cart, then a barely visible push-in as she raises her eyes and delivers one quiet line. Micro-expressions, blinks and breathing are the whole performance, and the negatives forbid exaggerated expressions, speed ramps and beauty filters. A template for founder films, healthcare or B2B testimonial openers.
entries.prompt:
Create a photorealistic 15-second observational documentary interview inside a modern scientific research laboratory. The video should feel like authentic behind-the-scenes footage captured by a professional documentary crew, emphasizing realism, subtlety, and natural human behavior.

A brilliant female scientist with dark hair tied in a relaxed low bun, thin black rectangular glasses, and a dark blazer over a neutral shirt prepares for an important interview. Preserve her exact facial identity, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions, and accessories throughout the entire sequence. Authentic skin texture, natural imperfections, and realistic facial details.

0–3 seconds: A locked eye-level 50mm interview shot. She quietly enters frame, gently pulls out a stool, sits down, smooths her blazer, adjusts the lavalier microphone cable, and takes a calm breath. Every movement is slow, deliberate, and naturally timed.

3–7 seconds: She straightens her posture, lightly rolls her shoulders back, adjusts her glasses with one finger, folds her hands in her lap, briefly looks downward, then settles into complete stillness. Small blinks, subtle breathing, and realistic micro-expressions only.

7–11 seconds: Cut to a reverse over-the-shoulder angle revealing the filming environment. A large soft light, camera tripod, monitor cart, microphones, and scientific equipment are visible in the softly lit laboratory. She remains composed and motionless while the camera quietly observes.

11–15 seconds: Return to the original interview framing with an almost imperceptible slow push-in. She takes one controlled breath, slowly raises her eyes to the lens, maintains unwavering eye contact, gives the slightest confident expression, and quietly says, "Alright. I'm ready." Hold on her gaze until the final frame.

Lighting is soft, natural, and motivated by practical sources with cool laboratory ambience. Neutral color palette, realistic exposure, natural depth of field, subtle handheld micro-vibrations, and authentic documentary camera language.

Audio consists only of natural room ambience: ventilation hum, distant equipment fans, fabric movement, stool scrape, microphone handling, subtle breathing, and clean close-recorded dialogue. No background music.

Negative constraints: no facial drift, no identity changes, no morphing, no beauty filters, no exaggerated expressions, no cinematic action, no extra people visible, no subtitles, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no text overlays, no speed ramps, no slow motion, no camera glitches, no unrealistic lighting, no artificial color grading, no AI artifacts.

entries.title: DV 16mm memory piece: a woman finds a dusty box of old photos under her dorm bed, with tape softness, focus hunting and reflective voiceover
entries.description: A 15-second Seedance 2.5 camcorder "memory piece" organised in labelled blocks (CAMERA / LOOK / STYLE / CHARACTER / STORYLINE): self-held POV with clumsy zooms, delayed focus pulls, occasional face cut-off framing and exposure flicker; "soft, slightly blurry tape quality, faint tape noise, bloomed highlights, muted contrast"; lighting that shifts from dorm daylight to storage dimness, window light and a bedside lamp, ending as the lamp clicks off and the camcorder struggles with the exposure. Voiceover replaces synced dialogue. Use for photo-printing, storage, memory-app or nostalgic brand films.
entries.prompt:
CAMERA:
DV 16mm tape camcorder handheld feel. POV of the woman holding the camera herself throughout each location, occasionally propped briefly for hands-free moments. Natural hand shake, imperfect framing, delayed focus pulls, clumsy zooms, occasional face cut-off framing, autofocus hunting, slight exposure flicker. Camcorder never appears on screen.
LOOK:
Soft, slightly blurry tape quality, faint tape noise, bloomed highlights, muted contrast, realistic skin tones, subtle analog imperfections. Lighting shifts naturally between locations: soft late-morning dorm light → dim storage light → warm afternoon window light → cozy evening lamp light.

STYLE:
Slow, intimate memory-piece rather than a conventional vlog. Gentle pacing with lingering shots and natural pauses. Reflective voiceover narration plays over the visuals instead of synced dialogue. Ambient sounds remain subtle and realistic. Everything should feel like genuine personal footage accidentally captured on an old camcorder.
CHARACTER:
A Korean woman in her 20s. Long straight black hair, natural and slightly undone, dewy realistic skin, minimal to no makeup, big expressive eyes, relaxed natural expressions. Wearing a cozy oversized sweater and loose lounge pants. Arms and torso fully covered throughout.

STORYLINE — 15 SECONDS, 5 CUTS
0–3s — Dorm bedroom, late morning
Handheld POV. She casually tidies her bedside table when she suddenly notices a small dusty cardboard box pushed underneath the bed. She pauses, crouches down, reaches underneath, and pulls it out. The camera follows awkwardly, briefly losing focus before finding the box.

VOICEOVER (woman):
"I found this while cleaning today."
3–6s — Dorm floor, storage corner
She sits cross-legged on the floor and opens the box. Inside are a few old photographs, a friendship bracelet, and a small handwritten note. She picks up the photographs one by one, looking increasingly curious. The camera slowly moves closer with a clumsy handheld zoom.

VOICEOVER (woman):
"I completely forgot I kept these."

6–9s — Macro insert
Close-up of her hands unfolding the old handwritten note. Her fingers carefully smooth the creased paper. She pauses while reading it. Only part of her face enters the edge of frame as she gives a small, genuine nostalgic smile.
NO VOICEOVER.
Only soft paper rustling and distant dorm ambience.

9–12s — Bedroom window, afternoon
Camera is briefly propped near the window. She sits beside it, slowly looking through the old photographs. She suddenly laughs quietly at one of them, then becomes thoughtful and looks outside through the window. Warm afternoon light falls across her face.
VOICEOVER (woman):
"I think I needed to remember who I was before everything got so busy."

12–15s — Bedroom, evening
Handheld close shot. She carefully places the photographs back into the box but keeps one photograph outside. She puts it beside her bed, looks at it for another second, then reaches over and switches off the bedside lamp. The image falls naturally into darkness with the camcorder struggling briefly with the changing exposure.
VOICEOVER (woman):
"Maybe some things are worth keeping close."

entries.title: One-take crying close-up where the state is locked: she has already cried for ten minutes, so only tears, breath and muscles may move
entries.description: A 15-second Seedance 2.5 (Arcads) extreme close-up of a woman on a cold, blurred shoreline, mid-cry. The useful idea is the PREMISE block: every sign of prolonged crying (puffy lids, raw nostrils, flush, salt tracks) is "ALREADY PRESENT IN THE FIRST FRAME and stays constant", and the prompt lists the only things allowed to change (facial muscle position, tear fluid, breathing, hair, cloth, wet gloss). That stops the model from "acting" the redness in and keeps the performance in the face muscles. Handheld long lens with micro-drift, focus locked on the near eye, flat overcast light, no music and no words. Good for testimonial, drama or charity spots that need raw emotion without melodrama.
entries.prompt:
One unbroken 15-second take. No cuts, no scene changes, no re-framing.

PREMISE: she has already been crying for ten minutes before this shot begins. Every sign of prolonged crying is ALREADY PRESENT IN THE FIRST FRAME and stays constant — it does not develop, appear, spread or intensify during the clip.

SUBJECT (fixed state from frame one): extreme close-up of a fictional young East Asian woman, late twenties, face filling the frame, outdoors on a cold shoreline. Ordinary face cast from the street, not a fashion model — slightly asymmetric features, one eyelid marginally lower, natural brows with visible individual hairs. Long dark brown hair, loose and windblown. Grey sleeveless cotton top. Large thin silver hoop earrings.

Already established at frame one and held constant: eyelids puffy and swollen, inner eyelid rims and waterline red, nostril rims raw and pink, a settled uneven flush across the nose bridge and upper cheeks, blotchy mottled patches on the neck, faint dried salt tracks on the cheeks from earlier crying. This is her baseline appearance for the entire clip.

Skin at full texture: visible pores across nose and cheeks, vellus hair along the jaw and upper lip, uneven undertone, a couple of dormant blemishes, dry cracked lower lip. No makeup, no smoothing, no beautification.

CRITICAL: no progressive reddening. No skin colour change of any kind across the 15 seconds. No swelling developing. No blotches appearing or spreading. No flush blooming, creeping or intensifying. Pigmentation and puffiness are locked at the frame-one state.

Within these 15 seconds, ONLY these things are permitted to change: facial muscle position, tear fluid, breathing movement, hair position, cloth position, and wet gloss on skin.

LIGHT AND BACKGROUND: soft flat overcast daylight, cool 6500K, no direct sun, no shadow direction, no exposure shift, no white balance drift. Behind her a completely blurred pale grey coastal background — sea and horizon dissolved into unreadable bokeh, no detail resolving.

CAMERA: handheld operator on a long lens. Continuous micro-drift, small weight shifts, faint breathing sway. No zoom, no push-in, no pull-out, no orbit, no rack focus. Focus locked on the near eye, far eye slightly soft. Face scale identical first frame to last.

CONTINUOUS: fine loose hair strands blow across her cheek, lips and eyeline in irregular gusts, sometimes sticking to wet skin. Involuntary blinks at uneven intervals. Real chest and shoulder breathing.

0.0–3.0s — Suppressing it. Lips compress to a thin flat line, the lip border blanching white under mechanical pressure. Chin muscle bunches and dimples in fast small tremors. One sharp shuddering inhale lifts the chest and catches in the throat; a visible swallow moves the neck. Nostrils flare open and relax. Tears build along the lower lash line and hold by surface tension without spilling; eye surface glassy and reflective.

3.0–6.0s — It breaks. Eyes squeeze shut, lower-lid creases compressing. Inner brows pull up and together, wrinkles forming between them. Mouth opens into a sob, lower lip pulled down and out, corners dragging toward the jaw, tendons standing in the neck. The held tears break and run in two uneven tracks down both cheeks, catching light, thinning over the cheekbone. Wet lashes clump into points. Wet skin gains gloss where the tears pass — moisture only, no colour shift.

6.0–7.5s — Head tilts downward, chin toward the chest, shoulders sinking. Eyes reopen a fraction, unfocused and streaming.

7.5–11.0s — She wipes her face with her own shirt. Her right hand enters from the bottom of the frame, fingers bunching the front hem of the grey top, and pulls the fabric up. She presses the balled cloth against her right cheekbone, holds a beat, and drags it upward and inward across the wet skin — fabric bunching in her fist, dragging the cheek flesh slightly, catching under the eye, pulling the lower lid down a fraction as it passes. Where the cloth presses hard the skin blanches pale for a moment and refills within a second, as real compressed skin does. The cotton darkens where it absorbs the tears. She switches to the left cheek with the same fistful of cloth, wipes across roughly, then presses it flat over her nose and mouth and breathes into it, the fabric denting inward on the inhale and puffing on the exhale. The knit stretches and thins under tension, hem curling, tension wrinkles radiating from her grip. A rough, functional, unglamorous wipe — not delicate, not choreographed.

11.0–12.5s — She lets go. The fabric drops with real cloth weight — a fast fall, a small overshoot, then settles onto her collarbones with residual creases and visible damp patches. Her hand exits back down out of frame. Her face is uncovered in the same position, nothing snapping or teleporting. The tears are physically gone from the cheeks, leaving only faint moisture gloss and a few hair strands pulled loose and stuck across the skin. Her underlying redness and puffiness are exactly as they were at frame one — unchanged by the wiping.

12.5–15.0s — Eyes open only partway, cast downward and slightly off-lens, lashes stuck in wet spikes. Mouth stays open, taking heavy uneven exhausted breaths, top lip trembling on each exhale. Nostrils flaring. Chest rising and falling out of rhythm. One fresh tear starts again at the corner of the left eye and begins to travel. No recovery, no smile, no resolution.

AUDIO: diegetic and sparse only. Steady offshore wind across the microphone, low distant surf, faint fabric rustle when the shirt moves and when it drops. Her breathing carries the scene: the sharp catching inhale near 2s, a broken wet sob on the break near 4s, muffled breath through the cloth around 9–10s, then slow ragged uneven breathing to the end. Small involuntary throat sounds and sniffs. No words, no dialogue, no speech of any kind. No music, no score, no sound design, no reverb, no interior room tone.

RENDER: photoreal cinema, ARRI Alexa 35, 85mm at T2.0, shallow depth of field, filmic contrast with lifted blacks and gentle highlight rolloff, muted desaturated cool palette, fine organic grain, faint chromatic fringing.

NEGATIVE: no progressive reddening, no flush blooming or spreading, no skin tone change, no swelling developing, no colour grading shift, no cuts or transitions, no zoom, no camera move beyond handheld drift, no face morphing or identity drift, no changing hairstyle, no extra or malformed fingers, no second hand entering, no background detail resolving, no lighting change, no text, no captions, no overlays, no logos, no slow motion, no speed ramp, no additional people, no spoken words, no music.

entries.title: Zero-gravity sacrifice in 30 timed beats: hull breach, one escape pod, "Go." / "I'm not leaving you.", tears floating in beads
entries.description: A 30-second Seedance 2.5 (Flova) sci-fi drama written as a one-second-resolution beat sheet. A CHARACTER LOCK fixes both astronauts (ages, hair, suit colours by shoulder patch), and the performance notes ask for "natural performances with no over-acting" while the physics notes make the emotion visible: tears lift off his cheek and drift in zero gravity, and vacuum shots go silent. Dialogue is short and assigned per beat, the score enters only at the pod hatch and swells at the beacon pulse, and the last shot holds on "a small tired smile". Useful as a template for emotional two-hander scenes with strict timing.
entries.prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic sci-fi drama short film, shot like a high-budget feature on anamorphic lenses with natural film grain, believable zero-gravity physics (floating tools, drifting tears) and no gore. Opens with an instant hook, no establishing shot. Setting: a small deep-space relay station orbiting a blue gas planet, cramped corridors, glowing consoles, a pod bay, a large observation window. No real logos, brands or agency insignia. CHARACTER LOCK: Commander Eli is a man in his 40s, short graying hair, stubble, plain white suit with blue shoulder patches. Mara is a woman in her late 20s, dark hair tied back, same suit with orange shoulder patches. Both keep identical faces and suits in every shot. Cold blue space light against hot red alarm light, realistic skin texture, natural performances with no over-acting. Sound in vacuum scenes is muffled and silent. No text overlay, no watermark.
>
> **[0-1s]** Hard cut: a hairline crack bursts across the observation window with the blue planet behind it, red alarm lights flashing.
> **[1-2s]** Extreme close-up: Mara's wide eyes, red light flickering across her face.
> **[2-3s]** Wide shot: debris spins past outside while loose tools and a drifting coffee bulb float through the cabin.
> **[3-5s]** Close-up, Mara: "Hull breach in section four. We're losing air." Eli, cutting in: "Seal the corridor. Now."
> **[5-6s]** Tracking shot: they pull themselves down the corridor as a heavy bulkhead door slides shut behind them.
> **[6-7s]** Close-up on the pod bay console: one pod glowing green, the second dark and offline.
> **[7-9s]** Mara, quietly: "There's only one pod." Eli looks at the pod, then at her, saying nothing.
> **[9-10s]** Extreme close-up: his calm face, a single tear lifting off his cheek and floating in zero gravity.
> **[10-12s]** Eli: "Go." Mara, voice breaking: "I'm not leaving you."
> **[12-14s]** He seals her helmet and rests his gloved hand on her visor. Eli: "Someone has to keep the beacon alive. That's the job."
> **[14-15s]** Close-up: she shakes her head, tears drifting in beads around her face.
> **[15-17s]** He guides her into the pod and the hatch closes, her glove pressed against the glass.
> **[17-18s]** Exterior wide shot, silent: the pod detaches and glides away from the station.
> **[18-20s]** Inside the pod: she presses her face to the window, the station shrinking, her shoulders shaking as she cries.
> **[20-21s]** Station interior: Eli alone, lights dimming, hauling himself to the beacon console.
> **[21-23s]** Close-up: he pulls a heavy lever, and a huge pulse of light flares from the station's dish across the dark.
> **[23-25s]** Radio static in the pod, Eli's voice: "Mara, you see that? Signal's out. Go home."
> **[25-27s]** Close-up: she covers her mouth, trembling, eyes shining with tears, replying in a whisper: "Come back."
> **[27-28s]** Wide shot: far off, a faint set of ship lights appears and pulses back in answer to the beacon.
> **[28-30s]** Final shot: Eli floats by the cracked window, the approaching lights reflected in his visor, a small tired smile. Cut to black.
>
> Audio: alarm klaxon and a metallic creak in the opening, muffled silence outside the station, a low heartbeat-like bass pulse, a minimal piano and strings score entering at the pod hatch and swelling at the beacon pulse, radio static, soft breathing and quiet crying. Camera: handheld close-ups for fear, smooth tracking in the corridor, slow orbit shots, a silent exterior wide shot, no slow motion.

entries.title: Four models, one 5-second egg test: crack it one-handed, keep the yolk whole, look up and say "One hand. No shell."
entries.description: A same-prompt, one-take-each comparison posted by Made (@madeonmade_): Seedance 2.5 Flash, Seedance 2.5, Kling 4 and Gemini Omni Flash 1.2. The prompt is a short vertical "filmed by a friend" phone video that chains a fine-motor action, a physical result and a spoken line. The creator's verdicts: Flash nails the one-handed crack, the whole yolk and the line, but cuts between four shots; Seedance 2.5 holds one unbroken take, but the shell never breaks; Kling 4 has the best sizzle but cuts away before the crack; Gemini Omni Flash 1.2 is a natural single take, but uses two hands and only says "No shell." A good stress test for hand action plus dialogue.
entries.prompt: Vertical phone video, filmed by a friend, in a small sunny kitchen. A man in his early thirties with a short beard stands at the stove and cracks an egg into a hot pan with one hand. The yolk lands whole and the white starts to sizzle. He looks up at the camera, grins and says, "One hand. No shell." Natural sound: the crack, the sizzle and his voice.

entries.title: Ten office outfits in 30 seconds on a locked tripod: palm-over-lens open, pose-matched cuts on the beat, palm-over-lens close
entries.description: A Seedance 2.5 outfit-change reel: one woman with round black glasses in the same charcoal-tiled office washroom, camera locked at eye level, mid-thigh up. A palm covers the lens to start, then nine more office looks (floral dress, lemon kimono blouse, ivory shirt with navy trousers, black sleeveless top, blush top, deep green blouse, blue paisley shift dress and others) arrive on pose-matched cuts timed to a 112 BPM fashion-pop track, about 2 s per look, ending in a burgundy dress and a palm back over the lens. The prompt holds body position, hair, glasses, background and light identical across every cut, and lists cloth failures to avoid ("cloth melting, floating clothing").
entries.prompt:
Create a 30 second photorealistic fashion transformation video in a 16:9 landscape frame. A stylish young woman with long softly waved brown hair, warm medium skin, round black glasses, small earrings, natural makeup, and consistent facial features stands in the same modern office washroom or dressing area for the entire video. The background has large charcoal gray stone tiles, a pale ceiling, a slim black wall rail on the left, and a narrow metal partition line on the right. Keep every architectural line perfectly fixed across all cuts.

Camera is locked on a tripod at eye level, medium full shot from mid thigh upward, using a natural 35 mm equivalent smartphone lens. The subject remains centered with enough space on both sides for the landscape composition. No camera shake, zoom, reframing, or perspective change. Use crisp realistic detail, true skin texture, fine hair strands, believable fabric folds, accurate hands, subtle breathing, and tiny posture adjustments. Lighting is soft cool overhead office lighting with gentle facial fill, mild reflections on the gray tiles, consistent exposure, and realistic shadow direction.

Begin with her palm very close to the lens, briefly obscuring most of the frame. She pulls her hand away and reveals the first outfit, a sleeveless pale blue floral office dress with a light scarf over one shoulder. She looks calmly into the camera, lowers her arm, places one hand on her hip, glances upward with a mildly unimpressed expression, then folds her arms. Match this exact folded arm pose for the first invisible jump cut.

Across the next twenty four seconds, reveal nine distinct office outfits through clean pose matched cuts timed to the music. Use a lemon yellow floral kimono blouse, a relaxed ivory button shirt with navy trousers, a fitted black sleeveless top with dark tailored pants and a brown belt, a soft blush pink top with black trousers, a deep green crew neck blouse, a vivid blue paisley shift dress, a black and white dotted peplum blouse, a camel blazer over a cream top, and a final elegant burgundy wrap dress. Between changes, give her natural confident gestures such as a small shoulder bounce, two thumbs up, hands settling on hips, crossing her arms, turning her chin, smoothing a cuff, lightly flicking her hair, pointing toward her cheek, and smiling directly at camera. Each gesture should begin in one outfit and end in the next so the cut feels practical and intentional, never like body morphing.

Hold each look long enough to read clearly, roughly two seconds per outfit, with cuts landing on strong beats. Preserve identical body position, hair direction, glasses placement, limb anatomy, background geometry, and lighting at every transition. Avoid warped fingers, changing facial identity, floating clothing, cloth melting, duplicated accessories, sudden camera motion, or artificial beauty smoothing.

For the final four seconds, she lands in the burgundy dress with one hand on her hip, gives a warm playful smile, taps one finger lightly against her cheek, then reaches toward the lens until her palm fills the frame, creating a natural practical ending. Do not add captions, logos, watermarks, interface graphics, or generated text.

Music should be an upbeat polished fashion pop instrumental at about 112 beats per minute with tight percussion, light bass, finger snaps, bright synth accents, and clean beat drops for every outfit change. Add subtle realistic clothing movement, bracelet clicks, and a soft hand whoosh at the opening and closing. The finished result should feel like a real creator filmed several office looks in one location and edited them precisely to music.

entries.title: Midnight ramen after a night shift: cold blue rain and neon to warm amber steam, told only through hands, breath and cooking sound
entries.description: A 30-second Seedance 2.5 3D-animated mood piece (stylized realism). The prompt sets the emotional arc in writing ("from cold, tired isolation toward warmth and comfort"), makes steam a recurring motif that grows until it wraps the finished bowl, asks for a new framing on every cut (wide, overhead, counter-level, macro), and keeps the acting tiny: posture, heavy eyelids, small breaths. Audio is rain on glass, gas ignition, boiling water, knife on wood and chopsticks, with no music and no dialogue. Good for food, comfort-brand or late-night delivery spots.
entries.prompt:
Environment: A small, lived-in apartment kitchen at midnight. Rain slides continuously down the window while distant neon city lights glow outside. The kitchen is clean but naturally lived-in, with a wooden cutting board, ceramic dishes, a few utensils and simple cooking ingredients.

Visual style: High-quality 3D animated cinematic short with stylized realism. Cozy, intimate and atmospheric. Warm amber stove and lamp light contrasts with cool blue window light. Realistic food textures, detailed steam simulation, soft reflections, shallow depth of field and subtle cinematic lighting.

Camera language: Use a different framing, height and angle for every cut. Alternate between wide environmental compositions, medium character shots, overhead food shots, low counter-level perspectives, close-ups and extreme macro details. Camera movement is subtle and controlled. No dramatic or exaggerated motion.

Character styling: A young night-shift worker with tired eyes, messy hair, oversized hoodie, loose pajama pants and bare feet. Quiet, exhausted and hungry after a long day. Movements are slow, economical and natural.

Core performance: Focus on the small ritual of preparing food after an exhausting night. The emotional progression moves from fatigue and loneliness toward warmth, relaxation and quiet comfort. Emphasize hands, cooking details, steam, breathing, tired expressions and subtle gestures.

Audio design: No BGM, no dialogue. Only realistic environmental and cooking sounds, including rain against glass, room tone, light switch, gas ignition, boiling water, knife against wood, ceramic contact, pouring broth, chopsticks and subtle breathing.

Negative prompts: No subtitles, no text, no logos, no extra people, no exaggerated cartoon motion, no distorted anatomy, no blurry hands, no malformed food, no unrealistic cooking physics, no dirty kitchen, no excessive clutter, no flickering, no abrupt lighting changes.

[00-03] ARRIVING HOME

Wide shot from a diagonal rear angle.

The worker slowly enters the dark kitchen, shoulders slightly lowered from exhaustion.

They reach toward the wall and switch on a single small lamp.

Warm amber light gently fills the kitchen while cool blue neon light remains visible through the rain-covered window.

The worker pauses for a moment, tired, then walks toward the stove.

Ambient sounds: Rain against glass, soft footsteps, room tone, light switch click.

[03-06] LIGHTING THE STOVE

Low-angle close-up from counter level.

A tired hand places a small metal pot onto the stove.

The fingers slowly turn the gas knob.

Click.

A blue flame ignites beneath the pot and reflects subtly across the metal surface.

Ambient sounds: Pot touching stove, gas clicking, soft flame whoosh, distant rain.

[06-09] WATER BOILS

Overhead macro close-up.

Water inside the pot begins with tiny bubbles forming against the metal.

The bubbles gradually increase until the surface reaches a rolling boil.

Steam begins drifting upward and briefly softens the lens.

Ambient sounds: Water heating, gentle bubbling, subtle metal vibration.

[09-12] NOODLES

Diagonal overhead close-up from the opposite side of the previous shot.

The worker slowly lowers dry ramen noodles into the boiling water.

The noodles soften and disappear beneath the bubbling surface.

Thick warm steam curls upward through the frame.

Ambient sounds: Noodles touching water, bubbling intensifying, subtle steam hiss.

[12-15] PREPARING TOPPINGS

Extreme macro side angle.

Green onions rest on a wooden cutting board.

The worker's hand slowly slices them with controlled, rhythmic movements.

Cut to an even tighter detail of the final pieces falling together.

Ambient sounds: Gentle knife taps against wood, rain in the distance, quiet breathing.

[15-18] THE EGG

Close-up from a low three-quarter angle.

The worker cracks an egg against the edge of a small ceramic bowl.

The shell separates naturally.

The egg falls cleanly into the bowl, the golden yolk catching the warm kitchen light.

The worker briefly stares at it with tired, unfocused eyes in the background.

Ambient sounds: Egg crack, ceramic tap, subtle kitchen ambience.

[18-21] WAITING

Medium profile shot from the opposite side of the kitchen.

The worker stands quietly beside the stove, leaning slightly against the counter.

Steam drifts around their tired face.

They rub one eye, exhale softly and watch the noodles cook.

Rain and blue city lights remain softly blurred through the window behind them.

Ambient sounds: Boiling pot, rain, quiet breathing, occasional water drip.

[21-24] NOODLES

Extreme close-up from pot level.

Chopsticks enter the steaming pot and slowly lift a bundle of glossy noodles.

Long strands stretch upward through the steam.

Small droplets fall back into the broth in slow, natural movements.

Warm highlights reflect across the wet noodles.

Ambient sounds: Wet noodles moving, chopsticks touching the pot, droplets falling, gentle bubbling.

[24-27] BUILDING THE BOWL

Direct overhead close-up.

The noodles settle into a ceramic bowl.

Hot broth pours around them in a smooth circular motion.

The egg, sliced green onions and a small amount of chili oil are added.

The chili oil spreads naturally across the broth in delicate red-orange patterns.

Steam continuously rises from the finished bowl.

Ambient sounds: Broth pouring, ceramic contact, ingredients settling, gentle liquid movement.

[27-30] QUIET COMFORT

Side close-up with very shallow depth of field.

The finished ramen rests on the small kitchen table beside the rain-covered window.

Steam rises in slow, soft waves.

The worker sits down.

Both hands gently wrap around the warm ceramic bowl.

Close-up on the tired face as the warmth reaches their hands.

Their shoulders relax.

Their eyes close briefly.

A tiny, peaceful expression replaces the exhaustion.

Hold on the steaming bowl and their hands as neon reflections softly shimmer across the wet window behind them.

Ambient sounds: Gentle rain, faint city ambience, ceramic movement, soft exhale.

Cut to black.

Maintain the same character, clothing, kitchen layout, bowl, pot, ingredients and lighting throughout all shots.

The entire sequence takes place continuously at midnight. Warm amber interior light and cool blue neon window light must remain visually consistent.

Each cut must introduce a noticeably different composition or camera angle. Do not repeat identical framing.

Prioritize tactile cooking details: bubbling water, glossy noodles, cutting-board texture, egg yolk, swirling broth, chili oil, condensation and physically realistic steam.

Steam should act as a recurring visual motif, beginning subtly with the boiling water and becoming increasingly visible until it surrounds the finished bowl in the final shot.

Character animation must remain restrained and realistic. Communicate exhaustion through posture, slow movement, heavy eyelids, small breaths and subtle gestures rather than exaggerated expressions.

The emotional progression should move naturally from cold, tired isolation toward warmth and comfort.

No dialogue, no subtitles, no on-screen text and no background music. Use only rain, cooking sounds, room ambience, footsteps, breathing and subtle city noise.

entries.title: Quiet Seoul hillside afternoon in a cream cardigan: bicycle, footbridge, notebook, wind bell, stone stairs, with a sound cue on every beat
entries.description: A 30-second Seedance 2.5 slice-of-life vlog with a calm, cool-toned mood: a woman walks and rides a bicycle through an old hillside neighbourhood in Seoul from overcast afternoon into early golden hour. Each 3-4 s beat carries its own "*sound:*" line (cicadas, stream, a faraway train, a single brass wind bell, pen on paper), and the FEEL line sums it up as "warm in feeling but cool in tone". Smooth, unhurried camera, fine film grain, no music. A good template for travel, stationery or tea brands that want a reflective mood.
entries.prompt:
SUBJECT: Young Korean woman, early 20s, natural refined everyday look. Oversized cream cardigan over a white tee, wide-leg light denim, plain leather loafers, small canvas tote on her shoulder, hair in a low loose ponytail with a few soft strands framing her face. Minimal makeup, dewy realistic skin, calm and warm reflective presence. Keep her identity, clothing, and hair consistent all the way through.

SETTING: A quiet old hillside neighborhood in Seoul, soft overcast late afternoon into early golden hour. Narrow sloping alleys between low brick-and-tile houses, blue and green painted metal gates, potted plants and styrofoam garden boxes along the doorsteps, a shallow stone-lined stream with a low footbridge, tangled power lines overhead, a parked bicycle with a wire basket, an old zelkova tree with a small wooden pavilion beneath it, a red post box on the corner, laundry drying on a rooftop, rooftop water tanks in the distance. Lived-in and peaceful — no stores, no crowds, no tourists.

LOOK: Cinematic slice-of-life vlog. Composed, intentional framing, quiet and observational. Soft muted natural tones, cool and gentle, realistic skin. Shallow depth of field, fine film grain, soft natural light. Smooth cinematic camera movement throughout — calm, unhurried, letting each moment breathe.

SEQUENCE:

**[0–4s]** Wide establishing shot of the empty sloping alley, power lines crossing overhead, potted plants along the walls. She enters frame from the far end, walking her bicycle slowly toward the camera. The camera holds still, then begins a slow push in.
*sound: distant cicadas / gentle wind / faint neighborhood ambience*

**[4–8s]** She rides the bicycle slowly down the lane, cardigan and loose strands drifting in the breeze. The camera travels beside her at an even pace, walls and blue gates sliding past.
*sound: soft bicycle wheels / cicadas / wind / a faraway train*

**[8–12s]** She stops at the low footbridge over the stream, leans her bicycle against the railing, rests her arms on it, and gazes down at the shallow water moving over the stones. The camera drifts gently toward her, then past her shoulder down to the water.
*sound: quiet running water / cicadas / soft wind*

**[12–16s]** She sits on the edge of the wooden pavilion under the old zelkova tree, opens a small notebook, and writes slowly, pausing to think and look up at the branches. The camera moves evenly around her, focus soft on her hands, then rising to her face.
*sound: pen on paper / cicadas softening / wind through leaves / distant wind bell*

**[16–20s]** She crouches by a doorway beside a row of potted plants and gently lifts a small brass wind bell hanging from the eaves, watching it turn in her fingers. The camera rises slowly from the bell up to her face, catching a small smile.
*sound: single clear wind bell / soft breeze / cicadas / faint chatter from a nearby house*

**[20–24s]** She walks up the lane holding a cold canned barley tea, condensation on the can, the red post box passing softly behind her. The camera moves ahead of her at a steady pace, keeping her centered as the light warms.
*sound: unhurried footsteps / cicadas / distant bicycle bell / wind*

**[24–27s]** She pauses at a low wall overlooking the neighborhood, tiled rooftops and water tanks layered below, and takes a slow sip. The camera drifts sideways past her, revealing the view opening out beneath the hill.
*sound: soft wind over rooftops / cicadas / a faraway train horn*

**[27–30s]** She reaches a long stone stairway between the houses, climbs the first steps, and glances back over her shoulder with a small calm smile before continuing up into the softening golden light. The camera holds low at the base of the stairs, letting her walk out of frame.
*sound: footsteps on stone / cicadas / soft wind / slow fade*

**AUDIO:** Natural ambient only — summer cicadas, shallow stream water, a distant train, wind through the power lines, a single brass wind bell, unhurried footsteps, faint neighborhood ambience. No music.

**FEEL:** A serene, composed afternoon in an old Seoul hillside neighborhood — smooth, warm in feeling but cool in tone, an unhurried and beautiful slice of everyday life.

entries.title: Rural Korea, 1995, one continuous take: dawn farmhouse, chickens, garden, rice paddies and a stream with the same village dog
entries.description: A 30-second Seedance 2.5 nostalgic countryside piece written as eight short timed beats in one continuous handheld take: a woman wakes at 5:45 AM to an old radio, opens a wooden window onto misty paddies, feeds chickens, picks vegetables and washes them in a stream, with the same medium-sized dog beside her throughout. The period is held with a "NO:" list (no modern cars, smartphones, scooters or post-1995 technology) and a STRICT CONSISTENCY line for the woman, outfit, basket and dog. Subtle 35mm grain and lens flare in the paddy beat; rooster, birds and water for sound. Good for heritage food or travel films.
entries.prompt:
Create a highly photorealistic rural South Korean village in 1995, authentic and lived-in, with traditional homes, rice fields, misty mountains, vegetable gardens, stone paths, clay jars and period-accurate farming tools.

0–4s | Home:
A young Korean woman in her early 20s wakes inside a modest traditional Korean farmhouse. Long dark hair in a simple low braid with a fabric ribbon. She wears an authentic 1995 rural outfit: loose cream cotton blouse, long muted-brown skirt, white ankle socks and simple canvas slip-ons. An analog clock shows 5:45 AM; an old radio plays softly.

4–8s | Window:
She opens the wooden window. Misty rice fields and distant mountains glow in early sunrise. Her same friendly medium-sized village dog waits outside.

8–12s | Chickens:
She walks outside with her woven basket, the same dog beside her. She scatters grain for chickens while passing traditional village houses, wooden fences and clay jars.

12–16s | Garden:
She picks dew-covered fresh vegetables and places them in the basket. The same dog waits nearby.

16–20s | Village Walk:
She walks along a quiet dirt-and-stone path with the dog beside her. She gently pats its head. Traditional farmhouse, firewood, clay jars and wooden fences surround them.

20–25s | Rice Fields:
She and the dog walk between green-golden rice paddies. Misty mountains, birds and distant farmers create an authentic 1995 Korean countryside atmosphere. Subtle 35mm film grain and natural lens flare.

25–28s I Stream:
She kneels beside a small wooden bridge and washes the vegetables in a clear stream. The dog waits beside her and looks curiously at the water.

28–30s | Home:
She walks back toward the village with her basket, the same dog happily beside her. Warm sunlight fills the road as she looks toward the mountains and smiles peacefully.

AUDIO: rooster calls, chickens, birds, gentle dog sounds, flowing water, wind, village ambience and faint old-radio music.

STRICT CONSISTENCY: Same woman, face, braid, outfit, shoes, basket and same dog throughout. Dog must keep identical breed, size, fur and markings.

NO: modern cars, smartphones, modern buildings, modern clothing, scooters, contemporary objects or post-1995 technology.

CAMERA: ONE continuous cinematic take; no cuts, transitions, montage or time jumps. Natural handheld camera movement.

entries.title: An ordinary humid summer day on a cheap old compact digital camera: laundry, watermelon, convenience-store walk, filmed by a friend
entries.description: A 30-second Seedance 2.5 found-footage home video of a Japanese man in his early 20s in an old residential neighbourhood. The prompt gets its texture from camera behaviour, not a grain filter: "slight autofocus hunting", brief exposure shifts from inside to outside, mild digital noise, soft detail, slight motion blur, "muted summer colours", occasional blown highlights and compression artefacts, framing that drifts too low or high and corrects. It explicitly says "No artificial film grain" and "no gimbal, no drone". Small human beats (a shirt slips off the line, a laugh behind camera) sell the realism.
entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic documentary-style personal home video capturing a completely ordinary summer day in the life of a Japanese man in his early 20s. The footage should feel accidental, intimate, nostalgic, imperfect, and genuinely lived rather than scripted or performed.
MAIN SUBJECT
The same Japanese man throughout the entire video.
Early 20s, naturally handsome without looking like a model, realistic skin texture, slightly tired eyes, relaxed facial expressions, naturally messy medium-length dark hair, a few loose strands across his forehead, very subtle stubble.
He wears a loose faded navy T-shirt, light gray relaxed-fit pants, worn canvas sneakers, and a simple silver wristwatch.
His identity, facial features, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, and overall appearance must remain completely consistent throughout.
SETTING
An older residential part of Japan during a humid summer afternoon.
Small apartment buildings, narrow streets, convenience-store refrigerators visible through windows, concrete staircases, old balconies, rooftop water tanks, bicycles, utility poles, tangled overhead wires, potted plants, faded walls, parked cars, open windows, and distant city buildings.
The environment should feel ordinary and genuinely inhabited.
No tourist landmarks, recognizable brands, advertisements, crowds, or staged-looking locations.
CAMERA
The entire video looks like footage recorded casually by a friend using an inexpensive older compact digital camera.
Handheld and imperfect.
Natural shake from walking.
Occasional awkward framing.
Slight autofocus hunting.
Brief exposure shifts when moving indoors and outdoors.
Mild digital noise.
Soft details.
Slight motion blur.
Muted summer colors.
Occasional blown highlights.
Subtle compression artifacts.
The camera operator does not behave like a professional cinematographer.
No gimbal.
No drone.
No cinematic tracking shots.
No dramatic lighting.
No slow motion.
No artificial film grain.
No polished commercial aesthetic.
The camera sometimes points slightly too low or too high and corrects itself naturally.
⸻
00:00–00:05 — LAUNDRY
The man stands on a small apartment balcony hanging freshly washed clothes.
A humid breeze moves the laundry around him.
One shirt slips from his hand and falls onto the balcony floor.
He looks down, sighs with a small amused smile, picks it up, shakes it once, and hangs it again.
The camera is positioned from inside the apartment doorway.
Someone quietly laughs behind the camera.
He briefly looks toward the camera with an expression that says he knows he’s being filmed.
Natural household ambience.
⸻
00:05–00:10 — KITCHEN
He walks into a small apartment kitchen.
He opens an old refrigerator.
Cold air escapes.
He takes out a bowl of watermelon and a bottle of water.
He closes the refrigerator with his hip because both hands are occupied.
He sits at a small table near the window.
He eats one piece of watermelon while looking outside.
A drop of juice runs down his finger.
He notices it and wipes his hand on a napkin.
The camera autofocus briefly locks onto the window instead of his face.
⸻
00:10–00:14 — OLD BUS STOP
Cut to outside.
He waits alone at a quiet neighborhood bus stop.
He checks the time on his silver watch.
He looks down the road.
A local bus approaches but passes through the frame without stopping.
He watches it disappear.
He gives a tiny disappointed shrug.
The camera operator slightly misses the bus while trying to reframe.
No dramatic reaction.
Just an ordinary inconvenience.
⸻
00:14–00:19 — SMALL STREET / PARKED CAR
He notices a stray cat sleeping underneath a parked car.
He crouches down several feet away.
The cat opens one eye.
He quietly smiles and reaches out his hand without touching it.
The cat gets up and walks away.
He remains crouched for another second, watching it disappear around the corner.
He stands up slowly.
The camera remains imperfectly framed around him.
A distant motorcycle passes.
⸻
00:19–00:23 — SUNSET CONCRETE COURT
He reaches a small empty neighborhood basketball court.
The evening sun is low.
He places his drink beside the fence.
He kicks a loose pebble across the concrete.
He notices a basketball sitting near the fence.
He picks it up and casually shoots once.
The ball hits the rim, bounces away, and rolls toward the camera.
The camera operator instinctively steps backward as the ball approaches.
The man laughs.
⸻
00:23–00:27 — WALKING HOME
He picks up the basketball and returns it to where he found it.
He walks home carrying the empty drink bottle.
The sky has become slightly darker.
Apartment windows begin glowing in the distance.
He walks slowly, occasionally kicking tiny stones along the pavement.
The camera follows several steps behind.
No posing.
No eye contact with the camera.
Just an ordinary walk home.
⸻
00:27–00:30 — FINAL MOMENT
He reaches the entrance of his apartment building.
He stops before going inside.
For a second he looks back toward the camera.
He gives a small tired smile.
He raises the empty bottle slightly like a casual goodbye.
Then he turns around and disappears through the entrance.
The camera stays pointed at the doorway for a moment.
Someone behind the camera quietly says something indistinct.
At approximately 00:29, the footage abruptly cuts to black.
No fade-out.
⸻
PHYSICAL REALISM
Everything must behave according to believable real-world physics.
Hands, fingers, facial expressions, hair, clothing, food, bottles, basketball, bicycle, cat, vehicles, laundry, and environmental objects must remain physically consistent.
No duplicated objects.
No disappearing objects.
No warped anatomy.
No extra fingers.
No fused limbs.
No floating objects.
No teleportation.
No impossible movements.
The basketball must bounce and roll naturally.
The cat must move like a real animal.
Laundry must respond naturally to wind.
The bottle must remain a separate physical object.
Maintain continuity of the subject and environment between every shot.
AUDIO
Only natural location audio.
Refrigerator hum.
Clothing moving in the wind.
Apartment ambience.
Distant traffic.
Bus engine.
Footsteps.
Basketball bouncing.
Cat movement.
Motorcycles.
Birds.
Distant voices.
Faint city noise.
Subtle handling sounds from the camera.
No music.
No soundtrack.
No narration.
No artificial sound effects.
No dramatic audio transitions.
FINAL FEEL
It should feel like an old personal recording that was never meant to become a film.
Nothing important happens.
That is the point.
A young man doing laundry.
Eating watermelon.
Missing a bus.
Noticing a cat.
Taking one basketball shot.
Walking home.
Small movements, awkward pauses, ordinary mistakes, and quiet moments should carry the emotion.
The video should feel warm, nostalgic, slightly lonely, youthful, masculine, intimate, imperfect, and completely believable.
The viewer should feel as though they accidentally found a 30-second fragment of someone’s real life from a summer years ago.
Prioritize human imperfection over cinematic beauty, continuity over spectacle, and authentic observation over performance.

entries.title: Kling Image 4.0 official example: 35mm suspense still through blurred chess pieces, Dutch angle, fine grain and amber-caramel palette
entries.description: An official example from the Kling Image 4.0 User Guide (published 2026-11-18, "Narrative Storytelling"): a 35mm film-photography thriller still of a freckled woman with pale blonde curls leaning over a chessboard. The prompt is a model of measurable framing: Dutch angle "tilted 45 degrees to the left", her face takes "more than 50%" of the frame, foreground pieces fill "approximately 45%" as a blurred natural frame, focus "precisely locked on the woman's right eye", warm side-top light from upper right, slightly overexposed highlights, fine film grain. Use it as a start frame for an image-to-video thriller beat.
entries.prompt: A cinematic 35mm film photography aesthetic, featuring fine film grain and the classic look of a Hollywood suspense thriller. The image captures a tense moment during a chess match, as a woman leans over the chessboard, studying the pieces and engaging in a psychological battle with her opponent. The main subject is a young woman with pale blonde curly hair, fair skin, freckles, light-colored lips, and light blue-green eyes. She wears silver hoop earrings and a black outfit decorated with white polka dots. Leaning forward with her face extremely close to the camera, she adopts the posture of someone looking down at a chessboard during a match. Her expression is tense and alert, as though she is carefully examining a crucial move. The setting is a warm-toned indoor space. In the foreground, a chessboard and chess pieces are visible, with the checkered pattern of the board faintly discernible. Soft, warm bokeh lights appear in the background. The shot uses a Dutch angle, tilted 45 degrees to the left, creating a sense of instability and suspense. The camera looks upward at the woman's face from between the chess pieces, creating an extremely close, low-angle voyeuristic perspective. She appears to be leaning over and scrutinizing the chessboard. Her face occupies the upper-middle portion of the frame, taking up more than 50% of the image. The foreground chess pieces fill approximately 45% of the lower and side edges of the frame. They are extremely blurred and enlarged, forming a natural frame around the subject. The warm bokeh lights in the background are further softened and reduced in scale, enhancing the sense of perspective and spatial depth between the subject, props, and environment. The lighting consists of soft, warm side-top lighting entering diagonally from the upper right of the frame, creating natural transitions between light and shadow across the woman's face. Noticeable highlights appear on the tip of her nose and cheekbones, while the tops of the chess pieces catch faint reflections. The image emphasizes the freckles and skin texture on her face, her light blonde curls, the cool metallic sheen of her silver earrings, the texture of her black polka-dot outfit, and the realistic refraction and soft-focus effects produced by the foreground chess pieces. The depth of field is extremely shallow, with focus precisely locked on the woman's right eye and the bridge of her nose. Her left eye, lips, and the foreground chess pieces are softly blurred. The overall palette is dominated by rich amber, caramel brown, and warm orange tones. The chess pieces are black and white, her skin has a warm fair tone, and her black clothing contrasts with the cool highlights of her silver accessories. Highlights are slightly overexposed, while shadows are rich and transition naturally through warm tones. The overall atmosphere is tense and suspenseful, evoking a chess match, psychological warfare, vintage warmth, and a struggle for power. The image conveys an immersive sense of intellectual confrontation, as though the viewer is secretly observing the match.

The warm terracotta wall contrasts naturally with the cool green-gray shop doors. Do not turn the store into a modern convenience store or remove the awning, snack boxes, or bicycle.

entries.title: Kling 4.0 observational macro: a dew-covered dragonfly on a grass stem for 30 seconds, nine stills used as references rather than keyframes
entries.description: A 30-second 16:9 Kling 4.0 nature film that stays photoreal by asking for very little to happen: the same resting dragonfly (colours, eyes, legs, veined wings with dew are all specified), soft green meadow, shallow depth of field and a "gentle cool-to-golden" light progression. Two reusable ideas: "Use the nine supplied images as ordinary visual references, not time-locked keyframes", and a negative list aimed at the usual macro failures ("no sudden takeoff, extra insects, deformed anatomy, artificial sparkles, species or location labels"). entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second home-video recipe vlog showing a young woman from London in her mid-20s making Turkish eggs in her small, sunlit kitchen. She wears relaxed home clothes, has her hair loosely tied back, and films everything herself with a consumer mini-DV camcorder. Some shots are handheld; others are recorded after she props the camera on the counter. Keep the footage candid and imperfect: gentle camera shake, occasional focus hunting, slightly awkward framing, natural zoom adjustments, subtle grain, mild motion blur, and automatic exposure changes caused by the bright morning light.

Follow this exact sequence:

0–3s: In a propped medium shot, she places a bowl on the counter, looks toward the camera, and says quietly, “Let’s make Turkish eggs.”

3–6s: Overhead close-up as she combines thick yoghurt, finely grated garlic, and a pinch of salt, stirring until smooth. Clearly hear the spoon moving around the bowl.

6–9s: Handheld detail shot as she spoons the garlic yoghurt onto a shallow plate and spreads it into soft, imperfect swirls.

9–12s: Close-up beside a saucepan of gently simmering water. She cracks an egg into a small bowl and says, “Keep the water gentle.”

12–15s: Overhead shot as she carefully slides the egg into the water. The white naturally curls around the yolk; the water never boils aggressively.

15–18s: Macro-style detail of butter melting in a small pan. She adds pul biber, creating a vivid orange-red mixture that blooms and audibly sizzles. No dialogue.

18–21s: Handheld close-up as she removes two softly poached eggs, lets them drain briefly, and places them over the garlic yoghurt.

21–24s: Extreme close-up as she pours the sizzling pul-biber butter across the eggs, creating rich red-orange streaks over the white yoghurt.

24–27s: Warm, propped shot. She adds fresh dill, tears off a piece of crusty bread, and breaks open one egg, revealing the flowing golden yolk. She says, “Look at that.”

27–30s: Handheld finishing shot. She scoops up yoghurt, egg, and chilli butter with the bread, takes a bite, smiles genuinely, and says, “Best breakfast.” She then reaches forward and covers the lens.

Prioritise intimate food sounds: yoghurt stirring, garlic scraping, simmering water, egg cracking, butter sizzling, ceramic clinks, and bread tearing. Dialogue should sound quiet and casually captured through the camcorder microphone. Preserve realistic imperfections such as irregular poached-egg whites, small splashes, messy spoon marks, brief pauses, natural blinking, and exposure shifts. It must look like a genuine personal breakfast vlog.

entries.prompt:
Seattle — Overlook Walk Tourist Photo Scene
Dreamina Seedance 2.5 | 12 Seconds | 3:4 Vertical
Create a 12-second hyper-realistic cinematic replacement scene for the existing Seattle video. Three distinct shots with hard cuts, natural American English dialogue, realistic physical interactions, and precise object continuity.
CHARACTER AND LOCATION REFERENCES

Use the original female streetwear reference image and existing Seattle video to preserve Woman 1's exact facial identity, black knit beanie, long dark wavy hair, beige puffer vest, fitted top, oversized blue jeans, belt, and accessories.

Use "OVERLOOK WALK.png" as the architectural and environmental reference.

The setting is Seattle's Overlook Walk, featuring landscaped terraces, wooden seating, pedestrian walkways, metal railings, and Elliott Bay in the background. Natural late-afternoon autumn lighting.

Woman 1 carries a small bouquet of yellow flowers in her LEFT hand throughout the entire scene. Her RIGHT hand is free to receive, operate, and return the tourist's smartphone.

Man 1, her male friend from the original Seattle video, remains nearby with consistent appearance.

The tourist couple consists of two American adults with consistent facial identities and clothing across all shots.

SHOT 1 — THE OFFER | 0:00–0:04

Medium-wide three-quarter camera angle showing Woman 1 approaching the tourist couple, who are struggling to frame a selfie with the waterfront behind them.

Woman 1 notices and gestures toward their phone with her empty right hand.
Woman 1: "You want the skyline in it too?"

Tourist: "Please."

The tourist extends the smartphone toward Woman 1.

Woman 1 takes the phone with her RIGHT hand. The handoff is clearly visible and physically completed before the cut.

Her yellow flowers remain securely in her LEFT hand.

Hard cut.

SHOT 2 — THE PHOTOGRAPH | 0:04–0:08

Over-the-shoulder camera angle from slightly behind Woman 1, looking past her toward the tourist couple and Seattle waterfront.

Woman 1 holds the smartphone upright in her RIGHT hand, camera facing the couple.

The couple stands together with Elliott Bay behind them, smiling naturally.
Woman 1 adjusts the framing slightly.

Woman 1: "Okay, got it."

She visibly taps the phone's camera shutter button with her right thumb.

The photograph is actually taken. The couple relaxes their pose.

The yellow flowers remain in her LEFT hand, clearly separate from the phone.

Hard cut.

SHOT 3 — THE PAYOFF | 0:08–0:12

Medium conversational shot showing Woman 1 handing the smartphone back to its original owner using her RIGHT hand.

The tourist receives the phone and looks at the photograph on its screen.

Tourist: "That's actually perfect."

Woman 1: "I charge by the compliment."
The couple laughs. Woman 1 smiles, turns, and begins walking away with Man 1.

The bouquet remains in her LEFT hand.

End with a natural walking movement suitable for cutting into the next Seattle waterfront scene.

CINEMATOGRAPHY

Hyper-realistic live-action photography with authentic skin pores, natural facial expressions, believable fabric movement, and accurate human anatomy.

Natural handheld cinematography with three distinct camera perspectives:

Shot 1: Three-quarter medium-wide interaction

Shot 2: Over-the-shoulder photograph

Shot 3: Medium conversational payoff

Use hard cuts only. No morphing, dissolves, or continuous camera orbit between shots.

Natural waterfront ambience, wind, footsteps, distant pedestrians, and casual conversation. No background soundtrack.

SUBTITLE DESIGN
All spoken dialogue uses Poppins SemiBold, weight 600, pure white #FFFFFF over a dark charcoal #17212B rounded rectangle at 60% opacity.
Dialogue font size 36–42 px at 1080 × 1440 resolution. Bottom-center, approximately 8–10% above the lower edge. Background padding 12 px vertical and 22 px horizontal, 10–12 px corner radius.

Synchronize subtitles precisely with the spoken words. Maximum two lines. No opening location title.

CRITICAL CONTINUITY AND ACTION RULES

The yellow flowers remain in Woman 1's LEFT hand from beginning to end. They never teleport, switch hands, disappear, or change appearance.

The smartphone begins in the tourist's possession, transfers visibly into Woman 1's RIGHT hand, remains in her right hand while she takes the photograph, and transfers visibly back to the original tourist.

The phone must never appear simultaneously in two people's hands except during the physical handoff.

Woman 1 must actually take the photograph. Show the phone aimed at the couple and a deliberate shutter-button press.

The tourist couple must remain stationary and visibly pose during the photograph.

Only the designated speaker delivers each line. Accurate lip synchronization, no overlapping or duplicated dialogue.

Maintain consistent character identities, clothing, props, background architecture, lighting, and spatial orientation across all three shots.

No extra characters entering the interaction, no duplicated people, no extra hands, no distorted phones, no unnatural gestures, and no unexplained object transfers.

Prioritize the physical sequence: offer → receive phone → photograph → return phone → joke → walk away.

The finished scene should feel like a spontaneous, slightly humorous interaction captured during a real afternoon in Seattle.

entries.prompt:
Create a 30 second cinematic nightlife video in native 16:9 that feels like genuine handheld MiniDV footage from an intimate early 2000s club party. The same stylish young woman anchors every shot, with long straight dark hair, narrow black sunglasses, a pale sleeveless top, layered silver jewelry and glossy makeup. Friends drift naturally in and out of frame.

0 to 3 seconds. Start from black, then reveal her in a tight chest up shot against ornate wallpaper and a dark doorway. Harsh on camera flash lifts her face from deep blue shadow. She raises both hands near her cheeks, makes playful finger poses, smiles and turns toward a friend entering from camera right. Let a phone and hands briefly crowd the foreground.

3 to 7 seconds. Two friends squeeze beside her, laughing shoulder to shoulder while one arm lifts overhead. The camera sways, tilts and reframes imperfectly. Cut to a looser waist up view as she dances alone, brings both hands beside her sunglasses and poses. Let exposure pump when a bright wall screen enters frame. End in close profile as she puckers her lips toward the lens.

7 to 11 seconds. Drop the camera toward torsos, hands, jewelry and crowded bodies, then cut to a darker area where a narrow blue spotlight crosses haze and a shadowed partygoer moves through it. Return to the woman from a low close angle. She raises a metallic drink can and takes a natural sip with believable fingers and reflections.

11 to 15 seconds. Use quick candid cuts through friends dancing close together, with hair and shoulders briefly blocking the lens. Return to a frontal close up as she looks into camera. A jeweled hand passes across her face as a natural wipe. Add one brief analog ghosted double exposure, then return to clean handheld footage. No titles, credits, captions, logos or watermarks.

15 to 21 seconds. She smiles, laughs, dips her chin and lifts her jewelry toward camera. A friend presses cheek to cheek with her and both react naturally. Keep the lens close enough for hands to partly occlude faces. Build through fast cuts of the group huddling, posing and laughing. Near 20 seconds she raises one arm overhead while a friend leans against her shoulder. Preserve tiny eye movements, breathing and loose hair strands.

21 to 25 seconds. Another friend enters from the side and briefly fills the frame. Cut to a blue spotlight through club haze catching a wrist stacked with reflective bracelets. Film from a low tilted angle as bodies cross the beam. Use realistic volumetric light and soft highlight bloom.

25 to 30 seconds. Continue with matching candid footage. Return to a wider crowded dance floor view, then move back into the woman and two friends for a final loose group pose. They laugh, sway and lightly bump the camera. Let a brief red light sweep cross one face, then return to deep blue. Finish with the camera dipping as someone passes close to the lens, fading naturally to black in the final second.

Keep the camera handheld and human, with small wrist shakes, accidental reframing, rolling shutter, motion smear, brief autofocus hunting and lens occlusion. Use a slightly wide consumer camcorder view, CCD style highlight bloom, mild chroma bleed, fine sensor noise, soft detail, crushed blacks and blue violet club color. Skin stays natural. Avoid warped hands, duplicated jewelry, face morphing, floating objects and synthetic smoothness.

Music and sound. Use a moody bass driven club instrumental around 100 BPM with warm sub bass, restrained kick, crisp closed hats, sparse dark synth tones and a subtle nostalgic R and B feel. Blend muffled crowd chatter, distant laughter, room reverb, clothing movement and slight camera handling noise. Keep music continuous and cuts loosely on the beat.

entries.prompt:
WORLD:
A quiet residential neighborhood at night with a warm, nostalgic atmosphere. A young man steps out for a late-night snack and slowly walks home through familiar streets. He buys food, sits outside for a while, encounters a small everyday moment, and continues home. The world feels ordinary, lived-in, nostalgic, and real.
CHARACTER:
Young man, early 20s, natural appearance, slightly messy dark hair, subtle stubble. Wearing a faded grey T-shirt, loose dark trousers, worn sneakers, and a simple wristwatch. Tired but relaxed. Signature gesture: runs his fingers through his hair when thinking.
Keep his face, identity, hairstyle, clothing, and proportions consistent.
STYLE:
Raw handheld personal-video footage. Natural camera shake, imperfect framing, autofocus hunting, exposure shifts between bright shop lights and dark streets, soft details, mild digital noise, muted colors, slight motion blur, and realistic low-light imperfections.

Action: he fires the final arc of orange spray onto a huge abstract mural and tosses the can high into the air; the camera rises with the tumbling can, and at the top of its arc, without the flight ever pausing, the can becomes an orange basketball that falls into the dusk of a rooftop court where he catches it, board under his arm; he dribbles once and shoots, the ball spinning off the rim toward the lens; the camera closes in until the spinning pebbled surface dominates the frame, and without the spin ever stopping it becomes a spinning vinyl record; the camera pulls back to reveal the graffiti-covered underpass, his hand on the record; he scratches, the soundtrack bending under his fingers, and the orange glare on the groove stretches into a streak of light; without the stretching ever stopping, the streak becomes the lengthening shower of orange sparks from his skateboard grinding a metal rail; the camera pulls back along the spark trail into the night skatepark, he pops off the rail, rolls out and stops in a held pose under the sodium floodlights.
Camera: a low tracking shot beside him at the mural; a rise following the tossed can that turns into a fall following the ball; a slow arc as he shoots; a push into the spinning ball that becomes a pull-back from the spinning vinyl; a locked shot on his scratching hand; a push along the stretching light streak that becomes a pull-back along the spark trail; a tracking settle as he rolls to a stop; no hard cuts anywhere, every scene change happens at the closest point of one continuous camera breath.
Timing: 0-3s: golden hour, the final arc of spray on the mural, he tosses the can up; 3-7s: the can tumbles through the air and at the apex of its arc becomes the falling basketball, caught on the rooftop court; 7-9s: one dribble and the shot, the ball spinning off the rim toward the lens; 9-12s: the spinning ball fills the frame and, never stopping its spin, becomes the spinning vinyl, the camera pulling back into the underpass; 12-14s: his hand scratches the record, the music bends, the orange glare on the groove begins to stretch; 14-17s: the stretching streak of light becomes the lengthening shower of sparks from his board grinding the rail, the camera pulling back along it; 17-20s: night skatepark, he pops off the rail, rolls out with an ease-out and holds a still pose for the final two seconds.
Audio: (a boom-bap hip-hop instrumental running through the whole film, a hard snare hit exactly on each body swap; when he scratches, the soundtrack itself bends, revealing it was his record all along); <spray can hiss>, <the rattle of the tumbling can>, <a slap as he catches the ball>, <the ring of the rim>, <vinyl scratch>, <crackling grind sparks>, <a clean snap as he lands off the rail>, then the beat falls away to quiet night city hum for the held pose; no dialogue.
Constraints: the flight never pauses while the can becomes the ball; the spin never stops while the ball becomes the record; the stretching never stops while the light streak becomes the sparks; no cuts, no wipes, no occlusion transitions, no whip pans, no fades, no cross dissolves, no random morphing; the same single young man in every scene with identical orange hoodie, backwards black cap and skateboard, exactly two arms and two hands, no other people anywhere; all graffiti is abstract shapes with no readable letters or words; no brand logos; no on-screen text, no subtitles.

Create a trendy, ultra-realistic 30-second fashion reel in true 16:9 landscape, featuring a stylish Gen Z female influencer demonstrating 10 ways to style the same oversized pastel-yellow button-up shirt.

Opening — 0–3s: In a bright, minimalist luxury apartment, she holds the shirt on a hanger, looks directly into the camera, smiles naturally, and clearly says: “One shirt, ten ways to style.” Show matching on-screen text: “1 Shirt 🤍 10 Ways to Style.” Her spoken words must be accurate, natural, clearly audible, and perfectly synchronized with her lip movements.

Main Montage — 3–27s: Use energetic whip pans, spin transitions, snap cuts, and match cuts to quickly showcase:

1. Casual Chic — open over a white crop top with wide-leg jeans.
2. Front Knot — tied at the waist with denim.
3. Off Shoulder — relaxed styling with sunglasses.
4. Tucked In — tucked into tailored white trousers with a belt.

10. Monochrome Minimal — buttoned with cream wide-leg trousers.

Include confident walking, posing, spinning, adjusting the collar and sleeves, fixing sunglasses, holding coffee, checking the mirror, and natural smiling. Mix full-body, medium, and detailed close-up shots.

Look & Camera: Bright natural daylight, warm minimalist interiors, luxury Pinterest aesthetic, cinematic handheld movement, shallow depth of field, realistic fabric physics, natural hair and skin movement, premium editorial fashion photography, smooth transitions, ultra-realistic 4K HDR.

Ending — 27–30s: Finish with a rapid, elegant reveal of all 10 looks surrounding the final outfit. On-screen text: “10 Looks. 1 Shirt. 🤍 Which one’s your favorite?”

No additional dialogue or narration after the opening line. Keep the pacing polished, fashionable, energetic, and suitable for a viral Instagram reel.
