Image 1 is the before state, Image 2 the after state. In 2.5 reference terms: one role per image, with 【Event Script】 start state → trigger → end state, twice.

Community, long ad continuity (PRP-048): a CONTINUITY block before the scenes fixes the hero object's exact geometry and counts (four vapour jets, a plate reading "RDSTR", yoke steering). A FINAL DIRECTIVE at the end ("Do not omit, repeat, or extend scenes") stops 7-scene scripts from merging or looping. Output check: a miniature-store prompt that named no brands still showed real snack branding on packages (PRP-049), so review prop close-ups for brands, as with MOO-052.

sections.title: 2026-10-25 additions: screen-direction continuity locks, prop scale written against the character, one-take cause-and-effect rules

items.text: Re-checked 2026-10-25 (about 6 AM PT): the BytePlus Seedance 2.5 prompt guide (.md md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 3ea0e876…) are unchanged, and the sd25-pe skill is still v0.1.1 (agent-skills index byte-identical, Last-Modified 2026-09-28; read only, not installed or run). The tutorial still lists 4K (10-bit) only under Seedance 2.0, so 4K for 2.5 remains unconfirmed in the official API docs. No new official material this run.

Community, screen-direction continuity lock (CAM-116): before any beats, a "CONTINUITY LOCK (MANDATORY)" block says the chase always moves LEFT to RIGHT of frame, the pursuer is always behind (left of) and above, "no teleporting. Every change of position is shown on screen in continuous motion", and "fewer, longer shots" with motivated tracking / drone-follow / push-in moves instead of random angle jumps. It also lists the only states the rider can be in (on the bridge, falling, seated) and requires the transitions between them to be shown. This adds screen direction to the 2026-10-21 staging lock; in sd25-pe terms, state the direction once and then repeat LEFT/RIGHT inside each timed beat.

Community, prop scale written against the character (PRP-050): every prop is sized relative to the hero ("approximately the same height as Milo's torso and head combined", bark "approximately twice Milo's body length", a doorway "visibly smaller than the giant apple"), its physical limits are stated ("far too heavy for him to lift but round enough that he can roll it"), and its history is fixed ("already detached before the story begins, and Milo never tears it from a tree"). The punchline (apple too big for the door) is set up by these sizes. The character sheet is scoped as "defines Milo's appearance only". The sound plan gives each contact its own cue (bark scraping, low roll, soft thud, leaf poof).

Community, one-take cause and effect (REA-056): a 30 s in-car phone video with no cuts, eight timed beats where each one causes the next (gate opens → melons roll → catch → crack → chain reaction → launch → landing), and a closing REALISM RULES block: "continuous physical cause and effect", real gravity, momentum and object weight, no teleportation, duplicated people, disappearing objects or impossible trajectories, and "keep the comedy non-graphic and injury-free". Phone artefacts (windshield raindrops, autofocus hunting, imperfect digital zoom) are written as camera behaviour. Compare the 2026-10-24 home-video notes (GRN-042).

sections.title: 2026-10-26 additions: chaining parts through a described held frame, cut points separate from beats, complete object handling

items.text: Re-checked 2026-10-26 (about 6 AM PT): the BytePlus Seedance 2.5 prompt guide (.md md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 3ea0e876…) are unchanged, and the sd25-pe skill is still v0.1.1 (agent-skills index Last-Modified 2026-09-28; read only, not installed or run). The tutorial still lists 4K (10-bit) only under Seedance 2.0. No new official material this run.

Community, multi-part chaining through a described held frame (REA-057): each 30 s part ends with "Final held frame (last second):" followed by a full description of that frame (pose, positions, light, camera height). The next part repeats the full style and character block and opens with "CONTINUITY: the video begins EXACTLY on the image [@startframe], same framing, same lighting, same position of Haruto and the Grey Coat Man in the fog … continue seamlessly from that frame as if the camera never stopped". Writing the end frame out in Part N gives the creator the exact still to extract and attach as the first frame of Part N+1. In official terms this is a first-frame task for each later part (ratio adaptive), with the character references carried over unchanged.

Community, cut points separate from choreography beats (TRN-055): a 15 s fight is written second by second, but the creator adds "Use motivated cuts around 2, 4, 7, 10, and 13 seconds. The one-second intervals describe choreography beats, not mandatory cuts." This stops dense one-second timecodes from being read as a cut every second. The same prompt replaces sparks with readable physical contact ("Show weapon contact through physical recoil, brief camera vibration, metallic sound, and a small cool-white daylight reflection confined to the contacting metal surfaces") and ties every effect to a cause ("Every destruction event follows visible contact, a collision, a rebound, or falling debris").

Community, complete object handling (GRN-046): before the scenes, an "IMPORTANT VIDEO INSTRUCTION" says "Every interaction must show the complete physical action clearly. Do not skip object handling." Each purchase is then written as a chain of hand actions (reach, pick up, hold, pay, receive change, carry). This targets objects that appear in or vanish from a hand between beats. It pairs with the 2026-10-25 cause-and-effect rules (REA-056).

sections.title: 2026-10-28 additions: Draft IDs now kept 14 days, storyboard-as-reference, expression arcs, reference isolation, motion transfer

items.text: Re-checked 2026-10-28 (about 6 AM PT): the BytePlus Seedance 2.5 API tutorial CHANGED (md5 now 2457c16c…, was 3ea0e876… on 2026-10-26). The change is to task retention: Draft task IDs created at or after Oct 28, 2026 10:00 (UTC+8), which is Oct 27, 7:00 PM PDT, are now valid for 14 days; older Draft task IDs stay at 7 days, and all other task IDs are kept 7 days. In practice, a Draft preview made today can be turned into a final render up to two weeks later. The prompt guide (.md md5 40fd6d36…) is unchanged, sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run), and 4K (10-bit) is still listed only under Seedance 2.0.

Community, storyboard as reference only (REA-060): a first frame plus a 16-panel storyboard grid, with the instruction that the storyboard is "only a visual reference" and the video must not recreate the 16-panel layout. It worked here even though the official guide caps storyboards at 15 panels (one sample only; stay at 15 or fewer to be safe). This matches the official "use only as shot guidance" wording already in this guide.

Community, expression arcs (PRF-067): every spoken line in a vlog is given a before, a during and an after expression, and the last beat is "Final Frame (hold exactly)". Writing the reaction after each line stops faces from going blank between lines, and the held final frame gives a clean end for chaining or extending.

Community, reference isolation (AES-058): with character references taken from different photos, the creator adds "Do not inherit reference backgrounds or poses", so only identity and costume carry over and the scene comes from the text. Add this whenever reference photos have busy settings.

Community, ordered continuity list (TRN-056): after the timed scenes, a "Strict Continuity and Physics" list fixes the order of the physical beats ("The first apple MUST strike the TOP OF HER HEAD before falling onto the grass"; it must bounce, land, "and only then be picked up"; "Never let the apple fall into her lap or skip the head-impact sequence") and says the golden effects build progressively. Naming the forbidden shortcut stops a causal gag from being skipped or merged.

Community, one-take crash zoom (CAM-127): a single continuous shot from orbit down to street level, written as timed stages of one camera move (orbit, crash zoom through the clouds, descent to a cobblestone intersection, swoop to settle in front of four walkers) with "Absolutely no cuts, stutters, or interruptions", and each walker gets a left-to-right stop action ending in the pose from Image 1. In official terms: one camera move with its start, direction and arrival all written out.

Community, one-line motion transfer (guide note, not an entry): "Apply the source video1 motion to the character in the reference image1, keeping their clothing, the framing and the timing." This is the same short video-reference pattern already noted for Runway; in Seedance 2.5 write it as a reference task with Video 1 for motion and Image 1 for the character.

Cross-model notes worth borrowing: Grok Imagine "viewfinder" (CAM-126): orbit slowly around a still insert to find the angle, then extend with "keeps moving quickly to complete the 180". Wan 3.0 Prime (MOO-056): the light, not the subject, moves second by second over a held pose. Both translate directly to Seedance 2.5 first-frame tasks (see the adapted templates on those entries).

sections.title: 2026-10-29 additions: style on reference assets for long projects, motion cues through dialogue, chained one-take parts, frozen-scene camera travel, ordered transformations

items.text: Re-checked 2026-10-29 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…, which includes yesterday's 14-day Draft ID change) are byte-identical to 2026-10-28. The agent-skills index is byte-identical, sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run), and 4K (10-bit) is still listed only under Seedance 2.0. The Runway help-center articles for Seedance 2.5 and 2.0 have not been updated since Oct 13 and Oct 15, 2026.

Community, where the style should live (GRN-047): a full Super 16mm style paragraph (organic grain "that changes frame to frame", gate weave, lifted textured shadows, warm halation, a 32mm spherical prime at about T1.5 with circular ghosts "not horizontal anamorphic streaks", and a closing palette of wardrobe colours) is enough for one shot or a few. The creator's rule for long projects is to "put the style on your reference assets first", so every shot inherits the look from the images rather than from re-typed text that drifts. This fits the official reference-task pattern: generate the styled references once, then bind them as Image N in every shot.

Community, keep a vehicle moving while people talk (REA-061): in-car dialogue tends to freeze the car. The fix is a dedicated VISIBLE CAR MOVEMENT block of concrete cues (fence posts with near/far parallax, the road receding in the rear window, reflections sliding over the windshield, bands of sunlight crossing faces, a trembling mirror) plus "Maintain these movement cues throughout every line of dialogue" and "Keep the car visibly traveling forward for the entire 15 seconds, including the final reaction".

Community, long action in chained one-take parts (PRF-068): a 45 s fight split into a 30 s and a 15 s part, each "ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE | NO CUTS BETWEEN BEATS" with 5 s (then 3 s) beats. Part 1 ends on a written [FINAL FRAME LOCK] that describes the exact end pose, and Part 2 opens with a [START-FRAME LOCK] repeating it, so the second generation (or an extend task) picks up without a jump. One prop drives all the choreography, and the exclusions name the shortcuts to avoid (no weapon switching, no second umbrella, no smoke teleport, no gore).

Community, wardrobe that changes by era but identity that does not (TRN-058): the identity lock says "Their clothing may change naturally between present and past, but…" the faces stay exact. Without that sentence a strict identity/outfit lock forces flashbacks into present-day clothes; with it, the costume change becomes the time cue.

Cross-model notes worth borrowing: Grok Imagine "frozen diorama" (CAM-134): first frame is a painting, then an explicit exclusion list ("No person, animal, object, water, foliage, cloud, flame… moves, animates, or changes state") so that only the camera travels. Hailuo H3 casting tape (PRF-069): performance written as an actor's brief (Objective, Obstacle, Tactic, Subtext, Voice recipe) with a timed peak where the laugh stops "MID-NOTE" into two seconds of silence. fal LTX-2.5 (TRN-057): a start + end frame transformation written in order ("the chandeliers come up one at a time from the far end of the room toward the camera… The parquet gains its polish last"), with the end frame made as an edit of the start frame at identical dimensions. All three translate to Seedance 2.5 first-frame or first/last-frame tasks (see the adapted templates on those entries).

sections.title: 2026-10-30 additions: one timed camera move per slot, stopping points, speed clauses, reference roles and thresholds (from Pika H3 Flex), DV camcorder look, silence as a beat, costume locks

items.text: Re-checked 2026-10-30 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…) are byte-identical to 2026-10-29; the agent-skills index is byte-identical and sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run). Everything below is community or cross-model practice, not an official Seedance change.

Cross-model, from the new open-weight Pika H3 Flex (released 2026-10-29, built on MiniMax H3) official prompt guide and showcases. These map cleanly onto Seedance 2.5 prompts: (1) one camera move per timed slot, each with a start and an arrival ("a smooth crane straight down from overhead to table height, ending right beside the net", CAM-138); (2) always give the camera a stopping point and a final hold, because amplitude words are only advisory and timing can drift by about 0.2-0.3 s; (3) a push-in is not a zoom, so say which one you mean; (4) "wide shot" alone tends to render as a medium shot, so describe what is in the frame instead of only naming the size; (5) give actions an endpoint ("place the spoon on the saucer and release it") and name who owns each step of a handoff. Points (2) and (4) come from the ComfyUI team's testing notes on the released adapters; the rest are from Pika's own guide.

Cross-model, speed clause (CAM-138): "SPEED IS CRITICAL: everything moves at normal real-time speed, like 24fps footage played back at 24fps - natural motion, NO slow motion." Busy action with many camera moves often drifts into slow motion; one explicit speed sentence is cheaper than re-rolls. Put sound and music on separate lines ("Sound: …" then "Music: …"), which is close to the official Seedance split between sound effects and background music.

Cross-model, reference roles (PRF-070, CAM-140): give every reference one job and say what NOT to take from it. Pika uses a character sheet for appearance only, "without the sheet panels, labels or alternative views", an environment image, and a motion video with "Take NOTHING else from @Video1 - not the person's face, body, clothes, props, location, background, colours or photographic look"; it marks each reference fully_preserved / attribute_transfer / weak_reference / removed. In Seedance 2.5 write the same roles in words against @image1 / @video1 (reference_image / reference_video). This is the same idea as the 2026-10-28 motion-transfer note, now with official wording from a second model.

Cross-model, thresholds in one move (CAM-140): when the camera travels from exterior to interior without a cut, write the threshold as its own beat ("the frame goes black for a beat at the threshold, and the hangar lights come up in rows from the far end toward the lens") and change the sound there (outside near-silence → rushing air → hangar hum; the music drops out at the threshold and returns). The sound change sells the single continuous move.

Community, DV camcorder look as a checklist (GRN-049): "Authentic handheld early 2000s consumer DV camcorder footage" followed by a short list (natural handheld shake, imperfect framing, autofocus breathing and focus hunting, slight auto-exposure fluctuation, soft digital detail, faded washed-out colour, subtle digital noise, natural motion blur, "occasional accidental zooming") and a hard negative line ("Absolutely no gimbal shots, drone footage, stabilized camera movements, slow motion, beauty filters, or polished cinematic aesthetics"). The person filming is written as a character ("a friend casually recording"), so the subjects can react to the camera.

Community, silence as the turn (MOO-062): the story beat is a sound change: "The music suddenly stops. Complete silence. The woman pauses naturally…" before the reveal. Writing the silence explicitly in its own time slot gives Seedance's native audio a clear cue and makes the reaction land. Pair it with "No exaggerated acting".

Community, gesture-triggered cuts (TRN-061): each set change is caused by an on-screen action (she tosses a pumpkin, snaps, claps) followed by "FLASH CUT TO …", and the climax is "Three rapid flash cuts: pumpkin studio, witch's parlor, haunted party". Tying each cut to a gesture keeps a fast commercial readable.

Community, doubles and costume locks (MOO-063, WRD-053): two versions of the same woman are kept apart purely by costume colour ("a woman in black" vs "another version of herself in ivory white"), and each later beat names her by colour. For a single character, a costume-lock negative list ("no identity drift, no face morphing, no costume changes, no missing witch hat") protects the outfit across scenes, which is useful when the wardrobe is the point of the shot.

sections.title: 2026-10-31 additions: Runway prompt-length limits, ghost-camera FPV rules, "Appearance only" reference blocks, final-frame extensions, lens-occlusion match cuts, prop/staging locks, segment chaining

items.text: Re-checked 2026-10-31 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…) are byte-identical to 2026-10-30; sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 in the agent-skills index (read only, not installed or run). 4K is still listed only for Seedance 2.0, not 2.5. Everything below is community, platform or cross-model practice, not an official Seedance change.

Platform limit (Runway, updated 2026-10-30): Seedance 2.5 on Runway now states a maximum prompt length of 15,000 characters (Seedance 2.0 / 2.0 Fast / 2.0 Mini: 10,000), and the 2.0 article's FAQ adds that the limit is counted in characters, not words. The longest community prompt added today (PRP-056, about 13,400 characters) fits under the 2.5 limit but not the 2.0 one. Other hosts may differ, so check before pasting a very long prompt.

Community, "ghost camera" FPV (CAM-143): write the camera as a set of rules rather than a list of moves: it is invisible (no drone, shadow, reflection or prop wash), stays low over the water, changes altitude only once, "NEVER reverses or plays backward", and allows "NO slow motion except one half-second beat at the reveal, then an instant snap back to full speed". Then give the route as a sequence of passes ending on the reveal. Rationing slow motion to one named beat stops a busy 30 s take from drifting into slow motion throughout.

Community, reference blocks with one job each (PRF-073): open with one named block per reference (Girl, Attackers, Passengers, Planeext, Planeint), each ending "Appearance only." or "Environment only.", then SCENE, TECHNICAL, timed CUTS and RULES. It is the same idea as the 2026-10-30 reference-roles note, in a shorter form that is easy to copy. The RULES line "Action is intense but not gory — no blood or graphic wounds, impacts sold through motion and body mechanics" keeps a fight readable without gore.

Community, extending a finished clip (TRN-062): give the earlier video as @video1, write the timeline so that one beat must "End exactly on the original video's final frame" and the next must "Continue directly from @video1", and close with a CONTINUITY block ("Preserve protagonist identity, wardrobe, props… End at exactly 45.0 seconds"). Cross-model version (PRF-074, Pika H3 Flex): chain 15 s segments by adding the last frame of the previous segment as an extra reference marked as the first frame of the new shot.

Community, lens-occlusion match cut (TRN-063): tie the one transition to a physical event: "At the exact moment her shoulder covers the camera lens, create a seamless action-match cut". Split the two worlds by grade (cold and desaturated vs warm golden hour) and repeat the cut instruction under a "MOST IMPORTANT" heading.

Community, prop and staging locks for long multi-part prompts (PRP-056): after the character and location sheets, a PROP LOCKS block says where every object is and stays ("helmet carried in his RIGHT hand… set at his LEFT elbow and it stays there"; "NO food appears in Part 1"), and a STAGING LOCK fixes left/right geography. Writing which hand and which side is what stops objects drifting between cuts and between parts.

Community, period film look in a few words (GRN-050): "35mm technicolor dye-transfer, 2.35:1 anamorphic", named saturated colours, "soft highlight bloom, visible fine grain" and a diffusion filter only on one character's close-ups, together with mostly static cuts and a period score that "cut[s] to total silence at 21s". Keeping the camera static is part of the look.

Model comparison (AES-066): the new Wan 2.2-based Mischief-1 (image-to-video, 720p, 5 s, no audio according to the poster) was run on one short prompt next to Wan 2.2, MiniMax H3 Max and Seedance 2.5. The poster's verdict is that H3 Max follows the prompt slightly better and Seedance 2.5 has the best overall quality. This is one creator's single test, not a benchmark.

sections.title: 2026-11-01 additions: Edit-mode templates for selective edits, camcorder-flaw checklists, labelled hard cuts, locked look/wardrobe/lighting blocks, exact object counts, one-take stress-test phrasing

items.text: Re-checked 2026-11-01 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…) are byte-identical to 2026-10-31; sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 and sd2-pe v0.1.0 in the agent-skills index (read only, not installed or run). Runway's two Seedance articles still show their 2026-10-30 update. Everything below is community, platform or cross-model practice, not an official Seedance change.

Applying the official Edit mode to selective edits (PRP-058, WRD-058 templates): Pika's deep-dive edit showcases ("Keep… Change only three things", numbered) map directly onto the official Seedance 2.5 Edit task: give the clip as content.role reference_video, set ratio to adaptive and duration to -1, include an explicit editing trigger ("edit", "replace", "change to", "add"), and say what to keep before the numbered changes. The official FAQ says source videos under 20 s are more stable. A useful pattern from these prompts is motion inheritance: the replacement object "rolls exactly as the red ball rolls in @Video1", and the new background figures react "exactly when" the old ones did.

Community, camcorder flaws as the look (GRN-053): instead of "DV look", list the defects (operator mistakes, subject near the frame edges, partial face crops, autofocus failure and focus hunting, lens breathing, exposure pumping, slight rolling shutter, washed-out colour, faded blacks, video noise, mild compression artifacts), move the light through the day across timed beats, and end with "Recording cuts to black abruptly like a real camcorder clip". Back it with a short stack of "ABSOLUTELY NO …" lines (posing, stabilization, modern grading, music).

Community, label each hard cut with what has to change (GRN-054): an IMPORTANT EDITING DIRECTION paragraph forbids reusing angles, framings and entrances, and each cut is written as "HARD CUT TO A NEW CAMERA POSITION", "HARD CUT TO A WIDER FRAME" or "HARD CUT TO A TIGHTER SHOT". In a fast multi-candidate sequence this keeps consecutive shots from repeating the same set-up.

Community, styling as three locked blocks (WRD-060): after one identity line ("the only identity source… Do not redesign or beautify her"), split styling into "Look (locked)" (hair, headpiece, jewellery, make-up), "Wardrobe (locked)" (fabric, colour, embroidery, collar, sleeves; "Full-body shots continue the same robe. No outfit changes.") and "Lighting (locked)" (key, rim, background colour, banned light types). A similar labelled format from @techhalla (text only; no output collected) names each reference by role, such as [image_1_initial_frame], and adds a "CAST + PROPS — LOCKED" block that counts every person and object ("one beer can, one landing net").

Community, exact counts for prop handling (PRP-060): "picks exactly one green olive from a dish containing three olives" plus beats timed to a tenth of a second (0.5-2.1 s, 2.1-4.7 s…) and a negative prompt that lists the likely failures (human hands, extra paws, duplicated objects, floating liquid, disappearing olives). Saying how many there are and how many get used is easier to check than "an olive".

Cross-model, one-take phrasing (CAM-144, CAM-145; Vivix W1 and Flux 3 Max): the Vivix W1 docs advise adding "one continuous shot" when you do not want cuts and moving the action on with first / then / finally. The Flux 3 Max tests go further with spatial rules: "No cuts, no dissolves, no morphing between spaces, consistent architecture and lighting logic through every transition, correct parallax and scale", with each space entered through a physical opening (keyhole, window, over a wall). The same wording works in a Seedance 2.5 text-to-video prompt, as in the adapted templates.

Cross-model, write constraints as positive facts (REA-063, TRN-064; Flux 3 Max): "Five fingers on each hand, anatomically correct… Hands never merge, fingers never multiply, tools stay rigid and consistent" and "Each stage must be clearly readable and physically motivated: paper, particles, feathers" state what must hold rather than listing artefacts to avoid. The creator presents these as single unselected takes, so they show phrasing that held at least once, not a benchmark.

Cross-model, prompt rewriting on Mischief 1 (PRP-059): the fal API has prompt_processing "original" (render the prompt as typed) or "enhanced" (rewrite it against the start image and clip length first, falling back to the typed prompt if the rewrite fails). The seed fixes only the render, so use "original" for reproducible results. The schema also says "Long, specific prompts steer WAN best" (2,000-character limit). Seedance 2.5 has no such switch in the official API; the official sd25-pe skill is the equivalent rewrite step, run outside the request.

Pika note: the Pika H3 Flex blog slugs are /blog/pika-h3-flex (launch post) and /blog/pika-h3-flex-research (technical deep dive with full prompts). The launch post says Flex comes to the hosted Pika product on November 2, so it was not live at the time of this run.

sections.title: 2026-11-02 additions: Pika H3 Flex live rules, no-camera-in-frame DV vlogs, per-reference jurisdiction, model-designed titles, matte-only lockups, native-output clauses, Edit @Video1 swaps

items.text: Re-checked 2026-11-02 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…) are byte-identical to 2026-11-01. The agent-skills index was re-published (Last-Modified 5:44 AM PT on Nov 2), but the only addition is ark-docs-reader 0.1.6, a docs-lookup skill rather than a video skill; sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run). Runway's Seedance 2.5 article shows a new updated_at (6:28 AM PT on Nov 1), but its body is unchanged and edited_at is still 2026-10-30. Note for adapted templates: the official tutorial allows 4-30 s output (or -1 for auto) on Seedance 2.5, against 4-15 s on the 2.0 series, so 30 s one-take sources can be adapted at full length.

Pika H3 Flex is live in the hosted Pika product (app card status "live", badge NEW), but no published prompt examples yet. Its documented rules: the attachments decide the route (none = text-to-video, exactly one image = first frame, anything more = an ordered reference set); up to 9 images, 3 clips and 3 audio tracks (12 in all), clips 2-15 s each and at most 15 s combined per kind; audio-only reference sets are held back; output any whole second from 5 to 15 s; the FAQ lists 480p or 768p while the feature card says "from 480 to 4K" with a draft mode; aspect 21:9 to 9:21 or Auto; native audio on every route with Dialogue / Music / Effect stems; "a 15-second clip with its full soundtrack… in as little as 7 seconds". In the Pika editor each attached reference is called by its @mention (@Image1, @Video1), the same convention used in every discover prompt below.

Community, never show the recording device (GRN-056, GRN-057): self-shot DV vlogs on Seedance 2.5 add an "ABSOLUTE RULE: no camera, camcorder, phone or recording device of any kind ever appears anywhere in the frame, in anyone's hands, on any surface, or in any reflection." The transition to hands-free is then written as picture behaviour, not an action: "do NOT show her putting anything down: instead the IMAGE ITSELF tips, swings down and settles at a wonky low angle on a surface", and switches to fixed angles use "a clean jump cut as if the camera had already been positioned". This fixes the common failure where the model draws the camcorder into a selfie shot.

Community, give every reference its own jurisdiction (WRD-062, PRP-064, PRP-065; PRP-067 cross-model): "Strictly separate the functions of the reference images" and then one line per @Image saying what it, and only it, defines (identity and make-up; headpiece; wardrobe; location; product). The product reference is fenced with "This is the only product design authority", and its colour rules are stated as invariants ("The rectangular bottle body always remains glacier blue; tomato red is restricted to the small circular atomizer only"). This is the official content.role reference_image mapping written out as a contract.

Community, let Seedance design the title (PRP-064): with "deliberately NO title-card, typography, logo or graphic image reference attached", the prompt says "Seedance itself must design and render the final title from the written typography direction below" and then describes the wordmark in words (style, lines, placement). The output shows a clean, correctly spelled end title generated in-shot, an alternative to supplying a type reference.

Community, supply type as a matte only (PRP-065): when a lockup image is attached as white type on black, "Take ONLY the letterforms from it and SUPERIMPOSE them over the live final shot… The black is a matte and is never reproduced: the film does not cut to a black card". A closing [Text law] block then limits on-screen words to "the exact strings named above", spelled exactly, with no other lettering. The same prompt gives the hero prop a "story state" (a box "almost empty, with exactly ONE chocolate left in its paper case") so the prop carries the plot.

Community, a native-output clause (PRP-063, PRP-064, WRD-065): several 30 s Seedance 2.5 ads end with "One untouched native 30-second Seedance output with native score and foley: no edit, trim, concat, overlay, reframing, stabilization, colour correction… Any defect requires a complete native reroll." It is a creator declaration that the posted clip is unedited, not a model parameter, but it doubles as an instruction for complete, self-contained endings (title, score and Foley generated together).

Community, Edit @Video1 performance swaps (PRF-078): on Pika's Seedance 2.5 route the prompt opens "Edit @Video1. Change the character to the character shown in @Image1. Rebuild the entire environment as the location shown in @Image2" and closes with a keep-list: "Do not change: the motion and blocking, the camera movement and framing, the performance, timing, expressions and lip-sync, the pacing and cuts, or the original audio." This matches the official Edit task (explicit edit trigger, say what stays); via the API use content.role reference_video with ratio adaptive and duration -1.

Community, broadcast-format realism without a film look (GRN-060, REA-065): @abulu8's archived 2003 reality-TV prompt (Seedance 2.5 in PixVerse) asks for 4:3 interlaced SD and ends "No gimbal smoothness, no stabilisation, no film look, no shallow depth of field, no modern colour grade", which keeps the MiniDV texture from drifting cinematic. @Zyvex_0x puts realism in its own REALISM block ("real live-action footage… real actors, real light and practical effects. Not 3D, not CGI, not animation") ahead of 8 timed shots in 15 s, each with camera height, distance and screen side.

Cross-model, a style "contract" for painted animation (AES-067; Wan 3.0 on Pika): "ART STYLE — hold this exactly in every frame, it is the contract" plus a separate, "equally binding" ANIMATION STYLE block: on twos at 12 fps, "the whole image BOILS", "Do NOT smooth, interpolate, stabilise or motion-blur between frames". Splitting look and motion into two binding blocks carries over to Seedance 2.5 (see the adapted template).

sections.title: 2026-11-03 additions: Change-the-camera-only edits, motion-only transfer, lip-sync audio lock, counted gestures with paired sounds, period production documents, one-second beats, product-physics rules

items.text: Re-checked 2026-11-03 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…) are byte-identical to 2026-11-02; the agent-skills index still lists sd25-pe v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run); the Runway Seedance 2.5 article body is unchanged.

Community, re-shoot with only the camera changed (CAM-147, CAM-148): Pika's "camera-director" app on Seedance 2.5 writes a fixed four-part edit prompt. (1) "Edit @Video1. Change the camera only:" plus the framing (extreme wide; full-body wide "with enough surrounding space to contain their entire original movement path"). (2) "Camera position:" (natural eye level; stationary tripod). (3) The movement ("Locked off… absolutely ZERO camera movement"; "no tracking, panning, tilting, zooming, reframing, or stabilization drift… Do not alter their path to keep them centered"). (4) "Apply ONE single camera setup to the ENTIRE video: every shot and every cut must be reshot… Do not retain the original framing", then a keep-list: "Do not change: the subject's performance, timing, expressions and blocking, their wardrobe and identity, the environment, the lighting… or the original audio." This is the official Edit task (reference_video, ratio adaptive, duration -1) used as a camera-only re-shoot; the slot structure reuses well for any framing, position or move.

Community, motion-only transfer (PRF-079): "@Video1 defines ONLY the body movement and its timing: copy that exact movement sequence (she raises both arms out to the sides, turns a full circle on the spot, steps forward once, and finishes with a wide wave of her right hand). Do not copy the man, his clothes or the white studio from @Video1." Writing the movement out in words and excluding the source performer, wardrobe and set by name keeps identity coming from @Image1; camera and sound get their own short lines ("full-body wide shot, static"; "No dialogue. No music.").

Community, lip sync to supplied audio (Flora workflow): connect the character image, background and song to a Seedance 2.5 node and include "Preserve the audio and music exactly" plus the song's lyrics in the prompt. Via the API this is a reference_audio with the lyrics written in the prompt as the line to be sung.

Community, counted gestures, each with its own sound (WRD-066): "The RIGHT hand performs exactly two right-to-left swipes, followed by one forward selection tap" and "The LEFT hand… never triggers an outfit change"; then the sound list mirrors the counts: "Two short directional whooshes for the two swipes. One precise selection tick for the forward tap… No constant whooshing." Pairing an exact action count with an exact sound count keeps generated audio from smearing across the clip.

Community, a period film written as a production document (GRN-061): a heading line ("1978 soviet science fiction film… practical model effects"), "characters, fixed for the whole film", "geography, fixed for the whole film" (hatch with the porthole "right next to it, on its right"), timed static cuts, an audio block where the score "stops completely at 16s", a style block ("35mm soviet svema color negative film, 1.66:1 frame… heavy grain, slight gate weave… faintly visible support wires") and a constraints block ("no readable text, no letters, no cyrillic, no flags… no morphing gloves"). The ban on readable text and script is a simple way to keep period props from producing garbled lettering.

Community, one-second beats (MOO-065): a 30 s drama listed as [0-1s] … [1-2s] … with one shot type and one action per second (hard cut, extreme close-up, side-tracking, through the glass), after a CHARACTER LOCK paragraph. Very dense beats work for montage-style emotional peaks; the creator saves slow motion "only on the embrace and kiss".

Community, product-physics rules for realistic ads (REA-066): the fictional product is explained as a mechanism ("The dock receives household electricity, while the lamp itself has no visible cable… continues operating from its built-in rechargeable battery") and pinned with invariants ("The lamp never moves, disconnects, breaks or changes position"; "Characters must physically move between locations; no sudden appearances or disappearances"), with "Use exactly three fictional Korean adults" and "never like an AI demonstration". Stating cause and effect stops the model from inventing how the product works.

sections.title: 2026-11-04 additions: storyboard grid as a shot-order reference, seamless loop seams, foreground-object wipes for first/last frame, one-hue palettes with bookend frames

items.text: Re-checked 2026-11-04 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…) are byte-identical to 2026-11-03; the agent-skills index (Last-Modified 2026-11-02, content unchanged) still lists sd25-pe v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run); the Runway Seedance 2.5 article body is unchanged.

Community, a storyboard grid as an ordered shot list (GRN-062): upload a 3×3 storyboard image as a reference and say what it is for: "The storyboard is a sequence reference. Do NOT reproduce the 3×3 grid in the output. Generate a continuous video with individual full-frame scenes, following the storyboard's order." Then repeat it in the negatives ("No split screens or storyboard grids"). Pair it with timed scene headings that match the panels, 3–4 s each. In the official API this is a reference_image whose role is spelled out in the prompt; without that line, grid references tend to come back as split screens.

Community, camcorder realism as a list of operator faults (GRN-062): instead of naming a camera, list what the person filming gets wrong ("Imperfect framing and accidental cropping. Natural autofocus hunting. Slight exposure fluctuations… Occasional delayed camera reactions"), keep the audio diegetic ("No soundtrack"), and ban polish explicitly ("No fashion-commercial aesthetic. No cinematic glamour… No modern colour grading").

Community, seamless loop seam (TRN-067): write the loop as its own block before the scenes. Open on "A dark, out-of-focus foreground object partially cover[ing] the lens", end with a camera move "toward the exact same dark foreground object" until the frame is dark, list what must match across the seam (camera position and height, lens angle, foreground placement, exposure and colour, motion direction and speed), and ban the cheats: "No fade-to-black followed by a separate restart. No sudden camera reset. No visible jump cut." Hiding the seam in a dark occluded frame is easier for the model than matching a fully detailed frame.

Community, first/last-frame transition driven by a foreground object (TRN-066): with a start frame and an end frame (Seedance 2.5 first_frame + last_frame), lock the camera ("Do not push in, pull back, pan horizontally, tilt up or down, orbit"), place a large object in the extreme foreground (a ceiling fan shot straight down), keep it legible ("only moderate, natural motion blur") and assign it the cut: "The transition is completed after the ceiling fan blades rotate, entirely executed by the spinning blades themselves." The model is not named for certain (Seedance or MiniMax), but the method fits Seedance 2.5's keyframe task.

Community, palette discipline and bookend frames for ads (PRP-069): state the palette as a rule rather than a list ("The whole film is one hue in four values… a single berry accent… is the only saturated colour"), fix the light for the whole film, give the rhythm in one sentence ("one long still opening, then a fast burst of hard cuts, easing back to stillness, then a graphic endcard"), frame repeated product heroes "exactly like" the first one, and end on a payoff shot "matching the opening frame exactly (same placement, distance, lens and light)" with one change (both models now smile).

sections.title: 2026-11-05 additions: LOST FILMS fixed-character + iris bookends, MiniDV FORMAT lock, phone-drop environment wipe, timed slapstick physics, "clearly adult" UGC lock

items.text: Re-checked 2026-11-05 (morning PT): no change to the official Seedance 2.5 docs. The prompt guide (md5 40fd6d36…) and the API tutorial (md5 2457c16c…) are byte-identical to 2026-11-04; the agent-skills index still lists sd25-pe v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run); the Runway Seedance 2.5 Help Center article body is unchanged (updated_at 2026-11-01 / edited_at 2026-10-30).

Community, LOST FILMS fixed-character + geography locks with iris bookends (GRN-063): declare characters "fixed for the whole film" with exact wardrobe and face notes, fix geography ("the young man always carries one very long wooden ladder horizontally on his right shoulder, until he puts it against the tree"), write timed static cuts (0-3s / 3-7s…), and bookend with iris-in / iris-out. Style as period stock ("shot on 35mm orthochromatic black and white film, 1.33:1… heavy grain, scratches, dust specks, flicker") and put safety constraints in the same block ("nobody is hurt, no children… no morphing hands"). The iris bookends double as a transition reference.

Community, MiniDV FORMAT lock before the story (GRN-064): open with a FORMAT block that names length, aspect, fps and the stock ("Exactly 30 seconds | 16:9 | 24fps | Photorealistic live-action | Authentic 1997 Sony MiniDV home-video aesthetic"), then CHARACTERS with clothing locks, then timed rural scenes. Keep audio diegetic and ban fashion-commercial polish so the camcorder faults stay readable.

Community, object-driven environment wipe (TRN-068): use a single prop as the continuity anchor across climates. Time the beats (0–3s desert selfie → phone falls in POV → black beat → gloved hand picks the same phone up on snow → alpine village wardrobe). Keep "the same face" and "natural smartphone camera shake"; do not dissolve — the fall and pickup are the cut.

Community, timed slapstick physics beat sheet (PRF-080): lock three adult characters and outfits, then write six action blocks with concrete physics payoffs (ramp jump, picnic leap, bag tug-of-war, scooter spin-out into a circular fountain, pigeons). Require "Believable momentum and water physics" and ban logos/brands/subtitles so the gag stays clean.

Community, explicit adult identity lock for UGC performance (PRF-081): when the concept could read idol/youthful, put "the same clearly adult …" in the first sentence of the prompt, keep vertical smartphone vlog framing, and describe small diegetic beats (good-luck card, frosting on lip, finger-heart under stage lights) rather than a polished MV.

sections.title: 2026-11-06 additions: 4:3-inside-16:9 MiniDV, AUDIO RULE + CHARACTER LOCK prop story, reference-mode UGC meta-prompt, three-role reference casting

items.text: Community, 4:3-inside-16:9 MiniDV (GRN-065): instead of just saying "MiniDV", specify "consumer MiniDV footage with 4:3 source-video characteristics inside a 16:9 frame" plus handheld shake, imperfect autofocus, soft tape detail, faded colours, warm fluorescents and exposure fluctuations, and end the style block with "Avoid polished commercial-style cinematography." For hand-detail ads, add a progression continuity line (unpainted → filed → painted) and "Only two anatomically correct hands with five fingers each." The creator ran the same prompt on Kling 4.0 side by side.

Community, rule blocks first (PRF-082): lead with an AUDIO RULE ("Natural sound only. No music, no score, no voiceover, no dialogue") and a CHARACTER LOCK that includes a behavioural lock ("She never stops, never breaks stride, never looks at the camera") and a prop lock (the same folded newspaper in every shot). Then give each shot separate Camera / Action / Sound lines with explicit HARD CUT separators, and close with an AVOID list covering outfit/prop drift.

Community, reference-mode UGC meta-prompt (REA-067): feed an LLM @Image1 (exact first frame), @Video1 (a real TikTok clip for performance, voice and accent) and @Image2 (product), and have it write a lowercase, plain-English Seedance 2.5 reference-mode prompt in 7 numbered sections: format & references, body language seen in @Video1, dialogue in brackets ("she says exactly what is written between the brackets"), line-by-line reactions, … room-matched audio, then one continuous shot with a NOT list (no music, cuts, zooms, captions). Ban vague words like "high quality" and "cinematic". The creator says 720p is enough.

Community, role-based multi-reference casting (REA-068): give each reference a role (@image1 MAIN CHARACTER, @image2 veteran squad leader, @image3 "generic tactical squad: faceless operators") so background extras can repeat without face drift, then run a timestamped shot list with whip-pans and selfie push-ins under one STYLE AND CAMERA block.

sections.title: 2026-11-07 additions: official re-check (formatting-only change), one-second beats ≠ cuts, reference-sheet overrides, camcorder fault list, one-outfit-per-scene, Gemini Omni 1.2 ports

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-07): the BytePlus prompt guide .md has a new md5 (ccef216d…, was 40fd6d36…), but a full diff shows that the only change is the code-fence language label on 24 example blocks ("Plain Text" → "plaintext"). No wording, examples, task rules or parameters changed. The API tutorial is byte-identical (2457c16c…). The agent-skills index is unchanged, so sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run). The Runway "Creating with Seedance 2.5" body is unchanged (md5 d1765502…, updated_at 2026-11-01).

Community, one-second beats are not cuts (AES-071): for dense 30 s action, write a 30-line timeline ("00-01:" … "29-30:") and state up front: "The intervals are choreography beats, not a requirement to cut every second. Keep contact, trajectories, and cause-and-effect readable." Add "The VERY FIRST FRAME already shows …" so the clip opens mid-action with no posing shot.

Community, reference-sheet roles with explicit overrides (AES-071): name each sheet's role ("Reference image 1 = THE DIRECTOR, the human before transformation"; "Reference image 2 = … the same man after transformation"), then override what the sheet gets wrong ("Override the reference-sheet height: his transformed height is 700 meters") and forbid the sheet layout ("Use the sheets for appearance only; never show their layouts, panels, labels, or measurement graphics"). This matches the official advice to bind every asset in the text and not rely on labels inside the image. Also lock per-character energy colours ("Do not swap colors"), keep the screen-direction axis fixed ("advances from screen left … Preserve this action axis"), and keep scale cues ("tiny yellow taxis, buses, and street-level humans … Never shrink the giants to fit a building").

Community, camcorder realism as a fault list first (GRN-066): open with the device and its faults before any subject ("Recorded on a compact pocket camcorder held by the subject herself. Slight rolling-shutter wobble …, occasional autofocus adjustments, minor exposure fluctuations when passing light sources, subtle digital noise in darker areas … authentic consumer-camera quality rather than cinematic footage"). Give 2 s arrow beats with the shot type in parentheses, and end found-footage clips with the camera being set down while "Recording continues for a brief moment before ending naturally."

Community, one outfit line per scene (WRD-068): for wardrobe boards as video, put one identity lock at the top, then exactly one outfit sentence per location scene, and put "sudden outfit changes" in the closing negatives so changes only happen at scene breaks.

Port from the Gemini Omni 1.2 official prompt guide (new this week): (a) First/last frame: "Clearly define what is in your initial frame, specify the exact camera movement or transition path …, and state precisely what the final frame should reveal." This maps directly onto Seedance content.role first_frame/last_frame plus a 【Camera】 line that names start → path → arrival (TRN-070 adapted). (b) Style progression on an input video: name the looks in order with a connective verb per change. In Seedance this becomes an editing task on Video 1 with timestamped style stages and "keep motion, camera and composition unchanged" (TRN-069 adapted). (c) Multi-turn extension: each turn says only what happens next, with quoted dialogue, one camera move and an audio cue ("The music swells."). In Seedance, use the extension trigger "Continue from the end of Video 1" (PRF-083 adapted). (d) Sync edits: "The lights of the apartments start turning on in sync with the music" becomes a Seedance edit with an add-music trigger plus a beat-timed change list (MOO-069 adapted).

Community (Seedance 2.0 → adapted to 2.5): a state-change reveal tied to contact. A character's first touch triggers an expanding ring, and the change then travels as a directional wave behind the moving subject until "the last … corner turns" (TRN-071). For product interiors, use a macro push-through: a beauty shot, then the shell "separates and peels back in layered mechanical sections" and the camera continues inside in a "probe-lens perspective" with micro focus pulls (PRP-071).

Community, guide-only: one creator packed a character sheet and a location storyboard into a single reference image and told the model which panels do which job ("The storyboard establishes the sequence of locations, while the character sheet establishes her exact appearance"). They called the result "kind of" working. The official guide warns against putting mapping only inside the image, so if you try this, describe each panel group in the text. Another creator's tip for effects: say where the effect starts and where it stops ("the pink dome grows out from behind the frog, spreads until its edge meets the ground, and the dust stays outside") instead of "a shield appears".

sections.title: 2026-11-08 additions: official re-check (no changes), FPV ghost-camera locks, garment-level wardrobe locks, garment-interaction beats, film-authenticity rule + silence beat, GPT Image 2.6 ports

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-08 ~6:05 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide .md is byte-identical to 2026-11-07 (md5 ccef216d…), the API tutorial is byte-identical (2457c16c…), the agent-skills index is identical so sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run), and the Runway "Creating with Seedance 2.5" body is unchanged (md5 d1765502…, updated_at 2026-11-01 7:28 AM PT). No official changes today.

Community, FPV oner with hard camera locks (CAM-151): put the camera rules in capitals before the story. "One CONTINUOUS FPV shot, no cuts… The footage NEVER reverses." Allow one exception and say how it ends ("NO slow motion except one half-second beat at the reveal, then an instant snap back to full speed"). Hide the operator ("GHOST CAMERA: INVISIBLE, no drone or reflection in frame"), give it one motion grammar ("ORBITS the fighters at street level and DIVES in on every strike — always moving, never climbs"), and lock the fight geometry ("the two face each other along the street, resetting after every exchange; blows land OFF-axis past the lens"). Bind references with roles and heights ("@Image2 is BIG BRO — 185 cm… @Image3 is LITTLE SIS — 160 cm… Her head reaches his shoulder"), and finish with a global style lock ("every animal and onlooker REACTS… playful, no injuries").

Community, vehicle-mounted POV (CAM-150): when the camera rides a vehicle, the environment carries all the variety (drop, cliff edge, tunnel, waterfall, corkscrew, cloud spiral, arrival), so list it as one continuous route. Close with a tech line of exclusions ("one continuous shot, vertical 9:16, no slow motion, no cuts, no looping"). The restraint bar in frame stays as a fixed foreground anchor for 30 s, which keeps the spatial continuity readable.

Community, garment-construction wardrobe lock (GRN-067): describe the outfit the way a pattern-maker would ("靛蓝底浅米色小碎花短袖连衣裙，浅圆领，腰间两道省缝自然收腰，裙摆到膝下": indigo short-sleeve dress with small beige florals, shallow round neck, two waist darts, below-knee hem), lock the hair to ONE object (a tea-coloured horizontal barrette at the centre back of a half-up style) and add the matching negative ("耳侧没有发夹": no clips at the sides). Then give each timed beat a reason to show the outfit (the friend follows half a step behind and "带到她的鞋和下装" catches her shoes and lower half). For camcorder realism, define the camera by its operator (a friend filming casually) and end on a hard cut "像朋友按下停录键" (as if the friend pressed stop). The creator ran the same prompt on Seedance 2.5 and Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: in this one comparison both kept the dress, sandals and barrette. Seedance used closer, looser handheld framing; Omni stayed wider and steadier.

Community, a garment-interaction beat sheet (WRD-072): for outerwear or layering spots, make the whole clip about one garment action, and include a believable failure beat ("slips one arm into a sleeve, then struggles briefly to get the other arm through. She wiggles her shoulder to settle it properly"). Ask for "Realistic shivering, fabric movement, sleeve interactions", and keep the sound to fabric rustle and room tone.

Port from MiniMax H3 (GRN-068): state film authenticity as a physical rule rather than a filter ("must convincingly look PHYSICALLY PHOTOGRAPHED ON 35MM FILM IN 1978, NOT like a modern digital movie with a retro filter"). Follow it with the actual faults (prominent organic grain, slightly soft resolving detail, mild analog colour instability, exposure breathing, crushed shadows, restrained dynamic range) and the modern looks to ban (HDR, teal-and-orange, razor-sharp 4K, gimbal movement). For tension, script silence as a sound beat: one sharp snap, then "all exterior ambience abruptly disappears for approximately HALF A SECOND". Also suppress sounds the model adds by default ("NO FOOTSTEP SOUNDS"). The GRN-068 adapted template moves these into 【Visuals】 and 【Sound】.

Port from the OpenAI GPT Image 2.6 official guide (new this week): (a) Try-on: say what may change ("Replace only the clothing"), list everything that may not (face, skin tone, body shape, pose, identity, background, camera angle, framing), and ask for lighting and colour-temperature matching "without looking pasted on". In Seedance this becomes one reference_image role per garment plus an identity reference (WRD-069 adapted). (b) Exact copy: quote it and say how many times it should appear ("Render the tagline exactly once") (WRD-070 adapted). (c) Camera specs are "cues for appearance, not a guarantee of exact physical simulation", so pair "35mm film / 50mm" with visible-texture words (pores, sun texture, worn materials) and an anti-retouch line (REA-069). (d) Period scenes: name the place and the exact date and ask for "period-accurate clothing, staging, and environment". Guide only: the official Bethel, NY, Aug 16 1969 crowd example was not ingested. (e) Loops: give the subject a start pose to return to and say whether the camera moves (from the GIF section).

Community (Seedance 2.0 → adapted to 2.5), painterly style pieces (AES-072): fix the medium and grade in the first two lines, give each 3 s shot a size and a lens (35/85/20/16 mm), write every action as a brush behaviour (ink "spreads outward like a shockwave", whiskers "painted in quick sharp strokes", the body "stretching into long brushstrokes"), and end on a graphic device (a vermilion seal stamping the corner).

sections.title: 2026-11-09 additions: official re-check (no changes), fisheye-peephole series template, film-stock opening line, photographer-fault realism ports from Seedream 5.5, counted constraints, order-of-events and state-link blocks

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-09 ~6:10 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide .md is byte-identical to 2026-11-08 (md5 ccef216d…), the API tutorial is byte-identical (2457c16c…), the agent-skills index is identical (0451c8c7…) so sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run), and the Runway "Creating with Seedance 2.5" body is unchanged (md5 d1765502…, updated_at 2026-11-01 7:28 AM PT). No official changes today.

Community, a reusable series template (Magnific, five prompts, one look): (1) one opening line fixes format, stock, grain and grade ("Create a fast-cut 15-second cinematic film, vertical 9:16, with a Kodak Vision3 500T look, heavy grain, soft halation, tungsten amber and teal shadows"); (2) one talent line made of wardrobe and detail items; (3) four timed beats (0–3 / 3–7 / 7–11 / 11–15 s) where beat 1 and beat 4 use the same device ("circular fisheye peephole on black"), so the film opens and closes on it; (4) one closing line for camera energy and sound ("Handheld energy … cuts on the beat and whooshes"). Seedance 2.5 kept the same structure across a kitchen, a farm, a desert gas station and a rooftop car park. Swap only the talent line and the middle beats to make a campaign series.

Community, gesture-driven transitions (TRN-072): let the talent operate the cut. The open is "finger tapping the lens, whip pan"; the close is "return to the peephole, lower the sunglasses and stare into the lens" and then "cut to black on the beat"; the farm variant ends with "push the lens away". Inside the film, "speed ramp", "Dutch-angle head tilt" and "stacked split-screen from two angles" do the internal transitions, and the split-screen beat is where accessory and detail inserts go (chain, rings, plating, hands).

Community, film-stock wording that Seedance 2.5 held (GRN-071/072, WRD-073): for night interiors use "Kodak Vision3 500T look, heavy grain, soft halation, tungsten amber and teal shadows"; for daylight, "Kodak Vision3 look … golden-hour amber and teal shadows"; for blue hour, "35mm film look, heavy grain, halation and an amber-teal grade". Put the stock in the first sentence with the format, not at the end, and give the light something to hit (flames, sunlit dust, headlight flares) so the halation reads.

Port from Seedream 5.5 official examples (new model, 2026-11-09): to get realism, name the photographer's faults instead of adding "ultra-realistic". Examples: "Slight underexposure, subtle high-ISO grain and foreground occlusion" (REA-071); "hurried framing and asymmetric cropping" plus a whole-frame tilt held with "consistent perspective across the figure, buildings, lamppost and pavement" (REA-072); a flash recipe of "low angle with a tilted composition, using flash, Fujifilm Provia colors and film grain" (GRN-070). In Seedance put the tilt and occlusion in 【Camera】 as constant for the whole shot, and the exposure/grain faults in 【Visuals】. Seedream also uses negatives as composition control ("No full building, people or vehicles appear", MOO-071) and colour planes for set dressing (PRP-072). Adapted templates on all five.

Community (Grok Imagine → adapted to 2.5), the minimal ad brief (GRN-073): five labelled blocks (SCENE / ACTION / CAMERA / LOOK / KEEP IT SIMPLE). The last block counts the allowed elements ("One cup. One hand. No cuts, captions, logos or extra people."), so the model has nothing to add. The creator's advice is to drop "cinematic, stunning, 8K" and to add the business name and offer in post so the text stays sharp. This fits Seedance 2.5 short spots of 5–8 s.

Community, an order-of-events block for many-scene clips (MOO-072): when cramming 8 scenes into 30 s, add a STRICT CONTINUITY line that states the order of events as well as the characters ("Pancakes before breakfast, cleaning after breakfast, cassette listening before dinner. Rain continues from morning to evening."), then a one-line FINAL GOAL and "Include all 8 scenes in exact order within 30 seconds." The output kept the scene order and the three characters.

Community, per-scene state links for process shots (PRP-073): for food, craft or product-build sequences, give every scene a Camera / Start / Action / Change / Texture / Link line, with a rule that states only move forward ("ingredient states progress forward only"). The Link line hands the exact object to the next scene ("all of these same pieces go into Scene 2"). Add an IP guard to the style block ("Do not imitate the distinctive look of any existing studio, artist, film, or character"). In the creator's 4-model grid, Seedance 2.5 kept the hands-only rule and the ganache → sheet → dough progression.

sections.title: 2026-11-10 additions: official re-check (no changes), lens-as-FOV, colour budgets, audio-bridged match cuts, camcorder-fault block, blocking video beats text, freeze-flash endings, locked-object match chains, one-line change prompts

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-10 ~6:00 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide .md is byte-identical (md5 ccef216d…), the API tutorial is byte-identical (2457c16c…), the agent-skills index is identical (0451c8c7…) so sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run), and the Runway "Creating with Seedance 2.5" body is unchanged (md5 d1765502…, updated_at 2026-11-01 7:28 AM PT). The BytePlus llms.txt index still has no Seedream 5.5 or new Seedance pages. No official changes today.

Community, lens as field of view plus focal length (TRN-073): instead of only "close-up" or "wide", give each shot both numbers, e.g. "S1 (18°/100mm close-up, gentle handheld)", "S6 (84°/22mm wide)", "S13 (fast horizontal orbit ending at 47°/50mm)". In a 15-shot, 2-s-per-shot montage the output kept the requested size changes shot by shot. Combine with a geometry line (sun upper left, birds travel screen-right to screen-left, window screen-left) so the screen direction holds across hard cuts.

Community, a colour budget (TRN-073): state the palette as rough percentages ("~70% soft white and sky blue, ~25% warm sun gold on skin, ~5% chrome glint from the dome") and give the later scene its own light line ("S14–S15: soft cool daylight through the cabin window"). It is a compact way to keep the grade consistent across many shots.

Community, audio-bridged match cut (TRN-073): to cut from fantasy to reality, keep the body and framing identical ("same head position, same angle, same screaming expression") and let the sound carry over ("The scream carries over the cut"). Put the cut in the closing LOCKS line too ("…jet, match cut to plane, hides face") so the order cannot be dropped.

Community, the mandatory camcorder-fault block (GRN-074): for MiniDV/found footage, write a CAMCORDER IMAGE (MANDATORY) block that lists every fault ("about 480 lines upscaled: soft image, interlacing combing on fast motion, mild sharpening halos, low dynamic range, ceiling lights and steel reflections blown to white, shadows crushed to black with chroma noise, warm yellow white balance, slow auto-exposure and autofocus") and what to remove ("No HDR, no smartphone sharpness, no cinematic grading, no shallow depth of field… No REC text, date stamp"). Keep operator behaviour in its own HANDHELD OPERATION block (shake that grows with emotion, late reframes, overshooting zooms, operator never visible "including in steel doors"). For an off-screen event, use sound (a screech that "travels rapidly downward, more muffled, lower in pitch"). Close with a continuity block that rules out gore.

Community, a blocking video beats text (no prompt shared): one creator blocked a 30 s chase in Blender (grey boxes, camera animated through an MCP link), previewed it, then fed the blocking as the reference video. Their finding: "Seedance follows your reference video over your text. Write 'shaky handheld' with a smooth Blender camera and you get smooth." So when a reference video sets the camera, the camera words in the prompt must agree with it (add shake in the blocking, not in the text). Guide-only, because the post has no prompt.

Port from MiniMax H3 (TRN-074), the freeze-flash cliffhanger ending: with two reference stills, ask for no motion at all ("All character images must remain completely motionless freeze-frames. Only editing transitions and subtle optical effects are permitted") and time each optical event to the millisecond (white flash at 00:00.850, hard cut at 00:01.000, ghosted afterimage, fade to black by 00:04.000), with one whoosh per flash. In Seedance 2.5, use omni reference with the two stills and duration 4 (adapted template on TRN-074). It works as a stinger for episodic vertical ads.

Port from MiniMax H3 (TRN-075), the locked-object match chain: keep one product exactly fixed ("The strawberry stays in exactly the same screen position, size, orientation and downward motion through every transition") while the world cuts four times, then end on one landing event and join the cuts with "one continuous musical phrase". This is the simplest reliable multi-transition product spot. In Seedance 2.5, give each environment a timestamp range.

Port from MiniMax H3 (TRN-076, MOO-074), one-line change prompts: GlennHasABeard writes only the changing line in quotes plus duration and camera ("the stripe it leaves is not paint but a view of a sunny green meadow" · Duration: 15s · Camera: locked, facing the wall). The "not X but Y" construction and material-behaviour verbs ("a slow thick river of fog rolls out") do the work. In Seedance 2.5, wrap that line in a short 【Subject】/【Action】/【Camera】 frame and keep the camera locked.

Port from MiniMax H3 (REA-074), light-physics negatives for moving light on a face: say the light change is slow and continuous and changes only temperature ("cool-to-warm… brightness roughly unchanged"), lands on everything at once ("never only on her face"), and list the failures ("no window-shaped light patches sweeping across her face", no flicker, exposure locked, no headlight flaring into the lens). Pair it with matte-skin rules ("No skin oil, sweat, water shine, specular spots… or droplets on the face").

Community (Seedance 2.0 → 2.5), part-to-part morph mapping (WRD-074): for a creature or object turning into a product, map each source part to a product part ("tail… into a gem-studded strap", "claws form the pointed toe box", "body shapes into a sleek, jeweled stiletto heel"). The morph reads clearly because the model knows where each piece goes. In 2.5, give the mapping in the order it should happen.

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-11 ~6:05 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide .md is byte-identical (md5 ccef216d…), the API tutorial (seedance-2-5.md) is byte-identical (2457c16c…), the agent-skills index is identical (0451c8c7…) so sd25-pe is still v0.1.1 (read only, not installed or run), and the Runway "Creating with Seedance 2.5" body is unchanged (md5 d1765502…, updated_at 2026-11-01 7:28 AM PT). The BytePlus llms.txt index changed only in Managed Agents pages (new "Schedule agent runs" and deployment APIs); there are no new Seedance or Seedream pages. No official changes today.

Community, Seedream 5.5 first frame → Seedance 2.5 prestige drama (GRN-075): open with an identity-and-set lock against the first frame ("Strictly keep both men's faces, clothing, the kitchen layout, the wooden table, the coffee pot and the cold window light from Image 1"), then one stock line ("35mm film look, Kodak Vision3 500T, fine grain, soft halation on the window, muted earthy palette, cold dawn light from the window as the only key light"), then a one-sentence story, then timed beats with exact quoted dialogue. Give the emotion to one prop (a watch slid "past the coffee pot, until it stops in front of the son's hands", whose ticking "becomes audible"). The output kept the grain, halation and single window key across 30 s.

Community, withhold the score (GRN-075): write the sound as a timeline: "no BGM until 21s; only room tone, wall clock, cups, breathing. From 21s, a single low solo cello note enters and swells gently until the cut to black." Silence first, then one instrument at the emotional turn, is a cheap and reliable way to make a 30 s spot feel like a film.

Community, anti-ghosting exits and no fake god-rays (GRN-075): when a character leaves frame through a door, say "stays solid and fully physical the whole time and is visible until the door closes", and for daylight through a doorway add "with no light beams or rays in the air". Caveats from the same post: the clip came out vertical although the prose said "Aspect ratio 2.39:1", and it has burned-in Arabic subtitles although the prompt said "Do not add subtitles". Set the ratio on the API line (official rule) and check the platform's caption or translation setting rather than relying on the prompt.

Community, counted continuity for animated mascots (AES-076): after ART STYLE / MAIN CHARACTER / SETTING and five timed scenes, a CONTINUITY line written as counts ("One delivery worker, one paper airplane, one yellow backpack, and one rainbow container… No duplicate characters, random objects, sudden transformations, or unexplained scene changes") kept the character and props consistent over 30 s. Add "Not photorealistic or anime" to the style line to pin the 3D look, and an audio rule against "recognizable existing music".

Port from MiniMax H3 (PRP-075), a timed on-screen callout: put the overlay at an exact time, attach it to a part, give its design and its exact copy in quotes, and say when it leaves: "At 9.2s, display a clean, partially transparent callout beside the ultrasonic plate… with a fine pointer line… thin champagne-gold border… The callout title reads: 'Silent Ultrasonic Diffusion'… The callout fades away before the final lockup." Both lines rendered legibly in the H3 output. In Seedance 2.5, keep the exact copy in double quotes and keep "no writing on the product" so the callout is the only text.

Port from MiniMax H3 (TRN-078, MOO-076), changes as timelines, not moods: list colours in order with where each starts ("the green drains from the edges inward… orange creeping in from the veins… brown starting at the tip"), and write slow changes as continuous ("the sunbeam on the floor sweeps steadily from left to right… warming from pale to gold"; the creator's fix for unwanted time jumps is "never jumps"). Two continuous clocks in one locked shot (a winding-down music box and the sun) read as time passing without cuts.

Port from MiniMax H3 (MOO-075), containment + anticlimax: for a surreal element in a real place, confine it in one sentence ("The miniature ocean exists only inside the washing machine"), give the music a hard stop on the payoff ("building from 4 seconds and stopping abruptly when the door opens"), and end on an ordinary result ("Only ordinary wet laundry falls onto the floor"). Useful for product reveals where the magic must not leak into the rest of the frame.

Port from MiniMax H3 (AES-077, REA-076), name the material faults and the real behaviour: for claymation, list the faults to keep ("Visible fingerprints, tool marks, and material imperfections in the clay. Slightly stepped, handmade movement") and make the sound material ("the dull slap of clay on clay"); for realism, a REALISM DIRECTIVE of the form "behaves like real X, not Y" ("Ice must behave like real compressed glacier ice, not glass. Light scatters through the walls naturally").

Community comparison (REA-075): a simple 6-line street-food prompt (one handheld push-in, one fire flare, one catch, one look to camera, lantern light, diegetic sound only) run on Seedance 2.5, Wan 3.0 and MiniMax H3 Max side by side. It is a quick benchmark for fire, steam and crowd before committing a food or travel spot to one model.

First frames from MiniMax H3 Image (PRP-077, official): H3 Image wants one detailed English paragraph that places each item by region ("In the center… To the left… On the right side… At the upper right…") and ends with a single light direction ("coming from the upper left and casting soft, long shadows to the lower right"). Its official expander (H3-Image-Context-IR, or the local H3-Image-PE model) turns a one-line brief into that form. For Seedance 2.5 image-to-video, keep the same region list and light vector in the prompt and say "Nothing is moved" so the layout holds (adapted template on PRP-077).

sections.title: 2026-11-12 additions: Seedance 2.5 Flash announced (official banner), draft-on-Flash workflow, sd25-pe section format in the wild at 4K, action-synced captions, claims-safe negatives, object persistence for builds, outfit locks, forbid the second action, audio-first dialogue

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-12 ~6:00 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide .md is byte-identical (md5 ccef216d…) and the agent-skills index is identical (0451c8c7…; sd2-pe and sd25-pe still listed, read only), the Runway "Creating with Seedance 2.5" body is unchanged (md5 d1765502…, updated_at 2026-11-01 7:28 AM PT), and llms.txt is unchanged from 2026-11-11 (70d85331…). The API tutorial (seedance-2-5.md) changed (2457c16c… → 57f7cad1…), but only by a new warning banner: "Dreamina Seedance 2.5 flash is now available… Starting at 14:00 (UTC+8) on November 15, 2026, the model will be available for online experience and API calls" (= Nov 14, 10:00 PM PT). The banner links a model page for dreamina-seedance-2-5-flash. No Flash-specific prompt rules have been published, so write Flash prompts exactly like Seedance 2.5 prompts.

Seedance 2.5 Flash, as reported on launch day (second-hand; check the model page before relying on numbers): a summary of the BytePlus announcement says results come "close to flagship Seedance 2.5 at nearly twice the generation speed", "up to 10 images, 5 videos and 5 audio clips as references", clips "up to 30 seconds in 480p or 720p", and 720p text/image-to-video at "USD 0.152 per second", about 34% below 2.5. It was live on Lovart, Higgsfield (early access, not in the US) and Newtake on Nov 12, with Renoise and WaveSpeed announcing it. One same-image, same-prompt test in Jimeng found Flash faster but 2.5 better on liquid motion (translated from Chinese: "look at the orange juice in the cup: 2.5's churn and foam are more natural"). Practical workflow: iterate on blocking, timing and dialogue with Flash at 480p/720p, then render the chosen prompt on Seedance 2.5 at 1080p or 4K, and recheck liquids, fabric and hair on the final model. Picsart's 2.5 "Draft Mode" (480p preview, then 4K) is the same idea inside one model.

Community, the sd25-pe section format at 4K (REA-077): a creator's 30 s tiger film uses the official skill's skeleton verbatim: [Generation Goal] → [Reference Material Roles] (<<<image_1>>> "defines the tiger and the look") → [Subjects and Relationships] ("exactly one tiger and it is the only animal in the film") → [Event Script] with eight [Stage N] blocks separated by "Hard cut." → [Maintain Consistency]. Each stage has one "Primary event:", one "Camera:" line and its own sound tags at the end ("<a soft heavy pad on damp earth> <a twig cracking>"). The output holds stripes and eye colour across all eight cuts, which is good evidence that the official format scales to 8 shots in 30 s.

Community, action-synced captions and claims-safe negatives (PRP-079): write 12 shots with millisecond timecodes ("SHOT 4 — 7.500–10.000s"), give each caption its own trigger ("ON-SCREEN CAPTION: 'ONE-TOUCH BREW CONTROL' Display exactly when the control is pressed"), and add negatives for ad-compliance risks as well as visuals: "no fake pressure readings, no invented temperature or extraction specifications, no unsupported certifications". The captions rendered legibly at 720p.

Community, object persistence for progressive builds (AES-079): when something is assembled on screen, lock the base ("Keep the mushroom in exactly the same position and shape throughout") and make every addition physical and permanent: "All additions must be physically carried and installed by the builder. Once placed, doors, windows, chimney, balcony, steps, flowers, and lanterns remain in their exact positions. No disappearing objects… sudden transformations, or random decorations." Useful for set builds, product assembly and before/after reveals.

Community, full outfit lock for talent-led product ads (WRD-077): spell out every garment with cut and colour ("high-waisted wide-leg charcoal trousers with a dramatic tailored silhouette, pointed black ankle boots, sculptural silver earrings"), add "Maintain the exact same woman, outfit and suitcase design throughout", and repeat the lock as negatives ("No outfit changes, no identity drift, no suitcase morphing, no changing luggage design"). The look held across about ten cuts.

Port from MiniMax H3 (PRP-078), forbid the second action: for a single physical change (frying, melting, blooming), forbid the follow-up action the model is likely to add ("It never flips and never leaves the oil"). The creator's reasoning: "Flipping is a second action, and second actions are where H3 slips." One continuous change with a locked camera is safer on any model; on Seedance 2.5 add the forbidden action as an explicit "never" sentence.

Port from MiniMax H3 Image (GRN-076, MOO-077; prompts shared by the official MiniMax account), first-frame recipes for texture: ask for optical rather than digital effects ("authentic optical motion trails, not a simple digital blur filter"), name the film behaviour ("fine grain, soft sharpness, slight underexposure, naturally blooming highlights"), reject the ad look by name ("commercial sports-advertising polish"), and for deadpan surreal stills direct the performance ("His posture is natural, with no exaggerated performance or forced humor"). Then animate the still with Seedance 2.5 image-to-video (ratio adaptive) using only small motions.

Community, audio-first dialogue (guide only; no prompt shared): one creator compares the same Seedance 2.5 prompt with native audio against dialogue generated first in Seed Audio 1.0 and then "synced with video in SeeDance 2.5". He generates non-dialogue shots first for visual flow and goes "audio first" only for dialogue shots, because speech models are much faster to iterate. With Seedance 2.5 this means supplying the voice track as an audio reference rather than relying on in-prompt {dialogue}.
