Seedance 2.5 Flash, first verbatim A/B tests (community; Flash is labelled Flash, not 2.5): with the same prompt and the same seed at 720p for 8 s, one platform found "Flash keeps the action and gets the sign text right. 2.5 gives a busier scene and finer detail" ($1.16 vs $2.24; REA-080). A same-prompt, same-reference sketch on Higgsfield cost 75 vs 105 credits for 15 s at 720p and took "about 3 min" vs "about 6 min"; the creator found "the acting better in the full model", had to crop one Flash shot "where a character showed up twice", and measured Flash's ambience "about 6 dB lower". Other early reports: a 480p Flash VFX test "missed the camera orbit", and a Spanish-language tester says Flash renders skin "con brillo" (shiny) and follows prompts only so-so. One creator's ladder renders the same prompt at 480p / 1080p / 4K on 2.5 and at 720p on Flash (REA-081). Practical checklist for Flash drafts: look for duplicated characters, dropped camera moves (orbits), sheen on skin and quieter ambience. Those four are the things to re-check when the locked prompt goes to Seedance 2.5 for the final.

Community, scale reveal by camera position (TRN-079): to make a miniature read as a real city and then reveal it, keep the camera "so low inside the miniature street that the scene looks like a full-sized city", state the mechanism ("The change in camera position reveals the true scale"), make the reveal one physical move ("In one physical movement, lift the camera above the rooftops and pull back past the front edge of the wooden table"), and keep one moving object as the continuity anchor (the same red train loops through every beat). End on a timed gag ("Cut on the second lick"). In the creator's stacked test, Seedance 2.5 held the reveal and Kling 4.0 glitched on the paw.

Community, portal chains in one shot (TRN-080): give each 5-second block one world and one verb for how the character goes through the portal (jumps through, punches through, drops through one opening under a leap). Then name what must carry across the cut ("preserve speed, identity, camera direction and momentum") and end with a reveal that stacks every world ("Three portals collapse into one giant circular gate… the full stack of worlds appears layered behind her"). Closing constraints that worked: "no teleportation glitches, readable world changes".

Community, time-progression lock (MOO-080): a CHARACTER LOCK can include a planned change ("hair and stubble growing longer as the shots progress"), so a 30 s montage reads as weeks passing without identity drift. Put mood on global lines that also have an arc: "cold blue tones that warm slightly at the end", plus a score "that never stops" under the cuts. In this example, 29 timed beats of about one second each in 30 s kept a coherent edit, with "No gore, no self-harm" as safety rails for a dark subject.

Community, anti-cheat lines for on-screen changes (technique only): when a transformation must be seen, say what may change and ban the usual ways of hiding it: "Its ONLY change is the disappearance of the triangular hole", "Keep the damaged area facing the camera during the repair. Do not hide the repair with a cut, steam, or bright flash. Show the actual golden threads closing the hole", then "Hold on the repaired sleeve for two seconds so the result is unmistakable." This pairs with the 2026-11-12 object-persistence rule for builds. (The source clip includes a child customer, so it is not a library entry.)

Community, hero-accessory lock (WRD-080, Seedance 2.0): list the full outfit once up front, then repeat only the hero accessory, with its colour, material and hardware, in every scene ("babypink bag with gold dome studs clearly visible on arm"). Combined with "Kodak Portra 400 film tone, natural film grain, handheld" and an AVOID list that includes "empty streets" and "fake crowd", the bag and outfit stayed identical across five locations at 4K. This should carry straight over to Seedance 2.5.

Ports from MiniMax H3 camcorder prompts (GRN-078/079): (1) make exposure part of the story: subject lit only "by a single candle flame from below", then "Total darkness on tape for two full seconds, only sound", then "The ceiling light snaps on, the frame blows out white then settles"; (2) for a 16:9 output that should feel like old tape, write "treated as a later widescreen transfer of the original tape. The extra width is used badly, not compositionally"; (3) list the camcorder faults as concrete events ("Autofocus hunting… repeatedly grabbing the wrong thing. Exposure pumping hard… One lazy unmotivated zoom that overshoots… one dropout glitch"). These are H3 prompts; on Seedance 2.5 keep each fault as its own sentence and the operator voice-only.

Seedream 5.5 RGBA assets as first frames (official facts + workflow note): the new official Seedream 5.5 tutorial shows text-to-RGBA (no image input; "Describe the subject and transparent-background requirement in the prompt"; API background "transparent" + output_format "png") and image-to-RGBA from up to 10 references without alpha. PRP-081 is its official example. Seedance 2.5 takes an ordinary first frame, so composite the RGBA asset onto the plate you want before image-to-video (ratio adaptive). Use the alpha version for graphics layers in the edit.

sections.title: 2026-11-14 additions: official re-check (no Flash page yet), Flash already live on partner platforms, the giant-double template, one-pass coverage generation, named object states, ten-beat lifestyle montages, sensitivity blocks, fictional-product UGC, and first-frame stills

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-14, ~5:53 AM PT): prompt guide .md unchanged (ccef216d…); tutorial unchanged (21eed415…), still with the banner that Seedance 2.5 flash opens for online use and API calls at 14:00 UTC+8 on Nov 15 (= Nov 14, 10:00 PM PT); agent-skills index unchanged (0451c8c7…; sd2-pe and sd25-pe, read only); Runway article body unchanged (d1765502…, updated Nov 1, 7:28 AM PT). llms.txt changed (b44b7c1f… → ba718751…) only by removing an OpenViking page and adding a monitoring-data page. There is still no Flash page, prompt section or parameter table; guessed .md URLs (seedance-2-5-flash, dreamina-seedance-2-5-flash, seedance-2-5-flash-prompt-guide) return 404. Until one appears, Flash prompts follow the Seedance 2.5 guide.

Flash is already live on some partner platforms (pre-API): Magnific posted Seedance 2.5 Flash outputs on Nov 14 ~1:45 AM PT and says Flash "is now available on Magnific". The draft-then-final workflow is now the common advice: "Draft at 480p/720p. Lock your prompt, then generate the 1080p final with Seedance 2.5." One secondhand summary puts Flash at "almost twice as fast and 34% cheaper" than full 2.5 (not confirmed by an official page yet). Keep using the 2026-11-13 Flash-draft checklist (duplicate characters, dropped orbits, skin sheen, quieter ambience) when promoting a Flash draft to a full render.

The giant-double template (Magnific, Seedance 2.5 Flash; MOO-082, REA-082): "[Person] is [activity] inside [room]. Outside the window, a building-sized identical double bends down and peers in. Both remain visible, with matching faces, hair and clothes. The giant stays outside. One continuous shot. Slow camera push-in." Four ideas make it hold on a fast model: an everyday activity that continues; an identity lock on the double ("Same face, hair and clothes"); a co-visibility rule ("Both remain visible"); and a containment rule ("Giant stays outside"), plus exactly one camera move. The window frame sells the scale. Swap the activity and room for brand use (a cook, a gamer, a commuter); keep the four rules.

One-pass coverage (creator template): instead of 24 single shots, ask for one 30 s "sequence with hard cuts. I'm pulling individual shots into an edit, so give each shot one clear action and a clean moment to cut around." Give each reference one job ("@image1 = character and wardrobe", "@image2 = location, layout and materials", "@image3 = framing and camera angle"), then write SEQUENCE beats as "[00–00s] [Framing + camera move] as [one visible action]", with "Cut to [an insert or cutaway…]" and "Cut to [a new angle that reveals something the earlier shots didn't]", and "Give the action a moment to read before the next cut." The creator's platform quoted 210 credits for the 30 s pass versus 732 for 24 separate shots. In Seedance 2.5, map the @image roles to reference_image entries and keep "Location sound only" if music is added in the edit.

Named object states (AES-084, Seedance 2.5, 15k-character prompt written with an LLM): define each changeable object as named states with the exact shots where each applies, e.g. pouch "normal" (Shots 1–3) / "stretched into a ball" (Shot 4 until Shot 8) / "stretched out and saggy" (after Shot 8), plus a one-way rule ("the pouch never goes back to normal"), and say what the state is NOT ("The ball is the pouch skin itself… not an object held in the mouth"). The model kept the pouch progression across 24 s. Use the same pattern for product states (closed / open / poured), packaging reveals or melting and inflating props.

Ten-beat lifestyle montage in 30 s (MOO-083): ten scenes of about 3 s each with a title per beat, one wardrobe and bag lock, "Authentic handheld travel vlog footage… like a real day filmed by a friend, not an advertisement", natural sound only, and a strict-continuity block that ends "Include all ten scenes within exactly 30 seconds." Seedance 2.5 delivered all ten beats in order with morning-to-golden-hour light. Three seconds is about the floor for a readable beat.

Sensitivity block (MOO-084): for faith, remembrance or charity work, write the restraint as direction: figures "from behind and in elegant silhouettes, without identifiable facial details", "No exaggerated acting, no dramatic crying", and an IMPORTANT paragraph of what must not be depicted. The output kept faces hidden throughout. End-line typography rendered only partly legibly, so add final text in the edit.

Fictional-product UGC (PRP-082): declare the product fictional and ban real brands and complex UI text ("No Apple, Samsung, Google, Instagram, TikTok or other real brand references. Do not generate complex readable UI text… a simple believable generic camera interface with a single obvious LENSO capture control"). Pair it with a smartphone-realism list (small hand movements, autofocus adjustments, exposure changes, tiny framing imperfections, "Do NOT make the footage excessively stabilized") and "Do NOT create a giant advertising end card." For Flash UGC remakes, one creator uses the original ad as the reference for shot order and pacing and a photo as the reference for the look, then describes when the product enters each shot.

Ports from today's non-Seedance entries: (1) period dialogue coverage (GRN-080, H3): "Fixed 180° axis, eye contact locked", hard cuts only, and "Frame freezes, end directly, no fade, no black screen" to stop end-of-clip fades; (2) first-frame stills (WRD-082, REA-083, GPT Image 2.6): the six-line SUBJECT / LIGHT / CAMERA / LOCK / NEGATIVE / TONE format makes clean Seedance first frames; for sequins and metal, the creator found the NEGATIVE line ("no blown-out speculars on the sequins") mattered most. In the Seedance prompt, state that as a positive look line (sequin highlights stay crisp); (3) a calibration shot (REA-084): "Night, heavy rain. A woman in a dark trench coat walks toward camera down a narrow alley, then stops and turns as headlights flare behind her." is a cheap three-event test to run on Flash at 480p before committing to a night-exterior look.

sections.title: 2026-11-15 additions: official Seedance 2.5 flash rules (model ID, 480p/720p only, no Draft mode, 10/5/5 references, pricing), Flash drafting in practice, one-way morph counters, object-count locks, trigger-based style switches, tape faults as story, and sound-led withholding

items.text: Official (2026-11-15, ~5:45 AM PT): the BytePlus docs now describe a "Seedance 2.5 series" = Seedance 2.5 + Seedance 2.5 flash, and the prompt guide applies to both (no separate Flash prompt rules). Flash model ID: dreamina-seedance-2-5-flash-261115 (2.5 stays dreamina-seedance-2-5-260628). Flash supports the same task types as 2.5 (text-to-video, first / first-last frame, image / video / audio / combined omni reference including audio-only, edit, extend, audio generation, return last frame), duration 4–30 s or -1, ratios 21:9 / 16:9 / 4:3 / 1:1 / 3:4 / 9:16 / adaptive, and mp4 or mov output. The differences: resolution 480p or 720p only (both 8-bit; default 720p; no 1080p), Draft mode is NOT supported ("supported only by Seedance 2.5"), and references are capped at 10 images, 5 videos and 5 audio clips (20 total vs 50 on 2.5). The edit / extend / first-frame constraints (ratio adaptive only; edit duration -1 only; source video 4–30 s) apply to the whole series.

Official pricing (resource-pack rules page): at 480p/720p Flash costs 0.0070 USD per 1K tokens without video input vs 0.0107 for Seedance 2.5 (about 35% less), and 0.0043 vs 0.0064 with video input (about 33% less); Flash has a 7-million-token resource pack with no minimum quantity. This confirms the "34% cheaper" claim from launch week. Practical rule: Flash is a 720p production model in its own right, not a Draft mode. If you need a cheap preview that can be promoted to a final with the same seed and settings, use Seedance 2.5 Draft mode (480p); if you draft on Flash, re-run the locked prompt on Seedance 2.5 for 1080p and expect a new take, not an upscale.

Flash in practice (launch day): a same-prompt test of Seedance 2.5 Flash, Seedance 2.0 and Wan 3.0 (TRN-082) shows Flash handling a long morph chain (paint burst → birds and waves → canyon fly-through → gallery pull-back) at 720p. An image-to-video tester reports that Flash at 480p held every identity marker of a character still (inner hair colour, earrings, a mole) and that three runs "came out nearly identical: predictable, in a good way. Variety has to come from the prompt, not the seed." So on Flash, vary the action or camera wording between takes instead of re-rolling, and keep the Flash-draft checklist from 2026-11-13 (duplicates, dropped orbits, skin sheen, quiet ambience).

"World Hook" prompts (TRN-082): open with one sentence that states the whole idea ("An artist flicks a brush—and the paint becomes an entire living world"), then list short visual beats in order, end with a reveal ("Final pull-back: the whole world is inside a framed painting in a gallery"), and add one line on what the shot must prove ("fluid detail, pigment texture, saturated colour, and seamless world-building"). The hook keeps a fast model on one concept through many changes.

One-way morph counters (TRN-085, 15 transformations in 30 s): the creator's notes are a reusable rule set: make every change "silhouette-level, not texture"; keep "the eye pinned in frame throughout"; give the change counters that cannot reverse ("legs 4→2→0, tail→fluke, nostrils→blowhole, 1m→30m"); and keep the camera pulling back for all 30 s "so scale is the drama". Time every beat (one every 2 s) and ban cuts, dissolves and cross-fades.

Exact object-count locks (AES-085): for object-driven stories, write a CONTINUITY line that counts everything ("One penguin, one shop, one snow globe, one ice cream cone, and exactly three cottages"), states how the hero object travels ("The penguin must carry the cone from the counter to the pedestal"), gives the order of effects ("The golden light spreads from the cone to the cottages in sequence") and bans "teleporting, duplicate objects, random transformations, or sudden scene changes". The output kept one cone and three cottages throughout.

Trigger-based style switches (TRN-084): to alternate live action and illustration, give the switch a visible trigger (a stylus tap) and keep the composition identical across both states, so each switch reads as a graphic match cut; name both styles exactly ("black-and-yellow 2D hand-drawn") and ban "random morphing" and "unexplained object changes". In-motion wardrobe changes work the same way (WRD-083): change the clothes during a continuing action (running), describe both outfits fully, add "Preserve their original faces" and ban "abrupt transformations or inconsistent outfits".

Period texture: (1) tape faults as story (GRN-083): list the faults of the format (interlaced combing on fast movement, chroma smear on red, clipped highlights, crushed blue shadows, tape noise, head-switching) and script one "camera error" as a beat (the auto-iris pumps down when light hits the face; the clip ends with the image tearing to blue-black); (2) one grade for the whole edit (GRN-084): "colour grade applied uniformly to the entire frame" plus grain, halation and bloom keeps a retro look consistent across cross dissolves; (3) sound-led withholding (GRN-082): "The sound recordings ARE the soundtrack… Do not show the woman. Do not explain the relationship" turns a short 16mm prompt into a story with a payoff.

Port from MiniMax H3 (PRF-084): for fast arguments, add a "Core tone" line ("nonstop rapid overlapping debate, fast snappy replies… minimal empty silence"), give each line a 2–3 s timecode with a hard cut, set delivery notes per actor in the character lock, and end with "Frame holds static, end directly, no fade out, no black screen". The Seedance 2.5 template on PRF-084 includes a Flash draft line (720p).

New source: renoise-ai/awesome-seedance-2-5-prompts holds about 2,850 X-sourced Seedance prompts from Jun–Sep 2026 (Seedance 2.5 launched in China on 2026-07-31), most never ingested here. Always re-read the X post: several prompts sit in a reply rather than the post, and the gallery text matched the X text verbatim in every case checked today.

sections.title: 2026-11-16 additions: official 4K output for Seedance 2.5 (10-bit H.265, Draft → 4K finals, 15 RPM / 1 concurrent), when to pay for 4K, Flash-to-2.5 drafting, one-impossible-detail dread, product-geometry locks, exact on-screen labels, brief-first spec ads, frozen-time macros

items.text: Official (2026-11-16, ~5:50 AM PT): the Seedance 2.5 series tutorial and the video-generation tutorial now list 4k as a Seedance 2.5 output resolution: 480p / 720p (8-bit), 1080p and 4k (10-bit colour, H.265/HEVC; some players need VLC, mpv or QuickTime). 4K sizes: 3840×2160 (16:9), 3326×2494 (4:3), 2880×2880 (1:1), 2494×3326 (3:4), 2160×3840 (9:16), 4398×1886 (21:9). Seedance 2.5 flash, 2.0 Fast and 2.0 Mini do not support 4K. Draft mode now finishes at "1080p or 4K" (resolution is required on the final call and is the only quality parameter you may change; prompt, references, duration, ratio, seed and audio are reused from the Draft). New 4K rate limits (Seedance 2.5 only): 15 requests per minute and 1 concurrent task for both enterprise and individual accounts (non-4K stays 600 / 10 and 180 / 3). The prompt guide itself did not change (7bf7bd78…), so 4K needs no prompt syntax: set resolution 4k on the API line.

Using 4K (community, first tests): Volcano Engine opened the 4K API in China the same day, after a month-long 20-studio trial (C1); CapCut PC exposes "Seedance 2.5 4K" outside the US (C4). A same-prompt / same-seed 30 s test at 4:3 (C2) got 3326×2494 vs 1664×1248 and found the 4K pass holds fine detail where the wind and fabric do the work (separate seed-fluff hairs, linen weave, clean shadow shapes, small facial changes) while 1080p "flattens first" there, at about 1.6× the credits. The two renders are separate samples, not one take at two sizes. Practical rule: lock the story with Draft (480p) or Flash, then spend 4K on shots with fine texture, hair, fabric or particles, and request it through the Draft → final call so the performance you approved is the one rendered.

Flash → 2.5 workflow (C3): across six prompts, Flash averaged 95 s vs 199 s per render at about two thirds of the credits and "followed all six"; the extra cost on 2.5 buys 1080p (now 4K) and up to 30 reference images. Keep the prompt identical, draft on Flash at 720p, then re-render the keeper on 2.5. Unlike Draft mode this is a new generation, so if the exact take matters, draft on Seedance 2.5 Draft instead.

One impossible detail (MOO-087): for unease, make everything ordinary and change one physical rule. Lock the format ("ONE CONTINUOUS STATIC SHOT from a ceiling-mounted security camera… The camera NEVER moves"), time the anomaly late (the shadow stays behind at 15 s and turns its head at 23 s), say "REALISM IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN DRAMA", and ban every horror cliché by name (glowing shadows, smoke, ghost effects, monsters, morphing, cinematic lighting). Mood comes from what is withheld, not from grading.

Product-geometry locks (PRP-086): describe an unbranded hero product as a spec sheet (body ratio "about 2.1:1", lens "about 68% of body height", six aperture blades, materials, seams), then forbid category drift ("never turn it into a phone, DSLR, or action camera; add no lenses, buttons, screens, grips") and the usual AI-ad tells (rainbow flare, blue-purple tech glow, mirror-like metal). Pair it with a lighting rig sentence and art-still cutaways for an industrial-design film.

Exact on-screen text in Seedance 2.5 (PRP-089): place graphics in one zone only ("Tiny white ingredient labels appear only at the very top of frame"), quote each label and its second line exactly ("garlic" above "4 cloves"), and add "spell every requested line exactly". The labels rendered cleanly over 30 s. For brand films, the opposite rule works (AES-087): keep "no text or branding until the final two seconds".

Brief-first spec ads (AES-087): put a four-line brand brief above the prompt (name, tagline, mascot, hex palette, and the "reveal mechanic": "the canyon is the bar's cross-section; the SNAP is the punchline"), then write three beats and a sound punchline (silence → SNAP → one piano note). The brief keeps the world, palette and reveal consistent.

Frozen-time macros (PRP-088): "one instant of time held perfectly still while the camera keeps moving through it" makes a bullet-time product hero; list the frozen parts (column, crown petals, ribbons, droplets), give the camera a path through them, and end on a described final frame with the camera at rest.

Motion graphics on Seedance 2.5 (AES-086): ratio the film ("80% bold graphic design in motion and 20% object action"), fix a three-colour palette, count the cuts (12 in 15 s) and name the transitions (snap zooms, ink-splash wipes); lock SFX to cuts. In the creator's three-model comparison Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3 and Gemini Omni all held the palette; check every hanzi, because the DO-NOT list ("extra glyphs, misspelled or deformed hanzi") is there for a reason.

Format-by-faults and observed behaviour (GRN-086, MOO-085): for home-video nostalgia list the camcorder faults in the order they would happen (delayed autofocus, exposure pumping as she moves to the window, awkward zooms, tape grain) and add "No polished cinematic look"; for calm lifestyle films direct the actor rather than the light: "Every movement should feel subconscious and naturally observed—never posed or performed. She never looks directly into the camera."

sections.title: 2026-11-17 additions: Runway 4K for Seedance 2.5 (100 credits/s), official Volcano Ark 4K price examples, Draft only on 2.5, PixelDojo's Flash formula and Flash limits (frames vs references), nadir layout references, inheritance-rule titles, non-reaction performance, depth-map motion refs

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-17 ~5:40 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide (7bf7bd78…), API tutorial (b964d8a7…), video-generation tutorial (58ccb89e…), agent-skills index (0451c8c7…; sd25-pe still read only), resource-pack rules (c606f553…; still no 2.5 4K token line) and Seedream 5.5 tutorial (03d680a2…) are unchanged. llms.txt changed (fdf8e5dd… → fa716a1e…) only by an inference-methods summary rewrite and a new "Online inference (low latency)" page (service_tier=fast, for LLM endpoints). No new prompt syntax today.

Runway (article updated 2026-11-17 3:37 AM PT): Seedance 2.5 in Runway now renders 480p, 720p, 1080p and 4K. 4K costs 100 credits per second (+55 per second of input video) against 68 (+34) at 1080p, so a 4K final costs about 1.5x a 1080p one. Audio references can each be up to 30 s; in Tools every reference video must be at least 2 s long. With Duration set to Auto the estimate reads "Up to X credits": Runway charges for the longest duration and refunds what the clip did not use. Drafts in Runway are still 480p only and "Enhance Draft" still produces 1080p, not 4K.

Official Volcano Ark 4K prices (Volcengine price examples, reported by TechNode on 2026-11-17): a 5 s 16:9 clip with no video input costs about ¥30.13 at 4K, ¥18.71 at 1080p and ¥3.36 at 480p. With a video input the same 4K clip costs about ¥33.24–129.28, depending on the input length. Draft (样片) is billed at 480p and the final is billed separately at its own resolution. The 4K model was released 2026-10-23 to about 20 studios, and the API opened to everyone on 2026-11-16. Rule of thumb: run blocking on 480p Draft (about 1/9 the cost of 4K) and render 4K only for the approved take.

Official capability table (Volcengine zh tutorial): Draft/样片 mode is available only on Seedance 2.5 (not 2.5 flash or any 2.0 model). The 2.5 series outputs mp4 or mov, while 2.0 outputs mp4 only. Seedance 2.5 renders 1080p and 4K at 10-bit, while Seedance 2.0 renders 1080p at 8-bit (4K 10-bit). Durations are 4–30 s or -1 for the 2.5 series and 4–15 s for 2.0. Reference caps: 2.5 = 50 (30/10/10), 2.5 flash = 20 (10/5/5), 2.0 family = 15 (9/3/3).

PixelDojo's Flash formula (works on Seedance 2.5 too, since Flash uses the same prompt language): "[shot size + camera move]. [specific subject] [one action beat], [environment], [light], [lens or film texture]. Sound: [what is heard], no music." Give the subject two or three visible details, keep one action per 5 s clip, and end with a named soundscape plus "no music" when you want only real sound. Dialogue goes in quotes or {braces} with the speaker, delivery and language ("says softly in American English: {…}"). For 9:16, open the prompt with the word "vertical" and keep the subject centred (REA-089, PRF-088, PRP-090, TRN-091).

Flash limits from the partner guide: up to 10 reference images, 5 videos and 5 audio tracks (2.5: 30/10/10), 480p/720p only, 4–30 s or Auto. Frames and references cannot be mixed in one request: pick a start frame (or start + end frame) when the first picture matters most, and references when you need the same person, product or voice across the clip. A start frame or reference video also sets the output's shape. In PixelDojo's six-prompt test Flash rendered in 95 s on average against 199 s for 2.5, at 20 vs 30 credits per 5 s 720p clip, and "both followed every prompt". Caveat from a creator test: Flash blinked in 1 of 3 eyes-open takes where 2.5 held all 3, and the retries erased Flash's savings, so draft on Flash only when the shot tolerates small misses.

Layout references (TRN-090): a 90-degree nadir (top-down) image of the set gives Seedance 2.5 the whole room's geometry, so the space stays consistent while an FPV camera whips, orbits and crash-zooms. Pair it with an object sheet for the hero product and assign roles explicitly ("Image 1 is the car… Image 2 is only a layout guide for the room's geometry"). Wipe all text off the layout image ("models love copying labels into the video") and repeat "zero lettering, signage or overlays anywhere in the room". Land each upgrade on a downbeat and end on the opening hero frame.

Inheritance-rule title sequences (TRN-088): one governing sentence ("every shot must inherit one visual object, shape, texture, or typographic element from the previous shot, and that inherited element must transform into the central subject of the next composition") produced a 30 s, 4K-posted title chain (sphere → ring → ORIGIN → iris → MATTER → LIGHT → CONTINUUM). Close with what you are testing: "long-range visual continuity, transformation logic, object permanence and design memory rather than … beautiful independent shots".

Non-reaction as performance (PRF-086): state the rule in capitals ("He NEVER looks up from his phone at any point, no matter what happens, until the final seconds"), lock the camera, and let the world do the work. Cut the sound on each door close ("the battle sound cuts off instantly, back to soft hum") and keep a persistent prop as proof of time passing (the arrow "stays embedded in the wall for the rest of the film"). For object-morph chains (TRN-086), list the order explicitly and tie the sound to each change: "each time the instrument changes, so does the sound".

Depth-map motion references (community; not ingested): to transfer only the motion and edit of a clip, feed its depth map as @Video1 and scope it: "@Video1 = depth map, motion and edit only: no grey figures, no grey walls; the person takes face, hair and clothing only from @Video2". Also tell the model that letterbox bands carry no depth: "the soft blurred grey bands … are letterbox padding, not scene geometry". The creator drafts on Flash at 480p and re-renders on Seedance 2.5 at 1080p once the motion is right. Only use footage you have rights to.

Cross-model doc-look tip (community; model not stated on the clip): shoot comedy "like a wildlife documentary": long telephoto lens, slight handheld shake, shallow depth of field and a hushed push-in. The creator's notes say "telephoto lens" and "handheld shake" do most of the documentary look, and that the models "handle one clear beat much better than three". This is the same one-action rule as PixelDojo's Flash formula.

sections.title: 2026-11-18 additions: official SeedAudio 1.5 prompt skill (how to write Seedance sound lines), locked-state performances, Flash vs 2.5 on hands, garments and anime, camera-fault texture instead of grain, Kling Image 4.0 start frames

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-18 ~5:38 AM PT): the prompt guide (7bf7bd78…), API tutorial (b964d8a7…), llms.txt (fa716a1e…), video-generation tutorial (58ccb89e…), resource-pack rules (c606f553…; still no 2.5 4K token line), Seedream 5.5 tutorial (03d680a2…) and the Runway article (878ea11d…, updated 2026-11-17 3:37 AM PT) are unchanged. The agent-skills index changed (0451c8c7… → 416f71bf…) only by one new official skill: seed-audio-1-5-pe v0.0.1, a SeedAudio 1.5 prompt optimizer that "also covers converting Seedance or other visual prompts into sound scripts". It was read but not installed or run. Its SKILL.md tells agents to run a self-update command; that was not done. No new Seedance prompt syntax today.

Writing the Sound line, per the official SeedAudio skill's "Converting visual scripts into sound scripts" rules (written for SeedAudio, but they map directly onto Seedance 2.5's 【Sound】 block). Keep explicit sounds and sounds the actions directly cause (footsteps, a bowl set down, tyres on gravel), using only the materials the prompt names. Add only the minimum spatial bed (tunnel reflections, driving airflow). Do not add sounds from association alone: "after rain" is not rain, a bottle close-up is not a spray, an orbiting camera is not a whoosh, high speed is not gear changes, and film grain is not noise. Ad, travel or suspense purposes allow a little fitting music. Realistic dialogue, ASMR and small foley do not need a score. "No subtitles" does not mean "no dialogue", and on-screen text is not spoken. The skill's worked example: "A 5-second travel ad. Wide shot of waves… Slow camera push, 4K. No voices or music." becomes "Waves wash onto the beach with a soft swell, a clear breaking rush, and a gentle receding wash… No voices or music."

SeedAudio 1.5 (the skill's provisional limits, not a formal API spec): generation up to 6 minutes (360 s), prompts up to 10,000 characters, up to 6 audio references and 1 video reference (usable together), 1 image reference that cannot be combined with audio/video, and up to 6 extracted stems from a source mix. Use timestamps "[start s:end s]" only for intervals you actually specify; a total duration does not mean the model should split the time by shot. This points to a Seedance → SeedAudio flow: generate picture on Seedance 2.5 and score or re-dub it with the same prompt, rewritten as sound only.

Locked-state performance (PRF-089): for crying, exhaustion or injury makeup, write the state as a PREMISE that is "ALREADY PRESENT IN THE FIRST FRAME and stays constant", then list the only things allowed to change ("facial muscle position, tear fluid, breathing movement, hair position, cloth position, and wet gloss on skin") and forbid progression ("no progressive reddening… no swelling developing"). Seedance 2.5 then acts with the face muscles instead of animating the redness in. Pair it with a handheld long lens, focus locked on the near eye, and a blurred background that never resolves.

Fine-motor actions plus a line (PRF-091, one take per model, same 5 s vertical prompt): Seedance 2.5 Flash did the one-handed crack, the whole yolk and the line word for word, but cut between four shots despite "phone video, filmed by a friend". Seedance 2.5 held one take, but the shell never broke. Kling 4 cut away before the crack, and Gemini Omni Flash 1.2 used two hands and shortened the line. Fixes for Seedance: add "one continuous take, no cuts" explicitly, and state the physical result as its own beat ("the shell splits in half; the yolk drops whole into the pan").

Garment fidelity, Flash vs 2.5 (WRD-089, PixelDojo): with "an emerald velvet suit", Flash rendered the full dark-emerald velvet suit, while Seedance 2.5 gave a bright green velvet jacket over a white shirt and dark trousers. Name every garment's colour and fabric separately ("emerald velvet jacket and matching emerald velvet trousers") when the whole outfit matters. In the other two PixelDojo pairs, the boxer (PRF-092) and the anime canal courier (AES-090), both models kept the look. PixelDojo times: Flash 84/90/103 s vs 2.5 156/197/210 s, at 20 vs 30 credits per 5 s 720p clip.

Emotion through physics and sound (PRF-090, MOO-088): a zero-gravity two-hander shows grief with tears that "lift off his cheek and float", keeps vacuum exteriors silent, and holds the score until the pod hatch closes. A midnight-ramen piece states the arc in one sentence ("from cold, tired isolation toward warmth and comfort"), makes steam a motif that grows until it surrounds the final bowl, and uses foley only (rain on glass, gas ignition, knife on wood). For calm moods (MOO-089), give each 3–4 s beat its own sound cue; a "FEEL" line such as "warm in feeling but cool in tone" sets the grade without naming one.

Texture from camera behaviour, not a grain filter (GRN-088): a compact-digital-camera home video asked for "slight autofocus hunting", short exposure shifts going indoors and outdoors, mild digital noise, soft detail, compression artefacts and framing that drifts and corrects, and it said "No artificial film grain", "no gimbal". This is the same "imperfections come from the camera's behaviour, not graphics" rule as the DV entries. For stills you will animate, Kling Image 4.0's official guide makes the same point: "Edges are soft before grain is applied, so the result feels genuinely photographic rather than a sharp digital portrait covered in noise."

Kling Image 4.0 as a start-frame source (new model, API live 2026-11-17, user guide 2026-11-18): native 2K/4K/8K stills, up to 10 references, and a Series Mode that plans up to 10 consistent storyboard frames in one run. Its official templates write composition in numbers ("tilted 45 degrees to the left", "face… more than 50% of the image", foreground "approximately 45%"), which carries into Seedance image-to-video. GRN-089 has a Seedance 2.5 adapted template. Keep Seedance's own rules: the first frame sets the ratio, and frames and references cannot be mixed.

sections.title: 2026-11-19 additions: official portrait-asset routes (asset:// characters, trusted outputs), scene replacement in an existing edit, Flash dialogue audio, references vs keyframes, measured camera offsets, liquid speed-ramps

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-19 ~5:38 AM PT): prompt guide (7bf7bd78…), API tutorial (b964d8a7…), agent-skills index (416f71bf…) and resource-pack rules (c606f553…; still no 2.5 4K token line) are unchanged. llms.txt changed (fa716a1e… → 738aaed2…) only in reworded page descriptions; the video-generation tutorial (→ d231f082…) and Seedream 5.5 tutorial (→ fbc2e3ea…) changed only model-list anchor links. Runway's Seedance 2.5 article was edited 2026-11-18 1:35 PM PT, removing one overview sentence; nothing about prompting changed. No new prompt syntax today.

Faces in references (official portrait-asset page, newly covered here): Seedance 2.5 and 2.0 do not accept uploaded reference images or videos containing real human faces. The page gives three routes: (1) preset digital characters from the ModelArk digital-character library, passed as asset://<asset ID>; (2) trusted outputs: your own original, unedited ModelArk outputs from the same account within 30 days can be fed back in (Seedance 2.x face videos since 2026-03-11; their last frames and Seedream 5.0 lite/pro/flash text-to-image faces since 2026-04-16); (3) authorized real-person assets after real-person verification. Compressing or forwarding a file can break the trust check, so save originals straight to TOS. Output URLs expire after 24 hours.

Naming assets in the prompt (official rule): refer to an asset by type and order among assets of the same type in the request ("the beauty influencer in Image 1"), never by its ID ("asset-2026**** is a beauty influencer" is the incorrect form). PRP-093 is the official example: a preset character as Image 1 and a product photo as Image 2, plus a spoken line in single quotes. In the Model Playground the same references are written "@Image1"; the Playground makes four clips per request by default, and BytePlus recommends one per request to save cost.

Trusted-output edit (official): the page's second example feeds the PRP-093 video back in and asks only "Change the color of the cream to white. Change the ratio to 16:9." The output re-frames the 9:16 spot as 16:9 and recolours the product while keeping the face, line and timing. Use this for quick colourway and aspect variants of an approved Seedance take without re-uploading a face.

Bad takes (official, BytePlus only): after opting in to Model Generations Quality Diagnostics in the console, a failed Seedance 2.x generation can be reported by task_id through CasePlatformV1BadcaseReport within 72 hours. Reported cases are kept for evaluation and "not used to train models". This is not available on Volcengine.

Scene replacement inside an existing edit (REA-096, Dreamina partnership): the prompt asks for "a hyper-realistic cinematic replacement scene for the existing Seattle video", with the original character image, the existing video and a location still as references. It is three timed hard cuts with dialogue, and then a block of continuity rules: a prop locked to one hand ("yellow flowers remain in Woman 1's LEFT hand"), every object transfer visible ("phone must never appear simultaneously in two people's hands except during the physical handoff"), and a final priority line for the physical order ("offer → receive phone → photograph → return phone → joke → walk away"). Burned-in subtitles are specified like a style sheet (font, weight, hex colours, box opacity, px sizes at 1080×1440).

Flash for dialogue (community test, same prompt, reference and settings; 19 s at 480p on Pollo): Seedance 2.5 cost 159 credits and Flash 102. Mannerisms and facial acting were nearly identical. Seedance 2.5 won on spatial audio (the voice "belongs in the room") and voice quality; Flash showed voice artefacts and jumbled a few words. The tester's workflow: on Flash, write acting directions very explicitly, replace the voice with your own recording or a TTS voiceover, and add ambience in the edit.

References are not keyframes: a Kling 4.0 macro film (REA-093) says "Use the nine supplied images as ordinary visual references, not time-locked keyframes". That is also Seedance 2.5's model: reference images guide identity and look, while first/last frames pin time, and the two cannot be mixed in one request. The adapted template for REA-093 uses the stills as references with no first_frame. Its negative list targets macro failures ("no sudden takeoff, extra insects, deformed anatomy, artificial sparkles").

Measured camera language for one-take chases (community, guide only; not ingested because the gag passes a projectile close to a child): the camera "flies 45 cm (1.5 feet) behind the dart's tail, at the same speed… matching its speed within 5%", field of view is fixed per segment ("0.0 to 0.9s at 47°, 0.9s to 30.0s at 63°"), and every target sits on one straight flight line with distances and speeds in metres and km/h. Numbers like these keep a 30 s follow-cam consistent where adjectives drift.

Liquid speed-ramps for drinks ads (PRP-091): write the ramp as named phases (real time → "super slow motion" → near-frozen → "Time Snaps Back to Normal"), give the camera a different behaviour in each (aggressive handheld outside, a smooth orbit inside), and add physics guard lines: "perfect preservation of glass shape, liquid volume and ice clarity", "sharp motion blur only on actively moving elements", "no floating garnish after time resumes", and "no magical glow or fantasy visuals".

Documentary stills as start frames (Kling Image 4.0 official, REA-090..092, AES-091): the guide's documentary template is "Subject's identity + Physical appearance and clothing + Specific actions/interactions + Everyday setting", and it says describing an action ("sleeping on a bus") works better than "realistic". Its examples fix camera height, list what sits on each edge of the frame, give the light direction, and end with what must not change ("No sunlight, romantic lens flare, empty platform, or frontal view of the subject"). In Seedance image-to-video, keep the motion small (a sip, a hand-off, a passing train) so the documentary look holds.

sections.title: 2026-11-20 additions: official 4096×2160 reference-video ceiling, physical object-swap transitions, walk-through morphs, outfit sequences without morphing, restraint and laughter performance, lighting ratios in start frames

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-20 ~5:41 AM PT): prompt guide (7bf7bd78…), agent-skills index (416f71bf…), resource-pack rules (c606f553…; still no 2.5 4K token line), portrait-asset guide (ea3ecbd7…), digital-character library, badcase API, Seedream 5.5 tutorial and the Runway article (c019a55d…) are unchanged. llms.txt (738aaed2… → c36f0eb5…) only renames the "Coding Plan" heading. The one substantive change is in the Seedance 2.5 tutorial (b964d8a7… → 6437d62d…) and the video-generation tutorial (d231f082… → 58d2aaff…), below. No new prompt syntax.

Reference videos up to 4096 × 2160 (official, new today): for the Seedance 2.5 series the total pixel count of each input video is now [614 × 664 = 407,696, 4096 × 2160 = 8,847,360]; the 2.0 series stays at 3326 × 2494 = 8,295,044. UHD 3840 × 2160 already fitted, so the practical gain is that DCI-4K camera originals (4096 × 2160) can go in as reference or edit sources without a downscale. Other video-input limits are unchanged: aspect ratio 0.4–2.5, each side 300–6000 px, 2–30 s per video (4–30 s for editing tasks), 30 s total, 200 MB, 24–60 fps, up to 10 videos (5 on 2.5 flash).

Physical match transitions (TRN-093): set one rule, that every scene change is an object becoming another object while its motion continues, and write each swap as "without the [flight / spin / stretching] ever stopping, A becomes B". Pair the camera across each swap (a rise following the can turns into a fall following the ball; a push into the spinning ball becomes a pull-back from the spinning record), carry one through-colour (orange) through every object, put a hard snare hit on each swap, and close with a ban list: "no cuts, no wipes, no occlusion transitions, no whip pans, no fades, no cross dissolves, no random morphing". The creator's notes: throw the object out of frame first to give the model room to swap it mid-air, and match the spin speed on both sides of a rotation swap.

Walk-through morphs (TRN-092): tie the transformation to the subject's own movement ("The transformation follows her movement like she's walking between two worlds") and name each pair that changes: landscape (bare forest → frozen lake with a manor), path (snowy path → icy shoreline), wardrobe (red scarf → red skirt; the coat gains a hood) and the framing device (impasto paint frame, wave → leaf). Finish with "smooth continuous motion, no scene cuts".

Outfit sequences without morphing (WRD-096): when the garment change should be a cut rather than a transformation, say so twice. Cuts happen "while the camera is stationary", "Outfits change only through clean cuts... No morphing or clothing transformations on her body", and each new look starts "from the exact camera position where the previous scene ended" as the orbit continues another 60°. The subject "stays in place and does not spin around her own axis", so the orbit reads as camera movement. A one-second black, silent beat sets up the payoff look. The X post adds caption cards in the edit, so those are not model output. WRD-095 is the montage version: ten named looks for one shirt, each with its pairing, and the transition types listed (whip pans, spin transitions, snap cuts, match cuts).

Performance through restraint (PRF-093): two lines of dialogue, beats timed to the second, "natural human performances", and an ending that has to land on the face, not on text: "The final recognition must come from the woman's reaction and the physical station sign"; "The station name should be visible but not digitally overlaid". Music is held back until the train reaches the countryside. For laughter (PRF-094, Magnific's Seedance 2.5 example), stage the laugh as beats with end positions ("end: both just outside the doorway, hand still on shoulder") and describe the audio as performance: "genuine overlapping male laughter, breathless/wheezing", with dialogue between laughs.

The garment as the only light source (WRD-094): a short prompt (a bioluminescent gold silk ballgown, a pitch-black underwater trench, "illuminated only by her golden dress", "OLED blacks") is enough for a 30 s fashion film, because one wardrobe idea defines the light, the contrast and the motion (underwater physics on dress and hair).

Lighting ratios in start frames (AES-093): GPT Image 2.5 stills follow lighting written like a gaffer's note. The light is named by its tool ("a hard optical spotlight and a narrow slit gobo"), the fill is given in stops ("approximately three stops below the red accent"), the band has to follow the face ("changing width across the nose, breaking into shadow where the face occludes it") and there is a clipping guard ("do not clip the red channel"). In the Seedance 2.5 image-to-video template the camera stays locked and a small head turn makes the band slide across the face, which keeps the lighting design intact.

Seedance 2.0 numbered shot lists on 2.5 (MOO-093): a 2.0 prompt written as "SCENE & SHOTS: 1… 6…" with a VISUAL STYLE and an IMPORTANT block maps directly onto 2.5's structure: keep the six shots in order as a 【Shots】 block, move the look into 【Visuals】, give each shot type one camera behaviour, and add a 【Sound】 line, which the 2.0 prompt did not have.

sections.title: 2026-11-21 additions: FOV degrees for lens compression, one-take time freeze and rewind, rhythm change as a mood device, window-as-frame era transitions, repeated look blocks per shot

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-21 ~5:40 AM PT): prompt guide (7bf7bd78…), series tutorial (6437d62d…), video-generation tutorial (58d2aaff…), agent-skills index (416f71bf…), resource-pack rules (c606f553…; still no 2.5 4K token line), Seedream 5.5 tutorial (fbc2e3ea…), portrait-asset guide (ea3ecbd7…), digital-character library (938dde5b…), badcase API (ff4729b5…) and the Runway article (body c019a55d…, updated_at still 2026-11-18 1:35 PM PT) are unchanged. llms.txt changed only in one Managed Agents heading. No new Seedance prompt syntax.

FOV degrees as a lens control (PRF-096): instead of shot-size words alone, give each cut a field of view and let it tighten as the scene intensifies: 45° medium two-shot, 30° over-the-shoulder, 20° tight close-ups, then about 48° for the wide return. Lower degrees mean a tighter, more compressed telephoto look (the creator maps 45° ≈ 45 mm, 30° ≈ 70 mm, 20° ≈ 100 mm). Pair it with framing marks ("short-sided" close-ups on the 33% / 67% verticals, faces inside 90% action-safe) and dialogue hygiene: a voice lock per character, blinks every 2–3 s, "only the active speaker's mouth moves". The creator measured about 85% FOV accuracy in a single 30 s generation; the wide return cuts snapped back to the reference booth.

One-take time freeze and rewind (PRF-095): freeze everyone except one character ("Time locks completely. Only the young woman in the front keeps moving"), give that character a deadpan action chain (eye-roll, mouthed line, unwraps gum, chews), then direct the reverse as its own beat ("The rewind is controlled and elegant… returns exactly to the moment…") and release time at full speed at the end. Bracketed shot labels per time block ([Medium Shot], [Dynamic Tracking], [Slow Orbital + Detail]) kept a 30 s 4K continuous take readable.

Rhythm change as a mood device (MOO-094): write the camera plan as an escalation curve and then break it on purpose: stable wide and medium shots while things are normal, tighter framing and more handheld instability as the threat grows, then "the instant the elevator reaches -100, completely change the rhythm. Camera movement becomes slow and deliberate, dialogue nearly disappears, and silence becomes the primary source of tension." Hold the threat back with sound only ("suggest its existence only through distant impacts, vibrations, structural sounds") and lock a visible continuity counter (the floor indicator sequence) so the model keeps the story order.

Window-as-frame era transitions (TRN-094): lock the camera beside one window for the whole clip (20% passengers, 80% outside), ban cuts and effects ("No portals, magic, glowing effects"), and change only the world beyond the glass every 3–4 s on a timed list of eras. A reaction arc for one passenger (curiosity → confusion → surprise → disbelief → awe) and a soundscape that "gradually evolves with each era" carry the transition; the last line ties it together: "Historical transitions must remain spatially continuous through the same bus window."

Period single takes (MOO-095): four time blocks with one camera behaviour each (low-angle tracking gallop → fluid steadicam follow onto the boat → drift → slow push-in on the face) plus a short look block ("ARRI Alexa look, anamorphic feel, rich film grain, deep shadows, volumetric moonlight") and "Sound: only natural" are enough for a 30 s mood piece; the mood is also stated at the end ("Mood: urgent, mysterious…").

Repeat the look block in every shot when grain and flare must match across cuts (GRN-093, LTX): the creator's prompt repeats the same light (one hard warm sun upper right, warm bounce, cool sky fill) and the same lens texture ("anamorphic film look: vertical oval bokeh… soft edge falloff, fine daylight film grain, wide 2.39:1 framing") after each hard cut, and puts the one flare only on the wide shot. The Seedance 2.5 template for GRN-093 keeps that block in 【Visuals】 with a "repeat in every shot" instruction.

sections.title: 2026-11-22 additions: link beats with continuous camera moves, screen-direction lineups, transition verbs in shot lists, two-sentence mood openers, UGC ad structure, community realism checklist

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-22 ~5:45 AM PT): prompt guide (7bf7bd78…), series tutorial (6437d62d…), video-generation tutorial (58d2aaff…), llms.txt (54b9896d…), agent-skills index (416f71bf…), resource-pack rules (c606f553…; still no 2.5 4K token line), Seedream 5.5 tutorial (fbc2e3ea…), portrait-asset guide (ea3ecbd7…), digital-character library (938dde5b…), badcase API (ff4729b5…) and the Runway article body (c019a55d…, updated_at still 2026-11-18) are all byte-identical to 2026-11-21. No new official Seedance syntax. The official docs still list no HDR / dynamic-range parameter (Kling 4.0 added one on 2026-11-19; see the Kling card).

Link beats with continuous camera moves (TRN-095): in a per-second beat sheet, start every beat with a camera verb (glide, crane up, push in, pull back, tilt up, track, pan, whip, drop, rise) and add one global rule: "Where no cut is specified, link adjacent beats through continuous camera movement." Then write "cut" only where you want a hard cut ("On a horn blast, cut head-on…", "Cut straight overhead"). The same creator words it as "Carry a camera move across second marks whenever the action continues." This stops 1 s beats from turning into thirty jump cuts while keeping the timing exact. For a key stunt, say it explicitly: "Track sideways without a cut."

Screen direction for groups (TRN-095): fix the lineup once and state how it flips with the camera: "@ Image5 elf always stands at @ Image1 Crimson Knight's left side… From behind, the elf is on frame left; from the front, the elf is on frame right." Also cap appearances ("Only @ Image2 and @ Image3 appear in ranks. @ Image1, @ Image4, @ Image5 and @ Image6 each appear only once"), give scale in metres ("3 m gray brutes", "One 10 m giant, measured to its horn tips"), and ask for readable beats ("Show contact before dust rises", "Hold that silhouette long enough to read"). Bloodless rules ("Fallen enemies collapse into dust. No visible wounds") keep battle content usable for ads.

Write the transition into each shot line (TRN-097): a compact line format, "SHOT n: size, lens + move / action / SFX", where the move names the join: "Match cut into her filling a transparent water bottle…", "Whip pan transition as she walks…", "Rhythmic cut into her walking towards the squat rack…". Useful for lifestyle montages where the edit rhythm is part of the brief.

Two-sentence mood openers (MOO-096): when the look and the people are fixed by reference sheets, the opening shot can be as short as "Extreme close-up of rain drops sliding down a big window glass, city neon lights blurred behind. The camera slowly pushes in through the glass into a dark, quiet apartment." Write the push through the glass as one move; the sound bed (rain, kettle, vinyl crackle) carries the mood.

UGC ad structure (PRP-096): name a fictional brand and print it on the packaging ("PRINTPOP MINI"), specify the product as materials and parts (matte-sand-beige body, brushed rose-gold accents, illuminated power button, LED battery indicator, paper output slot), then write 5–6 timed shots, each with a framing tag, one action, one dialogue line and an SFX line, and end on a hero product shot. Close with a style list ("Ultra-realistic smartphone footage", "Fast-paced jump cuts", "Consistent product design across every shot").

Light-ribbon outfit change (TRN-096, Seedance 2.0 port): put the change at a motivated spot (a shop window showing the new garment), describe it as "glowing red light trails swirl around her body… Her outfit transforms seamlessly from white into a sophisticated red sleeveless dress", and keep walking after it so the change sits mid-shot. The 2.5 adaptation keeps the change inside one continuous tracking move.

Community realism checklist (third-party GitHub skill, not official): six pillars to write as visible or audible detail instead of words like "cinematic / 4K / premium": capture medium (35 mm film look, fine grain, soft highlights, handheld breathing, natural motion blur), skin and materials (pores, sweat, stray hairs, worn fabric), spatial anchoring (numbers, left/right positions, distances), physical cause and effect (force → contact → reaction → follow-through), breathing and micro-expressions instead of emotion words, and synced dialogue. Its rules: write each dialogue line once at the moment it is spoken, with the mouth visible (it reports silent renders when only "generate sound effects" was written); time segments to 0.1 s ("[03.0-05.5s]"); one shot, one action per segment; write it as flowing prose, not labelled checklists. This conflicts in style with the official 【】 block format; treat it as an option for dialogue-led live action.

sections.title: 2026-11-23 additions: camera-fault realism in montages, stillness against a moving crowd, one-speaker dialogue with a sound-only creature, gravity anchors for folding worlds, build-order reveals, repeated touch triggers, narration-only fashion films, home-movie look blocks

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-23 ~5:50 AM PT): the prompt guide, series tutorial, video-generation tutorial, portrait-asset guide and Seedream 5.5 tutorial are byte-identical to the 2026-11-22 copies; llms.txt changed only in summaries of unrelated (LLM / understanding) pages. No new official Seedance syntax.

Camera faults as a realism block (REA-098): for candid montages, write the camera's imperfections, not "realistic": "Do not use a single camera angle or continuous take. Handheld documentary style… Slightly imperfect framing, subtle handheld shake, tiny reframing adjustments, gentle exposure breathing, and autofocus that settles half a beat late." Pair it with a shot count and length ("Total of 12 shots, 30 seconds") so the model cuts like an observational edit.

Stillness against a moving crowd (PRF-099): state both halves of the contrast and who is still: "everyone behind her begins moving in perfect synchronization — sharp head turns, shoulder jerks, folding forward and snapping upright… The woman does not move at all while the entire crowd moves behind her." Then add one slow push-in with focus held on her and depth-of-field blur on the crowd.

One speaker, one sound-only creature (PRF-097): assign voices explicitly: "Natural English dialogue for Daisy only, accurate lip-sync. The dragon NEVER speaks; it only makes giggles, gulps, whimpers, squeaks and purrs." Lock the creature's size against the set ("about as tall as a two-story house, much taller than the tent") and list who may appear ("Only Daisy and the dragon appear…"). Useful for mascots and pets in spots. (Matches the official "Character's line (emotion)" dialogue format for the speaking character.)

Gravity anchor for world-bending moves (TRN-101): when the environment folds, name what stays physical: "The woman always stays under normal gravity while the world folds around her. Continuous camera motion, no hard cuts." Then give the camera its own transformation per range ("The camera slowly rolls 90 degrees. The alley wall becomes the ground beneath her feet").

Build-order assembly reveals (TRN-099): write the reveal in the order the parts appear: blob → tendrils → "chassis and engine up" → "Body panels fold seamlessly into place" → "the LED headlights flash on". A launch-film beat for cars, devices or packaging.

Repeated touch trigger (TRN-100): one gesture, many payoffs (touch a leaf, a cone, a drain, a poster, a manhole; each becomes a new world), and protect the realism of the frame around the magic: "Use realistic smartphone footage, not glossy CGI or cinematic color grading", with the creator's own exclusions (smoke, melting, random effects, warped buildings).

Narration-only fashion film (WRD-097): "The narrator must speak throughout the film, synchronized with the corresponding visuals. Do not add character dialogue. Keep the narration clear and audible above the background music." The creator also writes "Duration: EXACTLY 30 SECONDS"; per the official guide, set the duration in the API parameters as well, since parameters belong outside the prompt body.

Home-movie look block (GRN-096): "4:3 vintage home-movie framing. Warm faded colors, gentle film grain, dust, subtle flicker, imperfect exposure, slightly soft optics, and occasional focus hunting. Natural handheld camera movement, imperfect framing". The last beat ends the clip like a real reel: "briefly loses focus, and ends abruptly like an old family recording."

Stop storyboard or reference leakage (AES-098): when a prompt was built from boards, say so up front: "IMPORTANT: Do not display, recreate, trace, reference, or imitate any storyboard, sketch, reference image, panel, annotation, or source material." (Complements the official FAQ fix for duplicated storyboard frames.)

Third-party summary that agrees with the official guide (HelloGen, 2026-11-14): order the prompt as references → one-sentence summary → plot by continuous timestamps or Shot N → notes that stay constant (character, place, camera, sound); keep time ranges continuous (the official guide warns against "0-3s… 5-6s…" gaps); ask for "No subtitles" / "No BGM" in plain words; set length, ratio and resolution in the settings. Their own tip, not official: one beat and one camera move per time range.

New community index: BravoNeo/awesome-seedance-2-5-prompts (updated 2026-11-18) lists 190 Seedance 2.5 X posts. Its prompts are marked "adapted", so the library reads the original X post for every verbatim prompt (15 of today's 26 entries came through this index).

sections.title: 2026-11-24 additions: numbers instead of adjectives, the failure modes that turn a take into cuts, POSITIVE LOCKS, practical-light and contrast-ratio lighting, end states, one camera axis for drops, colour-wave morphs, previs blocking

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-24 ~6:10 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide page now shows "Last updated: November 24, 2026", but its Markdown and the series tutorial differ from the 2026-11-23 copies only in whitespace and indentation. No new official Seedance syntax.

Numbers instead of adjectives (REA-100, Nabilidosoo thread): write speeds, distances and sizes ("gallops… at 35 km/h", "40-60 cm in front of the cat's face", "lower edge sits 3 meters above the lawn") and use real gravity (9.8 m/s2) for falls. The same thread says to write the prompt second by second and add something new every 2 s.

What turns one take into cuts (same thread): sharp camera turns become cuts, physically impossible actions make the model change shot, a still moment in the prompt makes the video stop, and references without limits bring in characters you did not ask for. Fix: scope each reference ("camera format reference only… The cat's identity comes only from @image1").

POSITIVE LOCKS block (REA-100): end the prompt with the rules that must hold in every frame, written positively ("From 1.6s to the very last frame the cat's right paw grips the camera… The dachshund is the only dog in the video… The only spoken words are the owner's four lines"). Then run 2-3 takes of the same prompt before rewriting. This matches the official advice to use positive descriptions.

Light like a set (Reddit, cinematographer): two short lines change how Seedance 2.5 lights a shot: "Practical in-scene lighting only." and a key-to-fill ratio such as "12:1 contrast ratio." The poster notes that the ratios are not measured stops, but the line changes the result.

Write the end state, and keep talking apart from doing (ChatCut): say where each motion stops ("settles into a still pool", "returns to the opening wide view"), give each action its own time range (two actions in 3 s usually loses one), and put dialogue and precise hand work in separate shots. Describe the sound, since Seedance 2.5 always generates audio. Draft at 480p (4.84 credits per 10 s against 26.89 at 1080p in their test).

Beat pacing for long takes (eroq): about one beat every 4-6 s (two beats for 10 s, five or six for 30 s), joined with "then / as / a moment later / by the end", and one camera move that develops over the take. Do not re-describe an @mentioned face (it pulls away from the reference); describe outfit and props instead.

One camera axis for drops (REA-101): pin camera, object and target on one vertical line ("The camera, snow boulder, and center of the lava lake are stacked along one vertical line") and state the physics ("a vertical free fall… no sideways momentum") so the model does not drift sideways.

Draft, then upscale (WRD-100): the creator drafts in Seedance 2.5 and upscales only the chosen take to 4K; the prompt itself asks for "no film grain, no motion blur on the costume details" so macro material texture survives the upscale.

Colour-wave morph (TRN-102): keep the material style fixed and move only the colour, giving it a direction and a time ("over 3 seconds… flows like a warm wave from foreground to background"), then let the motion start after the morph completes.

JSON prompts work (AES-102): a JSON object with camera, environment, a timeline array (time / scene / action / camera) and a negative_prompt list gave a clean 10 s diorama. Per the official guide, keep length, ratio and resolution in the API parameters even if the JSON repeats them.

Previs blocking for camera control (no prompt shared): @bekavisuals blocks the move in Blender and renders it in Seedance 2.5 as a one-shot ad; @EugenioFierro3 posted a similar 3D-previs to Seedream 5.5 to Seedance 2.5 workflow for "Bee 4K" (prompt held back behind a comment gate). This supports the official advice to use video references for camera moves.

sections.title: 2026-11-25 additions: prompt the camera operator, per-beat performance blocks, face-only references with an itemised wardrobe lock, hand-assignment locks, locked-camera hard cuts, MAGI-2 timing comparison

items.text: Official re-check (2026-11-25 ~6:20 AM PT): the BytePlus prompt guide and series tutorial Markdown differ from the 2026-11-24 copies only in whitespace. No new official Seedance syntax.

Prompt the person filming, not only the scene (REA-102, @mad_mask): give the camera operator a behaviour: "The person filming is reacting to the situation, not anticipating it", "The camera operator reacts slightly late, instinctively moving the phone to follow the pigeon", then "starts laughing, causing subtle camera shaking". The late reaction is what sells the clip as real phone footage. Pair it with "The character never anticipates the unexpected event."

Operator flaws as the grain recipe (GRN-100): for an early-2000s DV look, list the operator faults (strong handshake, imperfect framing, autofocus hunting, exposure shifts, accidental zooms, "her friend zooms awkwardly toward her face") plus "No stabilization, drone footage, gimbal movement". Small unscripted beats (a cat follows her, leaves fall in her hair) make it feel unplanned.

Per-beat performance blocks (PRF-102, written for MAGI-2 and transferable): for each speaking beat write Trigger -> Face -> Gaze -> Breath -> End state, e.g. "the boarding pass stops by the cup -> inner brows lift very slightly, lower lip pressed once and released -> eyes rise slowly from the cup and lock on him -> small breath in, then speak -> eyes bright, mouth level". Add timing limits ("no tear before 20.0 s", "0.5 s pause after this word") and close the mouth after the line ("lips close immediately after speaking").

Face-only reference + itemised wardrobe lock (WRD-103): "<<<image_1>>> defines ONLY the face... Do NOT use image_1 to determine her wardrobe", then list the outfit piece by piece (jacket colours by panel, innerwear, pants, shoes, bag) and end with a "CRITICAL WARDROBE LOCK" that names the wrong result you saw in drafts ("Never replace it with a teal/orange jacket"). Naming the specific drift worked better than a generic "no wardrobe changes".

Hand-assignment lock (@PixelDojoAI): say which hand holds the prop and which one gestures while talking, and add "never swap"; the prop stayed in the same hand for all 15 s. The same thread writes dialogue word for word with "exact lip-sync" and times every angle ("5.2-9.0s ANGLE 3, skin close-up: the camera leans in by hand to about 30 cm... autofocus hunts").

Locked-camera hard cuts (REA-103): "Six hard-cut scenes, always the exact same locked framing" from "one fixed, slightly wide-angle viewpoint positioned low on the center console", with "Identical framing and focal length in every cut. No camera movement, zoom, reframing". The location changes while the frame does not, which reads like a self-filmed dashcam vlog. End with an action that covers the lens.

Timing adherence vs the new MAGI-2 (community test, not official): one 30 s prompt with six timed beats was run on four models; the poster measured mean timing error of 0.21 s for MAGI-2, 0.22 s for Seedance 2.5, 0.56 s for Kling 4.0 and 0.72 s for Wan 3.0 Prime, and judged Seedance 2.5 still steadier on object continuity (a caught cup keeps its spilled water). Another side-by-side found both Seedance 2.5 and MAGI-2 ignored "no music" with six references, so check audio and remove music in post if needed.

sections.title: Community patterns seen in this library (Seedance 2.5 entries)

items.text: Creators who ship 30 s clips tend to use: a STYLE/LOOK block → identity-lock line ("Lock her exact face, identity…") → 5-6 s timestamped beats → AUDIO block ("No music") → an explicit continuity/exclusions list. See REA-022, REA-020, PRP-028, GRN-019.
Deliberately degraded capture language works well for realism ("old low-quality iPhone 1x look: heavy noise/compression, handheld shake"), e.g. REA-019, GRN-020, REA-016.
For hidden-cut outfit changes, use a locked camera and name the occluder ("hard outfit cuts hidden by passing cars"), e.g. TRN-013.
Match-cut lock: frame both shots as a "true 90° overhead" and add "circle size and center lock across the cut" so the shape carries across the cut.
Storyboard sheets duplicating a character: add "Multiple storyboard panels represent sequential shots, NOT multiple [name]s."

Two-character contact scenes: add a HAND & PROP CONTINUITY block ("A's right hand connects with B's left… Preserve this physical pairing across camera angles", "Never duplicate it") plus an explicit dialogue-assignment list. See PRF-028.
Selfie-POV drift in vlog prompts: state "Third-person movie-style footage filmed by another person. She does NOT hold the camera."
Camera-only blockouts: an untextured Blender scene with just the camera path, and no mannequins, is enough to lock the move.

The MiniDV/camcorder look was this week's strongest grain pattern: 4:3, focus hunting, auto-exposure shifts, "filmed by a friend", "found rather than filmed", and a hand covering the lens to end. See GRN-021 to GRN-024.

Platforms creators reported using: Dreamina, Higgsfield, WizstarAI, ImagineArt, Atlas Cloud, Dola AI and ElevenLabs. These come from the creators' posts and haven't been checked against each platform.

syntax: Multi-shot: "Shot 1: … Shot 2: …" in chronological order, each with camera/transition, action, location, sound. The community also uses timestamped beats like [00:00-00:05].
References: @Image1…@Image9 (upload order) plus video/audio refs. Bind each asset to one role: "@Image1 controls character identity; @Image2 controls scene style."
Community format that works well: [Style] / [Scene] / [Character] / [Shot Details] blocks, then explicit negatives ("ZERO cuts…", "no text, logos, watermark").
Long, production-brief prompts (logline, format, character lock, shot list, audio) are common for 15–30 s outputs.
guides.tips: For one-takes, state "ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN CONTINUOUS SHOT" and forbid cuts and dissolves. For hidden cuts, name the occluder ("hard outfit cuts hidden by passing cars"). See the Seedance 2.5 guide above for differences: 2.0 does not respond to timestamps and caps at 15 s.

syntax: Formula: cinematography + subject + action + context + style/ambiance.
Dialogue in quotes with a speaker and delivery cue: A woman says, "We have to leave now."
Audio as separate labeled lines: "SFX: thunder cracks in the distance." / "Ambient noise: quiet hum of a starship bridge." / "Audio: …"
Clips are 4/6/8 s, 16:9 or 9:16, 720p/1080p. Up to 3 reference images (character/product/scene); first+last frame interpolation; extend.
Negative prompts go in a separate field. Describe what you want instead of using "no …" in the main prompt.
guides.tips: Name one camera move and the lens/optics (shallow DOF, rack focus, fisheye). For performance, write voice and delivery ("in a weary voice") next to the line.

syntax: Duration, resolution and character references are API parameters (seconds: 4/8/12/16/20; size e.g. 1280x720, 1920x1080 on Pro). Prose like "make it longer" does nothing.
Prompt anatomy: style/format, then scene, then cinematography (shot, angle, lens, move), then actions as timed beats, then lighting/palette, then dialogue and sound.
Dialogue goes in a separate block under the visual description. Keep exchanges short so they fit the clip length.
Use image input for the first frame and the Characters API for reusable subjects (up to 2). Iterate with edits and extensions.
guides.tips: One clear camera move and one clear subject action per shot is more reliable than dense keyword lists. Anchor color with 3–5 named palette colors.

syntax: Subject + environment + action + camera movement + visual style, in plain language.
Time-coded beats: "0–5 s: wide shot …; 5–10 s: slow push-in …; 10–15 s: pull back."

References: @Image1…@ImageN and @Video1, e.g. "Reference the camera path and pacing of @Video1." / "Reference the facial features of the characters in @Image1, @Image2 … keep them strictly consistent."
UI camera controls: horizontal, vertical, zoom, pan, tilt, roll + 4 Master Shots.
Native audio/dialogue, Multi-Shot and Custom Multi-Shot (per-shot duration, size, perspective, move).
Kling 4.0 Omni Reference: give each reference a role and a scope, e.g. "@Image1 defines the scene; preserve layout and lighting. @Image2 defines the protagonist…" (Kling 4.0 User Guide).

Kling 4.0 prompt skeleton (official User Guide): [Asset Roles] → [Overall Settings] → [Sequence of Events] → [Audio] (dialogue/voiceover + ambient + music + SFX). Tell the model what each asset contributes.
Edits: write "Edit @Video1 …" plus "Keep everything else unchanged." Writing "Reference @Video1" may be read as reference generation, not an edit.

Long-form numbered format from the official examples: SCENE CONTEXT ("EXACTLY 1 DRAGON — NO DUPLICATES"), ACTIVE REFERENCES, LOCATION MAP, FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING, FORMAT MODE (timed shots and cut motivation), OPTICS, CAMERA, ACTION TIMING, PHYSICS, LIGHTING, AUDIO, CHARACTER ACTING, STYLE, QUALITY, POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS. Library: TRN-026, TRN-027, TRN-028.
Negatives: use descriptive language and few abstract terms or negatives. The guide says only "no subtitles" and "no background music" are truly necessary.

Style transfer (official User Guide): "Edit @Video 1 by transforming the entire video into the felt style shown in @Image 1. Preserve the original video's composition, camera shots, camera movements, character actions, timing, and sequence exactly. Change only the visual style …" When asking for an animation style, explicitly exclude photorealism. Library: AES-036.

Cut continuity (official counting-forest example): a LOCATION MAP, identical OPTICS (35mm, 54° FOV) and camera height in every shot, one light direction, ambience and music that "never reset at the cuts", and burned-in subtitles timed to the hundredth of a second. Library: TRN-030.

Kling O3 is the name third-party hosts use for Kling VIDEO 3.0 Omni (not a new model). Hosts expose multi_prompt shots of 1-12 s each, 3-15 s in total, prompts up to 2,500 characters, and up to 4 reference images (e.g. apidot, ImagineArt). Use the same syntax as 3.0 Omni above.

Community test (X, @HBCoop_, 2026-10-20; TRN-052): Kling 4.0 had no multi-shot switch in their API, but a single sentence listing four shots in order ("Cut between shots of the same scene: a wide …; a close-up …; …; back to the wide …") still cut in the written order, close to Kling 3.0 in multi-shot mode. Library also has CAM-110 (Kling 4.0, a focal length per numbered shot).

Kling 4.0 4K / HDR (official API update 11/19/2026): settings.resolution accepts "4k" (also 720p / 1080p) and the new settings.dynamic_range = "hdr" gives 10-bit HDR at 1080p or 4K only (720p is SDR); HDR costs extra per second. Writing "4K" or "HDR" in the prompt does not change the output; only the settings do. The official HDR example file is HEVC 10-bit HLG / BT.2020 (REA-097).

Kling 4.0 Video Prompt Guide (official API docs): keyframe patterns: "@Image1 as the first frame, [what happens next]"; "@Image1 as the first frame, @Image2 as the last frame, generate [the process in between]" (for transformations, craft demos, before/after); "@Image1 as the last frame, [what happens before]"; intermediate frames as "X-Ys | Keyframe 1: [what happens]" lines that also say how the camera arrives. The manual adds: prefer positive descriptions, but write "no subtitles" / "no background music" explicitly because the model may add them.
guides.tips: Use one main camera move per shot. Patterns: "Camera slowly pushes in on [subject] to emphasize [emotion]" and "Slow, stable pan left across [scene], no sudden motion." Kling 4.0 (launched 2026-10-15 per Kuaishou IR): native 30 s single pass; Omni Reference with up to 15 references (≤10 images, 5 videos, 7 subjects) and up to 10 keyframes; prompts up to 8,000 tokens; 10-bit HDR; white-model and depth-map video references; MCP/CLI access. 4K/1080p/21:9 and extension to 2 minutes are announced as coming. User Guide specs (Oct 14, 2026): 3-30 s single generation, multi-shot on by default; 720p/1080p/4K; 21:9 / 16:9 / 1:1 / 9:16 / Auto; up to 15 reference assets (≤10 images, 5 videos totalling ≤30 s, 7 elements, 3 voice profiles from 5-30 s of audio); up to 10 keyframes; ≤8,000 tokens. 4.0 Flash: up to 20 s at max 720p, with no start/end frames (per the FAQ). Community (@HBCoop_): Flash is about 60 vs 90 credits per 10 s; crop face references tight with no grey studio background; scope each image ("use image 1 only for style and color palette"); leave unwanted props out of world references. Community (@EndFolding79421): to drive a dance with a song, convert the audio to a black-screen MP4 and attach it as a video reference.
