syntax: Formula: [Overall description] + [Image N / Video N / Audio N references] + [Shot N (start-end s): shot size, lens, move, action] + [Dialogue: xx says: "…"] + [Sound effect / BGM] + [Style / Mood] + [Negative prompt list]. Library: MOO-029.
References are numbered by upload order, counted separately per type (Image 1, Video 1 and Audio 1 can coexist).
Shot joins: end a segment with "hard cut" or "dissolve", or start the next with "seamlessly continue from the last frame of the previous segment". Library: WRD-032 (five hard-cut beats).
Audio: write "No dialogue" explicitly, or the model decides for itself. Append "Lip sync" to dialogue lines. Use "voice timbre reference Audio N".

Clay render → realism: an "[Absolutely unchanged · highest priority]" block locks camera path, cut points, aspect ratio and duration, then material, character, lighting and quality blocks. Library: REA-029.

Line-guided camera: draw the path and waypoint order as red lines on the reference image, restate each segment (speed, pass-through, slow-mo) in the prompt, and say that all red lines and markers are removed in the final footage. Library: CAM-089.

Editing: "Edit the video: change xxx in video 1 to yyy, keep the rest of the frame unchanged". Use add / delete / replace / change to / reshape, one change at a time. Extension needs "extend / continue" plus a direction, and input + output must be ≤30 s.
Storyboard images: "use only as shot guidance" so the sketches are not rendered.

Edit wording examples (official): "Edit the video: brighten the overall lighting of video 1, applying soft three-point lighting …" (REA-035); "Reshape the plot of video 1: have the man directly pick up the guitar …" (PRF-039). Timbre transfer uses bracketed blocks: [Timbre and dialogue] [Lip sync and expression] [Lighting and scene] [Camera and quality] (PRF-040).

Extension: "Extend video 1 forward by 15s." Then restate every character's costume in full so wardrobe carries into the new segment (WRD-034). First frame: label every timestamped beat with Camera movement / Picture / Action / Details / Mood (AES-037). First+last frame: "35mm film stock" or "authentic film grain" per shot for a film look (GRN-026); bracketed second ranges for a single-take morph (TRN-031).
guides.tips: Specs (official guide): 2-30 s or -1 (smart duration), 480P/720P/1080P, 30 fps MP4, audio on by default; up to 20 references (≤10 images, ≤5 videos totalling ≤15 s, ≤5 audio clips totalling ≤15 s, plus 1 document or public web page). First/last frame cannot be combined with reference inputs. For editing, set ratio adaptive and duration -1. The /wan3-pe skill (wan3-pe.zip) refines prompts. Library examples: MOO-029, WRD-032, REA-029, CAM-089.

syntax: Image to video: the start image sets the look and the prompt directs motion, so spend words on motion, not appearance. Point at what is already in frame with "the …" ("the papermaker", "the crow on the rim").

Five-part shape (official): Camera ("Static symmetrical frame." / "A slow push-in" / "the camera cranes slowly down") → main action written as beats in order ("then", "as") → secondary motion in the environment (steam, spray, laundry, ripples) → sky/light change ("the colors deepen from tangerine to rose") → "Sound:" with 3-4 specific sounds. Library: MOO-031 and the other 2026-10-20 FLUX 3 Max entries.

One camera move per shot is the safe default; when you need two, give each its own verb. "Nothing else moves" or "The camera holds" stops invented motion. Similes set pace ("like petals breathing"). Use one small object for scale.

Frame for the subject: official examples run from 21:9 (horizons, flocks) to 3:4 (anything that rises). Say "one continuous shot" when it matters, because the model sometimes cut to a new angle on its own.

Text to video (model page examples): long single-shot specs with second-by-second timing, a period film-print look ("35mm colour negative … aged dye-transfer release print … coarse organic film grain, halation"), "Every person is an original fictional adult", and an "Avoid:" list. Library: GRN-030, GRN-031, AES-039.
guides.tips: Specs (fal, Oct 2026): text-to-video and image-to-video endpoints (blackforestlabs/flux-3-max/text-to-video and the image-to-video equivalent), 720p, native audio. A 10 s clip takes about 12 s; guide examples are 5-10 s. $0.17/s list, $0.0425/s until Nov 7, 2026. fal says it is tied for #1 on Artificial Analysis's preliminary I2V arena (1,139 Elo, same as Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3 at 1,141); that is a vendor-reported, preliminary ranking. The base FLUX 3 (BFL) adds draft, keyframe and extend endpoints. For Seedance 2.5 work, port the five-part shape into first-frame mode (ratio adaptive).

syntax: Formats (official): a short phrase ("A red fox leaping through fresh snow, telephoto."), long natural language, a one-liner shape "[camera] shot of [subject] [action] in [environment]. [supporting details]", labeled fields (Camera shot / Subject + action / Depth of field / Lighting + palette / Motion / Style), and timestep lines ("0.0–1.5s — …"; two or three beats per 5 s). Library: REA-040, AES-046, MOO-040.

Prompt schema for multi-shot (official): Core summary → Scene (per shot: setting, light, DOF) → Subject description (held identically) → Dynamic narrative (per shot, timecoded, camera + action) → Audio (per shot) → Style and color (realism level, palette anchors, grain).

Cuts: "SHOT ONE: … HARD CUT. SHOT TWO: … One music bed across all three shots." Shots should differ strongly in scale; 2-3 per generation (TRN-034). The cheatsheet names transitions directly: match cut, whip transition, foreground wipe, object portal, pass-through, quick cuts, jump cut, screen-in-screen (TRN-039..045, PRF-051).

Audio: four layers (speech, ambience, effects, music). Quote exact words with a visible speaker or "voiceover"; "No on-screen text, no subtitles"; for languages, label each line, set the order and say "same voice", or write native script (PRF-046..048, REA-042). Directions like "one audible breath" can become too prominent.

i2v keyframes field: one image = opening frame, two = start and end, three or more (or [seconds, image] pairs, up to 10) = waypoints; timestamped or 3+ keyframe requests need an explicit duration. Keep keyframes related so the path is plausible (TRN-035..037).

Video inputs: reference_video keeps the cast for a new shot (restate the staging to recast only the medium, e.g. a 1928 silent print where the sound is recast too); start_video continues from the final frames: name what they show first. Inputs are mp4 up to 50 MB / 15 s; reference_video at 720p caps output at 15 s (TRN-038, PRF-049).

FLUX Video Edit [fast] (/v1/flux-tools/video-edit-v1, send video + prompt, no mode): name the change only; add placement and look for added objects; restyle via materials; keep a replacement line as long as the speech it replaces; a silent source returns a silent result; chain edits one per pass (PRP-037/038, REA-043/044, MOO-041).
guides.tips: Specs (BFL docs, Oct 2026): POST /v1/flux-3-video with mode t2v / i2v / v2v / draft_enhance. Duration 5-20 s or auto; aspect auto, 21:9, 2:1, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16, 9:21; resolution hd (default, 1280×704 at 16:9), fhd, qhd, uhd (upsampled from the same generation); generate_audio on by default; draft: true gives a fast hd preview plus a draft_cache for draft_enhance. Rate limit is 5 concurrent generations per org (429 = wait for a slot). Omni Reference is listed as "Soon". FLUX 3 Max is fal's separate post-trained variant (see its own entry).

syntax: Single shot: one flowing present-tense paragraph of 4-8 sentences: shot, scene (light, palette, texture), action as verbs, characters (age, hair, clothing, emotion through physical cues), camera relative to the subject, audio. Quote dialogue and name the language and accent next to it (PRF-055).

Multishot (new in 2.5): one chronological paragraph, with no shot list or sluglines. At each transition, name the edit, re-establish the shot, re-identify the character with the same words, and say what happens to the sound. Lightricks recommends 2-4 shots per generation (WRD-037).

LTX docs: don't paste Kling/Seedance tag or shot-list prompts in unchanged. Rewrite them into the paragraph structure or run them through the prompt enhancer (turn the enhancer off for exact prompts).

Image-to-video: protect the still ("Hold the decanter, the bar top, the backlight and the framing of the still exactly as they are") and add one event (PRP-043). With start + end frame, make the end frame by editing the start frame at identical dimensions, then order the changes in the prompt (TRN-049).

Settings (fal): Pro t2v/i2v duration 6/8/10/auto, 720p/1080p, 24/25/50 fps; Fast 6-20 s up to 2160p. camera_motion is an 8-value enum that overrides prose, so leave it empty unless you want static. Stay at 24/25 fps for dialogue. Audio-to-video takes a 2-20 s track. Open weights need num_frames % 8 == 1 and width/height divisible by 32.

Community (X, @michaelricks; GRN-093): an LTX Desktop fork with custom look "skills" produced a 2.39:1 anamorphic three-shot scene; the prompt repeats the full light + lens + grain block after every hard cut and limits the flare to one shot.
guides.tips: Every sound should be "not visible, but locatable" in the frame (GRN-038). Keep signage out of shots; Lightricks says text spelling and stability are unreliable.

syntax: Brief, not a poem: subject + action are required. Add setting, style, camera (operator terms: push-in, rack focus, crane, locked-off), sound and a timeline only when the shot needs them. "Praise words" (stunning, epic, 8k) give the model nothing (REA-053 vs its vague version).
Dialogue: anything in double quotes is voiced and lip-synced in dozens of languages. Pin each line to a timecode (0-4s / 4-8s) and keep lines short (PRF-054).
Cuts happen only when asked: write "cut to" or a timecoded shot list (TRN-048). Sound: list what is audible and write "no music" (MOO-049).

Happy Horse 1.0 guide: ~20-word default "[Subject] [does action] in [setting], [time of day], [one atmosphere or camera cue]". Spend extra words only on camera and light. For long single takes, use markdown sections (## Subject / ## Action / ## Setting / ## Camera / ## Lighting / ## Mood; MOO-050).
Endpoint alibaba/happy-horse/v1.1/text-to-video (plus image-to-video and reference-to-video): 720p/1080p, 3-15 s, nine aspect ratios from 21:9 to 9:21, prompt up to 2,500 characters.
guides.tips: The more specifics, the more the model can get wrong. fal suggests iterating with video-to-video, reference-to-video and seeds rather than overloading one prompt.

syntax: Specs (Sand AI launch post): 480B-parameter MoE (~28B active); up to 30 s of 1080p, 25 fps video with native audio (dialogue with lip-sync, foley, ambience, music); six aspect ratios; omni-reference up to 20 items (10 images, 5 videos, 5 audio clips); "precision timeline and shot-cut control"; targeted editing of existing video. Open weights announced as "coming soon". [1]

API (Sand AI platform): POST /v2/generations with model "magi-2", a parts array holding exactly one text item (up to 15,000 Unicode code points) plus reference_image / reference_video / reference_audio items in input order, duration (whole seconds), aspectRatio ("16:9"), resolution 1080p only, optional enhancePrompt, generateAudio (default true) and seed. Reference videos 2-30 s each, 30 s combined. [2][3]

Write the clip as a timed shot list: one-line scene (place, time, light), subjects described the same way every time, then one line per shot ("0-8s: close-up, ...", "8-18s: low-angle view, ...") and say whether each cut is hard or on an action. Dialogue in quotes with the speaker named; sound last, including what to leave out ("no music"). Three or four shots in 30 s read better than ten. [6]

Prompt formula (VidMuse): reference descriptions (what each asset is for, numbered in upload order) + overall content + shot-by-shot action (one main action per segment, positions and facing, camera, dialogue, sounds) + overall visual and audio rules at the end. For one continuous take, say so and describe where the camera starts, its path and where it ends; time ranges then describe stages, not cuts. [5]

Higgsfield FAQ: framing, camera moves, timing and cuts can all go in the prompt, but for the most consistent results keep each clip to one or two actions and a single camera move. Start and end frames are supported. Edits are written as a change plus what to keep: "Change the jacket from red to navy and keep the original camera movement." For silence, turn off the Sound toggle rather than prompting it. [4]

Timing is executed rigidly (creator reports summarised by AIPick, Douyin): if a segment is too short for its action the pacing jumps and the last shot can be cut off, so give each beat enough seconds. Same reports: punchier colour and sharpness than Seedance 2.5, strong "does what you say" adherence, rougher face close-ups and slightly weaker character likeness than Seedance 2.5. [10]

Director-prompt pattern (PRF-102): header lines (Duration / Aspect ratio / Reference / Audio / Overall style), a GLOBAL CONTINUITY block (Setting, Main subject, Props with distances, Blocking with screen sides, Lighting in Kelvin, Colour ratio 60:30:10), per-beat Performance blocks (trigger, face, gaze, breath, end state, exact line with syllable-level lip-sync), a Camera line with lenses and cut times, Constraints and a Negative list. [7]

Community timing test (one 30 s prompt, six timed beats): mean timing error 0.21 s MAGI-2, 0.22 s Seedance 2.5, 0.56 s Kling 4.0, 0.72 s Wan 3.0 Prime; Seedance 2.5 kept object continuity better. Not an official benchmark. [9]
guides.tips: Treat MAGI-2 as a cheaper, sharper alternative for timed multi-shot drafts (Sand AI lists $0.08 per output second at 1080p) and keep Seedance 2.5 for final hero takes that need the best face likeness and object continuity. Write every beat with its own time range and enough seconds for the action. Mixed 2D-on-photoreal (AES-104) and dialogue dramas (PRF-102) were the strongest launch-day uses; both posted clips carry platform watermarks.

syntax: The model cuts by default and builds a few shots. For one take, say "In a single unbroken scene", "In a single continuous shot" or "No scene cuts".
Timing in natural language ("After 3 seconds, a woman enters", "Every 2s cut to a new frame") or timecodes "[0-3s] … [3-6s] …".

Edits: keep them simple and add "Keep everything else the same" ("Make the phone invisible. Keep everything else the same."). Short negatives work: "No dialogue", "No embellishments", "No extra sound effects".

Interpolation: first image + last image + one sentence naming the transition (TRN-050). Extension: video + "Continue the scene." Extension with a reference: address the image as <IMAGE_REF_0> in the text (PRF-056); optional "task": "extend". [1.1-era note; the <IMAGE_REF_0> tag is deprecated in 1.2, see below]

[1.1] Specs: 3-10 s output, 360p/720p/1080p/4K at 24 fps, inputs are text, image and video (up to 10 s for edit/extend), via the Interactions API. The preview model gemini-omni-flash-preview shuts down October 22, 2026.

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash (2026-11-05): text/image/video in, video with native audio out, 3-15 s (set duration in response_format as a whole second, e.g. "15s"; default 10 s; this overrides any length in the prompt). 360p / 720p (default) / 1080p and 4K (upscaled). gemini-omni-1.1-flash auto-routes to 1.2 on 2026-12-03.

Do NOT put control strings in prompts: <FIRST_FRAME>, <LAST_FRAME>, <IMAGE_REF_0> and <VIDEO_REF_0> are now deprecated and unsupported in future models. Describe each input's role in natural language instead (the official extension example now says "have the character shown in the reference image enter the scene and wave"; compare PRF-056, collected under 1.1).

References: up to 6 images (up to 3 per character, for up to 2 characters). Reference videos: 1 (≤3 s) for 11-15 s outputs, or up to 3 (≤3 s each) for 3-10 s outputs. Audio in reference videos is ignored, and reasoning across several videos is unsupported. The "task" field (text_to_video, image_to_video, reference_to_video, edit, extend) is a fallback only; try plain prompting first.

First/last frame: 3-10 s only (longer returns an error). Official recipe: define the first frame, then the camera path or transition, then exactly what the last frame reveals, e.g. "… transitions as the camera whip-pans to the side, revealing … One continuous shot, no jump cuts." (TRN-070).

Extension: 3-10 s per turn, up to 30 s total. The model reads only the last 10 s of the input, so re-mention anything that appeared earlier. Timestamps in an extension prompt count from the start of the new part. Some final frames of the input get edited to make the join seamless. Per turn, give only the next beat, quoted dialogue, one camera move and an audio cue (PRF-083). Note: the DeepMind page still says "10 second intervals, up to 40 seconds total" and "Omni 1.1" in that section; the API docs say 30 s.

There is no negative-prompt field (also no system instructions, temperature or top_p). Write negatives in the prompt: "No dialogue", "No embellishments", "Do not do X". The DeepMind page lists camera vocabulary that works: "one continuous shot"/"oner", "static"/"locked off"/"fixed", "push in", "punch in", "dolly zoom", "natural smartphone zoom", "film camera", "webcam style".

Editing style (official): short and scoped, e.g. "Change the butterfly to a bee.", "Change the camera angle to be over the violinist's shoulder.", "Edit this keeping everything the same. Add animated motion effects coming out of the skateboard." Restyles keep the motion of the input (TRN-069). Text renders reliably, so spell out any on-screen or background text (AES-070).
guides.tips: Audio is generated by default. Describe it explicitly, especially music, or the model chooses its own. English is the only fully evaluated language. For 1.2, prefer natural-language role descriptions over the deprecated <IMAGE_REF_n> tags.

syntax: Bracketed camera commands inside the prompt: [Truck left], [Truck right], [Pan left], [Pan right], [Push in], [Pull out], [Pedestal up], [Pedestal down], [Tilt up], [Tilt down], [Zoom in], [Zoom out], [Shake], [Tracking shot], [Static shot].

MiniMax H3 base modes (T2VA / I2VA / FL2VA / L2VA) use three fields: integrated_multimodal_description (with [Shot N] and timestamps like "At 00:04.500"), overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music. Library: MOO-028.
H3 I2VA opens with an alignment line: "For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced." Library: CAM-088.

H3 Ref2VA (full reference / editing) uses six sections: subject_definitions (<Subject N>, <Video N>, <Audio N>), summary, retention_analysis (fully_preserved / partially_copy / reference per asset), detailed_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music. Library: PRF-034.
Official prompt-writing skill: npx skills add https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3 --skill h3-prompt-writing (references base-en.txt and ref-en.txt).

H3 keyframe alignment lines (official base-en.txt): FL2VA starts with "How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot N) aligns with the S.SS-second mark of the target video." L2VA aligns only <Picture 1> to the last shot. FL2VA favours a single shot. Later shots start "[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, the camera cuts to …" (no timestamp on Shot 1).
Note: the README's "FL2VA" reproducible case uses the same prompt and output file as the I2VA case (CAM-088), so it was not added separately.

H3 Max (fal's post-trained H3; text-to-video and image-to-video with optional end_image_url for first/last frame): 480p/768p/1080p (768p default), 5-15 s, 21:9 to 9:16 for T2V. fal recommends 768p, 5-10 s, prompt_expansion_mode "balanced", and describing the sound in the same prompt. Official examples range from one-paragraph prompts ending in "Sound: …" (PRF-044, REA-039, PRP-036, AES-045) to a long shot brief with a 60:30:10 colour ratio, @tags and a timecoded one-take block (MOO-038), and a rules-based game-footage prompt (AES-044). Standard H3 (not Max) is the one with 2K, reference-to-video and editing.

FastH3 (MiniMax H3 distilled by FastVideo, served by Reactor; Reactor prompt guide): each clip has no memory, so re-describe the whole world every time. 1024-token hard cap (enqueue refuses longer prompts with prompt_too_long). Order: scene + subject → one camera instruction → a soundscape clause → quoted dialogue with the voice described. For several voices, tag speakers "S1 (the cook, low tired voice): \"…\" S2 (…)". Dense lane: split audio into Soundscape / Music / SFX. Don't write absences ("No crowds" renders crowds). continue_from_clip_id chains clips: each continuation opens on "Hard cut to …" and re-describes the scene. Clip length 5.167-14.375 s.

MiniMax H3 Image (early access on Hailuo from 2026-11-09; model id MiniMax-H3-Image): text-to-image via POST /v1/images/generations with model, prompt, n, area ("1K" / "2K" / "4K"), output_format and optional stream; image editing / multi-reference via /v1/images/edits with 1–16 reference images (JPG/PNG/WEBP/HEIC, 128–8192 px, aspect ratio ≤ 4:1), referred to in the prompt by order as 图1, 图2… ("image 1", "image 2"). Prompt enhancement is on by default in the official console and returns a revised_prompt per image; turn it off to run your prompt as written. The console tip: the more detailed the prompt (subject, style, lighting, composition) the better. Early testers report that very short prompts land behind rivals, while long art-director briefs with references do best.

H3 Image library examples: PRP-074 (same packaging prompt vs Seedream 5.5, Nano Banana 2.1 and GPT Image 2.6; the creator scored Seedream 5.5 first, and no model drew the asymmetric bent horn). Use H3 Image stills as first frames for H3 Video or Seedance 2.5.

Community H3 video patterns added 2026-11-10 (BeatAPI gallery): one-line change prompts with "Duration / Camera" lines (TRN-076, MOO-074), locked-object match chains (TRN-075), self-assembling stop-motion compositions (AES-073), live action + hand-drawn overlays (AES-074), one-take couture with music-mapped beats (WRD-075), millisecond-timed freeze-flash endings (TRN-074).

MiniMax H3 Image open weights (official repo, 2026-11-10/11): MiniMax-H3-Image runs locally (SGLang) or via the API. Local/open request fields: prompt (used as given, truncated to 4096 tokens), size WIDTHxHEIGHT (best around 16 MP; working range about 4–20 MP; e.g. 4096x4096, 4736x3552, 5472x3072, 6272x2688 for 21:9), seed, num_inference_steps omit-or-6 and guidance_scale omit-or-1 (other values return HTTP 400), and negative_prompt is not supported (rejected), so write exclusions into the prompt. Edits upload reference images whose order defines <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>… in the prompt (the console's 图1 / @Picture 1 mean the same).

H3 Image prompt syntax (official h3-image-prompt-writing skill): the model expects a detailed English description of the whole image; the API expands short prompts in any language with H3-Image-Context-IR (local alternative: MiniMax-H3-Image-PE). T2I rules: describe what is visible, not instructions; state grid rows/columns explicitly; keep screen-left/right, gaze and contact consistent; put literal text in single or double quotes on its intended surface and use full-width spaces (U+3000) next to Chinese text; do not delegate copywriting or calculations to the model. Edit rules: one continuous paragraph in the order source definitions ("The red cup at the left of <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>.") → "The target image…" overview and relationships → changed details, narrating the final state rather than issuing commands.
H3 Image library example (official): PRP-077 farm-to-table feast (expanded prompt with region-by-region placement and one light direction).

H3 Image library examples (2026-11-12): GRN-076 slow-shutter pan and MOO-077 dreamcore daisy field (both from the official @MiniMax_AI creator thread), WRD-078 early-1990s winter editorial (six-model comparison). H3 open-weight video tip (GlennHasABeard, PRP-078): give one continuous action and forbid the second ("It never flips…").

H3 open-weight video (2026-11-15, PRF-084, run locally with a Turbo LoRA at 6 steps): a 25 s rapid-fire argument held eight timed lines with tight close-up / reverse cuts when the prompt combined a "Core tone" line (overlapping debate, minimal silence), per-actor delivery notes, a fixed 180-degree axis and "Frame holds static, end directly, no fade out, no black screen".

H3 open-weight dialogue in Mandarin with English subtitles (community, EndFolding79421, 2026-11-18; not ingested: the scene relied on two unshared reference images): write each spoken Mandarin line in quotes, the English translation directly below it labelled "English subtitle:", require "natural Mandarin lip-sync", and use timestamped shots to say when subtitles appear and disappear ("No dialogue. No subtitle."). The creator warns generated subtitles may still need fixing in the edit.
guides.tips: Put the bracket right after the action it should accompany: "A runner sprints through a forest trail [Tracking shot]". MiniMax H3 is an open model (repo created 2026-07-30). Write prompts in its field format rather than as bracketed camera commands; the older bracket syntax above is for Hailuo 02.

syntax: Three modes: T2VA (text only), FL2VA (first and/or last frame), Ref2VA (references and editing). Write scene descriptions in English; keep dialogue and on-screen text in their own language.
T2VA fields: integrated_multimodal_description (visuals, action, camera and synchronized sound) / overall_soundscape (1-4 sentences, no dialogue) / non_diegetic_music (1-3 sentences or N/A).
FL2VA: open with an alignment line ("<Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) aligns with the 0.00-second mark…", times to two decimals), a blank line, then the T2VA fields.

Ref2VA fields: subject_definitions, summary (starts with [reference generation], [video editing] or [video continuation]), retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music.

Labels: <Video N>, <Subject N>, <Picture N>, <Audio N>. Visual retention markers: fully_preserved, partially_preserved, attribute_transfer, weak_reference, removed. Audio markers: fully_copy, partially_copy, reference, weak_reference.
Shots: [Shot 1] has no timestamp; later shots start "[Shot 2] At 00:03.000, …". Say "one continuous shot" or "The camera remains fixed." when that is the intent.

Dialogue: speakers (S1)/(S2), lines as <d>[Language] words</d>; <scenetrans> for speech that runs across a cut, <cutoff> for speech cut off by the end of the video; for voice-over say that the on-screen lips stay closed. On-screen text in double quotes.

Limits (README): 5-15 integer seconds on a 17n+5 frame grid at 24 fps; up to 12 references (9 images, 3 videos, 3 audio), each video/audio 2-15 s. ComfyUI: six steps, a 5 s 1344×768 clip in about a minute; English prompts; no negative prompt at cfg 1.
guides.tips: Give every camera move a start, a direction and an arrival, and end on a hold: amplitude is advisory and timing can be off by about 0.2-0.3 s. A push-in is not a zoom. "Wide shot" alone renders as a medium shot, so describe what fills the frame. Give each action an endpoint and name who does each step of a handoff. Use character sheets for appearance only, "without the sheet panels, labels or alternative views". The showcases also use plain timed prompts (00:00-00:03 — …) with a "NO slow motion" speed clause and separate Sound:/Music: lines (CAM-138). License: MiniMax H3 Community License for the adapters, Apache-2.0 for the code.

syntax: What is new in 5.5 (official blog): (1) more stable multi-turn editing that preserves unedited regions at the pixel level with no colour shift, demonstrated over 100 successive edits on one image; (2) native RGBA output with full and partial transparency, so assets need no background removal; (3) more realistic lighting, materials and skin with less gloss and overexposure, plus clearer complex and dense small text. A Pro version of the 5.5 series is announced as coming later.

Official example phrasing (model page): realism stills are 2–4 plain sentences: subject and place, then a camera/photographic method ("Shoot from a low angle with a tilted composition, using flash, Fujifilm Provia colors and film grain"), then the faults or textures to show ("Slight underexposure, subtle high-ISO grain and foreground occlusion"). Aspect ratio and orientation go in the prose ("A vertical 3:4 street photograph", "A candid horizontal snapshot").

Transparency phrasing (model page): "output it as a separate RGBA layer with a transparent background"; "Keep the background transparent outside the sticker elements"; "Output each character as a separate image with a transparent background"; "keep the area outside each circle transparent". Multi-turn edits are phrased as what changes plus what stays ("Adjust … while keeping the monitor and interface layout consistent").

BytePlus prompt structure for the Seedream family: coherent natural language rather than keywords, e.g. "Create [image type] for [purpose]. Show [subject and action] in [environment]. Use [style, color, lighting, and composition]. Preserve [fixed elements] and change [target elements]." Name the intended use, say what to take from each reference image, keep edits separate from constraints, and put any text that must appear in double quotation marks.

Library examples: official stills GRN-070 (flash + Provia + grain), REA-071 (candid bistro with photographic faults), REA-072 (25° tilt street candid), MOO-071 (puddle reflections), PRP-072 (colour-blocked set dressing). Community: REA-073 (same Japanese prompt vs GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst and Nano Banana 2.1).

Community (2026-11-10): one-warm-practical mood stills hold up well (MOO-073: "cold teal night tones broken by a single warm orange light source", 50mm anamorphic, oval bokeh, fine 35mm grain); in a 4-model packaging test Seedream 5.5 got the most details right (PRP-074). Seedream 5.5 is now on Dreamina, Renoise and Magnific (Retouch edits).

Official API facts (BytePlus Seedream 5.5 tutorial, read 2026-11-13): model ID dola-seedream-5-5-261028; text-to-image, single-image and multi-reference (up to 10 images); resolution presets 1K / 1.5K / 2K or pixel sizes; output png by default (jpeg optional); background auto by default (transparent / opaque); prompt optimisation standard mode. Text-to-RGBA: do not pass image, set background "transparent" and output_format "png", and say the transparent background in the prompt (official example ends "Set a transparent background."; PRP-081). Image-to-RGBA works from up to 10 references that need no alpha channel. Layer decomposition returns one base image plus up to 99 layers (output count 2–100), with rich-text OCR (text, position, approximate style) for regular text layers only.

Official multi-turn edit phrasing (tutorial example): one change, then an explicit preserve list: "Have the person blow a round, semi-transparent pink bubblegum bubble. Preserve the identity, facial features, gaze, hairstyle, pearl earrings, clothing, pose, blue background, composition, and visual style of the person." Official layer prompt: "Separate each animal into a complete, independent layer… Keep all non-animal elements in the base image and naturally fill the areas left after the animals are removed."

Official image-to-RGBA and layer phrasing (Seedream 5.5 tutorial, read 2026-11-14; PRP-084, PRP-085): image-to-RGBA names the sources, the single output, what to keep and the layout: "Extract the sticker elements from Image 1 and Image 2 separately, then place all extracted stickers in one transparent-background image. Preserve each sticker's original text, colors, shapes, and details; remove all background content other than the stickers. Arrange the stickers separately without overlap, with sharp and intact edges." Layer decomposition: layer_decomposition true with layer_decomposition_options.max_images (2–100 including the base image; default 30) and text_recognition true for rich-text OCR; the official animal example (max_images 40) returned 1 base + 32 layers. Layer resolution: 1K / 1.5K / 2K / auto.

Community (WRD-081, Seedream 5.5 on OpenArt): a wardrobe-led editorial prompt with every garment given colour + material, one warm accent against a muted palette, and a failure-targeted texture line ("Real skin texture, tactile wool, believable hands and bouquet construction"). The creator appended Midjourney-style flags (--ar 3:4 --style raw --s 150 --no …); the output was 3:4, but whether Seedream parses these flags is not documented, so set size through the API instead.
guides.tips: Seedream 5.5 stills make good first frames for Seedance 2.5 (same ByteDance family). Generate the still, then use it as first_frame with ratio adaptive. Every Seedream entry here has a Seedance 2.5 adapted template.

syntax: Official specs: up to 10 reference images; prompts up to 15,000 tokens (API: 50,000 characters English-only, 21,000 non-English); 2K / 4K / native 8K; aspect Auto, 3:4, 4:3, 9:16, 16:9, 2:3, 3:2, 21:9, 1:1; up to 2,000 characters of rendered text; 70+ licensed fonts or a font reference image; Series Mode up to 10 consecutive images.
Natural realism template (official): Subject + Action/State + Specific Setting + Smartphone Shooting Style; trigger words include "shot on my phone", "candid", "Unedited camera photo", "SOOC".

Character template (official): Age + Identity/Background + Body Type + Facial Features + Hairstyle + Clothing/Accessories + Personality/Expression. Avoid generic phrases like "refined facial features"; give one prop or gesture that shows personality.

Narrative still template (official): [Visual Style] + [Environment] + [Subject] + [Action / Expression] + [Composition] + [Camera Position / Angle] + [Focus] + [Lighting] + [Texture / Details] + [Color Tone] + [Mood / Atmosphere]. Library: GRN-089.

Documentary template (official): Subject's identity + Physical appearance and clothing + Specific actions/interactions + Everyday setting. Write what the person is doing ("sleeping on a bus") rather than "realistic".
Stylization template (official): [Target Style] + [Features to Preserve] + [Shape and Material] + [Color and Lighting] + [Environment and Composition].

Storyboard / Series Mode (official): [Overall Style and Aspect Ratio] + [Character Descriptions / Reference Images] + [Individual Frame Descriptions] + [Consistency Requirements]; say "Do not combine them into a nine-panel grid" when you want separate frames.

References: cite @Image1…@Image10 in upload order (API: @id) and give each one job (identity, garment, place, style) plus what must not change. Text: put the exact words in quotes, say where they go and describe the lettering.

Documentary Photography template (official): "Subject's identity + Physical appearance and clothing + Specific actions/interactions + Everyday setting"; describe what the subject is doing rather than writing "realistic", and match the texture to the subject (crisp digital for press events, natural colour or film for everyday life, fading and scratches for archival). Examples: REA-090..092 (ferry, corner shop, subway), AES-091 (roadside, direct flash).

Film-still texture (official example, GRN-094): lead with the texture words ("realistic, cinematic aesthetic with film grain, live-action photography, commercial photography, and film-still styling"), then the lens and angle (extreme low wide-angle through a glass panel), then lighting as "dark, low-key lighting with low contrast".
guides.tips: Use Kling Image 4.0 to make start/end frames for video: make the first frame, reuse it as @Image1 for the last frame and change only the moment. Write composition as numbers (angle in degrees, share of frame in %), and for film texture ask for soft edges before grain ("Edges are soft before grain is applied"), not a sharp image with noise. 8K only pays off for crops and print.

syntax: Natural language and JSON work equally well. Official JSON schema: scene, subjects[description, position, action], style, color_palette (hex), lighting, mood, background, composition, camera{angle, lens, depth_of_field}.
Send the JSON as a string in the prompt field.

Refer to up to 10 inputs as "image 1", "image 2", and so on. Bounding boxes go as a JSON list at the end of the prompt, each [top, left, bottom, right] on a 0 to 1000 grid. syntax: Long art-direction briefs work well: FORMAT (ratio, poster or storyboard), subject, styling, lighting, typography with exact text in quotes, and negatives.
Popular uses: ad storyboards, campaign posters, contact sheets and multi-panel product boards.

GPT Image 2.6 (official guide, read 2026-11-08): two models. gpt-image-2.6-flare is the smaller, faster one; gpt-image-2.6-sunburst is the base model for detail, layout and precise edits. Migration advice: 2.5 Flare → 2.6 Flare, 2.5 Sunburst → 2.6 Sunburst, GPT Image 2 → Flare first unless it fell short.

GPT Image 2.6 parameters: quality auto/low/medium/high/xhigh/max (detail such as texture or small lettering); complexity low/medium/high (how much the model plans before rendering; default high); size auto or e.g. 1024x1536, custom sizes in multiples of 16 with an aspect ratio from 1:3 to 3:1; background transparent supported; output_format png/jpeg/webp plus svg and animated gif for generations; markup = a transparent PNG overlay (same pixel size as the first input) for circle-to-edit. Omit input_fidelity on edits.

GPT Image 2.6 prompting fundamentals (official): define the result and intended use; any format works (short prompt, paragraphs, JSON-like, tags), so pick the one that is easiest to maintain; describe visible details and ask for "photorealistic" or "real photograph" explicitly; treat camera specs as appearance cues; describe body framing, gaze and object interaction ("full body visible, feet included"); quote exact text and say where and how often it appears; for edits say "change only X" and list what to preserve; assign each reference a number and a role (subject, style, clothing, background); iterate one change at a time.

Library examples from the official guide: candid realism (REA-069), identity-locked outfit swap from garment references (WRD-069), and a streetwear campaign with an exact tagline (WRD-070). Community GPT Image comparisons: WRD-071.

Community format (X, @lin86996587, GPT Image 2.6; WRD-082, REA-083): six labelled lines, SUBJECT / LIGHT / CAMERA (lens, aperture, framing) / LOCK (what must stay the same across re-runs) / NEGATIVE / TONE. For sequins and metals the creator found the NEGATIVE line ("no blown-out speculars on the sequins") mattered more than the positive description.

Wardrobe tip (WRD-084, @lin86996587, GPT Image 2.6 qipao): use the LOCK line for the garment's defining feature ("silk sheen and the standing silhouette") and control the one detail that decides whether the garment reads correctly (for a qipao, collar height: "too high and the neck disappears; too low and it stops reading as qipao").

Lighting-led stills (X, @CharaspowerAI, GPT Image 2.5; AES-093): name the light by its tool (hard spotlight + narrow slit gobo), give the fill as a stop ratio ("approximately three stops below the red accent"), say how the light must follow facial geometry, and add a clipping guard ("do not clip the red channel into a featureless patch"). Wardrobe stills (WRD-092, WRD-093) work best when the garment is written by construction (neckline, waist, fringe; panels, shards, train) rather than by adjectives.
guides.tips: See the Prop styling and Wardrobe categories for verbatim examples. For 2.6, compare Flare vs Sunburst on the same prompt, size and quality before changing complexity.
